The report also showed that Sheffield Wednesday’s football ground was unsafe in important ways, and the Football Association chose it for the match without checking if it had a valid safety certificate, which it did not.

Because of this neglect, it was the poor management of the crowd by the police, led by the inexperienced Chief Superintendent David Duckenfield, that was the main cause of the disaster. The police lost control outside the stadium, where 24,000 Liverpool fans had to go through only 23 turnstiles. Duckenfield then ordered a large exit gate to be opened, letting in many people at once. His big mistake, according to the inquiry, was not closing the tunnel that led to the already overcrowded central area of the Leppings Lane terrace.

The inquiry found this, but the police still repeated their false claims at the later inquest. The inquest did not look at what happened after 3:15 pm on the day of the disaster, so it did not include the emergency response, which the panel found was chaotic. The panel found that 41 of the 96 people who died might have been saved if the police and ambulance service had done their jobs properly. This is very serious and hard for the families to accept.

Now, because of the panel’s report, the Attorney General will decide whether to ask the High Court to cancel the inquest’s verdict of accidental death and hold a new inquest. There may also be prosecutions, even after all these years, against Sheffield Wednesday, South Yorkshire Police, and Sheffield City Council, which did not make sure the football ground was safe. Trevor Hicks, President of the Hillsborough Family Support Group, whose two teenage daughters, Sarah and Victoria, died in the disaster, said: “The truth is out today. Tomorrow is for justice.”

Independent data shows that Facebook is losing millions of users each month in its biggest markets, as people look for new social networks. While Facebook is about to report a 36% increase in revenue compared to last year, studies show that its growth in the US, UK, and other large European countries has stopped. In the last month, Facebook lost 6 million users in the US, a 4% drop, according to Socialbakers. In the UK, 1.4 million fewer people used Facebook in March, a 4.5% decrease. These drops have continued for months. In the past six months, Facebook lost almost 9 million monthly users in the US and 2 million in the UK.

People are also leaving Facebook in Canada, Spain, France, Germany, and Japan, where Facebook is very popular. A Facebook spokeswoman did not comment on this.

Ian Maude, a new media expert at Enders Analysis, said, “In the US and UK, most people who want Facebook already have it. People get bored and want to try something new. There is a small risk that Facebook could become less popular, like MySpace did.” Other social networks, like Instagram, have become very popular with young people. Instagram got 30 million users in 18 months before Facebook bought it.

Path, a mobile social network started by former Facebook worker Dave Morin, only allows 150 friends per user. Path is getting 1 million new users every week and now has over 9 million users. In one weekend, 500,000 people in Venezuela downloaded the app.

Facebook is still growing quickly in South America. In Brazil, monthly users increased by 6% last month to 70 million. In India, users rose by 4% to 64 million, which is still a small part of the country’s population, so there is room for more growth.

But in developed countries, other companies are also reporting that Facebook is losing users. Analysts at Jefferies bank made a program that connects to Facebook and found that user numbers may have dropped from their highest point in the first quarter of the year. Jefferies saw global user numbers reach 1.05 billion a month in January, then fall by 20 million in February. Numbers went up again in April. In the UK, Facebook has lost almost 2 million users since December, according to Nielsen, and the total number of users is the same as last year at 27 million.

Americans are also spending less time on Facebook. In December 2012, people spent 121 billion minutes on Facebook, but this dropped to 115 billion minutes in February, according to comScore.

Facebook has said that people are spending less time on Facebook from personal computers because they are using smartphones and tablets more. Time spent on Facebook from smartphones has doubled in a year to 69 minutes a month, but this may not make up for the drop in computer use.

Facebook is the best source for its own user numbers, and the company will soon update investors on its results for the quarter. Wall Street expects Facebook to report about $1.44 billion in revenue, up from $1.06 billion in 2012.

Investors especially want to know how quickly Facebook’s mobile user numbers are growing, and if advertising money is growing at the same speed. At the end of 2012, almost a quarter of Facebook’s advertising income came from mobile users, and Facebook had 680 million mobile users each month in December.

The company has warned in recent reports that it might be losing younger users to other products and services that are similar to Facebook. Because of competition from services made for mobile phones, Facebook founder Mark Zuckerberg has started new projects to attract smartphone users. The most important is Facebook Home, software for some Android phones that shows news, photos, and ads from friends directly on the phone’s home screen.

Vienna is the best city in the world to live in, while Baghdad is the worst, according to an international study about quality of life. London, Paris, and New York are not even in the top 35 cities.

Cities where people speak German are at the top of the list in the 18th Mercer Quality of Life study. Vienna is joined by Zurich, Munich, Dusseldorf, and Frankfurt in the top seven cities.

Paris has dropped ten places to number 37, just ahead of London at number 39. This is mostly because Paris is seen as more at risk of terrorist attacks.

The study looked at social and economic conditions, health, education, housing, and the environment. Big companies use this study to decide where to open offices and how much to pay their workers.

Helena Hartlauer, who was born in Vienna, said she was not surprised that her city is number one. Vienna’s government has a long history of spending money on good social housing, which makes the city much more affordable than other big cities.

She said, “I live in a 100-square-meter apartment from the early 1900s in a good area, about 20 minutes’ walk from the city center. My rent is only €800 (£625) a month.” A similar apartment in London would cost at least £2,000, and even more in New York, which is number 44 on the list.

US cities do not do well in the study, mostly because of problems with safety and crime. The best US city is San Francisco at number 28, and Boston is number 34. Canadian cities, especially Vancouver, are much higher on the list than US cities.

Hartlauer said, “You don’t realize how safe Vienna is until you travel abroad. We also have great public transport. The underground runs all night on weekends, and it only costs €1 per trip.”

Vienna became much more important after the Berlin Wall fell, because it became a gateway to Eastern European countries that have historic connections to Austria.

Martin Eichtinger, the Austrian ambassador to London, said, “Our big advantage is our location. The fall of the Berlin Wall made Vienna the center for companies wanting to do business in Central Europe.” He lived in Vienna for 20 years.

According to the World Bank, Austria has one of the highest GDP per person in the world, just behind the US and ahead of Germany and Britain, but still lower than Switzerland.

Zurich in Switzerland is named by Mercer as the city with the second highest quality of life, but people from Vienna say their city is more fun. Hartlauer said, “There are more students in Vienna than in any other German-speaking city. It’s a fast-growing, young, and lively city.” She also works for the city’s tourist board.

British tourists often ignore Vienna for weekend trips, choosing Barcelona or Berlin instead, and think of Austria as a place for skiing, lakes, and mountains. But now, with more cheap flights from British cities like Manchester and Edinburgh, Vienna is becoming more popular. In 2015, 588,000 British people visited Vienna, which is 18% more than the year before. Austrians also visit London a lot; it is now the top city for Austrian visitors.

Mercer said, “Vienna has been number one in the last seven rankings. It scores high in many areas: it is safe and stable, has good public services and transport, and good places for fun and relaxation.”

The European migrant crisis, which brought many refugees through Vienna on their way to Germany, has not had much effect on the city of nearly 1.8 million people, said Eichtinger. “We have managed to take in 90,000 refugees in Austria, but the numbers have slowed down recently.” London has never been in the top ten for quality of life, mostly because of bad air, traffic, and weather. After London, Edinburgh is the next best British city at number 46.

Paris has dropped the most in the latest rankings. Mercer said, “Paris was stable for several years but dropped ten places this year, mainly because of the terrorist attacks in 2015. Safety is a very important part of the ranking, so even small changes can have a big effect.”

Auckland in New Zealand is the highest English-speaking city in the survey, at number three, followed by Vancouver at number five. Australian cities also do well, with Sydney at number 10 and Melbourne at number 15. The Economist magazine often says Melbourne is the world’s most liveable city, but some people say their survey is too focused on English-speaking countries.

War and political problems are the main reasons for the lowest-ranked cities. Surprisingly, Damascus is only the seventh worst city, doing better than Baghdad, Bangui (Central African Republic), Sana’a (Yemen), Port-au-Prince (Haiti), Khartoum (Sudan), and N’Djamena (Chad).

The Moroccan city of Ouarzazate is used to hosting big film productions. It is on the edge of the Sahara Desert and is the center of Morocco’s “Ouallywood” film industry. Many famous movies and TV shows, like Lawrence of Arabia, The Mummy, The Living Daylights, and Game of Thrones, have been filmed there.

Now, Ouarzazate is the site of another big project: a group of four connected solar power plants. Together with hydro and wind power, these plants will help Morocco get almost half of its electricity from renewable sources by 2020. Morocco also hopes to have extra energy to sell to Europe. This project is important for Morocco’s plan to use its deserts to become a world leader in solar energy.

When finished, the Ouarzazate complex will be the largest concentrated solar power plant in the world. The first part, called Noor 1, will start working in November 2015. The plant uses special mirrors, which are less common and more expensive than the solar panels seen on many roofs. However, these mirrors can keep making electricity even after the sun goes down.

People have known for a long time that deserts have great potential for solar power. After the Chernobyl nuclear accident in 1986, German scientist Gerhard Knies calculated that the world’s deserts get enough energy in a few hours to power the whole world for a year. The problem has been how to collect this energy and send it to where people live.

As engineers finish Noor 1, its 500,000 crescent-shaped mirrors shine in the desert. The 800 rows of mirrors follow the sun as it moves across the sky, turning quietly every few minutes.

When all four plants are finished, they will cover an area as large as Morocco’s capital, Rabat, and produce 580 megawatts (MW) of electricity, enough for one million homes. Noor 1 alone can produce 160 MW.

Morocco’s Environment Minister, Hakima el-Haite, says solar energy could change the region as much as oil did in the past century. But the $9 billion project started because Morocco needed to solve more urgent problems. “We are not an oil producer. We import 94% of our energy as fossil fuels, which is very expensive for our country,” she said. “We also used to pay subsidies for fossil fuels, which cost a lot. So when we learned about solar energy, we thought, ‘Why not?’”

By 2020, solar energy will provide one third of Morocco’s renewable energy, with wind and hydro power each providing another third.

“We are very proud of this project,” el-Haite said. “I think it is the most important solar plant in the world.”

Each curved mirror is 12 meters high and focuses sunlight onto a steel pipe that carries a special liquid called ‘heat transfer solution’ (HTF). This liquid is heated to 393°C as it moves along the pipe, then goes into a heat engine. There, it mixes with water to make steam, which turns turbines to generate electricity.

The HTF is made of synthetic thermal oil and is pumped to a tank with molten sand that can store heat for three hours. This lets the plant provide electricity even at night. The mirrors are arranged in tiers to protect them from sand blown by the wind.

Technicians say that Noor 2 and 3, which will open in 2017, will be able to store energy for up to eight hours. This could make 24-hour solar energy possible in the Sahara and nearby areas.

“The biggest challenge was finishing the project on time and meeting our performance goals,” said Rashid al-Bayad, the project director.

Even as the first part of the project is almost done, Morocco is planning bigger things. “We are already working on high-voltage power lines to cover southern Morocco and Mauritania as a first step,” said Ahmed Baroudi, manager of the national renewable energy investment company. He says the project could have an even bigger impact, possibly reaching as far as the Middle East. “The final goal, given by the king, is Mecca.”

It is not certain if this goal will be reached, but exporting solar energy could help bring stability to Morocco and its neighbors, according to the Moroccan solar energy agency (Masen). Morocco is talking with Tunisia, and sending energy north to Europe is still a main goal.

“We believe it’s possible to export energy to Europe, but first we need to build the necessary connections, which do not exist yet,” said Maha el-Kadiri, a Masen spokeswoman. “We would need to build new connections, not use the one in Spain, and then start exporting.”

Spain has stopped new solar projects because there are not enough connections to send energy to France. The European Union wants each member country to be able to send 10% of its power abroad by 2020.

For now, Morocco is focused on using solar energy to become more independent. In the future, this could include using solar power to turn seawater into drinking water, which is important as Morocco faces more droughts due to climate change. Officials know that Morocco is leading the way in renewable energy in the Middle East and North Africa. “We are at the front of solar energy,” el-Kadiri says.

About $9 billion has been invested in the Noor Complex, mostly from international organizations like the European Investment Bank and World Bank, with support from the Moroccan government. Secret subsidies from King Mohammed VI have kept the costs from being passed on to customers.

One month before opening, more than a thousand workers, mostly Moroccan, are still working hard to finish the project. They are fixing electric wires, removing scaffolding, and wrapping insulation around steel pipes. They work in yellow and orange vests, 12 hours a day, with the Atlas Mountains in the background. They wear hard hats, safety shoes, and ear plugs.

For Hajar Lakhael, a 25-year-old environment and safety manager from Meknes, the preparations are almost finished and the big project is nearly ready to start.

“We’ve finished building, and now we will see how the project works when it starts,” she says. “It is just like getting ready for a big show.”

People around the world will be watching with interest.

Swedish prisons are known for being modern and progressive. But are they too easy for prisoners? In November 2013, Nils Oberg, the head of Sweden’s prison and probation service, said that four prisons in Sweden would close because there were fewer prisoners than before. This was unusual. 

Even though crime rates did not go down, the number of prisoners in Sweden dropped by 6% between 2011 and 2012. Now, there are just over 4,500 prisoners. A similar drop was expected in 2013 and 2014. Oberg was surprised by this, but he hoped it was because of the way Swedish prisons focus on helping prisoners not to commit crimes again. He said, “We hope our work in rehabilitation and stopping people from reoffending has made a difference.”

Kenneth Gustafsson, the governor of Kumla Prison, Sweden’s most secure prison, said that prisons in Sweden have changed a lot since he started working in 1978. Back then, the focus was on treating prisoners well. Some people thought prisoners were treated too well. But after some famous escapes in 2004, prisons became stricter and focused more on security. Still, Gustafsson does not think Swedish prisons are too soft.

Even after making prisons more secure, Sweden still tries to treat prisoners humanely, even those who commit serious crimes. Prison sentences are usually not longer than ten years. People with life sentences can ask the court after ten years to change their sentence to a fixed number of years, usually between 18 and 25 years. Sweden was the first country in Europe to use electronic tags for criminals. The country also tries to avoid short prison sentences by using community service and other programs, which have been shown to help stop people from committing crimes again.

In Sweden, about 30 to 40% of people released from prison commit another crime within three years. This is about half the rate in the UK. One reason for Sweden’s low reoffending and prison rates (less than 70 prisoners per 100,000 people) is that the age of criminal responsibility is 15. In the UK, children as young as ten can be held responsible for crimes, and young people under 21 have the highest rates of reoffending. Many of these young offenders end up in adult prisons. In Sweden, no one under 21 can get a life sentence, and the country tries hard to keep young people out of prison.

Another reason for fewer prisoners in Sweden may be the strong support given to people after they leave prison. The probation service, a government agency, not only supervises people on probation but also gives them treatment for drug, alcohol, or violence problems. About 4,500 volunteers from the public help support and befriend people under supervision.

Gustafsson says that in 2013 and 2014, the main focus was on helping young offenders and men with violent crimes. Sweden has had programs for drug addiction for many years, and now there are also programs to help with aggression and violence. These programs are important for society when prisoners are released.

A former prisoner, Peter Soderlund, now runs a group called X-Cons Sweden. He spent almost three years in prison for drug and weapons crimes and was released in 1998. He got help from an organization called Kris, which is run by former prisoners. Soderlund says that X-Cons is different from Kris because they allow people who are still taking addiction medicine to join. Both groups help prisoners return to society after release. Soderlund says that when he was in Osteraker Prison, he was treated well, but not all prisons were the same. He met many people who needed help. After getting help from Kris, he wanted to help others. With X-Cons, they meet prisoners at the gate, help them find a place to live, and give them support.

Gustafsson says, “In Sweden, we believe in rehabilitation, but we are not naive. Some people cannot or do not want to change. But most prisoners want to change, and we must help them. Sometimes, one prison sentence is not enough. Rehabilitation is not just about prison—it also involves probation and help from society. We can give education and training, but when people leave prison, they also need housing and jobs.”

The normal eight-hour workday is finished. The most important tasks are done; anything left can wait until tomorrow. At this time, many workers would think about going home. 

However, for millions of Japanese workers, leaving work on time and being home for dinner can make others think they are not loyal to their company. 

For many years, Japanese companies have expected workers to work very hard and for long hours. Now, the government is challenging this culture of overwork. The government is thinking about making a law that would require workers to take at least five days of paid holiday each year.

Japanese workers can get an average of 18.5 days of paid holiday each year, which is only two days less than the world average. The minimum is ten days, plus 15 national holidays. But in reality, most workers do not take all their holidays. Usually, they only use about nine out of their 18.5 days, according to the labor ministry. While many British workers see a two-week summer holiday as a basic right, Japanese workers think that even a four-night trip to Hawaii is a big luxury.

This possible new law will be discussed in the current parliament session. It comes after some companies started telling workers to take naps at work to help them perform better.

By the end of the decade, the government hopes that, if the law passes, Japanese workers will start to use more of their paid holidays, like British workers who use about 20 days a year, and French workers who take about 25 days.

Japan’s strict work culture has helped make the country very rich, and Japanese workers are respected around the world for their loyalty. But this has often meant they have little time for anything else.

Japan’s low birth rate and the expected fast drop in population are partly because couples do not have enough time to start families. More workers are getting sick from stress, or even dying from overwork, a problem called karoshi.

Studies show that working longer hours does not always make people more productive. But today’s workers still feel pressure from the habits of the 1980s, when people worked even more.

About 22% of Japanese workers work more than 49 hours a week. In the US, it is 16%, and in France and Germany, it is 11%. In South Korea, the number is even higher at 35%.

Erika Sekiguchi, a 36-year-old trading company worker, spends 14 hours a day at work and does not use many of her paid holidays. In 2014, she used only eight out of 20 days, and six of those were for sick leave. “Nobody else uses their vacation days,” she said.

She faces the same problem as many other workers in Japan: either never take time off to rest, or risk being criticized for leaving work while others are still working hard.

Yuu Wakebe, a health ministry official who works on working hours policy, says he does 100 hours of overtime each month. He says there is strong pressure to work as much as your coworkers. “It is a worker’s right to take paid vacations,” he said. “But working in Japan often means having a lot of volunteer spirit.”

This fear of being left out at work is causing more stress, illness, early death, and suicide. Official data says about 200 people die each year from heart attacks, strokes, and other problems caused by overwork.

Prime Minister Shinzo Abe is not known for taking long holidays himself. But even he has spoken against the unfair demands companies put on workers as they try to survive in a difficult global market. Abe recently said that Japan’s work culture “falsely makes long hours look good.”

David Mitchell, who often competes for the Man Booker literary prize, is used to critics closely examining his books. So, the British author feels relieved that his newest work—finished at 1am on a Tuesday before he left for Norway—will not be read by anyone until the year 2114.

Mitchell is the second writer to join the Future Library project, created by Scottish artist Katie Paterson. In 2014, 1,000 trees were planted in Oslo’s Nordmarka forest for this project. Starting with Margaret Atwood, who gave her manuscript called Scribbler Moon in 2015, one author each year for 100 years will give a new piece of writing. These works will only be read in 2114, when the trees are cut down to make paper for printing all 100 texts.

Each year, the name of the chosen author is announced. The authors are picked by a group of experts and Paterson, as long as she is alive. Each author travels to the forest near Oslo to hand over their manuscript in a small ceremony.

Mitchell said, “It’s a small sign of hope during a time of sad news. It shows that maybe civilization will still exist in 100 years. Everything seems bad now, but the Future Library gives us hope for the future. It suggests we are stronger than we think: that people, trees, books, readers, and civilization will still be here.”

Mitchell said writing the book was “freeing because I won’t be here to see if people think it’s good or bad... But I am between Margaret Atwood and probably another great writer, so it should be good. I would look very foolish if people in 2114 read it and it wasn’t good.”

Usually, Mitchell, who was shortlisted for the Man Booker for his books number9dream and Cloud Atlas, edits his writing many times. “I usually over-edit. But this time was different—I wrote until the last minute. The first two-thirds are well-edited, but I didn’t have time to edit the last part. That felt freeing.”

Paterson, who has made art about dead stars and the history of darkness, asked the writers to think about “imagination and time” in their work. Mitchell only shared the title of his manuscript, From Me Flows What You Call Time, during a ceremony in the Norwegian woods near the 1,000 trees. The title comes from a piece of music by Japanese composer Toru Takemitsu. Mitchell said only that the work is “more substantial than I expected,” but gave no other details.

When he handed over his text in the forest, Mitchell stood under an umbrella, surrounded by the young pine trees. He read a short story and a poem by William Wordsworth, A slumber did my spirit seal, to the audience of children and adults. The poem’s ending, “Rolled round in earth’s diurnal course / With rocks, and stones, and trees,” felt right for this forest, which will be cared for over the next 98 years before it is used for the Future Library books.

Mitchell wrote for the Future Library, “It seems silly to think my writing will still matter to people in the future. But it also feels quiet and humble to work hard on a book that no one will ever praise or say, ‘I loved that part.’”

Now that his manuscript is delivered, it will be sealed and kept with Atwood’s in a wood-lined room in Oslo’s new public library, which will open in 2019. A group of experts will watch over it until it is finally printed. Mitchell says the book is now “as gone from me as a coin dropped in a river.”

An octopus escaped from the National Aquarium in New Zealand by getting out of its tank, moving down a 50-metre drainpipe, and disappearing into the sea.

The octopus, named Inky, is a common New Zealand octopus. He escaped after someone accidentally left the lid of his tank slightly open. Staff think that during the night, when no one was there, Inky climbed to the top of his glass tank, went down the side, and crossed the floor of the aquarium.

Rob Yarrell, the national manager of the aquarium, said, “Octopuses are famous for escaping. I don’t think Inky was unhappy or lonely, because octopuses like to be alone. But he is very curious. He always wants to know what is happening outside. That is just how he is.”

One idea is that Inky moved across the aquarium floor, which is about three or four metres, and then, feeling freedom was close, went into a drainpipe that leads straight to the sea. The drainpipe is 50 metres long and opens into the waters of Hawke’s Bay, on the east coast of New Zealand’s North Island.

Another possible way Inky escaped is by squeezing into an open pipe at the top of his tank, which goes under the floor to the drain. “When we came in the next morning and saw his tank was empty, I was really surprised,” said Yarrell, who has not started a search for Inky. “The staff and I are pretty sad. But this is Inky, and he always surprised us.”

Reiss Jenkinson, who takes care of the exhibits at the aquarium, said he is sure that no one took Inky. “I know how octopuses behave very well,” he said. “I have seen octopuses on boats slip through small pumps. Also, the security here is too good for anyone to steal Inky, and why would they?”

Octopuses have no bones, so they can fit into very small spaces and have been seen squeezing through holes as small as coins. They are also very smart and can use tools. At the Island Bay Marine Education Centre in Wellington, one octopus was found visiting another tank at night to steal crabs and then returning to its own tank. Another octopus there, named Ozymandias, was thought to have broken a world record for opening a jar before being released into the ocean.

A local fisherman brought Inky to the National Aquarium a few years ago after finding him caught in a crayfish pot. Inky had scars and short arms, said Yarrell. “He had been living on the reef and fighting with fish, so he was not in good shape.” Inky, who is about the size of a rugby ball, was a very smart octopus. “He was very friendly, very curious, and popular with visitors. We have another octopus, Blotchy, but he is smaller and does not have Inky’s personality.”

The aquarium does not plan to increase security because Inky’s escape was a special case, but the staff now know more about what octopuses can do. The aquarium is not looking for a new octopus, but if a fisherman brings one, they might accept it. “You never know,” said Yarrell. “Maybe Inky will come back to us one day.”

Why do they do it? When you ask the men who want to be top referees in the future, they smile because they understand the question well. This season, people have criticized referees more than before, and even some former referees have complained about the quality. This is surprising because referees usually support each other no matter what happens.

So why do they do it? Why spend many hours traveling around the country to enforce rules, knowing that some people will be unhappy, and try to move up until you can make decisions on TV in front of millions of people who watch your every move with many camera angles and slow-motion replays?

We see part of the answer on Lee Swabey’s face after he finishes a match where Grimsby beat Woking 2–1, a game in the fifth level of English football. He gets what every referee wants: “Twenty-two handshakes,” he says proudly. Getting a handshake from every player, plus a “well done” from both managers, means he did a great job. He loves the excitement of a game that goes well. “I wouldn’t spend so much time away from my family if this wasn’t so important to me,” he says.

Swabey is seen as a referee with a lot of potential by the Professional Game Match Officials Limited (PGMOL). He knew he was being watched at that match. PGMOL’s boss, Mike Riley, was there, along with Steve Dunn, the coach for this level, who took notes and timed everything the referees did.

A few weeks before, Riley, Dunn, and another former referee, Peter Jones, went to another level-5 match to watch another referee, John Brooks, who is also expected to move up. “I hope to get promoted to the Premier League and referee some of the top games in this country,” Brooks says.

But at that match, Brooks had to deal with a difficult situation: he had to cancel the game because the pitch was frozen. This is part of the experience Brooks needs before he can referee bigger games. There are many problems to solve—clubs often do not want to cancel games late, especially when they have to pay staff but will not get any ticket money.

Brooks called his coach for advice and made the hard but correct choice. Later, the club secretary came with envelopes to pay the referees—at level 5, the match fee is £95, so it is clear these men do not do it for the money.

Brooks, like Swabey, wants to move up. He knows he needs to be strong and learn how to deal with disappointment. How does he feel when he sees a referee criticized on TV? “Erm… not great,” he says. “I’ve been in that situation once when I made a wrong decision, and it was a goal that was just offside. Your heart sinks. You can’t stop thinking about it.

“I sometimes wish people understood how much time and effort we put in. It is easy to criticize, but we do everything we can to make the right decisions. Sometimes, people will not like you, but if you can’t handle that, you are probably in the wrong job.”

The former referees agree that today’s referees have much better support, education, and tools than they did. When Riley was a young referee, he had to buy his own books on psychology and nutrition because there was no information for him.

Now, Brooks has a coach he can call anytime. They talk every week, discuss his games, watch videos of important decisions, and work on how to improve. He also gets help from a sports psychologist, Liam Slack, who gives him advice and helps him with his exercise routine so he can run the 11km needed during a game.

Brooks says psychology is very important for him. “One thing we talk about is forgetting decisions and moving on,” he says. “You might have to make a big decision in the first 30 seconds of a game. After that, you need to stay focused for the next 89 minutes and not worry about whether you were right. Liam has taught us ways to let go of those decisions. Working with the sports psychologist is really important for mental strength.”

Jones thinks this new way of working is very helpful. “I refereed in professional football, but looking back, I was an amateur,” he says. “I had a regular job at British Telecom, and I might referee in Newcastle on Wednesday night, then be in Leicester at 9am the next morning talking to customers. Sometimes I hadn’t slept. Training was not organized. We were amateurs in a professional world compared to now.”

When they talk about technology, all three former referees agree it is a good thing. “We all support anything that makes the referee’s job better and helps them do better on the field,” says Riley. The goal is to make fewer mistakes. After all, a bad decision can stay with you for a long time. “The rest of your life,” Jones says, laughing.

There are people watching you in stores, even if you don’t see them. When you pick up a boot, a camera checks to make sure you don’t steal it. When you enter a department store, you are being watched. But now, new technology is giving stores different ways to watch you. They are less interested in stopping shoplifting and more interested in things like your age, gender, body size, and what you are wearing.

A few months ago, a company called Computer Sciences Corporation (CSC) made a report. It said that about 30% of stores use facial recognition technology to watch customers. Facial recognition is a technology that can identify people by looking at their faces and comparing them to a database. It uses special cameras, like Intel RealSense, which can study your face, your expressions, and even the brands of clothes you wear.

Joe Jensen from Intel says that the goal of using RealSense in stores is not to make a list of every customer. Instead, it is to learn about general shopping habits and lifestyles. He says, “It’s not important to know exactly who the customer is. It’s more important to know what kind of person is shopping and what people like them usually do.”

If you use recognition technology together with information about past customers, you can start to guess what a person might do in a store. For example, if a woman who wears size 10 and a gold necklace walks quickly to the sock section, the store can guess she wants to buy socks. The store can then show her ads for socks on screens. If she looks like someone who wants socks, she will see sock ads.

This idea is not new. Online stores have used these methods for years. If you search for something on Amazon, you will see ads for similar products on other websites. If you show interest in canoes, you will see canoe ads everywhere online. But using these systems in real stores is not as easy as copying what happens online. People do not react to cameras in the same way they react to online tracking.

Hoxton Analytics, a company in London, has made a technology that uses machine learning and artificial intelligence to study people’s shoes. By looking at the style and size of shoes as people walk by, the system can guess if a customer is male or female with 75-80% accuracy.

Owen McCormack, the CEO of Hoxton Analytics, says the idea came as a response to facial recognition. He said, “Why don’t we just look at the clothes people wear to understand who they are?” He also said that pointing a camera at someone’s chest or hips feels just as uncomfortable as facial recognition. So, they decided to look at people’s shoes instead.

The word “creepy” is often used when talking about tracking people in stores. Stores and data scientists want to get information without making people feel uncomfortable. Hoxton Analytics and the stores using their technology try to avoid looking at faces and instead look at shoes. This shows that people feel differently about being watched in real life compared to online. If cameras look at our bodies, we feel invaded. But is judging people by their shoes really less invasive?

McCormack says that their system is less invasive because it does not collect personal information. He says, “Shops already do many invasive things, but we don’t know about them. If you know if someone is male or female, you can show better ads. For example, if everyone in the shop is male, you can show ads for PlayStations instead of hairdryers.”

If stores keep their monitoring hidden, they can improve their sales without customers knowing. But if they use screens and targeted ads, it becomes clear that machines are watching you. Stores say they do this to give you a better shopping experience, but it still feels uncomfortable.

Stores want the same information that online shops collect. We allow this online, so why not in real stores? But the rules are different. In a shopping center, you can walk from one shop to another without being asked to accept cookies, so the rules about permission are not the same.

For young people who grew up with the internet, these methods may not feel as invasive. In the CSC report, a survey showed that 72% of people aged 55 and older felt very uncomfortable with these technologies in stores, but only 51% of people aged 16-24 felt the same.

Are young people more comfortable because they know more about technology, or do they just trust big companies more? Is feeling “creeped out” by technology always the same, or does it change as society changes? Whatever the answer, there are more and more eyes watching you in stores, and they care a lot about what you are wearing.

Insects are crunchy, full of protein, and you can find them under rocks. People in most places have not eaten insects as food, except in a few countries. But now, insects are becoming more popular as food. In spring 2013, there will be efforts to make people less disgusted by eating insects and to put them not only in fancy restaurants but also in supermarkets.

In April, London will have a festival called Pestival 2013, supported by the Wellcome Trust, to help people appreciate insects. Eating insects will be an important part of the event. The Nordic Food Lab, a team from Scandinavia behind the famous Danish restaurant Noma, will run a two-day “pop-up” restaurant at the festival. In 2012, Noma served ants at Claridge’s hotel in London for ten days, and all the seats were sold.

Noma has been named the world’s best restaurant by Restaurant magazine for three years in a row. The chef, René Redzepi, says ants taste like lemon, and a purée made from fermented grasshoppers and moth larvae tastes like strong fish sauce. Bee larvae can be used to make a sweet mayonnaise instead of eggs. Scientists are always finding new ways to use insects in food.

In March, a BBC documentary will show food writer Stefan Gates eating deep-fried locusts and barbecued tarantulas. But behind the jokes about eating bugs, there is a serious message. Many experts think that eating insects is good for the environment.

The United Nations’ Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) has been supporting projects since 2011 to encourage eating and farming insects in southeast Asia and Africa. In these places, about two billion people already eat insects and caterpillar larvae as a normal part of their diet. In 2012, the FAO published a list of 1,909 types of edible insects. With help from the Dutch government, the FAO plans to hold a big international conference about insects as food in 2013.

There are many insects in the world. For every person, there are 40 tonnes of insects, so they are not likely to become endangered. Insects are also less likely to have chemicals on them. Redzepi says, “I know it’s not normal to eat bugs in the western world, but why not?” In southeast Asia, eating insects is common. People around the world eat bugs. If you like mushrooms, you have probably eaten many worms without knowing it. Also, we eat honey, which is actually bee vomit. Think about that next time you put honey in your tea.

Redzepi says the main idea behind Nordic Food Lab is: “Nothing is not edible.” Insects are very important for life on Earth. There are more than a million species of insects, making them the most diverse group of animals. But people often do not understand them, dislike them, and kill them just because they are there.

In the next 30 years, the world’s population will grow to nine billion. Already, one billion people do not have enough food. This growth will put more pressure on farmland, water, forests, fish, and other resources, as well as on nutrients and energy.

Meat is becoming more expensive, not only in money but also because rainforests are destroyed to make space for cattle or to grow their food. Cows also produce methane gas, which is bad for the environment. Livestock farming creates a lot of greenhouse gases: 35% of the world’s methane, 65% of its nitrous oxide, and 9% of its carbon dioxide.

Edible insects produce fewer gases, have high-quality protein, vitamins, and amino acids, and need less food to make the same amount of protein as sheep, pigs, or chickens. They produce less greenhouse gas and ammonia than cows and can be raised on organic waste. China already has large maggot farms. Zimbabwe has a successful caterpillar industry, and Laos received almost $500,000 from the FAO to develop an insect-harvesting project. In the UK, the insect business is growing, even if not always legal. Recently, a man was stopped at Gatwick airport with 94 kilos of caterpillars from Burkina Faso, worth almost £40,000.

A study by FoodServiceWarehouse.com said that replacing pork and beef with crickets and locusts could reduce greenhouse gas emissions by up to 95%. But maybe the most fair thing about eating insects is that, when we die, insects will get a chance to eat us too.

Coal may soon become as important as oil as the world’s main source of energy in the next five years. This could be very bad for the climate, according to the International Energy Agency (IEA), a top group for energy economics.

One big reason for the rise in coal use is the large increase in shale gas use in the United States. The IEA’s new research shows that coal use is going up in almost every country, even in places that want to cut carbon emissions. The only exception is the US, where shale gas has replaced coal. Because the US uses less coal, coal prices have dropped around the world. This makes coal more attractive, even in Europe, where the Emissions Trading Scheme was supposed to reduce coal use.

Maria van der Hoeven, the IEA’s Executive Director, said, “Coal’s share of the world’s energy keeps growing every year. If nothing changes, coal will catch up with oil in less than ten years.”

Coal is easy to find in most parts of the world, unlike oil and gas, and it is cheap to mine. Because of this, coal provided almost half of the increase in world energy demand in the last ten years. The IEA says that China and India will use more coal in the next five years. India will probably become the second biggest coal user, passing the US. China is the biggest coal importer, and Indonesia is now the biggest exporter, ahead of Australia for now.

The IEA’s Medium-Term Coal Market Report says that by 2017, the world will burn 1.2 billion more tonnes of coal each year than today. This is as much as Russia and the US use together now. By 2017, world coal use is expected to reach 4.3 billion tonnes of oil equivalent, while oil use will be 4.4 billion tonnes.

Coal produces more carbon emissions than any other major fossil fuel. This makes it a big cause of climate change, especially when burned in old, inefficient power stations. If these stations do not have special equipment to clean the smoke, burning coal also releases sulphur, which causes acid rain, and other pollutants like mercury and soot.

Van der Hoeven said that, unless there is a high price on carbon to make coal less attractive and to support cleaner energy like renewables, only cheaper gas can really reduce coal use. This has happened in the US because of the big increase in shale gas production in the last five years.

She said, “The US shows that a better gas market, with flexible prices and local, sustainable production, can lower coal use, carbon emissions, and electricity bills. Europe, China, and others should pay attention.”

This would mean producing much more shale gas, because the easy-to-get conventional gas is running out.

In Europe, the Emissions Trading Scheme was supposed to reduce high-carbon energy by making companies pay for carbon emissions. Companies got a set number of permits and had to buy more if they wanted to emit more carbon. But too many permits were given out, and the financial crisis made things worse. Now there are too many permits, so prices have dropped. At today’s low prices—just a few euros per tonne—there is little reason to use cleaner fuels, and coal use is rising again in Europe.

This means that one of the world’s main systems to cut greenhouse gas emissions is not working well. Because of this, the world is at greater risk of climate change from the growing use of coal, the fossil fuel that produces the most carbon.

Many people know they do not get enough sleep, but imagine if we could solve this problem by simply getting up later. At the British Science Festival, Dr. Paul Kelley from Oxford University said that schools should start at different times to match students’ natural body clocks. This would help students think better, get better exam results, and be healthier. Not getting enough sleep is linked to diabetes, depression, obesity, and a weak immune system.

In a 2014 paper, Dr. Kelley explained that children around ten years old naturally wake up at about 6:30am. At age 16, their natural wake-up time is about 8am, and at 18, it is around 9am. So, the usual school start time is good for 10-year-olds, but not for 16- to 18-year-olds. For older teenagers, it would make more sense to start school at 11am or even later. Dr. Kelley and his team wrote that waking up at 7am for older teenagers is like a teacher in their 50s waking up at 4:30am.

Dr. Kelley says it is not easy to just tell teenagers to go to bed earlier. The body’s natural rhythm is controlled by a special kind of light. The eye has special cells that send signals to a part of the brain called the suprachiasmatic nuclei in the hypothalamus. This part of the brain controls our body clock over 24 hours. Light controls this rhythm, so it is not something we can easily change, like our heartbeat.

It is not only students who would benefit from starting later. Dr. Kelley says workdays should also match our natural body clocks. He explains that people between 14 and 24 years old lose more than two hours of sleep each night. People between 24 and about 35 lose about an hour and a half. This continues until about age 55, when sleep and wake times are balanced again. Ten-year-olds and 55-year-olds naturally wake up and sleep at the same times.

This may be why the usual nine-to-five workday is so common. Many bosses are in their mid-50s or older, and this schedule works best for them. Dr. Kelley suggests that workplaces could also have different starting times. For example, people in their 50s could start at 8am, people in their 30s at 10am, and young interns or apprentices at 11am. He says that matching work hours to people’s natural rhythms could have many good effects. People would do better at work, feel happier, and be healthier. It could also mean fewer accidents because drivers would be more awake. Rush hour traffic could be less crowded if people start work and school at different times. Dr. Kelley says starting later would help everyone, especially families. Parents would not have to wake up teenagers too early, which often causes stress.

So, what time does Dr. Kelley start work? He is 67 years old, so his natural wake-up time is just after six o’clock, like a ten-year-old. He wakes up naturally and says starting his workday is much easier now than when he was younger.

Felix Baumgartner stood at the edge of space above the deserts of New Mexico. He paused for a moment. It was just a small step from his capsule, but he was about to fall 24 miles down to Earth. Mission control told him, “Our guardian angel will take care of you,” and then Felix, known as Fearless Felix, jumped.

Ten minutes later, Felix landed safely on Earth. During his fall, he reached speeds up to 725 mph and broke three world records. He became the first person to skydive faster than the speed of sound, reaching Mach 1.24. The control room cheered, “We love you Felix,” and his mother, Ava Baumgartner, cried with happiness. Felix also set records for the highest manned balloon flight and the highest skydive. He raised his arms to thank his team.

Felix wore a special suit that protected him from the changing air pressure during his fall. Without this suit, his blood could have boiled and his lungs could have exploded. At a press conference, Felix said, “When I was standing there on top of the world, you become so humble, you don’t think about breaking records.” He said he only thought about staying alive, but added, “Sometimes you have to go up really high to see how small you are.”

The mission had been delayed twice the week before, but finally got permission to go ahead on Sunday morning because the weather was good. Felix went up into the clear sky in a huge balloon. The balloon was 30 million cubic feet in size, and its skin was only one-tenth as thick as a sandwich bag. Felix sat in a capsule at the bottom of the balloon, wearing his suit.

When he reached the right height, Felix checked 40 items with his mentor, Joe Kittinger, who held the previous record for the highest manned balloon flight. There was a problem with the heater for Felix’s visor, which made it foggy. Felix told Joe, “This is very serious. Sometimes it’s getting foggy when I exhale. I do not feel heat.” But they decided to continue. A record 8 million people watched the jump live on YouTube.

The trip up took two and a half hours. Felix could see the curve of the Earth, and the sky turned black. His fall back to Earth was much faster. Three cameras on his suit recorded his free-fall, which lasted just over four minutes. He did not break the record for the longest free-fall, but his parachute opened safely.

The success of the mission and the suit means that astronauts might survive accidents at high altitudes, like the space shuttle Columbia disaster in 2003, by jumping out. Felix’s main doctor was Dr. Jonathan Clark, whose wife died in the Columbia accident. Dr. Clark now works to help astronauts survive high-altitude disasters.

Felix is known for his daring jumps. He is a former paratrooper and has parachuted off buildings, mountains, and even into a 600-foot-deep cave. He did two practice jumps before this one: one from 71,000 feet in March and another from 97,000 feet in July 2012. But nothing compared to his jump above Roswell, a town famous for UFO stories.

Felix tried to break five records: first person to break the sound barrier in free-fall, highest free-fall jump, highest manned balloon flight, longest free-fall, and using the largest manned balloon in history. The jump took seven years to plan and was sponsored by Red Bull. Felix broke two of Joe Kittinger’s records. Kittinger had jumped from a balloon 19 miles above Earth in 1960. During Felix’s jump, Kittinger, now 84, was the only person talking to him on the radio.

After the jump, Felix said he wanted to inspire others. He hoped that in four years, a young person would ask him for advice to break his record, just as he had asked Kittinger. Felix said the most exciting moment was standing outside the capsule “on top of the world.” He joked that the best moment was when he landed and saw Mike Todd, the engineer who helped him with his suit, smiling like a child.

Felix said he felt like Mike Todd’s son and that Todd was very happy he was alive. Earlier, Todd told reporters, “The world needs a hero right now, and they got one in Felix Baumgartner.” Joe Kittinger also joked at the press conference, giving a “special one-fingered salute” to people who said Felix would not survive going supersonic.

Felix said this would be his last jump. He promised to settle down and spend time with his girlfriend, Nicole Oetl, and to fly helicopters on rescue missions in the US and Austria.

Barack Obama returned to Washington and his office on Wednesday, just hours after giving a victory speech in Chicago. In his speech, he asked Americans to come together and support him. Obama said, “You voted for action, not politics as usual.” However, it did not seem likely that everyone would listen to his call. The President would have to work with a Republican-led House of Representatives, which was not friendly to him, for at least two more years. He also faced a big argument about government spending and debt, known as the “fiscal cliff.”

Unlike after his 2008 election, Obama was not expected to get a “honeymoon period” where people give him time before criticizing. Both Republican House Speaker John Boehner and Democratic Senate Leader Harry Reid said they needed to work together to solve the crisis, but it could become one of the biggest fights between the White House and Congress during Obama’s time as President.

Obama easily defeated his Republican opponent, Mitt Romney, winning many important states. However, the election showed again that America is still very divided. Although Obama’s second term officially starts in January, he began working on it right away. Many supporters were disappointed with his first term, so now he wants to create a legacy that will make him remembered as a great president.

Obama hopes to continue improving the economy and also wants to work on immigration reform, better education, fighting climate change, and foreign policy issues like Iran and the conflict between Israel and Palestine. He won more than the 270 electoral college votes needed and also got a higher share of the popular vote.

Boehner sounded willing to work together in his statement. He said both parties need to find common ground and work together to help the economy grow and create jobs, which is important for solving the debt problem. Obama reportedly called Boehner to start talks. Reid, who often disagrees with Boehner, also said he wanted to work together, asking his Republican colleagues to join him in solving the country’s problems.

During the campaign, Obama said he was hopeful about making a big agreement with the Republicans, something he could not do in 2011. The problem is that Republicans want to protect military spending, while Democrats want to cut it. Obama wants to raise taxes on households earning more than $250,000, but Boehner does not agree with any tax increases.

Stock markets dropped because investors expected more political fighting. By lunchtime, all major US markets were down over 300 points.

The new House of Representatives, which will start in January, will be similar to the current one, with a large Republican majority. The Senate also stayed almost the same, with Democrats keeping a small majority, gaining three seats and losing one.

In the presidential race, Romney only won one important state, North Carolina. Obama won New Hampshire, Virginia, Ohio, Wisconsin, Nevada, Iowa, and Colorado. In his victory speech, Obama talked about the long lines to vote and said the voting system needs to be improved.

Obama used the inspiring language that made him famous in 2008, but which he did not use much in 2012 because of disappointment with his presidency and the difficult economy. His campaign team thought it was not the right time. But after winning, he used his old slogan about “hope” again.

Obama walked up to the stage while Stevie Wonder’s “Signed, Sealed, Delivered, I’m Yours” played. He told his happy supporters, “Tonight in this election, you, the American people, reminded us that while our road has been hard, while our journey has been long, we have picked ourselves up, we have fought our way back. And we know in our hearts that for the United States of America the best is yet to come.” In his speech, which lasted more than 25 minutes, Obama thanked his wife Michelle, his daughters Malia and Sasha, and his Vice-President Joe Biden. He repeated the message that first made him famous.

“We are not as divided as our politics suggests,” he said. “We’re not as cynical as the experts believe. We are greater than just our own ambitions, and we are more than just red states and blue states. We are, and always will be, the United States of America.”

Obama made it clear he had plans for his second term, including changing the tax system, immigration reform, and making America safe from climate change.

Shortly before, Romney called Obama to admit defeat. In a polite speech in Boston, Romney told his supporters, “The nation is at a critical point. At a time like this, we can’t risk fighting between parties. Our leaders have to work together for the people.” He added, “This is a time of great challenges for America and I pray the President will be successful in guiding our nation.”

The campaign was mostly about Obama. Even though many people were unhappy with the slow economic recovery and high unemployment, Americans chose to keep him as President. If Obama, the first black President, had lost, it would have been a disappointment for African Americans and many white liberals.

Sweden is the best country for older people, while Afghanistan is the worst, according to the first global index on ageing. However, being a rich country does not always mean better conditions for people over 60. Sweden is ranked first, followed by Norway, Germany, the Netherlands, and Canada. These results are not surprising, but the Global AgeWatch index also shows some unexpected findings.

The United States, which is the richest country in the world, is only in eighth place. The United Kingdom is not in the top ten and is ranked 13th. Sri Lanka is ranked 36th, much higher than Pakistan at 89th, even though both countries have similar levels of GDP. Bolivia and Mauritius also have higher scores than their economies suggest. The large economies of Brazil, Russia, India, and China have mixed results: Brazil and China are ranked higher, while India and Russia are much lower.

Mark Gorman, director of the HelpAge International group, said, “This survey shows that history is important. The top countries are as expected, but Scandinavian countries were not rich when they started giving pensions to everyone. Older people in Sri Lanka now benefit from good basic education and health care because of past policy choices. Every country has limited resources, but when making decisions, they should also think about older people.”

The index was made with the UN Fund for Population and Development and covers 91 countries, including 89% of the world’s older people. The survey comes at a time when the world’s population is changing. By 2050, there will be about two billion people aged 60 and over, making up more than 20% of the world’s population.

Population ageing, which means a larger share of older people, is happening fastest in developing countries. More than two-thirds of older people live in poor countries, and by 2050, this will rise to about four-fifths. In France, it took 115 years for the older population to double from 7% to 14% between 1865 and 1980. In Brazil, the same change will happen in just 21 years, from 2011 to 2032.

The index shows that the fastest ageing countries—Jordan, Laos, Mongolia, Nicaragua, and Vietnam—are in the lower half of the ranking. In these countries, the number of older people is expected to more than triple by 2050. This suggests that governments need to act quickly to support their ageing populations.

There are also differences between men and women among older people. Women usually live longer than men. In 2012, for every 84 men aged 60 and over, there were 100 women. Many older women face problems because they have less paid work, less power in the family, and are more at risk of violence.

The report says that if the right steps are taken, an ageing population does not always mean much higher health care costs. It is important to invest in education and health care for older people. Bolivia, ranked 46th, is one of the poorest countries but has good policies for older people, such as a national plan on ageing, free health care, and a pension for everyone. Nepal, ranked 77th, started a basic pension in 1995 for people over 70 who have no other pension. Although this pension is small and not everyone gets it, it shows how a poor country can start to help older people.

Good basic health care started many years ago in Chile and Costa Rica has helped older people there. A good education system is also important. Basic reading and writing skills help older people deal with pension systems. In the Philippines, older people have benefited from education reforms after 1946, which made elementary and high school education required. Armenia, like other former Soviet countries, also benefited from a strong education system. South Korea is ranked a low 67th on the ageing index, doing worse than similar countries for its level of wealth, partly because it only recently started a pension system.

The ageing index uses 13 indicators in four areas: income security, health care, employment and education, and a supportive environment. All indicators are equally important, except for pension coverage, life expectancy at 60, healthy life expectancy at 60, and psychological well-being, which are given more weight because there is better data for them. Countries were only included if there was enough data.

Professor Sir Richard Jolly, who created the human development index, said: “This new index helps us better understand the needs and opportunities of older people. It encourages countries everywhere to aim higher for what is possible.”

Clay Cockrell is in his office at Columbus Circle, across from 1 Central Park West, where the Trump International Hotel and Tower is located. In front of the tower is Central Park, where Cockrell does his popular walk and talk therapy sessions.

Cockrell used to work on Wall Street but is now a therapist. He spends much of his time walking through Central Park or Battery Park in downtown Manhattan, near Wall Street, listening to and advising some of New York’s richest people.

He says he became a wealth therapist naturally. “Many very rich people—the top 1% of the 1%—feel their problems are not real problems. But they are. Many therapists do not take their issues seriously enough,” he said.

What problems do America’s richest people have? “They feel guilty about being rich,” Cockrell said. “They feel they have to hide their wealth. Also, being in the 1% can be lonely.” F. Scott Fitzgerald was right: the very rich “are different from you and me.”

Counsellors say things have gotten worse since the financial crisis and the debates about income inequality, which were made bigger by movements like Occupy Wall Street and the Fight for $15 campaign.

Jamie Traeger-Muney, a wealth psychologist and founder of the Wealth Legacy Group, said, “The Occupy Wall Street movement was good and talked about important issues like income inequality, but it made the 1% look bad.” She also said the media makes rich people “feel like they need to hide or feel ashamed.”

“Sometimes, I am shocked by what people say. You would never talk about another group the way people talk about the rich,” she said.

Barbara Nusbaum, an expert in money psychology, said, “It’s really lonely to have a lot of money. People’s reactions can be scary. We are all taught not to talk about money. It’s not polite. Strangely, it’s harder to talk about having money than not having money. It’s more acceptable to say, ‘I am broke. Things are hard.’ You can’t say, ‘I have a lot of money.’ You have to keep much of your life private.”

Because of this, Cockrell says, rich people often spend time with other rich people—not because they are snobs, but because only other rich people understand their problems.

The gap between rich and poor is growing around the world. Oxfam says the richest 1% owned 44% of global wealth in 2009, 48% in 2014, and were expected to own more than the other 99% by 2016.

In the US, in the last 30 years, the top 0.1% of households increased their share of wealth from 7% to 22%, while the bottom 90% lost wealth.

There are also more very rich people now. According to Spectrem Group, in 2014, there were 10.1 million US households with $1 million or more in assets (not counting their main home), up from 9.2 million in 2007. Households with $5 million or more reached 1.3 million, and 142,000 households are now worth $25 million or more.

Since the 2008 financial crisis, the income gap has grown, and things “have gotten worse for the wealthy,” Cockrell said. The main reason is not knowing if friends like you for who you are or for your money.

“If someone else is also a billionaire, they don’t want anything from you. But with people who have less money, you can never be sure if they are true friends. That is hard,” Cockrell said. “As the gap has grown, the rich have become more and more isolated.”

These are real fears for the richest people. In 2007, the Gates Foundation and Boston College’s Center on Wealth and Philanthropy studied what it feels like to be in America’s 1%. For four years, they surveyed 165 of America’s richest households—120 of them had at least $25 million in assets. The average net worth was $78 million. The study, called The Joys and Dilemmas of Wealth, was 500 pages long and showed that money cannot buy happiness.

“Wealth can make it hard to connect with other people,” said the spouse of a tech entrepreneur who made about $80 million. Some Americans now keep their wealth secret. “We call it stealth wealth. Many people hide their wealth because they are afraid of being judged,” said Traeger-Muney. If rich Americans talk about their special problems, people often do not take them seriously.

“People say, ‘Oh, poor you.’ There is not much sympathy,” she said. “Wealth is still one of our last taboos.”

Cockrell, who speaks in a soft, calming voice, said that many of his rich clients make the mistake of letting money define who they are.

“I don’t think it’s healthy to ignore your problems. If you are in the 1%, you still have problems, and they are real for you. Even if you don’t have to worry about money, there are other parts of your life. Money is not the only thing that defines you,” he said. “Your problems are real.”

Takahito Iguchi says the problem with Google Glasses is that they are not cool. He might be right. There is already a website that shows people wearing Google Glasses looking silly or proud, or both. Google may have made a mistake by giving the first 10,000 pairs to software developers instead of famous models or celebrities like Scarlett Johansson. If you search Google Images, one of the first pictures you see is a big, naked man wearing Google Glasses in the shower. Iguchi, a Japanese businessman, thinks this could be Google’s weakness. He is making a new product that looks better, more like something from the movie Blade Runner, and more Japanese.

Iguchi’s product is called Telepathy One. It is not really glasses, but a single piece of metal with a camera and a small projector. He showed Telepathy One at the South by Southwest festival in Austin, Texas, and has already received $5 million from investors. Like Google Glass, Telepathy One is planned to come out in 2014.

Telepathy One is a simpler version of Google Glass. Iguchi says Google Glass is “an egotistical device” with many uses – you can browse the internet, read emails, take photos, and use different apps. Telepathy One will be “more of a communication device.” It connects to your phone with Bluetooth and focuses on sharing pictures and sound in real time. You can post photos and videos from your point of view on Facebook or send them by email. You can also see and talk to a video image of a friend.

“It will help you feel closer to your friends and family. We are very focused on communication and sharing,” says Iguchi, who has worked in Japanese technology for 20 years. He recently made a location-based phone app called Sekai Camera.

Not everyone wants to get closer to someone wearing a futuristic headset, I say. Iguchi shakes his head. “I’m a visionary. I dream that people will understand each other. When I go to London, I am a stranger. Sometimes I feel afraid. But I believe everyone wants to be understood and to understand others. With this device, you can know more about people before you even talk to them.”

Compared to Google, Telepathy is very small. But this does not scare Iguchi. In his shared office in San Francisco – a cool, old warehouse full of young people – he quotes Sun Tzu’s The Art of War and says that even small armies can sometimes beat big ones. When he was young, Japanese technology was the best in the world: the Sony Walkman was like the iPhone of its time. Now, to compete, he has left Tokyo for Silicon Valley.

“Tokyo has a lot of fashion and culture, but it is still an island. It is isolated. There is no way to grow. In Silicon Valley, everyone is from everywhere. It is the place to connect with the world.” The hardware will be made in Japan, but he is building a team of software engineers in the US to make the apps. On the day I meet him, a Japanese news crew is following him because they are interested in Japanese business people who are leaving Japan.

“We are losing our confidence,” says the reporter, Takashi Yanagisawa. “We need to find a way to get our power back. Iguchi is like a new hope. We hope he can be a new solution.” Iguchi says building the first Telepathy One was easy. “We have all kinds of technology in Tokyo. The hard part is showing it to the world.” Big manufacturers want to work with him because they have the technology but have trouble selling it. “A product needs a story. Like Apple did with the iPod – 1,000 songs in your pocket. And the way Apple competed with Microsoft and IBM was like the story of David and Goliath. Steve Jobs was inspired by Akio Morita, the co-founder of Sony, and he inspired me, so maybe things will come full circle.”

Maybe. Iguchi is very confident, like Steve Jobs, but sometimes people do not understand him because of his strong Japanese accent. This may be one reason he created Telepathy One. When he went to London to show the headset at the Founders Forum, he stayed in an Airbnb. “The owner was not my friend, but I talked with him for three hours, and now he is my friend. That is how long it takes to understand each other, to share our feelings, backgrounds, and jobs. Maybe Telepathy can make that faster. If you get information from the cloud and social networks, it will be easier. This man works on getting investment from the UK to Africa, and he was very excited about Telepathy. He thought it could help teach people about Africa and show them other people’s points of view.”

This is Iguchi’s biggest hope – that seeing someone else’s real point of view will help you understand their ideas and feelings. As a student, he studied philosophy during the day and taught himself computer programming at night. “One day, I opened my apartment door and suddenly realized that everything is code. That was my big idea. Everything is coded and can be shared between people. Everything can be encoded and decoded. If code can be exchanged between people, that will end all wars.”

A lot of digital material—like blogs, tweets, pictures, videos, and official documents such as court rulings and emails—could be lost forever because the programs needed to open them might stop working, warned Google’s vice-president, Vint Cerf. He told the American Association for the Advancement of Science in San Jose, California, that the first digital records of humanity could disappear for future historians. Cerf called this problem “bit rot,” where old computer files become useless because the software to read them no longer exists. He warned that we could have a “forgotten generation or even a forgotten century.”

Cerf suggested creating a “digital vellum” to save old software and hardware, so that even very old files could still be opened in the future. He said, “When you think about how much of our daily lives is saved in digital form—like emails, tweets, and everything on the web—it’s clear we could lose a lot of our history. We don’t want our digital lives to disappear. If we want to keep them, we must make sure the digital things we create today can still be opened far into the future.”

Some people question if “bit rot” is really such a big problem. Today, we often save music, photos, letters, and other documents in digital form to keep them safe for a long time. But while scientists are finding ways to store digital files for hundreds of years, the programs and machines needed to read these files are quickly becoming outdated.

Cerf said, “We are carelessly putting all our data into what could become an information black hole. We digitize things because we think it will save them, but unless we do more, these digital versions might not be better—and could even be worse—than the original items. If you have photos you really care about, print them out.”

Ancient civilizations did not have this problem. Their histories were written on clay tablets or papyrus scrolls, which only needed eyes to read. But future historians studying our time will find PDFs, Word documents, and many other file types that need special software and sometimes special hardware to read.

This problem is already happening. In the 1980s, people saved documents on floppy disks, played games from cassettes on the ZX Spectrum, used joysticks, and had Atari game cartridges. Even if the disks and cassettes are still good, the machines needed to use them are now mostly found only in museums.

Video games are an important part of digital culture, but Cerf warns that important political and historical documents could also be lost to bit rot. In 2005, historian Doris Kearns Goodwin wrote a book about Abraham Lincoln. She found old letters in libraries and used them to tell the story. Cerf said, “Today, those letters would be emails, and in a hundred years, it will be almost impossible to find them.”

Cerf admits that historians will try to save important material, but he says we often do not know what will be important until many years later. For example, historians learned about the ancient mathematician Archimedes and his ideas about infinity and calculus from a hidden manuscript found under a prayer book from the thirteenth century. Cerf said, “We have learned a lot from things that were saved by chance and give us a look into earlier civilizations.”

Researchers at Carnegie Mellon University in Pittsburgh are working on a solution to bit rot. Mahadev Satyanarayanan takes digital copies of computer hard drives while they are running different software. These copies can be used on a computer that acts like the old one, so it can read files that would not work otherwise. In a project called Olive, the researchers have saved the original 1982 game Mystery House for the Apple II, an early version of WordPerfect, and the 1993 game Doom.

However, inventing new technology is only part of the solution. It can be even harder to get legal permission to copy and save software before it disappears. When tech companies go out of business or stop supporting their products, they might sell the rights to someone else, making it very difficult to get approval. Cerf said, “To do this properly, we might need to include the right to preserve software in our laws about copyright, patents, and licenses. We are talking about saving these things for hundreds or even thousands of years.”

A day that started with early morning police raids at the Baur Au Lac hotel in Zurich ended with 16 football officials being charged with corruption in the United States. Five of these people were current or former members of FIFA’s executive committee. Among them were Ricardo Teixeira, the former head of Brazil’s football federation, and Marco Polo Del Nero, who recently left the FIFA executive committee.

These 16 people were accused of fraud and other crimes by the US Department of Justice. The new 240-page document replaced the earlier one from May 2015 and described several kickback schemes. Now, 27 people have been charged by the US, and there are 24 more unnamed “co-conspirators,” including former FIFA executive committee members. US Attorney General Loretta Lynch said, “The betrayal of trust here is outrageous. The level of corruption is completely unacceptable.”

On the same day, FIFA’s executive committee had planned to show new reforms during the ongoing corruption crisis. However, Swiss police arrested Juan Ángel Napout, the president of the South American football confederation from Paraguay, and Alfredo Hawit, the head of the North and Central American and Caribbean football body. Hawit had only taken over in May 2015 after Jeffrey Webb was arrested as part of the US investigation that caused a crisis in FIFA and led to Sepp Blatter’s downfall. Webb’s predecessor, Jack Warner, was also arrested in May.

The Swiss Federal Office of Justice said about the new arrests: “They are being held in custody while waiting for extradition. According to the US, they are suspected of accepting millions of dollars in bribes.” Webb and Luis Bedoya, a former executive committee member from Colombia, were among those who pleaded guilty in the US. Lynch said that eight people, five of whom were not named in the first document, had pleaded guilty since May.
