Now, eleven current and former members of FIFA’s executive committee have been charged in the investigation. The investigation says there were $200 million in bribes, mostly as kickbacks from TV and marketing contracts, but also from FIFA’s development programs. The last three presidents of the regional football bodies CONCACAF and Conmebol have all been charged.

Lynch said, “The message from this announcement should be clear to anyone guilty who is still hiding: you will not escape our investigation.” Teixeira, who was once married to the daughter of former FIFA president João Havelange, was charged along with Del Nero and José Maria Marin, who was charged in May.

Fourteen men were charged in May 2015, and four more pleaded guilty. A few days later, Blatter won a fifth term as FIFA president but later agreed to step down as the crisis got worse. He was then temporarily suspended along with UEFA President Michel Platini because of an alleged £1.3 million “disloyal payment” to Platini. Both men could be banned for life if the FIFA ethics committee finds them guilty in December.

Others charged on Thursday included Rafael Salguero from Guatemala, who left the executive committee in May; Eduardo Deluca, the former South American Confederation Secretary General; Manuel Burga, the former president of Peru’s football federation; and Carlos Chaves, the president of Bolivia’s football federation, who is already in jail in his country.

Lynch said, “The Department of Justice is committed to ending the widespread corruption we have described among the leaders of international football. This is not only because of the size of the corruption and the effort needed to keep it going, but also because this behavior goes against international principles.”

The acting FIFA President, Issa Hayatou, refused to talk about the details of the latest arrests. But he said that neither he nor FIFA was corrupt. Speaking to the media for the first time since becoming acting president in September 2015, when Blatter was suspended, Hayatou said, like his predecessors, that the current crisis was caused by only a few bad individuals.

“FIFA is not corrupt. We have individuals who have behaved badly. Do not generalize the situation,” said Hayatou, who has been president of the Confederation of African Football for more than 25 years. “There are many people who have been in FIFA for more than 20 or 30 years who have not been accused of anything.”

How long can you hold your breath? I am trying it right now. The first 30 seconds are easy. At 45 seconds, I want to stop, but I keep going and it feels a bit easier for a short time. But after one minute, I know I cannot last much longer. My heart is beating fast. I let out a small breath, which helps. Finally, I have to stop, so I breathe out all the air in my lungs and take a big breath in. I keep breathing heavily for a few more breaths, and my husband asks what I am doing. I manage to hold my breath for one minute and 12 seconds. I am quite proud of myself.

Being able to hold your breath is very important in some sports, especially freediving. In 2006, I was making a TV show about how the lungs work for a BBC series called Don’t Die Young. I was lucky to meet Sam Amps, who was the captain of the UK freedive team. At a swimming pool in Bristol, she taught me some simple exercises to help me hold my breath longer while swimming underwater. By the end of the lesson, I could hold my breath for 90 seconds, which was enough to swim across the pool. Sam could swim across the pool three times easily. She could hold her breath for five minutes while swimming. Five minutes!

I asked her how she did it. She said she breathed very slowly for several minutes before each dive, then took a big, deep breath before going underwater. She also said that training helped her resist the need to breathe for much longer than most people.

Some people think that being able to hold your breath is proof that humans had a water-based period in evolution. Some say that humans can slow their heart rate and body processes to hold their breath longer. Other things about our bodies, like having little body hair, the way our fat is under the skin, and even walking on two legs, have been linked to an “aquatic phase” in our evolution. But the “aquatic ape hypothesis” does not have good scientific evidence. It sounds interesting, but when we look at the facts, it is just a story, not the truth.

When we look at breath-holding, humans are not the only land mammals that can do it. (It is hard to test this in other mammals because, unlike humans, they do not follow instructions to hold their breath.) Experiments show that heart rate does not go down when holding your breath on land. But when you are underwater in cold water, cooling the face does slow the heart rate in most people. Still, this is not proof of an aquatic past, because this reaction is common in many air-breathing animals. This slower heart rate is part of what is called the “mammalian diving reflex.” These body reactions can help with diving, but they are also important for not drowning.

Even though our breath-holding ability is not very special compared to other animals, it is now very useful in medicine. Radiotherapy for breast cancer uses radiation aimed exactly at the tumor. This can take several minutes, so it is usually done in short bursts between breaths. But if the patient can keep her chest still for several minutes, the whole dose can be given at once, in the right place. The problem is that most people, like me, cannot hold their breath for more than a minute. But doctors at University Hospital Birmingham have done experiments showing that if patients breathe oxygen-rich air before holding their breath, they can hold it for five and a half minutes.

Surprisingly, the trick is not about fooling the body’s sensors for low oxygen or high carbon dioxide in the blood, but about fooling the diaphragm. When you breathe in, your diaphragm muscle contracts and pulls flat, making your chest bigger so air comes in. When you hold your breath, you keep your diaphragm tight. Breathing in oxygen-rich air and lowering carbon dioxide before holding your breath, as in the Birmingham experiments, may help by stopping the diaphragm from getting tired quickly. Also, breathing out a little air lets the diaphragm relax a bit and helps you hold your breath longer, just like I found when I tried it.

So, your diaphragm, the main muscle for breathing, is in control when you try to hold your breath. In the end, even if you trick it for a while, the signals from the diaphragm become too strong, and you have to breathe.

The Duke and Duchess of Cambridge won the first part of their fight for privacy on Tuesday. A French magazine was stopped from selling or using photos taken of them at a private house in Provence.

However, the fight is not over. French prosecutors now have to decide if they will start a criminal case against the magazine editor and the photographer or photographers who took pictures of the duchess sunbathing topless while on holiday in the south of France.

A court in Nanterre, Paris, gave an order that the gossip magazine Closer must give the digital files of the pictures to the court within 24 hours. The magazine is also not allowed to share the pictures anymore, including on its website and tablet app.

The court’s four-page decision only affects Mondadori Magazines France, which publishes Closer. The court also ordered the company to pay €2,000 in legal costs. If the magazine does not follow the order, it will have to pay a €10,000 fine for every day it does not comply. The couple did not ask for any damages.

The court said, “These photos showed a couple in a private moment, partly naked, on the terrace of a private home, far from a public road, and they could expect to be safe from people passing by. These photos are very intrusive.”

The judges also said that if Mondadori, the company owned by former Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi, publishes any more photos in France, it will have to pay a €10,000 fine for each photo. But this order only covers the 14 photos that have already been published. The editor of Closer has suggested that there are more, even more private, photos.

St James’s Palace said the couple “welcome the judge’s ruling.” A source said, “They always believed the law was broken and that they had the right to privacy.” Maud Sobel, the couple’s lawyer in Paris, called it “a wonderful decision” and said, “We’ve been proven right.”

Even though they are happy with the civil court’s decision, the couple are also trying to start a criminal case for breach of privacy against the magazine and the photographer or photographers. The prosecutor must decide who will be charged, and the complaint mentions “persons unknown.” But it is believed the couple want charges against the editor of Closer, which published the photos on Friday, and the person who took the pictures of them sunbathing at the chateau, which belongs to Lord Linley, son of the late Princess Margaret.

Paris police started a preliminary investigation on Tuesday. In France, breaking privacy laws can lead to up to one year in prison and a fine of €45,000.

This legal action is important because the couple want to send a strong message to the world and hope to stop paparazzi from doing this in the future.

Their lawyers did not ask for Closer magazines to be removed from shops.

On Saturday, the Irish Daily Star published the photos, and on Monday night, the editor was suspended while the newspaper investigates. Also on Monday, the Italian magazine Chi, owned by Mondadori, quickly released a special edition with 26 pages of the private photos of the future queen.

The couple’s lawyer, Aurélien Hamelle, told the Paris court that it was important to block the “highly intimate” photos of the duchess without her bikini top because she is “a young woman, not an object.”

But Delphine Pando, the lawyer for Closer, said the legal action was “too strong” for just publishing the photos. She also said the magazine could not control the resale of the photos because it did not own the original images.

Copies of Closer magazine were selling quickly on eBay, with one selling for £31.01, until eBay removed all listings after getting “strong feedback” from its users.

Galina Zaglumyonova was woken up in her apartment in central Chelyabinsk by a huge explosion. The blast broke her balcony windows and smashed her clay flower pots. When she got out of bed, she saw a big white trail in the morning sky and heard car alarms on the street. “I didn’t understand what was happening,” she said. “There was a big explosion and then several smaller ones. I first thought a plane had crashed.”

But what she saw was a ten-ton meteorite falling to Earth in fireballs just after sunrise. Officials said almost 1,200 people were hurt, and more than 40 went to the hospital. Most people were injured by flying glass from windows broken by the loud sound made by the meteorite. No one died.

The meteorite entered the atmosphere at a speed of at least 33,000 miles per hour. It broke into pieces between 18 and 32 miles above the ground, according to the Russian Academy of Sciences.

The event caused panic in Chelyabinsk, a city with over one million people south of Russia’s Ural mountains. Mobile phone networks quickly stopped working because so many people tried to call at once. Videos taken by local people showed the meteorite pieces glowing brighter as they got closer to the ground.

The white trail in the sky could be seen for hundreds of miles, even in nearby Kazakhstan. Tatyana Bets was working at the front desk of a hospital in the city center when the meteorite hit. “First we felt the wind, then the room was filled with a very bright light, and we saw a cloud of strange smoke in the sky,” she said. After a few minutes, the explosions happened. The Ministry of the Interior said at least three craters were found and were being watched by the military. One crater was more than six meters wide. Another piece of meteorite broke through the thick ice of a nearby lake. Local military officials said radiation levels at the impact sites were normal.

In Chelyabinsk, schools and universities were closed, and many workers were told to go home early. About 200 children were among the injured.

Many people with small injuries, mostly cuts from flying glass, came to the clinic where Bets works. She said a nearby student dormitory was badly affected, and many students came in scared. “There were a lot of girls in shock. Some were very pale and many fainted,” she said.

Early reports said more than 100,000 square meters of glass were broken and 3,000 buildings were damaged. The total cost of the damage in the city was estimated at over one billion roubles (£20 million).

The meteorite over Chelyabinsk came less than a day before asteroid 2012 DA14 was expected to pass close to Earth (about 17,510 miles away), the closest ever recorded. But experts said the two events were just a coincidence.

However, rumors and conspiracy theories spread quickly after the incident. Some Russian news reports said local air defense units shot at the meteorite and broke it apart more than 15 miles above the ground.

Vladimir Zhirinovsky, the leader of Russia’s Liberal Democrat party, said it was not a meteorite but a military attack by the United States. He repeated what some people said in videos. “It’s not a meteorite falling – it’s a test of new American weapons,” Zhirinovsky said.

Some people tried to make money from the situation. They offered pieces of meteorite for sale on the internet just a few hours after the impact.

President Vladimir Putin and Prime Minister Dmitry Medvedev were told about the event. Putin held a meeting with the head of the Emergency Situations Ministry. “It shows that not only economies are at risk, but the whole planet,” Medvedev said at an economic meeting in Siberia.

Dmitry Rogozin, Russia’s Deputy Prime Minister and former Ambassador to NATO, wrote on Twitter that the world should work together to create a warning system for all “objects from space.” He added that neither the US nor Russia could stop such objects from hitting Earth.

Glastonbury Festival wants to fight the problem of plastic water bottles as part of its plan to become the world’s most environmentally friendly outdoor music festival.

The organizers are focusing on disposable plastic bottles, which are a big part of the throwaway culture. Every year, about one million plastic bottles are used at the 900-acre festival site in Somerset, leaving the area covered in plastic waste.

To help stop this, 2,000 road crew and band members will get stainless-steel reusable bottles. Many more reusable bottles will be sold to festival-goers, so they do not have to use plastic bottles. The 140,000 people with tickets are also being asked to bring their own reusable bottles, which they can fill at 400 water taps around the site.

Lucy Smith, who organizes green issues for Glastonbury, said, “We have great water quality in the UK, but everyone wants to drink bottled water.”

She said this plan comes before another idea for Glastonbury 2015, where all plastic beer glasses and cutlery will be replaced with reusable items. The goal is to get rid of plastic waste at the large rural site.

Environmentalists say there are about 150 million tonnes of plastic waste in the world and in the oceans, which poisons nature and kills animals.

In the end, the organizers want Glastonbury to be the greenest festival in the world, like the Burning Man festival in Nevada, USA. At Burning Man, people must take away everything they bring, leaving no trace.

People going to Glastonbury are also being asked to use public transport or share cars with friends. Smith said, “We want to be as sustainable as possible. We do everything we can, but cleaning up after 140,000 people is hard. We can’t put bins everywhere.”

Campaigners say plastic water bottles can take hundreds or even thousands of years to break down. Making these bottles also harms the environment, because millions of barrels of oil are used, and transporting bottled water creates more carbon emissions.

About 13 billion plastic water bottles are sold in the UK every year, but only one in five is recycled.

Smith said festival-goers should use the tap water, which comes from large underground reservoirs, instead of buying bottled water. In the past, water came from old tanks and had a lot of chlorine. The charity WaterAid will set up water kiosks around the site, selling reusable bottles and cups, and giving free refills. In 2015, these kiosks will also be DJ booths at night, like those in Africa.

Organizers say that almost half of all rubbish left at the site was recycled in 2013, and there will be 15,000 recycling bins at the festival in 2014.

Even though Glastonbury is becoming more eco-friendly, some people still criticize it. For example, Bruce Dickinson from Iron Maiden said he will never bring his band to Glastonbury, calling it “the most bourgeois thing on the planet.”

The weather forecast for Glastonbury is good, with sunny and dry weather expected. Experts say there will not be a repeat of 1985 (the windiest year), 1997 (the muddiest), or 2005 (the “year of thunder”).

The world sees William Shakespeare as a shared figure, and London claims him as their own. However, Stratford-upon-Avon, the town where he was born in 1564 and died 400 years ago, plans to celebrate Shakespeare as their own important person in 2016. Paul Edmondson, head of learning and research at the Shakespeare Birthplace Trust, says that Stratford was always important to Shakespeare. 

Some people think Shakespeare left Stratford and his family to make money in London and only returned to die. But Edmondson explains that Stratford is where Shakespeare bought land and houses, kept his library, and spent time reading and thinking. In 2016, Stratford wants to remind everyone how important the town was to Shakespeare.

John Aubrey, a writer and historian from the seventeenth century who was born 11 years after Shakespeare died, said there was nothing very special about Shakespeare. Aubrey, who went to university (unlike Shakespeare), said Shakespeare acted very well and that his plays were popular. However, the world does not agree with Aubrey. The anniversary of Shakespeare’s death, who is the most famous and most performed playwright in the world, will be celebrated across Britain and around the world.

For example, Macbeth will be performed in Singapore, and Romeo and Juliet in Brussels. Shakespeare’s Globe Theatre is finishing the first world tour in theatre history, bringing Hamlet to almost every country—North Korea is the only country left. In London, there will be a special cinema with 37 screens, one for each of Shakespeare’s plays, along the South Bank.

The National Theatre, the Royal Shakespeare Company, and almost every other theatre company in the country will celebrate the anniversary. There will be both traditional and creative performances, such as Spymonkey’s Complete Deaths, a funny show about the 74 deaths (75 if you count a fly in Titus Andronicus) in Shakespeare’s plays, by stabbing, poisoning, smothering, and smashing. There will also be hundreds of lectures, readings, international conferences, films, concerts, operas, and big exhibitions.

Although Shakespeare was famous when he was alive, there is not much written evidence about his life. His plays might not have survived if his friends and fellow actors had not collected every piece of every play they could find—drafts, scripts, actors’ notes, and 17 plays not known in any other version—and published them in the First Folio in 1623, seven years after Shakespeare died.

The actor Mark Rylance has called the First Folio his favorite book in the world. Most of the surviving First Folios will be shown to the public, including copies from the British Library, the Bodleian Library, and a damaged copy recently found in France. Some of the most valuable documents will be shown together in an exhibition at Somerset House in London, organized by the National Archives and King’s College London. This will include four of Shakespeare’s six known signatures, which are all a little different.

The exhibition, called By Me, William Shakespeare, will also show his will, court papers about the time when Shakespeare and his fellow actors took apart a theatre on the north side of the Thames and rebuilt it as the Globe on the South Bank, and records showing payments from the royal treasury for performances for King James I and Queen Anne on Boxing Day.

Dominic Dromgoole, the outgoing director of the Globe, recently joked that Shakespeare was a true Londoner, but admitted that Stratford-upon-Avon also has a claim. Stratford will insist that the town helped make and educate Shakespeare. His old school room is being restored with a £1.4 million Heritage Lottery grant and will open as a permanent visitor attraction.

Shakespeare bought New Place, the second best house in Stratford, where he died, according to legend, on St George’s Day, 23 April, the same day as his birth. Paul Edmondson says, “You don’t buy a house like New Place and not live there.” He believes that after Shakespeare bought the house in 1597, he spent all his thinking time there, and that his later plays, including The Tempest, were at least planned and probably written there. The Shakespeare Birthplace Trust calls New Place “the jewel in the crown of the 400th anniversary celebrations,” but in reality, the house is gone.

Shakespeare’s house was destroyed 300 years ago, and the house that replaced it, which may have used some of the original materials, was also destroyed in 1759 by a clergyman named Francis Gastrell after a fight over taxes. Gastrell had already cut down Shakespeare’s mulberry tree, where the writer is said to have worked, because he was annoyed by tourists looking into his garden.

The empty space in Stratford has never been filled, but a five-year archaeology project has uncovered more about the site. News that Shakespeare’s kitchen was found in the remaining cellars spread around the world. The whole site is being redesigned for the anniversary, with the foundations marked and the garden restored. Paul Edmondson says, “Without Stratford, there would have been no Shakespeare.”

On one day in August, one out of every seven people in the world, or 1 billion people, used Facebook, according to its founder Mark Zuckerberg. In just ten years, Facebook has changed how people connect with each other, how they think about privacy, how they do business, how they get news, and even the meaning of some everyday words. It has also helped people organize protests and has changed society in many ways, both good and bad.

Zuckerberg said, “A more open and connected world is a better world. It brings stronger relationships with those you love, a stronger economy with more opportunities, and a stronger society that reflects all of our values.” Here are some of the ways Facebook has changed our lives:

1. Facebook has changed the meaning of “friend”
Now, “to friend” is a verb. On Facebook, it is easy to “unfriend” someone, which means to remove them from your friend list. This is much easier than ending a friendship in real life. Words like “share” and “like” are still used, but Facebook has made them more important. School and university reunions are less needed because you can already see what your old classmates are doing, who is successful, who has broken up, and you can see many photos of their children. You also know if your ex is dating someone new because of their photos.

On Facebook, all friends are equal. A classmate you haven’t seen in 15 years, a friend of a friend, or a colleague you never met in person are all called “friends” just like your best friend, your partner, or your mother. But this does not mean you feel the same about all of them. Professor Robin Dunbar, who studies social groups, says people can only really have about 150 friends. He thinks Facebook has not changed this yet, but he worries that because it is so easy to end friendships online, people may not learn how to get along with others.

2. We care less about privacy
There is a saying: if you are not paying for something, you are the product. Facebook is a good example of this, and it has created a whole industry from people’s information. The surprising thing is that users know this and still give their information willingly.

The Pew Research Center found that most young people are happy to share their details. 91% post a photo of themselves, 71% share the city or town where they live (up from 61%), more than half give their email address, and one in five give their phone number. Because people share so much online, Facebook lets everyone create an image of themselves and build a group of followers. In a psychology journal, researchers wrote about the new idea of the “Facebook self.” More than 80% of users list their interests, which helps companies target them with ads. However, most young users do make their profiles private, with 60% allowing only friends to see their information.

3. Facebook has created millions of jobs – but not just in its own offices
Facebook has created a whole new industry, including many jobs for people who help companies use Facebook for their brands. Michael Tinmouth, a social media expert, said, “It is a tool like no other. Marketers now understand their customers better than ever before. The data and information you get are amazing. You know who your customers are, who their friends are, and how they interact with your brand.”

Advertisers pay a lot for this information. Facebook’s ad revenue went up 46%, reaching $3.32 billion. But Facebook can also be difficult for brands. Now, instead of customers complaining by phone or on small websites, they can post their complaints for all their friends to see, or even on the brand’s own page. If something is unfair, it can quickly become very popular and spread to many people.

4. Facebook has helped organize revolutions
Even though the Arab Spring was called the Twitter revolution, Facebook has changed how people organize protests and actions. Olga Onuch from Manchester University found that Facebook was the main way to reach half of the protesters in Ukraine’s Euromaidan movement. Facebook posts started the Maidan protests after Ukraine said it would not sign an agreement with the EU. The posts helped organize real-life actions, not just online anger. Ukrainian activist Mustafa Nayyem posted: “If you really want to do something, don’t just 'like' this post. Let’s meet near the independence monument in Maidan.”

Many people in Onuch’s research said they used Facebook to find out the truth about what was happening, because they did not trust traditional news.

5. Facebook makes news, breaks news, and decides what is news
About 71% of people aged 18 to 24 say the internet is their main source of news, and 63% of all users agree, according to the Pew Research Center. About one third of Facebook users post about politics and government.

Most people first see news stories or breaking news on Facebook or other social media, usually on their phones. Now, users do not even have to leave Facebook to read news. With Instant Articles, news stories appear inside Facebook. News companies can sell ads around their articles and keep all the money, while Facebook can also sell ads and give 70% of that money to the news companies.

Facebook has also changed how journalists write stories. Many reporters now depend on Facebook to find and contact people for their stories. Facebook is a directory to find almost anyone, who might suddenly become part of a big news story. Facebook even has its own newswire, sharing the most useful user reactions to breaking news, including photos and videos.

6. Users are changing Facebook
Facebook started as a site for students, and only students at top US universities could join. In 2014, ten years after it started, 56% of internet users aged 65 and older had a Facebook account. Also, 39% of users are connected to people they have never met in real life.

Groups have become less popular, and now people use pages more. Writing on each other’s walls is old-fashioned, and people now upload photos instantly from their phones instead of making special albums. More than ever, Facebook is a way to connect not just with friends, but with the whole internet.

David Kirkpatrick, author of The Facebook Effect, said we should get used to Facebook. “It might go away one day, but something this big takes a long time to disappear,” he told BBC Radio 4. “Facebook has shown it can change, and it will continue to be very important.”

Low-income countries will continue to be most affected by climate change caused by humans over the next 100 years. These countries will see sea levels rise slowly, stronger storms, hotter days and nights, more unpredictable rain, and longer, bigger heatwaves. This information comes from the most detailed study on the subject so far.

The last big United Nations (UN) report in 2007 said temperatures could rise by 6°C or more by 2100. Scientists now think this is unlikely, but land and sea temperatures will still rise during this century, possibly reaching 4°C above today’s levels. This would destroy crops and make many cities too hot to live in.

As temperatures and ocean heat increase, tropical and subtropical areas will see big changes in yearly rainfall, according to the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) report, released in Stockholm and online in September.

East Africa will likely get more short rains, while West Africa will have heavier monsoons. Burma, Bangladesh, and India can expect stronger cyclones. Other parts of southern Asia will get heavier summer rains. Indonesia may get less rain from July to October, but coastal areas near the South China Sea and Gulf of Thailand will get more extreme rain when cyclones hit.

The report’s authors said, “It is almost certain that, in the long term, global rainfall will change. Countries in high latitudes, like Europe and North America, will get more rain, but many dry and semi-dry subtropical areas will probably get less. In wet tropical areas, heavy rain events will very likely become stronger and happen more often in a warmer world.”

They also said, “Monsoon seasons will probably start earlier or stay the same, but will very likely end later, making the season longer.”

Scientists and experts in developing countries welcomed the report, saying it matches what they see in their own countries.

Saleemul Huq, director of the International Centre for Climate Change and Development in Dhaka, said, “The IPCC shows that climate change is real and happening more strongly than before. We already see the effects in Bangladesh and across South Asia. This is not new for us. Most developing countries are already facing climate change. They do not need the IPCC to tell them the weather is changing.”

Scientists have also lowered their predictions for sea-level rise. Depending on future greenhouse gas emissions, sea levels will rise by an average of 40 to 62 centimeters by 2100. However, the rise will not be the same everywhere. Many millions of people in big cities in developing countries, like Lagos and Calcutta, are at risk.

The report also says that weather disasters will be more likely in a warmer world. Even though the total number of tropical cyclones may go down or stay the same, they could become stronger, with higher winds and heavier rain.

Life in many cities in developing countries could become almost impossible, because city temperatures are already much higher than in the countryside. Much higher temperatures could shorten the growing season in some parts of Africa by up to 20%, the report said.

Dr. Camilla Toulmin, director of the International Institute for Environment and Development, said, “Climate models are not yet good enough to predict local and regional impacts, but it is clear that everyone is at risk in some way.”

The charity Oxfam said world hunger will get worse as climate change hurts crop production and people’s incomes. They said the number of people at risk of hunger could rise by 10% to 20% by 2050, and the amount of food available per person each day could fall worldwide.

Oxfam said, “The changing climate is already putting progress against hunger at risk, and it will probably get worse. A hot world is a hungry world. If the rest of the 21st century is like the first decade, we will soon see climate extremes that humans have never experienced before.”

Sometimes, men feel sadder and think more about death as they get older. Some people react by spending all their money on things like a sportscar. Making big and risky changes in life is often called a midlife crisis. But maybe humans are not the only animals who feel this way.

Now, a group of scientists from different countries say they have found signs that middle-aged chimpanzees and orangutans also feel less happy. They think this drop in happiness is like a midlife crisis for apes.

The study was published in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. Some scientists are surprised by these results. But the authors say their findings show that the midlife crisis might come from something in our biology that we share with apes.

Alex Weiss, a psychologist at Edinburgh University, said that many people believe there is a drop in happiness in middle age. He and his team wanted to know if this is not just a human problem, but something that happens to other animals too, not only because of social reasons, but because of evolution.

The team from the US, Japan, Germany, and the UK asked people who work with apes, like zookeepers and carers, to fill out forms about the animals. The forms had questions about each ape’s mood, how much they enjoyed being with others, and how well they reached their goals. The last question asked how the carer would feel about being that ape for a week, with answers scored from one to seven.

More than 500 apes were studied in three groups. Two groups were chimpanzees, and the third group was orangutans from Sumatra or Borneo. The apes lived in zoos, sanctuaries, and research centers in the US, Australia, Japan, Canada, and Singapore.

When the scientists looked at the answers, they found that apes felt less happy in middle age, but their happiness went up again when they got older. In captivity, great apes often live to 50 years or more. The lowest point in happiness was at about 28.3 and 27.2 years old for chimpanzees, and 35.4 years old for orangutans.

Weiss said, “In all three groups, we see that happiness is lowest in chimpanzees and orangutans at an age that is similar to midlife in humans. On average, happiness scores are lowest when the animals are around 30 years old.”

The team thinks that this drop in happiness might happen because apes see other sad apes die younger, or because of changes in the brain as they age, which also happens in humans. Weiss admitted that, unlike men, apes do not make big or risky changes in their lives during middle age.

Robin Dunbar, a professor at Oxford University, was not sure about the results. He said it is hard to know what could make apes feel more or less happy at different ages, because apes do not think much about the future, which is a big difference between them and humans. Alexandra Freund, a professor at the University of Zurich, also doubted the idea. She said that even in humans, there is little proof of a midlife crisis. She said that if there is any drop in happiness in middle age, it is very small, and many studies do not find it at all.

But Weiss thinks the study could help us understand why some men have a midlife crisis. He said, “If we want to know what causes the midlife crisis, we should look at what is the same in middle-aged humans, chimps, and orangutans.”

When you hear the word Amazon, what do you think of first – the world’s biggest forest, the longest river, or the largest online store? Which one do you think is most important?

These questions are now important in a big debate about how to change the rules of the internet. Brazil and Peru have complained about a request from the American online store Amazon. The company wants to use “.amazon” as a new internet ending, like “.com”.

Amazon, which is based in Seattle, wants its brand to be a top-level domain name. But the governments of Brazil and Peru say this would stop people from using this internet address for things like protecting the environment, helping indigenous people, and other public uses.

There are many other arguments about names like “.patagonia” and “.shangrila”. These arguments are about who should control important internet names and how the internet should be managed.

Until now, it was easy to see if a website was for business, government, or something else because of endings like “.com”, “.gov”, and about 20 others. But now, these endings – called generic top-level domains (gTLDs) – are about to get much bigger. The Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers (ICANN), a non-profit group in the US that helps manage the internet, has received requests for hundreds of new gTLDs. Each request costs almost $200,000. There are already 22 gTLDs.

Amazon has asked for many new domain names, like “.shop”, “.song”, “.book”, and “.kindle”. But the most argued one is “.amazon”.

Brazil and Peru want Amazon to cancel its request for “.amazon”. They say a private company should not get a name that is also a big geographical area in their countries and is used by some organizations. The Brazilian Ministry of Science and Technology said, “Letting private companies use geographical names as gTLDs to help their brand or make money from these names does not help the public interest.”

Brazil also said that other members of the Amazon Cooperation Treaty (Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Guyana, Suriname, and Venezuela) agree with them.

Many other protests have been made about new top-level domains that use geographical, cultural, or disputed brand names.

Argentina is unhappy that the US clothing company Patagonia wants to use “.patagonia” as a domain name. Patagonia is a famous region in Argentina with its own parliament, beautiful nature, and important resources like oil, fish, minerals, and farms. It is also a popular place for tourists. The Argentine government said, “Argentina rejects the ‘.patagonia’ request for a new generic top-level domain.”

China has also protested the domain “.shangrila”, which a hotel group wants to use. The Chinese government says “shangri-la” is the name of a region in Yunnan province. However, this area was only given this name in 2001, long after the hotel group started, to make money from the famous story “Lost Horizon” by British writer James Hilton.

In April, at a meeting in Beijing, ICANN’s Governmental Advisory Committee, which represents national governments, suggested stopping these disputed requests for now. They will talk about them again at a meeting in Durban in July. The first new domain names should be used before the end of 2013.

He is not the first person to doubt Mars One, a very ambitious private project that wants to send people to live on Mars starting in 2025. But Joseph Roche is different from most critics because he is actually on the shortlist to become an astronaut for the mission.

Roche is an astrophysicist at Trinity College Dublin. In February, he was named as one of the 100 people chosen for the mission. He wrote in the Guardian about his serious doubts that Mars One can really work.

Roche says the selection process “was not strict enough to meet the standards of traditional astronaut programs.” He also says the Dutch Mars One team is “naive” to think they can succeed alone with a mission that is supposed to cost $6 billion, and that they should now accept it is very unlikely to happen.

He writes: “More openness and transparency would help Mars One a lot, but I think the problems with the selection process, and their unwillingness to work with the scientific community, mean that it is time for Mars One to admit this project is not realistic and to support other, more possible space missions instead.”

Roche also worries about how the mission organizers announced a so-called top-ten list of candidates. He says this ranking did not show who was most likely to become an astronaut, but was based on how many “supporter points” each person had. People got these points by doing things like buying official Mars One merchandise.

He writes: “These points are Mars One’s supporter points, which ‘show how much you support Mars One’s mission’.” These points do not affect the selection process and only show how much money each supporter has given to Mars One.

The official plan for the mission says the group wants to send a lander and a satellite to Mars in 2018, a rover in 2020, and cargo missions starting in 2022. Humans would start arriving in 2025, and groups of four people would be sent every two years to join the settlement. They would not come back to Earth.

In February, Gerard ’t Hooft, a Dutch Nobel Prize winner in physics and a supporter of the project, said he did not believe this schedule was realistic. He said: “It will take much longer and cost much more. When they first asked me to be involved, I told them: ‘You have to add a zero to everything’.”

Roche also spoke to Medium, a US blogging website that has also doubted Mars One. Medium reported that the supposed 200,000 applications to be astronauts were actually only 2,761.

He told Medium more about the selection process: “I have not met anyone from Mars One in person. At first, they said there would be regional interviews. We would travel there, be interviewed, and tested for several days. That sounded like a real astronaut selection process.

“But then they made us sign a non-disclosure agreement if we wanted to be interviewed, and suddenly, instead of a proper regional interview over several days, it became a ten-minute Skype call.”

Roche told the Guardian he did not want to give more interviews because he did not want to be negative about space travel.

In his article, he writes: “I am passionate about pushing the limits of science, and that is why I liked the ambitious Mars One plan. Even though Mars One was never likely to solve the financial and technical problems in their timeline, it was exciting to hear a new idea that makes us think about our future in space.

“Being part of the public debate about the ethics and morality of future missions has been one of the most interesting and enjoyable parts of my time with Mars One. If a one-way mission to Mars ever became possible, I would always volunteer. For an astrophysicist, that is an easy decision, but it does not matter because I do not think we will see a one-way mission in my lifetime.”

The small room looks like a classroom. The walls are made of corrugated iron and have educational charts, like pictures of the alphabet and a map of Bangladesh. But it is hard to focus because there is always loud hammering and strong chemicals in the air that hurt the throat and eyes. Still, the children who study in this three-square-metre room are lucky. They do not have to work in the factories across the street.

For 14 years, SOHAY, a local non-governmental organization (NGO) supported by the Global Fund for Children and Comic Relief, has worked in the slums of Dhaka to help child workers go to school. SOHAY helps children who work in dangerous places, like aluminium and plastic factories and tanneries.

This classroom is one of 23 urban development centres that SOHAY has opened in the city. These centres help children catch up on their education so they can join primary school. After they start primary school, children can come back to the centres to do homework and get help from other students.

Alamin, who is ten years old, used to work in a plastic factory. Now he goes to one of the centres. His father sells things on the street and his mother works part-time as a house cleaner. They are all happy that Alamin is now in school and not doing dangerous work. His friend Rabi also wants to forget his time in the factory. “I like school,” he says.

SOHAY’s programme manager, Mohammed Abdullah al-Mamun, says, “The urban development centres want to make the community more friendly to education and change how people think about children.” SOHAY also has meetings for parents and employers to stop child labour and gives skills training to help families earn more money.

Mamun says, “It is very hard to get working children into regular school. Their minds and bodies are not like other children’s. After they stop working, it can be hard for them to make friends and get used to school. It is also hard to keep them in school—many drop out. So, it is important to work with schools so they understand and care for these children.”

Seven-year-old Zhorna Akter Sumayya has two older brothers who work (one in a restaurant, one at a local club). After learning about education at a SOHAY centre, she now goes to a government primary school. Her family lives in the slum, and her parents need the money her brothers earn. Her father works in a rickshaw garage and her mother is a house cleaner, but they wanted their daughter to go to school.

In 2015, SOHAY helped 1,540 children leave dangerous work and helped 2,125 children who were at risk of working to go to school. About 780 more children are getting ready to start school in 2017. The organization is also teaching 635 children who still work in dangerous jobs about their rights under Bangladesh’s 2010 child labour law. This law wanted to end all child labour by 2015, but that goal was not reached.

Bangladesh’s Labour Law from 2006 says children under 14 cannot work. But UNICEF says 4.7 million children under 14 still work in the informal sector, and 1.3 million children aged five to 17 work in dangerous jobs.

Sadia Nasrin, who runs another NGO called Sonjag in Dhaka, says, “It was hard to get children into school because they did not get paid for their time.” To solve this, Sonjag started working closely with the slum community where the children live.

The organization talked to people in the community about why school is important. They chose volunteers who wanted to help children and made groups with social workers, community leaders, mothers, young volunteers, and local government.

Nasrin says, “These groups help convince employers to let children leave work for two or three hours a day to go to school and to make the workplace safer for children. The real change comes from the community.”

She also says that people in slums face problems like being forced to leave their homes, police raids, and losing their homes. “The national plan for children does not help street children,” says Nasrin. “The laws are not enough.”

When children miss starting school at age five, it becomes a race against time to stop them from growing up without education. Mamun says, “After they are too old for school, it is very hard to get them in. Children are just waiting to start dangerous work. We are working to stop child labour.”

A senior US researcher warns that people today are in danger of losing the peaceful sounds of nature because they ignore the noises around them. Kurt Fristrup, a senior scientist at the US National Park Service, says that more background noise in some places is making people forget about the pleasant sounds of birds singing, water flowing, and trees moving in the wind. These sounds can still be heard in cities, but they are often covered by traffic, music, and other noises.

Fristrup says the problem is worse because many people listen to music with earphones instead of paying attention to nature. He calls this “learned deafness,” meaning people are training themselves to ignore the sounds around them. He explained at a science meeting in San Jose that people are losing the natural ability to hear things far away because they are not listening to their environment anymore.

He also warns that there are two dangers: one is losing the sharpness of hearing because of too much noise, and the other is losing the habit of listening to the world around us. For the past ten years, the US National Park Service has measured sound levels at over 600 places in the US, including famous parks like Yosemite, Yellowstone, and Denali. All of these places had some noise from human activities, such as airplanes, motorbikes, boats, or tour buses.

Fristrup’s team used these sound measurements and similar data from cities to make a map of noise levels across the US. They found that noise pollution is increasing faster than the US population and more than doubles every 30 years.

He says it is not surprising that people use earphones or noise-cancelling headphones to try to make their surroundings quieter. He compares high background noise to fog for your eyes: you can only notice sounds close to you, not the full range of sounds around you. Even in cities, there are birds and other natural sounds to enjoy, but these are being lost.

People get used to changes in their environment, including more noise. Fristrup worries that, over time, people will accept much worse noise levels and forget how quiet the world used to be. He says that if it becomes too hard to find peace and quiet, many children will grow up without ever experiencing it, which is a real problem.

Other scientists at the same meeting talked about the health benefits of listening to natural sounds. Derrick Taff, a social scientist at Pennsylvania State University, described early experiments showing that listening to recordings of waterfalls, birds, and wind from national parks helped people recover from stress. In one experiment, people had to give a surprise speech in front of researchers. Their heart rate and stress hormone levels were measured before and after the speech. People calmed down faster when they listened to nature sounds than when the sounds were mixed with traffic, airplanes, or conversation.

Taff said that natural sounds are very important to people and are a main reason why people visit protected areas. He believes that even though people listen to music devices a lot, they still appreciate natural sounds. He advises people to visit protected areas and experience these sounds for themselves.

It is not clear why natural sounds are calming, but Fristrup thinks that, over millions of years, humans have learned to connect peaceful natural sounds with safety. He believes that these natural soundscapes make our brains feel safe, while noisy environments make us feel less secure because we cannot listen for danger as well.

Race engineer  
A race engineer is the link between the driver and the mechanics.  
Typical salary: New graduates earn £25,000 to £30,000. After a few years, junior engineers can earn over £40,000. Senior race engineers earn £50,000 to £90,000, and with promotion, salaries can go over £100,000.  
What the job involves: A race engineer listens to the driver, looks at the data, and decides how to set up the car for best performance. Then, the engineer tells the mechanics what changes to make.  
Qualifications: You need a university degree, usually in automotive or mechanical engineering, or motorsport technology. Practical experience is very important.  
To succeed as a race engineer, you must be able to handle pressure.  
Worst thing about the job: The long hours. Race engineers often work all day and night.

Ethical hacker  
Typical salary: Team leaders earn £60,000 to £90,000. New ethical hackers start at £35,000 to £50,000.  
What the job involves: Companies pay ethical hackers to try to break into their computer systems to test how strong their security is.  
Qualifications: You do not always need a computer science degree. People with many different backgrounds and skills can become ethical hackers.  
To succeed as an ethical hacker, you need to love technology and details. You should be good at analyzing and solving hard problems.  
Worst thing about the job: Sometimes, you find out a company has already been hacked before you test their security.

Bomb-disposal diver  
Typical salary: In private companies, you can earn up to £100,000 by working two months out of every three.  
What the job involves: You dive to the sea floor to look for unexploded bombs, shells, grenades, and landmines. You then collect or safely get rid of them.  
Qualifications: You need diving-inspection and medical-technician certificates to work offshore. You also need a qualification in explosive ordnance disposal and many years of experience.  
To succeed as a bomb-disposal diver, you must stay calm under stress. You work alone underwater, often in the dark, and you must be comfortable living in small spaces with other people.  
Worst thing about the job: You will be away from home for at least six months each year.

Social engineer  
Typical salary: Usually between £50,000 and £80,000. Graduates start at £25,000, but salaries rise quickly with more experience and qualifications.  
The job: A social engineer is paid by a company to try to trick employees into giving away secret information, so the engineer can access company data or computer systems.  
Qualifications: Most social engineers have a degree in IT. Knowing psychology helps, and experience in marketing, teaching, or customer service is useful.  
To succeed as a social engineer, you need to be confident when lying and able to fit in anywhere. You also need strong personal ethics and knowledge of the law.  
Worst thing about the job: People often misunderstand your job and think you are a spy, even though you are not.

Power-line helicopter pilot  
Typical salary: £65,000  
The job: You fly a helicopter close to high-voltage power lines so they can be checked with a camera. This helps the power company find problems.  
Qualifications: You need a private helicopter pilot’s licence, a commercial pilot’s licence, and about 2,000 hours of flying experience at low heights in the right type of helicopter.  
To succeed as a power-line helicopter pilot, you need steady hands and to stay calm. Pilots often fly as close as 20 feet from the power line and 30 feet above the ground.  
Worst thing about the job: According to Robin Tutcher, chief helicopter pilot, there are no negatives.

Private butler  
Typical salary: £60,000 to £90,000  
The job: A private butler does many things for their employer, such as managing clothes, driving, caring for pets, managing other staff, serving meals, running errands, looking after guests, booking restaurants, keeping the house safe and clean, cooking, and anything else needed.  
Qualifications: You do not need special qualifications, but you can take a course at the British Butler Academy or the British Butler Institute.  
To succeed as a butler, you must enjoy taking care of others.  
Worst thing about the job: The hours are long and the schedule is unpredictable, making it hard to have a family life. Butlers can also feel lonely, have cultural differences with their employer, and sometimes have to work for people who are not nice.

They call it the Richie Rich Club, and it is about to get even richer. According to a report, India’s richest people will have four times more money by 2018. Hundreds of thousands of new business owners and people who inherit money will become multimillionaires. The survey is based on interviews with 150 very rich people and comes at a time when business confidence is returning in India, the world’s largest democracy.

In recent years, India has had slow economic growth, higher prices for basic foods, and a weaker currency. But in May 2014, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) won a big election by promising to improve the weak economy. Even with the slowdown, there are almost 17% more Indians worth over $3.75 million than in 2013, according to the report for Kotak Mahindra Bank. “Cities are growing quickly, the middle class is getting bigger, there are many more opportunities, and the political situation has improved a lot in recent months,” says Murali Balaraman, a co-author of the report.

Together, India’s rich people own assets worth $1 trillion, which is about 20% of all the wealth in the country. By 2018, this could reach $4 trillion, and the number of multimillionaires could triple.

The luxury market for the new rich and old rich is growing fast. “They want to show their wealth in a quiet way, and buying luxury goods is a good way to do it,” Balaraman said. Abhay Gupta, CEO of Luxury Connect, said the market for expensive goods and experiences will “only get bigger.” “There is a large group of people who want to be like the very rich and copy what they do,” he said.

Cars are some of the most popular things the rich buy, the report says. In 2009, rich people showed off Indian-made SUVs, but now only foreign cars get attention. Mercedes had a 47% increase in sales in India in 2013. BMW launched a new $200,000 model in Delhi. However, India’s poor roads and traffic limit demand. Lamborghini’s CEO, Stephan Winkelmann, said in 2013 that India’s roads “are not so suitable” for their $450,000 sports cars. In India, Lamborghini sells two models: the Gallardo and the Aventador, which can go up to 217 mph. Winkelmann said Indian Lamborghini buyers are much younger than in Europe, usually in their 30s. Still, the most popular investments are real estate, mostly in India, and jewelry.

India’s super-rich are known for their big spending. Mukesh Ambani, the richest man in India, built the world’s most valuable home in Mumbai. The 27-floor tower has helicopter pads, indoor cinemas, and over 600 staff, and is worth about $1 billion.

The three-day wedding of the niece of Lakshmi Mittal, a steel tycoon in the UK worth about $16 billion, reportedly cost $80 million. Hundreds of guests were flown to Barcelona for the ceremony and party, which took place in a museum.

But buyers of luxury goods who want to feel special are becoming more demanding, the Kotak Mahindra report says. One person ordered nine cases of Japanese whisky costing over $750 a bottle for a wedding. The reason was that no one at the wedding would know how to buy the same whisky in India. Another big spender bought many pairs of Louis Vuitton bags, then cut up half of them to make clothes that matched her accessories. Even traditional weddings are changing. Gifts like silver plates, dried fruit, or sweets that were once sent with wedding invitations are now being replaced by gifts from top Western designer brands. “These days, it’s Rolex watches and Louis Vuitton bags,” says Gupta.

Almost half of the new very rich people live in smaller cities. Many give large amounts to charity, but the report says that giving to charity has not grown as fast as the wealth of the very rich.

Co-author Balaraman says that more rich people will not cause social problems because big differences in income and wealth are “normal” in India. “People know that some are rich and some are poor, and they just continue with their lives,” he explains.

Margaret Thatcher, the most powerful British prime minister since Winston Churchill in 1940 and a world leader for free market economics in the late 20th century, has died. The British government said she would have a ceremonial funeral with military honours at St Paul’s Cathedral.

British prime minister David Cameron, who is returning early from a trip to Europe because of the news, said: “It was with great sadness that I learned of Lady Thatcher’s death. We’ve lost a great leader, a great prime minister, and a great Briton.” He also said: “As our first woman prime minister, Margaret Thatcher succeeded against all the odds. She didn’t just lead our country, she saved our country, and I believe she will be remembered as the greatest British peacetime prime minister.”

President Barack Obama said in a statement: “Here in America, many of us will never forget her standing together with President Reagan, showing the world that we are not just moved by history – we can shape it with strong beliefs, courage, and determination.”

Lady Thatcher was the first woman elected to lead a major western country. She served as prime minister for 11 years without a break, the longest since 1827.

Thatcher, who was 87, had been in poor health for several years and suffered from dementia. After several small strokes in 2002, she left public life and could no longer make the sharp comments she was known for.

Her death brought tributes from all political sides.

The Labour Party said it would stop campaigning in local elections to show respect. Its leader, Ed Miliband, said: “She will be remembered as a unique figure. She changed politics for a whole generation. She was Britain’s first woman prime minister. She moved the centre of British politics and was important in the world. The Labour Party disagreed with much of what she did and she will always be a controversial figure. But we can disagree and still respect her political achievements and personal strength.”

Deputy prime minister Nick Clegg said: “Margaret Thatcher was one of the most important people in modern British politics. No matter what side you are on, no one can deny that she left a unique and lasting mark on the country.”

Former Conservative prime minister Sir John Major called her a political phenomenon and said: “Her main qualities will always be remembered by those who worked with her: courage and determination in politics, and kindness and generosity in private.”

The “Iron Lady” was a strong ally of US president Ronald Reagan during the last years of the Cold War against the Soviet Union, which broke up under reforms led by Mikhail Gorbachev, a Soviet leader Thatcher said she could “do business” with. Because of this, many people in former Soviet countries saw her as a brave supporter of their freedom, a view shared by many in the US, but not always at home or in the European Union.

Thatcher was not well known in her party until she surprisingly became leader in 1975. Within ten years, she was famous around the world, both admired and disliked, for her support of free markets and her tough foreign policy, including her long fight with the IRA, who almost killed her with a bomb at the Grand Hotel in Brighton in 1984.

In Britain, Thatcherism meant selling state-owned industries to private owners – the word “privatization” became common in many countries – and defeating strong trade unions, especially the National Union of Miners, whose year-long strike from 1984 to 1985 was very bitter and difficult.

With new money from Britain’s North Sea oil, Thatcher was able to change the old industrial economy and defeat her enemies, including moderate members of her own party.

She was also known for her strong arguments in the European Union to get a British rebate, which she called “my money.” She was less successful in stopping the European Commission, which she called the “Belgian Empire,” especially when it was led by French socialist Jacques Delors.

Her supporters in the tabloid newspapers encouraged her. As the British economy recovered from a deep recession caused by her strict economic policies to control unions and inflation, she seemed unbeatable for a short time.

But with more power and the loss of allies who had balanced her, she made mistakes and became less popular. When her deputy, Sir Geoffrey Howe, finally disagreed with her, mainly over Europe, his powerful resignation speech led to a leadership challenge. Thatcher stepped down for John Major instead of risking losing to him in a vote.

After retiring, she wrote two successful memoirs and worked hard for the Thatcher Foundation, which tried to spread her ideas around the world.

When the children at a primary school in Stirling hear the words “daily mile,” they stop what they are doing and go outside to run or walk laps around the school field. For three and a half years, all students at St Ninian’s Primary have walked or run a mile every day. They do this at different times during the day, and they seem happy to do it. Even though childhood obesity is rising in the UK, none of the children at this school are overweight.

The daily mile has helped the children become fitter, behave better, and concentrate more in class. Because of this, many nursery and primary schools across Britain are now doing the same thing. They ask students to leave their desks for 15 minutes each day to walk or run around the school or a nearby park.

Elaine Wyllie, the headteacher of St Ninian’s, said, “I get at least two emails a day from other schools and local authorities asking how we do it. It is amazing to think that children across the country are running every day because of something we started.”

According to the Health & Social Care Information Centre, one in ten children are obese when they start school at age four or five. In the summer of 2015, a study showed that schoolchildren in England are less fit than ever before. Because of this, primary schools have quickly noticed the benefits of the daily mile. Schools in London, Gateshead, Wales, and other parts of Scotland have started the daily mile, and more plan to begin during the 2015-2016 school year. In Stirling alone, 30 schools have already started or will soon start the daily mile.

Wyllie said, “It’s a simple and free way to help children get fit. The most important thing is that the children really enjoy it; otherwise, it would not last. They come back looking happy and healthy, like children used to look. It’s wonderful to see.” At St Ninian’s, teachers take students out for their daily mile on a special track around the school field whenever it fits best in the day’s schedule. Only ice or very heavy rain stops them.

Researchers from Stirling University have started a study to find scientific proof of the physical, mental, and emotional benefits of the daily mile. Dr Colin Moran, who leads the study, said, “The children at St Ninian’s do not seem to have problems with obesity; they seem happier, and staff say they settle into lessons faster. So we designed a study to test all these things. There are many stories about the benefits, but there are no scientific facts yet.” The study will compare St Ninian’s students with children from another school in Stirling that has not started the daily mile.

Kevin Clelland, a primary school teacher from Leeds, visited St Ninian’s before telling his colleagues it was a great idea. He said, “It’s such a simple thing to do but seems to have a big impact. We are really committed to improving our students’ fitness beyond the two hours of PE we are required to give.” His school is now building a track.

Active Cheshire, a group that works to improve sports and fitness in Cheshire and Warrington, is taking local leaders to Scotland to see the results of the daily mile. If a test run is successful, they hope to start the daily mile in all 450 schools in the region.

Paralympian Tanni Grey-Thompson, chair of ukactive, the UK’s main health group for physical activity, said, “All children need to be active for 60 minutes every day, whether in lessons, walking to school, or playing outside. It’s great to see projects like the daily mile, which show real leadership from schools to improve children’s fitness and thinking skills, and make a real difference to schools, teachers, parents, and young people’s lives. We know sitting still is bad for health; moving helps children build skills for life.”

The Scottish government also supports the daily mile. A spokesperson said, “Learning in PE is better with projects like the daily mile, which can help parents encourage healthy habits in their children from a young age. We are happy to see so many Scottish schools taking part or planning to do so.”

Canadian tennis player Frank Dancevic criticized the Australian Open organizers for making players play in very hot and unsafe conditions after he collapsed on the court when the temperature reached 41°C. Dancevic fainted during the second set of his first-round match against France’s Benoît Paire on an uncovered court at Melbourne Park. He was unconscious for about a minute. He said the conditions were clearly dangerous for players. He also said the heat made him see things that were not real: “I felt dizzy from the middle of the first set and then I saw Snoopy. I thought, ‘Wow, Snoopy – that’s strange.’”

Dancevic said, “I think it’s inhumane. It’s not fair to anyone – not to the players, not to the fans, not to the sport – when you see players quitting matches or fainting.” He added, “I have played five-set matches all my life, but after just one and a half sets, I passed out from heat stroke. That’s not normal. Many players are having problems and telling the tournament it’s too hot to play. But until someone dies, they keep playing matches in this heat. I don’t think it’s fair, and I know many players agree with me.”

Other players agreed. British number one Andy Murray said, “It’s something you have to think about. Even if people say the conditions are safe, it only takes one bad thing to happen. It looks bad for the sport when players, ball kids, and fans are collapsing. That’s not good. When I went out to practice before my match, the conditions at 2:30–3:00 pm were very, very hard. I don’t know if it’s safe. In other sports, players have had heart attacks.”

Caroline Wozniacki said, “I put my water bottle on the court and it started to melt a little under the plastic. So you know it was hot.”

John Isner, who stopped his first-round match because of a right ankle injury, said, “It was like opening an oven when the potatoes are done. That’s what it felt like.”

Defending champion Victoria Azarenka said, “It felt very hot, like you’re dancing in a frying pan or something like that.”

The tournament’s “extreme heat” plan was used for women’s matches on Tuesday, giving an extra ten-minute break between the second and third sets. In 2014, the rules changed so that the tournament director, Wayne McKewen, decides whether to stop matches. Instead of just using the temperature, organizers use the Wet Bulb Globe Temperature, which also measures humidity and wind to see how the weather feels. Organizers said the temperature reached 42.2°C on Tuesday evening, but conditions never reached the level where play would be stopped. McKewen said, “We have to reach a minimum level and have a forecast that it will last for a reasonable time. That didn’t happen. While it was hot and uncomfortable, the low humidity meant play could continue.”

Dancevic, who said he felt dizzy from the middle of the second set, continued playing after getting medical help but lost the match 7–6, 6–3, 6–4. He said, “I was really close to stopping. I wasn’t running much at the end. I wasn’t tired; I just felt my body temperature was too high.”

A ball boy also needed medical help after collapsing during Milos Raonic’s 7–6, 6–1, 4–6, 6–2 win over Daniel Gimeno-Traver on another uncovered court. The tournament then made ball boys work shorter, 45-minute shifts. China’s Peng Shuai said the heat made her cramp and vomit, and she had to be helped off the court after losing 7–5, 4–6, 6–3 to Japan’s Kurumi Nara. Officials said the health risks were not serious, and most matches finished without medical problems.

Tim Wood, the tournament’s chief medical officer, said, “Of course, a few players had heat-related problems or felt uncomfortable, but none needed serious medical help after their match.”

Most players, like Roger Federer, said that even though the conditions were tough, they were the same for both players. Federer said, “It’s just a mental thing. If you have trained hard enough and believe you can do it, you can get through it. If you can’t handle it, you give up.”

Dancevic disagreed. He said, “I don’t think it’s about how fit the players are. Some players are used to the heat – their bodies can handle it, but others can’t. It’s dangerous to be out there. It’s been an hour and a half since my match and I still can’t pee.”

Sir Alex Ferguson will retire as Manchester United manager at the end of this season, after 27 years in charge. He is the most successful manager in British football history. After retiring, he will become a director and ambassador for Manchester United. The club now needs to find someone to replace him. Ferguson has won 13 English Premier League titles, two Champions Leagues, the Cup Winners’ Cup, five FA Cups, and four League Cups.

Ferguson said, “I have thought a lot about retiring and it was not an easy decision. But now is the right time. I wanted to leave the club in a strong position, and I believe I have done that. The team that just won the league is very good, with a good mix of young and older players, so the club can continue to be successful. The youth system is strong, so the club’s future looks bright.

“Our training facilities are some of the best in the world, and Old Trafford is one of the top stadiums. I am happy to become a director and ambassador for the club. I also have many other interests, so I am looking forward to the future. I want to thank my family for their love and support, especially my wife Cathy. She has always been there for me and helped me a lot. I cannot say enough how much this means to me.

“I also want to thank all my players and staff, past and present. Their hard work and professionalism helped us win many trophies. Without them, the club’s history would not be as rich. In my early years, the board and especially Sir Bobby Charlton supported me and gave me time to build not just a team, but a whole football club.

“In the last ten years, the Glazer family gave me the chance to manage Manchester United as well as I could. I was also lucky to work with a talented and trustworthy chief executive, David Gill. I am very grateful to all of them. To the fans, thank you. Your support over the years has been amazing. It has been an honour and a great privilege to be your manager, and I have loved my time at Manchester United.”

Ferguson’s retirement was sudden, but he had once said he would retire after the 2001/2 season before changing his mind. On Wednesday morning, he called the players into the changing room after they arrived for training and told them he was stepping down. He then spoke to his backroom staff and later to the rest of the staff in the canteen.

Joel Glazer, one of the club’s owners, said, “Alex has shown many times what a great manager he is, but he is also a wonderful person. His hard work and dedication to the club are amazing. I will always remember the great moments he gave us, like the special night in Moscow.”

Avie Glazer, his brother, said, “I am happy to say that Alex will stay with the club as a director. His work over the last 27 years has been incredible, and like all United fans, I want him to be part of the club’s future.”

David Gill, the outgoing chief executive, said, “I have had the great pleasure of working closely with Alex for 16 unforgettable years – through many trophy wins and signings. We knew he would retire one day, so we have been planning for it by making sure the team and club are in great shape. Alex’s vision, energy, and skill have built teams on and off the field that his successor can rely on as some of the best and most loyal in the world.

“He cares deeply for the club, his staff, and the football family. This is something I admire and have seen myself over the last 16 years. What he has done for this club and for football will never be forgotten. Working with Alex has been the best experience of my career, and I am honoured to call him a friend.”

First-team coach René Meulensteen explained how Ferguson told the staff on Wednesday morning. “I found out this morning when I came to the club,” he said. “He called us into his office and told us his decision. There are always rumours every season, but the manager kept it secret. I think he felt now was the right time and made his choice.

“He is a man who thinks very carefully, so I am sure he thought a lot about this. I wish him well. He has been fantastic for this club, and I hope the fans support the next manager as much as they supported him.”

Lego’s profits went up a lot in the first half of 2014, helped by the success of The Lego Movie, which was very popular in cinemas in the US and UK.

The Danish toy company’s sales increased in Europe, the Americas, and Asia because children bought many products connected to the film. The movie, which came out in February, made more than $250 million in the US and £31 million in the UK by the first weekend of April.

The movie cost about $60 million to make and is seen as a very good example of content marketing, because it entertains people and also encourages them to buy Lego products.

Lego’s finance director, John Goodwin, said: “The strong sales of Lego Movie products helped us in the first half of 2014, and we will see how sales continue when the movie comes out on DVD in the second half of 2014.”

Lego’s operating profit for the first six months of the year went up by 12% to $630 million. Sales increased by 11%, which is more than three times higher than six years ago.

Jørgen Vig Knudstorp, Lego’s chief executive, said: “This is a very good result that shows our big growth in recent years, even though the economy is difficult. The result for the first half of 2014 shows that we can develop, launch, and sell Lego products that children all over the world really want.”

Lego, which is based in the small town of Billund, started making its plastic bricks in 1949 and became a popular children’s toy around the world by the 1970s. But the company had problems and almost failed in 2003. Knudstorp became chief executive, ending 70 years of family leadership, and removed hundreds of extra products to focus again on the famous Lego bricks.

In April, the company opened its first factory in China and also opened an office in Shanghai to help it grow in the world’s second-biggest economy.

He liked the things that most millionaires like. He owned a gold and silver Rolex watch and many expensive cars. He enjoyed buying modern art. But even though this Chinese businessman had several companies and a large, fancy house in the suburbs of Madrid, he had almost no money in the bank. This made Spanish authorities suspicious.

Gao Ping, who spent most of his adult life in Spain, controlled the supply to 4,000 Chinese shops across Spain. Authorities thought he was not paying taxes on the clothes, furniture, and other goods he brought from China.

In 2012, when police searched his warehouses, they found piles of cash: bundles of €100, €200, and €500 notes tied with rubber bands. Police took away about €12 million in trolleys. This was the biggest cash seizure ever by Spanish police. The group, with Gao as the suspected leader, is accused of laundering up to €300 million a year, selling fake goods, and selling toys with fake safety marks. The government prosecutor said Gao’s illegal business was so big that it was hurting Spain’s economy. Gao is out on bail, and the case has not gone to trial yet.

Police have worried about €500 notes for a long time. These notes are small and easy to carry, but worth a lot of money. Criminals, tax evaders, and drug dealers like to use them. For example, €1 million in €500 notes can fit in a small laptop bag, but the same amount in €50 notes would need a small suitcase.
