Some people have even swallowed the notes after folding them into plastic pellets. Others hide the notes inside car parts.

The UK stopped giving out €500 notes in 2010 because most people who wanted them were criminals. In 2009, Italy’s central bank warned that mafia and terrorists used these notes. Other countries have also limited high-value notes because of crime. For example, Canada stopped its $1,000 note in 2000 after police advice.

Now, with electronic payments and contactless cards, more people are asking if we still need these big notes. Peter Sands, the former head of Standard Chartered Bank, wants to get rid of high-value notes like the €500, the $100, the 1,000 Swiss Franc note, and the £50. In a report for Harvard Kennedy School, Sands said it is time to stop printing these notes because they help criminals avoid taxes, commit financial crimes, fund terrorism, and do corruption. He said that if criminals had to use smaller notes, gold, or diamonds, it would be harder for them to hide and easier for police to catch them.

At a conference in London, Rob Wainwright, the head of Europol, asked the European Central Bank (ECB) to think about whether it should keep making and using these notes, since they help criminals and terrorists hide their money and fund illegal activities. According to Europol, the €500 note makes up 30% of the value of all euro notes, even though most people have never seen one.

The €500 note was introduced in 2002 when the euro started. It replaced other high-value notes like the 1,000 Deutschmark, the 10,000 Belgian franc, and the 500,000 Italian lira. Many European countries liked high-value notes. Pia Hüttl, a researcher at the Bruegel thinktank, says this is because cash is cheaper to use and accepted everywhere.

Cash is still very popular in Germany and Austria, where more than half of all payments are made with cash. Hans-Jürgen Papier, the former president of Germany’s constitutional court, said that limiting cash goes against personal freedom. The German newspaper Bild started a petition to protect cash, including the €500 note, saying “hands off my cash.”

Police are not so sure, as they keep finding suspicious bundles of cash. In one case, two men tried to deposit €200,000 in torn and dirty €500 notes at a bank. In the same week, €1.3 million in €500 notes was found hidden in a suitcase with a false bottom. But just suspecting a crime is not enough to arrest people. Jennifer MacLeod, a financial crime expert at Europol, said it is hard to prove a link between suspicious cash and crime. It is even harder because of time limits and poor cooperation between countries.

Europol wants central banks to take more responsibility for strange uses of €500 notes. For example, in 2013, Luxembourg gave out more than twice its yearly GDP in banknotes, even though people there do not use much cash. Europol asked Luxembourg’s central bank why this happened. The bank said it just gives out the notes people ask for and does not know why people want them. MacLeod said she was surprised that the central bank did not feel responsible.

This may be changing. Mario Draghi, the head of the ECB, said he does not want the money the bank makes from these notes to help criminals. Other ECB leaders, like Yves Mersch, say there is no proof that the €500 note is used for crime. But, because of more worries about terrorism, this argument may not work anymore. EU finance ministers have asked for a report on possible limits on high-value notes by May 1, 2016.

McDonald’s is not only the world’s biggest burger chain, but also a symbol of American consumer culture. However, the famous golden arches are not as popular as before. After many years of growth, fewer people around the world are enjoying McDonald’s. The company announced that global sales dropped by 3.3% compared to 2013, and the results were called terrible.

McDonald’s is facing problems in many places. In China, sales fell by 23% after a food safety scare. Local media showed workers at a supplier saying they used old beef and chicken for McDonald’s and KFC. In Europe, sales dropped by 4%, mainly because of the conflict in Ukraine and anti-Western feelings in Russia. In Russia, about 200 out of 450 McDonald’s restaurants are being checked by health inspectors, possibly for political reasons. Ten restaurants have been closed.

The biggest problem is in the US, where McDonald’s has about 40% of its restaurants. Almost 60 years after Ray Kroc opened the first McDonald’s in Illinois, Americans are losing interest in Big Macs and fries. McDonald’s has had 12 months in a row of falling sales in the US, with a 4.1% drop in the latest quarter. Young people are choosing other places like Chipotle Mexican Grill. The number of 19-to-21-year-olds visiting McDonald’s once a month has dropped by 13% since 2011, and the number of 22-to-37-year-olds has not increased.

McDonald’s hamburgers were recently voted the worst in America by over 32,000 people. They preferred burgers from Five Guys, Smashburger, or Fuddruckers. Chick-fil-A was chosen as the best for chicken. Many people also think McDonald’s food is less healthy than its competitors, especially Chipotle, which advertises antibiotic-free meat and “locally sourced, seasonal produce,” even though “local” can mean up to 350 miles away.

Many US customers do not trust McDonald’s. In October, the company started a website to answer questions about its food. People asked if McDonald’s used “pink slime” (a beef filler made from gristle and fat, treated with ammonia) in its burgers. This product, banned in Europe, was stopped by McDonald’s in 2012. But the issue still worries customers. Someone else asked if McDonald’s beef contains worms (“No. Gross. End of story,” the company replied). Others wanted to know if McDonald’s uses real eggs or if the McRib is made with the same plastic as yoga mats. McDonald’s CEO Don Thompson admitted the company needs to fix misunderstandings about the freshness and quality of its ingredients.

At the same time, McDonald’s is losing customers who want fresher and healthier food, and it is also losing its reputation for fast, cheap service. Since adding $2 items to its dollar menu, people think McDonald’s is more expensive than other fast-food places, and many complain that service is slower.

Mary Chapman from Technomic said the “expensive” label is not fair. Prices at McDonald’s have gone up by 4.8% since 2009, which is less than the average increase for other fast-food chains (19.4%). “Fast casual” places like Chipotle have raised prices by 16.9%. US consumer prices overall rose 11% in the same period.

However, critics are right about longer waiting times. McDonald’s menu is bigger and more complicated than some competitors. For example, the chicken McWrap takes 60 seconds to make. Chapman said, “I think it is worth waiting, but the person behind me who wants a double cheeseburger for a dollar might not.”

In the UK, McDonald’s has improved its business and is doing well. A better breakfast menu, improved coffee, and free wi-fi have made McDonald’s more popular in Britain. Peter Martin from CGA Peach said 56% of British adults have visited McDonald’s at least once in the last six months.

McDonald’s leaders promise to fix misunderstandings about its food in the US. Thompson said the company will offer more organic food and custom-made burgers, but also wants to make the menu simpler to reduce waiting times. Experts are unsure how McDonald’s can offer both simpler menus and more choices for customers.

Mark Kalinowski from Janney Capital Markets said, “They want to simplify the menu but also let people customize their food, and that sounds difficult.” Only four out of 14,000 US McDonald’s restaurants have tested “build your own burger,” so it is unclear how this could work in all locations. “Right now, we are not sure; we want to see more details,” he said.

Even though sales are falling, McDonald’s is still opening new restaurants around the world. By the end of 2014, it expects to have 1,400 new locations. Kalinowski thinks McDonald’s market share will keep getting smaller, but he also said not to count the company out. “You can never really count McDonald’s out. We think it will be number one in total sales for not just years but decades to come.”

How close are we to a world where drones deliver packages? Amazon says it will happen soon, but others are not so sure. The problem is not just about new inventions; it is also about public safety.

Paul Misener, Amazon’s vice-president of global public policy, told Congress that Amazon will be ready when all the rules are made. However, he did not give details, except for joking that a basket of fresh fruit was being delivered to a congressman to show the technology works.

The Federal Aviation Authority (FAA) will have rules for commercial drones by June 2016. But the technology still needs to improve, and bigger drones are not allowed yet. Only drones up to 25kg will be included in the new rules. The FAA also says that if many drones are flying, they must use different radio frequencies so that no one can block or take control of them.

Professor Sajiv Singh from Carnegie Mellon University, who runs a company called NearEarth, said that flying a modern drone is like giving it simple instructions: go to this height, do a short task, then return home. But even short flights from a moving landing pad are difficult to organize.

He explained, “They want to deliver from a warehouse to the customer, who is probably in a city or suburb. There will be dangers along the way that the drone must see and avoid. There might be things on the ground that are not on the map, like new construction equipment. Sometimes GPS signals are blocked, so the drone might not know where it is.” He said these problems can be solved, but it is hard. One big problem is keeping radio contact with the drone and planning what to do if contact is lost. Roboticist Daniel Huber said, “If you use a normal drone, it will just keep going and crash if it loses contact.”

This problem is not hard for engineers to fix, but the solution is not yet standard in the industry.

Jay McConville from Lockheed Martin said, “You can’t do everything with a 25kg drone.” Lockheed Martin is working to make drone controls easier to use. He said, “People who fly drones want to see important information and video on their devices, not control every small detail.” Daniel Huber said, “Most of the technology needed is already here.”

Huber is working on a program that uses drones to check things like pipelines, telephone lines, and bridges. “We made a system where you draw a box on a map, and the drone flies around that area by itself and checks everything, then reports back,” he said.

Huber also said about Amazon’s plan, “Many packages are light. A drone can carry one kilogram for 15 minutes. If you have a base in a neighborhood, the drone can deliver from there. Most drones can fly for about 15 minutes.” This helps keep people safe, because bigger drones are more dangerous. Huber said that some delivery problems are being solved in exciting ways. At a recent conference, a company called SkyCatch showed a drone that could take off and land by itself, and when its battery was low, it landed, changed its battery, and took off again.

Safety is still a big worry. Singh said that for a commercial plane to be safe, it must have only one serious failure every 1 million hours. Drones are still far from this goal. For example, the Reaper drone fails once every 10,000 hours. A small problem like an oil leak does not count as a serious failure; something must actually fall from the sky. Singh said, “We are getting closer. There is a lot of interest.”

Air travel is always risky, so safety standards are very high. Singh said, “If you fly on a commercial airline, sometimes they say, ‘A part failed, we have to go back to the gate.’ And that’s in an industry with 60 years of experience! I worry that a drone could fall on a busy road.” Singh said part of the answer is to have good backup plans: “If something goes wrong, the drone must do something safe.”

Angry waiters are asking the public to support them in keeping their tips. Protesters will target PizzaExpress restaurants to try to stop the company from taking part of the tips that staff get from credit and debit card payments. Campaigners have also started an online petition, hoping that customers will support their demands.

PizzaExpress keeps 8p out of every £1 given as a tip by card, calling it an admin fee. This policy has made some workers very upset. PizzaExpress has 430 restaurants in the UK and is popular with families. The union Unite says the company makes about £1 million a year from this practice.

Chantal Chegrinec, a campaigns officer at Unite, said, “We think this 8% fee is unfair. If the company values its staff, it should give them all the tips customers leave.” She also said that PizzaExpress is not the only company doing this, and Unite will look at other companies next.

Local Unite branches are organizing protests, starting at the British Museum PizzaExpress in London. The union has also written to the company’s CEO, Richard Hodgson. Unite started the campaign after asking its PizzaExpress members about their concerns, especially after the company was sold to a Chinese private equity firm, Hony Capital, in 2014. One of the main problems was the 8% taken from their tips.

One unhappy PizzaExpress worker, who wants to stay anonymous, said the admin fee costs her £3 every night. She wrote to Unite, “I have worked at PizzaExpress for 15 years. I still only get the national minimum wage of £6.50 an hour. My coworkers and I depend on tips to increase our low pay. I work hard, but when PizzaExpress takes a percentage of our tips left on a card, I get upset.”

PizzaExpress is not alone. Other restaurant chains like Ask and Zizzi also take 8% of card tips. Some chains take even more: Café Rouge, Bella Italia, Belgo, Strada, and Giraffe (owned by Tesco) all take 10%.

A PizzaExpress spokesperson said the admin fee pays for running a “tronc,” which is a system to share tips among staff. She said, “We worked hard to set up this tronc system. It is managed by a troncmaster and a committee of waiters and pizza makers, who decide how card tips are shared between front and back of house. It is a system run by employees for employees.”

PizzaExpress sells 29 million pizzas a year in the UK. The company says it does not make a profit from the admin fee. However, some other restaurant groups do not take any admin fee from tips. Wagamama, Pizza Hut, and TGI Friday do not take anything. The Restaurant Group, which owns Frankie & Benny’s, Chiquitos, and Garfunkels, used to take 10% but stopped this policy years ago.

Unite recently protested at ten PizzaExpress restaurants in south London, giving leaflets to customers who were “shocked and disgusted” by the practice. PizzaExpress says the admin fee is mentioned in small print at the bottom of its menus, but the worker who wrote to Unite said customers are always surprised when she tells them. Most then choose to leave tips in cash. Almost 6,000 people have signed Unite’s online petition so far.

One waiter, who does not work for PizzaExpress but has worked for another restaurant chain for 11 years, said that at least a third of his income comes from tips. He does not want to give his name because he is afraid of losing his job. He said, “I work in a busy London restaurant. On an average night, I serve 150 people and get £40 to £50 in tips. That sounds like a lot, but it is very important to me because my basic pay is only £6.50 an hour.”

Conservative MP Andrew Percy wants to change the law so restaurant staff have more control over their tips. He said he will talk about this issue in parliament after the summer break.

The National Security Agency (NSA) has gained direct access to the systems of Google, Facebook, Apple, and other large US internet companies, according to a top-secret document. This access is part of a secret program called PRISM. PRISM lets officials collect information such as search history, email content, file transfers, and live chats.

The Guardian has confirmed that the document is real. It is a 41-slide PowerPoint presentation marked as top secret and not to be shared with foreign allies. The presentation was used to train intelligence workers on how PRISM works. The document says the NSA collects data directly from the servers of major US companies. The presentation also claims that the companies help with the program, but all the companies that responded said they did not know about PRISM.

Google said in a statement: “Google cares a lot about the security of our users’ data. We only give user data to the government when the law requires it, and we check all requests carefully. Sometimes people say we have created a secret way for the government to access our systems, but Google does not have such a back door.”

Several top technology company leaders said they did not know about PRISM or any similar program. They said they would never take part in such a program. One said, “If they are doing this, they are doing it without our knowledge.” An Apple spokesperson said he had “never heard” of PRISM.

The NSA was able to get this access because of changes to US surveillance law. These changes started under President Bush and were renewed under President Obama in December 2012. The program allows the government to watch live communications and stored information in detail. The law lets the government target any customers of these companies who live outside the US, or Americans who communicate with people outside the US. It also means that sometimes communications inside the US can be collected without a warrant.

The news about PRISM came after The Guardian reported on a secret court order that forced Verizon, a phone company, to give the government the phone records of millions of US customers. The involvement of internet companies in PRISM will increase the debate about how much the government is watching people. Unlike the collection of phone records, PRISM can include the actual content of communications, not just information about them.

Some of the world’s biggest internet companies have been part of PRISM since it started in 2007. Microsoft was the first to join in December 2007. Yahoo joined in 2008; Google, Facebook, and PalTalk in 2009; YouTube in 2010; Skype and AOL in 2011; and Apple in 2012. The program is still growing, with more companies expected to join. Together, these companies cover most online email, search, video, and communication services. The type and amount of data collected from each company is different. Companies must follow US law and give user data when asked, but PRISM lets the NSA access the companies’ servers directly. The NSA document says the operations have the “assistance of communications providers in the US.”

This news also supports concerns from some US senators who, during the renewal of the FISA Amendments Act (FAA) in December 2012, warned that the law could allow too much surveillance and did not have enough safeguards. When the FAA was first made, supporters said the NSA could not get electronic communications without the companies’ agreement. But PRISM makes that agreement unnecessary, because it lets the NSA take communications directly from the companies’ servers.

A chart in the NSA document shows the wide range of data the NSA can get: emails, video and voice chats, videos, photos, Skype calls, file transfers, social network details, and more. The document is from April 2013. Such a leak is very rare for the NSA, which is known for being very secret.

PRISM lets the NSA, the world’s largest surveillance agency, get targeted communications without asking the companies or getting individual court orders. With PRISM, the NSA can go directly into the servers of the companies and get both stored and live communications from targeted users.

A senior government official said: “The Guardian and Washington Post articles talk about collecting communications under Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA). This law does not allow targeting any US citizen or anyone inside the United States. The program is watched over by the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court, the Executive Branch, and Congress. There are strict rules, approved by the court, to make sure only non-US people outside the US are targeted, and to limit collecting, keeping, and sharing information about US people by accident.

“This program was recently approved again by Congress after many hearings and debates. The information collected under this program is some of the most important intelligence we have and is used to protect our country from many threats.”

Do you want your child to be good at sports, join the school team, and maybe even compete internationally one day? If so, try to have your future champion born in November, or if not, in October. A study by one of the UK’s top experts on children’s physical activity found that students born in these months are fitter than others in their class.

Children born in October and November were found to be fitter, stronger, and more powerful than those born in the other ten months, especially compared to children born in April or June. Dr. Gavin Sandercock from the Centre for Sports and Exercise Science at Essex University and his team found that children born in autumn had a clear physical advantage over their classmates.

The research included 8,550 boys and girls aged 10 to 16 from 26 state schools in Essex. Between 2007 and 2010, all students were tested on three types of fitness: stamina, handgrip strength, and lower-body power. The results showed that the month a child is born can make a big difference in their cardiovascular fitness, muscle strength, and ability to accelerate. These are all important for being good at sports. School sports day results in the coming weeks may support these findings.

Children born in November were the fittest overall. They had the most stamina and power and were the second strongest. October-born children were almost as fit, being the strongest and third in power, with December-born children close behind.

The difference in physical ability between children in the same class but born in different months was sometimes very large. For example, a boy born in November can run at least 10% faster, jump 12% higher, and is 15% more powerful than a boy of the same age born in April. Dr. Sandercock said this is a huge physical advantage. Such differences could decide who becomes a top athlete, because selection for elite sports often depends on small differences in performance.

The study, published in the International Journal of Sports Medicine, found that when all three fitness scores were combined, children born in April were the least fit, followed by those born in June. Dr. Sandercock said this could mean these children are left out of school teams and do not do as well in sports.

The findings suggest that children born early in the school year have a double “autumn advantage.” They are already known to do better academically, and now they also seem to be better at sports. The results show that something more than just being older in the school year is helping, because the fittest children were not the tallest or heaviest.

The researchers believe that children born in autumn get more vitamin D from the sun during the last months of pregnancy, which could explain their better fitness. Vitamin D is known as the “sunshine vitamin” and is linked to many health benefits. John Steele, head of the Youth Sport Trust, said that a good start in PE and sport at school is also very important for a child’s sporting development. Children who have a good first experience in PE develop better agility, balance, and coordination, and are more likely to enjoy and do well in sports as they grow up.

UK Sport could not say if more of the 1,300 athletes it supports in 47 sports were born in November and October. Natalie Dunman, head of performance pathways at UK Sport, said that while these differences are seen in teenagers at junior competitions, they disappear by the time athletes compete as adults. She said that many things are important for becoming a champion, and their work has not found that month of birth is a key factor.

The last time Kate Bush performed on stage, the first mobile phones were just being tested. Now, thirty-five years later, she is performing again in a very different world. Today, most concerts are full of people using phones and tablets, but Bush wants to change this. She does not want fans to watch her shows through their screens.

Before her much-awaited concerts at the Hammersmith Apollo in London, Bush asked her fans not to use their phones during her shows. On her website, she wrote: “I have a request for everyone coming to the shows. We chose a small, intimate theatre instead of a big stadium. It would mean a lot to me if you do not take photos or videos during the shows. I want to connect with you as an audience, not with your phones or cameras. I know it’s a big request, but it will help us all enjoy the experience together.”

Bush is known for her dramatic shows and beautiful costumes. She may also want to keep her concerts a surprise for the thousands of fans who bought tickets for her 22 shows, and not have poor-quality videos appear on YouTube.

Bush is not the first artist to complain about phones at concerts. Many musicians have told their fans not to watch live music through their screens. Roger Daltrey, the lead singer of The Who, recently said it was strange that people come to concerts but spend their time looking at their phones instead of the artist. He said, “I feel sorry for them. If you’re looking at life through a screen, you’re only half there. It’s weird.”

In 2013, Beyoncé told a fan off for filming her at a concert. She said, “You can’t even sing because you’re too busy filming. I’m right in front of you. Enjoy the moment. Put that camera down!”

The argument about phones at live events is not just about music. Sports fans also talk about it. Recently, Dutch football fans at PSV Eindhoven protested against wi-fi in their stadium. They held signs saying, “No wi-fi. Support the team,” “You can sit at home,” and “Stand united.” Manchester United also told fans not to bring large electronic devices and banned filming on tablets this season.

Jarvis Cocker has said that people using phones at concerts drives him “crazy.” He said, “It seems silly to watch something happening in front of you on a small screen.”

Johnny Marr said in 2013 that fans miss the real feeling of live music when they are busy recording it. He said, “If you just watch through your phone, you waste the chance to enjoy the concert. I don’t want to be rude, but you should put your phone down and enjoy the show. Concerts are about being with other people and enjoying the moment, not watching it on a small screen.”

The band Yeah Yeah Yeahs put up a sign at one of their shows asking fans to put away their devices. The sign said: “Please do not watch the show through a screen. Put it away to be polite to the person behind you and to the band.”

Even in classical music, this is a problem. In June 2013, famous pianist Krystian Zimerman left the stage because someone was filming him on a smartphone. He came back and said, “YouTube is destroying music.”

However, Sam Watt from Vyclone, a phone app that lets people film concerts and then mixes the videos together, said that artists cannot stop people from filming. He believes filming makes the concert experience better, not worse. He said, “Fans filming is now part of concerts. Our app lets people upload their videos, and then we mix them together to make great content. We think filming adds to the experience. If Kate Bush talked with us, maybe we could change her mind. People want to keep memories, so it’s important to accept filming at concerts.”

Top water scientists have given a strong warning about the world’s food supply. They say that by 2050, most people may need to eat almost only vegetarian food to avoid very serious food shortages.

Right now, people get about 20% of their protein from animal products, but this might need to go down to just 5% to feed the extra two billion people expected by 2050. This is according to research from leading water scientists.

The report from Malik Falkenmark and his team at the Stockholm International Water Institute (SIWI) says, “There will not be enough water on current farmland to grow enough food for the expected nine billion people in 2050 if we keep eating like people in western countries.” The report also says, “There will be just enough water if animal-based foods are only 5% of total calories, and if regions with not enough water can get food through reliable trade.”

Warnings about water shortages affecting food come as Oxfam and the UN prepare for a possible second global food crisis in five years. Prices for important foods like corn and wheat have gone up almost 50% since June because of bad droughts in the US and Russia, and weak monsoon rains in Asia. Over 18 million people in the Sahel region already face serious food shortages.

Oxfam says that the rise in food prices will badly affect developing countries that depend on food imports, such as parts of Latin America, North Africa, and the Middle East. In 2008, food shortages caused unrest in 28 countries.

The scientists say that eating a vegetarian diet is one way to save water and grow more food as the climate becomes more unpredictable. Foods high in animal protein use five to ten times more water than vegetarian foods. One third of the world’s farmland is used to grow crops to feed animals. Other ways to feed people include reducing food waste and increasing food trade between countries with extra food and those without enough.

The scientists also said, “Nine hundred million people already go hungry and two billion are malnourished, even though food production per person is still going up. With 70% of all water used in farming, growing more food for two billion more people by 2050 will put even more pressure on water and land.”

The report is being released at the start of the annual world water conference in Stockholm, Sweden. Here, 2,500 politicians, UN groups, non-governmental organizations, and researchers from 120 countries are meeting to talk about global water problems.

The scientists say that competition for water between food and other uses will increase pressure on important resources. “The UN says we must increase food production by 70% by the middle of the century. This will put more pressure on our already stressed water resources, especially since we also need more water for energy, which is expected to rise by 60% in the next 30 years, and to make electricity for the 1.3 billion people who do not have it,” the report says.

Overeating, undernourishment, and food waste are all increasing, and making more food in the future may be limited by water shortages.

“We will need a new way to feed the world in the future,” said Anders Jägerskog, the report’s editor.

A different report from the International Water Management Institute (IWMI) says the best way to protect millions of farmers in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia from food insecurity is to help them buy small pumps and simple technology, instead of building expensive, large irrigation systems.

Dr. Colin Chartres, the Director General, said, “We have seen many times what happens to the world’s poor—most of whom depend on farming and already suffer from water shortages—when they are affected by our weak global food system.”

He added, “Farmers in developing countries are increasingly using and benefiting from small, local water solutions. These methods could increase crop yields by up to 300% and add tens of billions of US dollars to household incomes in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia.”

Cities do not usually move to a new place, but that is what Kiruna, a town in northern Sweden, must do to avoid sinking into the ground. Kiruna is in the Arctic and has about 23,000 people. The city is moving because a huge iron-ore mine under the town is making the ground unsafe.

Krister Lindstedt, from the architecture firm White in Stockholm, says it is a difficult choice. If the mine stops working, many people will lose their jobs. If the city does not move, it will be destroyed. The city was started in 1900 by the state-owned mining company LK. Kiruna became rich because of the iron ore, but now the mine is causing problems for the town. Deputy Mayor Niklas Siren says the town only exists because of the mine.

Kiruna is 145 kilometers inside the Arctic Circle. The winters are very cold, with no sunlight and temperatures below -15°C. Still, the large amount of iron ore has kept people living there. The mine is the biggest underground iron-ore mine in the world. It produces 90% of all the iron in Europe, enough to build more than six Eiffel Towers every day. The demand for iron is still growing.

In 2004, the mining company told the town that the mine was getting too close. The tunnels are being dug at a 60-degree angle towards the city, and soon the ground would start to crack and buildings would collapse. Now, ten years later, cracks are appearing and getting closer to the town.

Viktoria Walldin, a social anthropologist working with the architects, says people in Kiruna have been waiting for ten years. They cannot make big decisions like buying a house, having a child, or starting a business because they do not know what will happen.

After many years, the city has made a plan. Lindstedt says the city will move slowly, like a walking insect, to a new place east of the current town. By 2033, the whole city should be safe from the mine. A new town square is already being built 3 kilometers to the east. There will be a new round town hall designed by a Danish architect. Twenty important buildings will be taken apart and rebuilt in the new town, including Kiruna’s famous red wooden church and the iron bell tower. However, not everything can be saved.

Walldin says that people will lose places that are important to them, like the bench where someone had their first kiss or the hospital where their child was born. These places are part of people’s identity, and they will disappear.

The project is called “the most democratic move in history.” The mining company is giving £320 million to build new things like a high school, fire station, community center, library, and swimming pool. But most people are worried about where they will live and how homes will be given out.

Lindstedt says these details are not decided yet. People in Kiruna are used to low rents and high incomes, but this will change. The mining company will pay people the value of their homes plus 25%, but many say this is not enough to buy a new house.

To help decide the value of homes, the architects have studied housing in nearby cities and listed what each home in Kiruna has, like space, gardens, and how close they are to bus stops or the city center. They also suggest making a “Kiruna Portal,” a place where materials from old homes can be saved and used to build new ones. But in Sweden, people do not usually build their own homes, so this idea may not work well.

The new town will look very different from the old Kiruna. The current town has many houses with gardens and winding streets. The new plan has more apartment buildings around shared courtyards and straight streets, where cold winds will blow.

The architects say this is a chance for Kiruna to become a modern, sustainable city. They hope it will attract young people with new cultural places and ideas like a cable car above the main street. But many people who live in Kiruna now may not be able to afford to live in the new town.

Collecting large amounts of telephone records through government surveillance programs is a clear threat to the privacy of normal people, according to US researchers. These researchers used simple phone records to identify people and find out private details about their lives.

With only anonymous “metadata” (information about calls and texts, but not the actual conversations), two scientists at Stanford University figured out people’s names, where they lived, and the names of their partners. But they found even more. The same data helped them discover sensitive information about some people. For example, they found out that one man owned a rifle, another had recently been told he had an irregular heartbeat, one person was pregnant, and another had multiple sclerosis.

These results show how powerful telephone metadata can be. Metadata includes the number called, the time, and the length of the call. When this information is combined with public data from websites like Google, Yelp, and Facebook, it becomes even more valuable. This kind of data is not protected by law in the same way as the content of calls and texts. Security agencies have known for a long time how useful this data is. Stewart Baker, a former lawyer for the US National Security Agency (NSA), said after Edward Snowden’s leaks: “Metadata absolutely tells you everything about somebody’s life.”

Patrick Mutchler, a computer security researcher at Stanford, said that while people collecting the data understand its power, the public does not, because there are not many studies showing how much can be learned from metadata. “That makes it hard for people who are against these programs to argue against them. Now, we have real evidence we can show,” he said.

For their study, the researchers asked 823 people to let them collect metadata from their phones using an Android app. The app also got information from their Facebook accounts, which the scientists used to check if their results were correct. In total, the researchers collected metadata from over 250,000 calls and more than 1.2 million texts.

NSA analysts who used the metadata system could look at data up to three “hops” away from a person. One hop is a call from the target person to another number. Two hops is a call from that second number to a third, and so on. Analysts could see records from the past five years. Now, the rules have changed, and they can only look two hops away and for up to 18 months.

In the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, Mutchler explained how he and another graduate student, Jonathan Mayer, found a lot of personal and sensitive information about the people in the study, even though they had little money. By using both automatic and manual searches, they found 82% of people’s names. They also found the names of businesses people called. When they put these businesses on a map, they saw groups of local businesses, which helped them guess where people lived. They correctly named the city 57% of the time and were almost 90% correct in placing people within 50 miles of their home. Mutchler thinks some mistakes happened because people did not update their Facebook page when they moved, for example, to go to college.

The scientists then looked for more personal details. By using a simple computer program to study call patterns, they guessed which people were in relationships. Once they knew someone had a partner, it was easy to find out who that person was.

In the last part of the study, the researchers tried to find out even more sensitive information from the metadata. They looked at calls to and from organizations like hospitals, pharmacies, religious groups, legal services, gun shops, and repair companies. From this, they put together some detailed stories about people’s lives.

For example, one person had a long call from a heart doctor, a short call with a medical lab, several short calls from a pharmacy, and then called a hotline for heart-rate monitors. Another person often called a gun shop that sold semi-automatic rifles and later made long calls to a gun manufacturer’s customer support. Metadata from two other people suggested one had multiple sclerosis and the other was pregnant.

“All of this shows what is possible with just two graduate students and little money,” said Mutchler. He believes these findings should make leaders think carefully before allowing mass surveillance programs. “Large-scale metadata surveillance programs, like the NSA’s, will always reveal very private information about normal people,” the scientists wrote. “To balance national security and civil rights, future laws must use information from science.”

Ross Anderson, a security engineering professor at Cambridge University, said the study gives numbers that people can now use in discussions. “With the right analysis of national communication data, you can find out a lot of sensitive information about everyone. We always thought this was true, but now we have the data.”

Angela Erdmann never met her grandfather because he died in 1946, six years before she was born. But on Tuesday, April 8, 2014, she talked about an amazing moment when she received a message in a bottle, 101 years after her grandfather had thrown it into the Baltic Sea. This bottle is believed to be the oldest message in a bottle ever found. The museum in Germany that now shows the bottle gave it to Erdmann.

“It was very surprising,” said Erdmann, who is 62 years old. She remembered how she learned about the bottle. “A man came to my door and told me he had mail from my grandfather. He said a message in a bottle had been found, and the name on the card was my grandfather’s.” The man was a family history researcher who found Erdmann in Berlin after the letter was given to the International Maritime Museum in Hamburg.

The brown beer bottle had been in the sea for 101 years. It was found by Konrad Fischer, a fisherman, while he was fishing in the Baltic Sea near Kiel. Holger von Neuhoff, who works at the museum, said this was the oldest message in a bottle he had ever seen. “There are older documents in the museum, but they were found without bottles. With both the bottle and the message, this is the oldest. It is in very good condition,” he said.

Researchers think Erdmann’s grandfather, Richard Platz, threw the bottle into the sea in 1913 when he was 20 years old and hiking with a nature group.

Most of the postcard inside the bottle could not be read, but the address in Berlin was clear. The writer also politely asked the finder to send the note to his home address.

“He also put two stamps from that time in the bottle, so the finder would not have to pay,” Erdmann said. “But he did not think it would take 101 years.”

Erdmann said she felt emotional when she got the message, even though she never knew her grandfather because he died at age 54, six years before she was born.

“I knew very little about my grandfather, but I learned he was a writer who was open-minded and believed in freedom and respect for everyone,” she said. “He helped young people and later traveled with his wife and two daughters. It was wonderful because I could see where my family came from.”

Erdmann said she is also interested in culture and traveling, just like her grandfather. She said she is open-minded too. “What he taught his daughters, my mother taught me, and I have taught my sons,” she said. Even though she was happy to get the message, she hopes people will not throw more bottles into the sea. “Today, the sea is already full of bottles and trash, so we should not add more,” she said.

The message and the bottle will be shown at Hamburg’s Maritime Museum until early May 2014. After that, experts will try to read the rest of the message. It is not known what will happen to the bottle after that, but Erdmann hopes it will stay in the museum.

“We want to put some photos with the bottle, so visitors can see the young man who threw it into the water,” she said.

The customer next to you in the line looks normal. But instead of a shopping list, you see she has handwritten notes about how the store looks and how clean it is. She is timing how fast the line moves on her phone, and you notice a small camera lens in her purse. You have probably just seen a mystery shopper.

According to the Mystery Shopping Providers Association, about 50,000 mystery shopping trips happen every month in the UK. As more people shop online, the need for mystery shoppers is increasing. Simon Boydell, a spokesman for Marketforce, which has over 300,000 mystery shoppers, says, “Retailers know that people who come to a real store want good service and a special experience they can’t get online. Our clients want to check how well their stores give that experience.”

Jill Spencer from the mystery shopping company ABa says, “We give each shopper different store locations and change them so they don’t go back to the same shop within three months. Each day, they usually spend up to eight hours visiting five to ten stores, and then another hour or two writing detailed reports about every part of their visit.” For this work, mystery shoppers can earn up to £155 a day. They also get money back for petrol and hotel stays, and are paid for car wear and tear, since they might drive up to 20,000 miles a year. Video mystery shoppers, who use a hidden camera in a buttonhole or handbag, can earn even more—about £300 a day.

Shoppers usually get back any money they spend in the stores and sometimes can keep the things they buy. Laura, a 50-year-old mystery shopper from Devon, says, “I’m usually given between £5 and £20 to spend at each store to check the service at the checkout.” The things she buys are usually linked to a service or product the store wants her to check. “I’m always given a situation, like buying something from a certain department or a new product range, but I can often choose what I want—and keep it.”

Like most full-time mystery shoppers, Laura is self-employed and takes jobs from ABa and other companies when they are available. She usually earns £30,000 to £40,000 a year, not counting all the free things she gets. “With the extra benefits, it’s enough to live on. But I don’t do it because I love shopping. In fact, I hate shopping now. When I’m not working, I don’t even want to go out to buy a pint of milk.” However, she feels good when she returns to a store she has checked before and sees that things have improved. “I know it must be because of my feedback, or why would they pay me to give it? Some stores I shop at win awards for customer service, and I think that’s because of us mystery shoppers. I feel I’m helping not just my company, but all shoppers.”

Sadly, regular mystery shopping jobs that pay like Laura’s are rare. The competition is so strong that she keeps her job a secret—even her friends and family don’t know who she works for (Laura is not her real name).

It is estimated that more than 500,000 people have signed up as mystery shoppers in the UK, but only about 10% or less get regular work each month. This has caused a big drop in pay. Val, a 51-year-old former mystery shopper, says, “Before, you got a fee, money back for your purchase, and petrol costs. Now, you often just get some money towards your purchase. I worked for 40 different companies for almost 20 years, but I stopped three years ago because I had bills to pay and very few jobs paid enough.”

Now, most mystery shopping companies use the promise of free things to attract workers. Boydell says, “Marketforce shoppers usually get a few pounds for a visit as a small thank you for their time and effort. At most, we pay £15 to £25 plus money back for a meal for two or a hotel stay. We don’t directly employ any shoppers, so we don’t have to pay them the minimum wage.”

Laura says, “I’d go on a cruise for nothing. But I think companies that pay you just a small amount to travel to a restaurant and eat a meal are taking advantage of people. I don’t take those jobs anymore.” However, many people still do. Hannah, a 41-year-old lawyer, has done almost 500 visits for the Mystery Dining Company in her free time without getting paid or having her travel costs covered. As a top “platinum diner,” she is often chosen by the company for their best jobs, enjoying £200 meals at Michelin-starred restaurants, five-star hospitality at Ascot, and overnight stays at boutique hotels.

But even for mystery diners, there is no such thing as a free meal. Hannah says she usually spends two to four hours after each visit writing detailed reports about everything from the quality of the food to her interactions with staff, whom she must be able to name or describe. The hardest part is remembering all these details while eating, because she cannot write anything down openly.

“There’s a lot to remember and sometimes it makes the experience less enjoyable. You have to give feedback while it’s still fresh, so I’ve had to get up at 5am to write a report before work. It’s a hard job; you need to be focused, able to explain things well, and pay attention to details.”

More than one million British workers may have jobs with zero-hours contracts, according to new information. This means British companies are using these contracts much more than people thought before. 

This number comes from a survey of over 1,000 employers by the Chartered Institute of Personnel and Development (CIPD). Because of this, people are asking the government to investigate how these contracts are used. In the past week, several organizations, including shops and even Buckingham Palace, have been criticized for hiring people without promising them any work or pay each week. Workers on zero-hours contracts often do not get holiday or sick pay, and they must ask for permission if they want to get another job. The CIPD found that 38% of people on zero-hours contracts say they work full-time, usually 30 hours or more each week. One-third of voluntary sector employers and one in four public sector organizations use these contracts.

The new numbers also make people question if the official data is correct. The Office for National Statistics recently raised its estimate of UK zero-hours workers by 25%, to about 250,000.

Peter Cheese, the head of the CIPD, said there should be a closer look at what zero-hours contracts really are, the different types, and clear advice on good and bad ways to use them. He said it is important to think about both the good and bad sides for businesses and workers.

The shop Sports Direct was recently criticized because it has about 20,000 of its 23,000 workers on zero-hours contracts. After this, other companies were also found to use these contracts, including the cinema chain Cineworld and Buckingham Palace, which uses them for 350 summer workers.

The pub company J D Wetherspoon has 24,000 staff, or 80% of its workers, on zero-hours contracts.

Vidhya Alakeson, from the Resolution Foundation, said, “If there are really about one million people on zero-hours contracts, this is a big part of the workforce. We cannot say it is only a small problem anymore. The new number shows the government must urgently review zero-hours contracts, looking at how big the problem is and how these contracts affect workers’ rights, pay, and well-being.”

Unions and groups fighting poverty say employers are forcing workers to accept these contracts to avoid giving them benefits. Dave Prentis, from the union Unison, said, “Most workers are on these contracts because they have no other choice. They may give some flexibility, but employers have more power, making it hard for workers to complain.”

Workers on zero-hours contracts usually only find out how many hours they will work when the weekly or monthly schedule is made. They must be ready to work extra hours at short notice. They should get holiday pay based on the hours they work, but they do not get sick pay.

The charity National Trust, which hires many seasonal workers on zero-hours contracts, said it gives these workers the same pay and benefits, based on hours worked, as full-time staff. However, it needs some workers to have flexible hours. A spokeswoman said, “We think zero-hours contracts are important for us because our work depends on the weather. We need to change staff schedules quickly, and zero-hours contracts help us do this.”

Politician Chuka Umunna said zero-hours contracts should be rare. “Some workers like the flexibility, but for many, these contracts make them feel insecure and unsure about when they will work,” he said.

Some people think zero-hours contracts helped the UK avoid higher unemployment during the economic downturn. The CIPD found that only 16% of people on zero-hours contracts said their employer often did not give them enough hours each week.

The CIPD also found that 17% of private sector employers use zero-hours contracts, compared to 34% in the voluntary sector and 24% in the public sector.

Industries most likely to have workers on zero-hours contracts are hotels, catering and leisure (48%), education (35%), and healthcare (27%).

There are now more tigers in Nepal than at any time since the 1970s, according to a new count. This gives hope to people who want to save tigers, whose numbers have been falling in south Asia for 100 years. The number of wild royal Bengal tigers in Nepal has grown to 198, which is a 63.6% increase in five years, the government survey showed. “This is very encouraging,” said Maheshwar Dhakal, an ecologist from Nepal’s Department of National Parks and Wildlife Conservation.

The count was done by looking at pictures from over 500 cameras placed in five protected areas and three wildlife corridors. More than 250 conservationists and wildlife experts worked on the survey, which cost about £250,000.

Dhakal said that a similar survey was done in India, and the results from both countries will be published later in 2013. “It will take a few more months for India, which now has 1,300 big cats in several large protected areas, to finish the data,” he added.

Nepal has promised to double the number of tigers by 2022, starting from 121 tigers in 2009, when the last full count was done. As people in Asia become richer, the price for tiger skins and body parts used in traditional Chinese medicine has gone up. International criminal groups pay poor local Nepali people a lot of money to kill tigers. The skin and bones are given to middlemen, who easily cross the open border to India, where the main dealers are.

One big problem is that some high officials work together with mafia groups involved in this trade. Experts say the increase in tiger numbers is because of better protection of national parks, stronger anti-poaching efforts, and better management of tiger habitats in Nepal, where forests cover 29% of the land. But they also say Nepal needs to do more to protect the land and the animals that tigers eat, so tigers have enough space and food.

As the number of tigers has grown, there have been more problems between tigers and villagers. In 2012, tigers killed seven people near national parks, compared to four in 2011, park officials said. Villagers want better protection. “The government is making plans to protect tigers. But it should also make plans to protect people from tigers,” said Krishna Bhurtel, a village leader in Chitwan, to the Nepali newspaper Nagarik.

Wildlife officials caught a tiger in Chitwan after it killed two people, including a villager who was pulled from his bed in May. Thousands of tigers once lived in the forests of Bangladesh, India, and Nepal. But now there are only about 3,000 left, which is a 95% drop in 100 years. Chitwan National Park in central Nepal has the most adult tigers, with 120, followed by Bardiya National Park with 50, and Shukla Phanta Wildlife Reserve with 17.

Diwakar Chapagain, who leads a World Wildlife Fund Nepal group that watches the wildlife trade, said tiger skins are wanted in Tibet, where rich people use them as costumes for festivals.

In Nepal, kings used to stand on tiger skins in front of stuffed tigers for special events. Some rich Nepali people have put tiger heads on their living room walls. Tiger bones are also wanted for traditional Chinese medicine. “The trade in tiger parts is very profitable and brings thousands of dollars in illegal markets,” Chapagain said, showing the danger tigers face.

“I bought a Dyson vacuum cleaner, but I’m not sure if I even want it. I just picked it up,” said Louise Haggerty, a 56-year-old hairdresser and waitress, about her 1am trip to the Black Friday sales. “It was wild in there. It was crazy. It was absolutely disgusting.” 

Haggerty went to the 24-hour Sainsbury’s supermarket in Harringay, north-east London, with a friend, hoping to get a cheap flat-screen TV. “But so many people pushed into the line that we didn’t have a chance,” she said. “A poor woman who was second in line was pushed out by a group of young people. She didn’t get anything. People were acting like animals – it was horrible,” she said. “I only saw two security guards.” 

Haggerty was upset that she couldn’t buy a Blaupunkt 40” TV, which was reduced from £299.99 to £149.99, so she quickly picked up a Dyson Animal Vac, which was down from £319.99 to £159.99. “I don’t even know how much it costs; I don’t even know if I’m going to buy it. I just wanted something,” she said. “There are guys in there with three, four, five TVs. It’s not fair.” 

One of those guys was Andy Blackett, 30, an estate agent, who had two shopping carts full of bargains. “I got two coffee makers, two tablets, two TVs, and a stereo,” he said. “I don’t know the prices, but I know they’re good deals.” But his friend Henry Fischer, a 19-year-old student, was not as lucky. “Someone grabbed my TV from me – it’s because I’m the smaller one.” 

Blackett, Fischer, and some friends drove to Sainsbury’s at 12:45am after leaving the “crazy” Tesco’s 24-hour Lea Valley supermarket, where the Black Friday sale started at midnight. “Tesco was scary, so we came here instead,” Blackett said. 

More than twelve police officers went to the Tesco store on Glover Drive, Upper Edmonton, because fights broke out between excited and angry shoppers. Customers were seen tearing down cardboard barriers that were put up to hold back sale items until midnight. Tesco delayed selling its most popular items – TVs – for almost an hour until police controlled the situation. One police officer was heard criticizing the manager for not having enough security and suggested stopping the sale completely. The Tesco store is across the road from an IKEA furniture store that had riots when it opened with a midnight sale in 2005. 

Police also had to help at other stores, including Tesco in Willesden and Surrey Quays, just before the doors opened at midnight. Greater Manchester Police said at least two people had already been arrested at Black Friday sales that morning. The police wrote on Twitter: “Keep calm, people!” South Wales Police also said they got many calls from Tesco staff who were worried because so many people came to the sales. 

One of the first people to buy a flat-screen TV, just before 1am, was James Alled, 30, a businessman. He bought two TVs and was already trying to sell one to someone further back in the line. “I bought them for £250. I’ll sell it to you for £350, £300 cash,” he said. Further back in the line, Christine Ball, 62, was not happy. “I got here at 10:15pm and now I’m further back than when I arrived,” she said. “None of those people know what a line is.” 

Ball, like most shoppers, had not heard of the American Black Friday sales until now. She came out especially to buy her grandson a TV for Christmas. “Not one of those huge ones; just a normal one for about £100,” she said. In her basket was a pint of semi-skimmed milk and a loaf of bread. “TV, milk, and bread – the basics,” she said. 

Mel Mehmet, 23, had been to Black Friday sales in 2013 and expected lines, but said the atmosphere in Tesco scared her this time. “It’s crazy, really, having it at midnight – the police must have more important things to do at night than be called to sales. We’re going to PC World first thing – their sale starts at 8am.”

Barack Obama told young people not to be negative and to talk with people who have different opinions if they want to change the world.

On his last visit to Britain as US president, Obama spoke to 500 young leaders at a meeting in London. He said, “I’m here to ask you not to believe that there are problems we can’t fix. As JFK said, our problems are made by people and can be solved by people.”

He told the students, “You have better tools than ever to make a difference. Don’t be negative or think nothing can change. Progress is possible, but it doesn’t happen by itself. It needs hard work, discipline, and hope.”

Obama also said he knows young people face many problems: “Your generation has not had an easy time, with big changes like 9/11, 7/7, and living in an age of constant news and social media, where there is always bad news.”

The audience cheered when Obama was introduced. He talked about his policies, like healthcare and education.

He told the audience to talk with people who have different political views: “Find people who don’t agree with you. This will help you learn to compromise.”

Obama also said, “You should feel good that social attitudes are changing. It’s not happening fast enough, but you should keep trying. This is partly because of brave young people like you.”

When someone asked about his time as president, Obama said he was proud of the healthcare reforms, which made the audience cheer. He also talked about the US response to the 2008 financial crisis: “Saving the world from a great depression – that was pretty good.”

He also mentioned making deals with Iran and fighting the Ebola crisis as important parts of his presidency. “I’m proud; I think I have stayed true to myself during this time.”

But he added, “Don’t give up or listen to negative people if, after five years, poverty is still here. That’s OK. Dr Martin Luther King said the path to justice is long, but it moves in the right direction.”

When asked about the Transatlantic Trade and Investment Partnership (TTIP), he said, “The answer to globalization is not to close ourselves off,” but he said it is important to protect workers’ rights.

Before Obama arrived, Tanya Williams, a community worker, told the Guardian, “I love Michelle but I like Obama, and it’s exciting to hear someone who has changed so much and inspired many people who didn’t vote before.”

Oliver Sidorczuk, 26, said, “Everyone is very excited to hear him. I want to ask him about voting rights and if he will help our campaign to ask David Cameron for automatic registration.”

Obama finished the meeting by answering a question from a young Sikh man from London, who asked about being racially profiled at airports and being mistaken for a Muslim.

Obama said that, even though there are people with dangerous ideas, it is important to have a society with many different groups. “I visited a mosque a few months ago and said our best allies are American Muslims who are well integrated and successful,” he said.

Furqan Naeem, a campaigner from Manchester, said, “I recently visited the US through the embassy’s community leaders program and saw important work the president did to celebrate America’s diversity and bring communities together.”

Kenny Imafidon, head of the youth group ClearView Research, said after the event, “It was a great chance, and I will remember what he said about meeting people with different politics and making compromises. Also, what he said about being a good leader and finding talented people.”

Later, Obama met Jeremy Corbyn, who said they had a very good 90-minute talk.

The Labour leader said they talked about “the problems facing modern societies, the power of big companies, and how technology is changing the world.”

When asked if they talked about Obama’s comments on Britain’s EU membership, Corbyn said they talked about it briefly.

After the meeting, Obama played golf with Cameron at the Grove in Hertfordshire. He ended the day with dinner with the prime minister and the US ambassador, Matthew Barzun, at the ambassador’s house, before traveling to Germany.

It is well known that millennials use technology a lot. More than 80% say they sleep with their mobile phone next to their bed. Almost two thirds admit they text while driving. One in five has posted a video of themselves online, and three out of four have made a profile on a social networking site.

A 2010 report says millennials are the most active generation on social media, with 75% having at least one social media account. In comparison, only 50% of Generation X, 30% of baby boomers, and 6% of people aged 65 and older use social media. However, there are some millennials who do not use social media at all. Here are some of their stories.

Celan Beausoleil, 31, from Oakland, California, is a social worker. She has had an “on and off, more off than on” relationship with Facebook. She last deactivated her account in December 2015 because she found that people shared too much personal information, which was hard for her to handle along with her busy job.

She said, “A lot of my job is listening to people’s lives all day, every day, and it started to feel too much to go on social media and see every detail of everyone’s life, even people I don’t really know. It feels like too much closeness.” She added, “I already deal with a lot at work, and sometimes it felt too heavy to do the same in my personal life.”

But Beausoleil does like how social media connects people around the world. This was one of the main reasons she stayed on Facebook for so long. She said, “One thing I really liked about Facebook was that I could spend hours clicking from one friend to another, and end up on someone’s page from the other side of the world. I used to do that a lot.”

“One day, I realized I was spending a lot of time doing this. These small moments add up. I wondered what would happen if I used this time for something else. Would I enjoy it more?”

Mathias, who works for the Baltimore City government, had Facebook and Twitter accounts for years before deleting them both in November 2012. After he left social media, he quickly forgot about Facebook. He still sees some good things about social media, like when he met his girlfriend’s friends for the first time. It was easier to remember people if you could look at their photos and information online. It is also easy to organize big events online. Now, Mathias depends on friends to invite him to parties, and he knows he sometimes misses out.

However, he enjoys the extra time he has now. He spends his free moments reading news articles and books instead of scrolling through social media. Without friends’ accounts to follow, he has to call them on the phone, which he now really enjoys.

Lauren Raskauskas, 22, from Naples, Florida, says she is a “pretty private” person. She does not like how social media lets others see and judge your life. “I care about privacy and worry about giving out my data,” said Raskauskas, who is looking for a job.

She recently deleted her Twitter account and deactivated her Facebook account two years ago because she “didn’t like everyone knowing what I was doing.” Raskauskas started using Facebook late because her parents were strict about technology. She can see some good things about social media. For example, when a friend she had lost contact with moved to Naples for a month, Raskauskas did not know until after her friend had left. She said this “was a bummer.”

But in the end, her worries about privacy were stronger than the benefits of social media. She also found it helpful during a recent break-up. The last time she broke up with someone while using Facebook, it was not pleasant. She said, “One time, I broke up with somebody while I was on Facebook and I wondered, ‘Should I change my profile photo? Should I change my status?’ This time, I don’t have to worry about that, because it’s hard.”

Rajagopalan, a student at Boston College, does not see any problems with not using social media. He says he “hasn’t seen any effect at this point.” Even though classmates post about parties and events on Facebook, they also send him text messages. “Since I was young, I was always a step behind on that kind of thing, so it never really mattered to me,” he said.

The only time Rajagopalan used social media was when he had no other choice: it was the only way to contact his new roommate at college. Before starting his first year, he made his first and only social media account to talk with his future roommate about their plans.

Months later, he still has the account, but he says, “I don’t use it. I don’t check it or anything like that.” The only activity is when his two sisters tag him in family photos. He has avoided social media in all other situations, though he sometimes wants to use Twitter because, as a sports fan, “it’s where most of the news breaks out.” But he refuses to get an account, saying, “I don’t really need one to read tweets.”

Europe’s forests and suburbs are now home to many large predators, such as brown bears, wolves, and lynx, according to a new study. This study, published in Science, shows that these animals are doing well in Europe, even though many people thought they would disappear because of more people and too much use of land and resources.

Brown bears, wolves, Eurasian lynx, and wolverines now live in almost one-third of mainland Europe (not counting Belarus, Ukraine, and Russia). Most of these animals live outside of nature reserves. This means that new ways of thinking and large conservation projects are helping to protect these animals, which people have hunted for a long time.

There are about 17,000 brown bears, 12,000 wolves, 9,000 Eurasian lynx, and 1,250 wolverines in Europe. Wolverines only live in the north of Scandinavia and Finland. Only Belgium, Denmark, the Netherlands, and Luxembourg in mainland Europe, like Britain, do not have any breeding groups of at least one large carnivore. The main author of the study, Guillaume Chapron, and other experts say that because these animals live in busy parts of Europe, even the British countryside could have big predators.

Chapron and other researchers found that wolves sometimes live in suburbs with up to 3,050 people per square kilometre, which is more crowded than cities like Cambridge or Newcastle. On average, wolves in Europe live in areas with 37 people per square kilometre, lynx with 21 people per square kilometre, and bears with 19 people per square kilometre. The Scottish Highlands have only nine people per square kilometre.

Chapron said, “We don’t need to remove people to have wolves.” He and his team believe that the return of big carnivores shows that the “land-sharing” way of protecting nature works. This is different from North America and Africa, where people and predators are kept apart by fences.

Chapron also said, “It’s not always easy—living together can mean problems—but it’s important to manage these problems and solve them. Wolves can be hard to live with. The real conflict is not between people and predators, but between people who have different opinions about predators. These animals make us think about how we use the land.”

The researchers think this “land-sharing” idea could work in other places too. Reasons for its success in Europe include stable governments, more wild prey animals like deer, and money to help farmers protect their animals without killing predators, for example by using electric fences. The most important reason, Chapron said, is the EU Habitats Directive, which makes countries protect and help rare species recover.

Chapron said, “Without the Habitats Directive, we would not have seen this recovery. It shows that if people want to protect nature and make strong laws, it is possible to help wildlife.”

George Monbiot, a writer and supporter of rewilding, welcomed the news. He is starting a new charity called Rewilding Britain to bring back wild areas and lost species. He said, “It’s good to see these animals coming back, but Britain is very different—we have lost more big mammals than any country except Ireland. Apart from wild boar coming back by accident, we have done almost nothing, while other European countries have bears, lynx, and wolves returning. This is a big change after centuries of hunting.”

The study found that Eurasian lynx now live in 11 groups across 23 European countries, but only five of these groups are native. This shows that bringing lynx back has worked. Monbiot said there is growing support for bringing lynx back to the Cairngorms in Scotland.

He said, “If it works in the rest of Europe, there is no reason it can’t work in the UK.” He pointed out that bears and wolves live close to Rome. “There is no reason why we can’t have wildlife returning in the UK too.”

The view from the visitors’ centre at the south edge of Doñana National Park in southern Spain is very impressive. This place is perfect for people who love birds: it has 200,000 hectares of salt marsh, which is very important for birds in western Europe. Many of Britain’s favorite migratory birds, like house martins, swallows, cuckoos, and warblers, stop here every year when they travel from Africa. Doñana is a UN World Heritage Site and is home to some of Europe’s rarest birds, such as the Spanish imperial eagle. It also has the very endangered Iberian lynx.

The park is beautiful and full of life, but it is also in danger. In 1998, a dam at the Los Frailes mine, 45 km to the north, broke. Almost two billion gallons of dirty, acidic water mixed with waste metals flooded into the park. This toxic wave went down the Guadiamar river and covered a large area with a thick layer of metal waste. More than 25,000 kilos of dead fish were collected, and almost 2,000 adult birds, chicks, eggs, and nests were killed or destroyed.

This was Spain’s worst environmental disaster, and cleaning it up cost €90 million. After this, Spain realized how important Doñana was and decided to spend another €360 million, some from the EU, to restore the land. In the 1950s and 60s, parts of the park had been drained to make rice and cotton fields. Now, some of this farmland is being turned back into wetlands.

Restoring Doñana has been expensive but hopeful. However, the park is still at risk because of modern problems. There are plans to build an oil pipeline through Doñana, and some developers want to expand tourist resorts. New hotels and golf courses would need more water, which would lower the water table even more. Mud from nearby farms is also blocking the park’s channels.

But the biggest problem for people who want to protect the park is the recent decision by the Andalucían government to reopen the Frailes mine, which almost destroyed Doñana in 1998. Laurence Rose from the Royal Society for the Protection of Birds (RSPB) said, “This is Europe’s most precious bird sanctuary, both for local species and for birds that migrate between Africa and Britain and other parts of north-west Europe. Doñana already faces many threats, but now they want to bring back the very thing that almost destroyed it 16 years ago. It is extremely worrying.”

It may seem strange that, after spending so much to restore Doñana, the local government now wants mining companies to bid for the Los Frailes mine. But the local economy explains this. The crash of Spain’s banks in 2008 was very bad for the region, and in some parts of Andalucía, unemployment is now over 30%. Reopening the mine would create more than 1,000 much-needed jobs.

Vicente Fernández Guerrero, secretary-general of Innovation, Industry and Energy for Andalucía, said, “There are riches here, riches that local people really need. We think mining is a good way to help people keep living in the area. This is a mining area. People have been digging metals here since Roman times.”

Fernández also said that the mine would only use modern techniques that do not create poisonous liquid waste. The Canadian company that ran Los Frailes before cannot bid for the contract. Sixteen years after the accident, there are still arguments about compensation. Fernández said, “The best technology in the world will be used here. Liquid will not be used. We are going to insist on that. Our tender makes that clear.”

Some people in the area support the plan, but many are against it. One road sign was covered with rude words about the workers’ union UGT, which supports reopening the mine. Carlos Dávila, who works for the Spanish Ornithological Society in Doñana, is also very worried. He said, “This is a very, very bad idea. They say the new mine will be safe, but they said that in 1998 and look what happened. We had the worst environmental disaster in Spain’s history.”

People like Dávila are worried that a new mine will hurt the money spent on eco-tourism in Doñana. For example, at the restaurant Dehesa de Abajo, you can eat or drink while watching storks and black kites nesting in the trees.

Almost every visitor has a camera with a long lens or binoculars. There is a clear tourist business based on Doñana’s birdlife. This is not surprising, because Doñana is a very special place. The sky is huge above the flat but interesting land. Birds of all kinds fill the air and sometimes the roads. During my visit, a stork stood calmly in front of our car until it decided to fly away.

Rose said, “The problem is that Spain does not have as much public money as it did 16 years ago. If there was another toxic spill today, it would be much, much worse.” Dávila agrees. “After the disaster, Spain realized it had a place of real ecological importance and did a lot to clean it up and protect it,” he said. “Now, we seem to be forgetting that lesson. It is very depressing.”

Introduction
Did you know that in the UK, restaurants do not have to give tips to their staff by law? This was discussed in a government review in May 2016, where workers, employers, and customers shared their opinions about tipping. After this, government ministers said they wanted to change the rules to make sure low-paid workers get the tips that customers leave for them. The government started a two-month consultation to look at new proposals to stop unfair practices.

The review found that some waiters are charged up to 15% as an administration fee on tips left by credit or debit card. In some restaurants, waiters even have to pay their own money if they do not get enough tips to cover these fees. The government said it would think about stopping employers from taking admin fees or other deductions from tips.

The government also wants customers to know that tips are voluntary. They want restaurants to clearly show their tipping policy so the system is more open.

We asked waiters across the UK what they think about tipping, how much they earn from tips, if they think it is fair, and what could make it better.

1. Rodri, 37, London: "Around 50% of a waiter’s income is tips"
Average tips: £60 per eight-hour shift

I think waiters are treated best in the US. Things have become fairer since the tipping scandal in summer 2015, when it was found that many restaurants were taking tips from staff for admin fees. But there are still bad stories from new workers at some restaurant chains. I have heard of restaurants not giving chefs a share of the tronc (a system to share tips). Some restaurants take 4% of all sales to pay chefs and for admin fees. So, if you sell £1,000 of food, the company takes £40, no matter how much you get in tips.
