Living in New York, Bowie performed at the Concert for New York City in October 2001, joining Paul McCartney, Jon Bon Jovi, Billy Joel, the Who, and Elton John in a benefit show after the 9/11 attacks. He returned to the studio in 2002 for the album Reality. However, during his Reality tour in 2004, Bowie had chest pains while performing in Germany and needed emergency surgery in Hamburg for a blocked artery.

After this health scare, Bowie slowed down his work. In 2006, he said he would take a year off from touring and recording. That year, he received a Grammy lifetime achievement award. He had already been inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1996.

The Next Day (2013) was his first new album in ten years. The single Where Are We Now? became his first UK top 10 hit since 1993. The album was number 1 in the UK and other countries. In 2014, Bowie won the Brit Award for Best British Male, becoming the oldest person to win this award. He is survived by his wife Iman, their daughter Alexandria, his stepdaughter Zulekha, and his son Duncan from his first marriage.

At Addis Ababa airport, visitors see pictures of golden grains, small red seeds, and men around a large pancake. Signs say: “Teff: the ultimate gluten-free crop!”

Ethiopia is one of the world’s poorest countries and often has problems with food security. However, it is also the original home of teff, a very healthy ancient grain that is now becoming popular in health-food shops and supermarkets in Europe and America.

Teff seeds are very small, about the size of poppy seeds. They are rich in calcium, iron, and protein, and have many important amino acids. Teff is naturally gluten-free, so it can replace wheat flour in bread, pasta, waffles, and pizza bases. Like quinoa from South America, teff’s excellent nutrition is creating new and profitable markets in the West.

In Ethiopia, teff is very important. About 6.3 million farmers grow it, and teff fields cover more than 20% of all farmland. Teff is ground into flour to make injera, a spongy, fermented flatbread that is a basic part of Ethiopian food. Injera is also important in many religious and cultural events. In Ethiopia and neighboring Eritrea, people eat together from large pieces of injera, using it to scoop up stews and feed each other as a sign of loyalty or friendship. This tradition is called gursha.

Outside Ethiopian communities in the West, teff was not well known for many years. But now, more people want traditional grains, and the health-food and gluten-free markets are growing. Because of this, teff is becoming more popular and is called Ethiopia’s “second gift to the world” after coffee.

Sophie Kebede, a businesswoman in London who owns a company that sells teff, was very surprised when she learned how healthy it is. She said, “I didn’t know it was so popular. I am Ethiopian and have eaten injera all my life.”

However, the growing demand for ancient grains does not always help poor communities. In Bolivia and Peru, the global demand for quinoa has increased incomes, but it has also caused malnutrition and land conflicts, as farmers sell all their crops to foreign buyers.

In Ethiopia, the growing middle class also wants more teff, and prices are rising. Now, the poorest people cannot afford teff. Most small farmers sell most of their teff to city consumers. This has helped some rural families earn more money, but it has also caused nutrition problems, because teff is the healthiest grain in Ethiopia. People in cities eat up to 61kg of teff each year, but in rural areas, people eat only 20kg. Rich people usually eat the more expensive magna and white teff, while poorer people eat cheaper red and mixed teff, and more than half mix it with cheaper grains like sorghum and maize.

The Ethiopian government wants to double teff production by 2015. Its plan, published in 2013, says teff could be important for school meals, emergency food programs, and reducing malnutrition, especially in children and teenagers.

Even though Ethiopia’s economy is growing fast, it is still on the UN’s list of least-developed countries. About 20% of children under five are malnourished or have stunted growth.

The government’s Agricultural Transformation Agency wants to increase teff harvests by creating better types of teff, new planting methods, and tools to reduce losses after harvest.

Since 2006, the government has banned the export of raw teff grain. Only processed products like injera can be exported. But this may change. The government’s plan is to produce enough teff for Ethiopians and also have a strong export market.

Mama Fresh is a family business that has sold injera to top restaurants and hotels in Ethiopia’s capital for years. It also sends injera to Finland, Germany, Sweden, and the US, mainly for Ethiopian communities there. The company also wants to sell to the gluten-free market. It plans to double exports to America in 2014 and will soon make teff-based pizzas, bread, and cookies.

David Hallam, a director at the UN’s Food and Agriculture Organization, says, “Usually, these products pass through many hands before reaching shops like Sainsbury’s. There are profits at every step, and small farmers often cannot negotiate well with big traders.” He thinks quinoa’s story is a warning that export opportunities can be both good and bad for poor countries.

Regassa Feyissa, an Ethiopian agricultural scientist, warns that if not planned carefully, growing more teff for export could replace other important crops for farmers. Also, efforts to increase production might help businesses more than small farmers.

Because there is little Ethiopian teff on the world market, farmers in the US have started growing it. Farmers in Europe, Israel, and Australia have also tried growing teff.

Kebede says she gets her teff from farms in southern Europe, but she would rather buy it from Ethiopia. “Teff is natural for Ethiopians, so who better to supply it? We have this popular grain in our country, so why can’t Ethiopian farmers benefit from it?”

David Cameron, Barack Obama, and Pamela Anderson have refused to take part in the Ice Bucket Challenge. George W. Bush, Benedict Cumberbatch, and Stephen Hawking have joined in. The Ice Bucket Challenge has raised $100 million for a US charity that helps people with motor neurone disease, and £4.5 million for a similar British charity. It has also raised thousands more for charities in Hong Kong and Australia. However, there has also been criticism.

Some people say that celebrities are just showing off, that people are having fun without donating, and that the challenge wastes water. These complaints have come from writers, animal rights groups, and environmentalists. The US ALS Association, which is not connected to the UK’s MND Association, has also been criticized for paying high salaries to its top staff.

Even with the criticism, the challenge is still growing. For those who don’t know, the challenge works like this: someone talks briefly on camera about the charity, then pours a bucket of ice water over their head or has a friend do it. After that, they nominate three other people to do the same or to donate money.

The challenge started in the US in July, but it is not clear if it began on a golf course or a baseball field. It first appeared on American TV on July 15. The ALS Association tried to trademark the phrase “Ice Bucket Challenge,” but after people complained, they decided to stop. Their spokeswoman, Carrie Munk, said, “We understand the public’s concern and are withdrawing the trademark applications.” The ALS Association has not yet answered questions about its high costs and salaries.

The timing of the challenge was awkward because World Water Week was from August 31 to September 5. During this week, people from around the world met in Stockholm to talk about the global water crisis. The charity WaterAid has asked people to use recycled water from bathtubs or gardens, or to use sea water for the challenge.

Douglas Graham, the fundraising director of the MND Association, said, “The backlash is to be expected but, really, this is just a wonderful surprise and we’re so grateful. We didn’t expect it, but suddenly, the donations just started.” The extra money is a big help to a small charity that supports people with a serious, little-understood disease that has no cure and kills five people a day in the UK.

Pamela Anderson, who supports animal rights, wrote a public letter to the ALS Association saying she could not support them because they test on animals. Some US celebrities have refused the challenge because of California’s drought. Actor Matt Damon used water from his toilets to show that many people in the world have less clean water than that. Actor Verne Troyer used milk instead of water for environmental reasons. On the Scottish island of Colonsay, the challenge caused a water shortage after its 135 residents joined in.

In Australia, a TV news presenter, Lincoln Humphries, apologized after refusing the challenge strongly. He said, “Instead of pouring fresh water over your head and wasting ice, here is a list of charities helping people in need around the world. I’d like to nominate everyone who has more than they need to donate what they can to those who need it most. That is what charity is about, not making yourself uncomfortable with a bucket of icy water.”

Some people worry that small charities cannot handle so much extra money, but the MND Association disagrees. Graham said, “We can handle it. We pay for world-class research to find the causes and, hopefully, a cure. We care for 3,500 people, and they need it because this disease gets worse quickly and is expensive to manage. Over 50% die within two years of diagnosis. It’s heartbreaking to see people get worse so quickly.”

For many people affected by the disease, the awareness from the challenge is as important as the money. Graham says it is priceless. Usually, the MND Association’s website gets about 300,000 visits a year. On one day recently, it got 330,000.

“We could not have made this happen ourselves. All charities are important, and I understand that some people want to give to other causes. In 2013, British people gave £62 billion to charity – we should be proud of that. It’s wonderful for us to get this extra money. We will decide in the next few weeks how to use it best, but I promise, every penny will be used for good.”

Dan Sullivan was late to breakfast with the Guardian because the police stopped him while he was riding his motorcycle. He says he works too much, misses dinner dates, and forgets to give presents. To solve this problem, like many people in Silicon Valley, the 27-year-old venture capitalist started a company called BetterBoyfriend.me. This service sends a present every month to girlfriends and wives for about $70.

Sullivan works in finance. He has been testing the service quietly and now has about 350 boyfriends using it, making about $17,000 each month. Most of the members are his friends from Harvard and people who work at companies like Apple, Google, and Facebook. Their girlfriends have been getting presents from Sullivan for the past year.

Each month, members can choose one gift from a list of seven options, such as chocolate, tea sets, or manicures. The package is sent to the boyfriend without any brand or label. Sullivan tests his ideas by buying Facebook ads to see how much interest they get. BetterBoyfriend.me became popular quickly. Sullivan said, “BetterBoyfriend hit something. It’s a problem everyone has.”

BetterBoyfriend.me was not Sullivan’s first idea. For a short time, he thought about a dog-sharing business. He noticed rich men looking unhappy while walking dogs and thought, “A dog is only fun 5% of the time. What if someone could babysit the dogs and others could rent them?” 

Another company, called InvisibleBoyfriend, lets users create a fake boyfriend who is always available to talk by text. The founder, Kyle Tabor, started it to help people avoid unwanted attention, but he found that many users actually wanted someone to talk to. Tabor said, “Many more users want companionship through conversation, not just to show others they have a boyfriend.”

For Sullivan and Tabor, it was surprising to see real relationships form with their customers. Sullivan now sees himself as a kind of relationship advisor for the boyfriends. He admits he made mistakes. At first, the packages included receipts with his name, Dan Sullivan, on them. One boyfriend wrote to him and said, “Listen, dude, she’s not mad but Cynthia found out.”

About half of the women who get packages from BetterBoyfriend.me know about Sullivan’s role in their relationships. He says this depends on age. “After you’ve been married a while, you don’t keep many secrets.” Over the year, Sullivan says he has gotten to know the boyfriends very well. They even delivered a package to a hospital delivery room. He says the important thing is to remember that his relationship is with the boyfriend.

When he first started the company, he put BetterBoyfriend.me tags on flower bouquets and went to Dolores Park, a popular place in the Mission District. He looked for couples and gave the flowers to the women, but the boyfriends did not like this. He realized it made sense and started giving the flowers to the boyfriends instead.

Scientists have created a special mirror that can send heat into space. This mirror could replace air-conditioning units that cool buildings on Earth. The researchers think the mirror could greatly reduce the energy used to keep buildings cool, especially in offices and shopping centers, by removing the need for energy-hungry cooling systems.

In the US, about 15% of the energy used by buildings goes to air conditioning. The researchers’ calculations show that, in some cases, the mirror could completely remove the need for extra cooling. In a test on a rooftop in Stanford, California, scientists found that a black-painted surface became 60°C hotter than the air in sunlight, and bare aluminum became 40°C hotter. But the mirror was up to 5°C cooler than the air around it.

“If you cover large parts of the roof with this mirror, you can see how much electricity it can save. You can greatly reduce the power used for air conditioning,” said Shanhui Fan, a photonics expert at Stanford University who led the project. “In some situations, our calculations show you can completely remove the need for air conditioning.”

Buildings get warm in several ways. Hot-water boilers and cooking equipment release heat inside. In hot countries, warm air comes in through doors and windows. Sunlight and infrared rays from the sun also heat up buildings.

The Stanford mirror is designed to reflect 97% of the visible light that hits it. More importantly, it acts as a thermal radiator. When the mirror gets warm, it releases heat as a special type of infrared light. This light passes easily through the atmosphere and goes out into space.

To cool something, engineers use what is called a heat sink—a place to send unwanted heat. The heat sink must be cooler than the object being cooled. For example, a bucket of ice cools a bottle of wine because the ice takes in the heat from the wine. The Stanford mirror uses the universe as the ultimate heat sink.

The mirror is made from several very thin layers. The first layer is reflective silver. On top of this are layers of silicon dioxide and hafnium oxide. These layers help the mirror reflect light and also make it a good thermal radiator. When silicon dioxide gets hot, it sends out heat as infrared light at a wavelength of about ten micrometers. The atmosphere does not absorb much at this wavelength, so the heat goes straight out to space. The total thickness of the mirror is about two micrometers, or two thousandths of a millimeter.

“The cold darkness of the universe can be used as a renewable resource for cooling, even during the hottest part of the day,” the scientists wrote in the journal Nature. In tests, the mirror could cool at a rate of 40 watts per square meter at normal air temperature.

Fan wrote in the journal that the cost to install the mirrors would be between $20 and $70 per square meter. He calculated that a three-story building could save 100 megawatt-hours of electricity each year.

Fan said the mirror could cool buildings or other objects by putting it directly on them. Covering a building’s roof with the mirror would stop sunlight from heating it, but would not remove heat from inside the building. More likely, the mirror would be used to cool water or another liquid, which would then be pumped around the building.

He said the mirrors would not be useful for slowing global warming. “Roof space is only a small part of the Earth’s surface, so we don’t think this is a solution for climate change. Our main help with greenhouse gases is to reduce electricity use,” he said.

“I am very excited about what this mirror can do and how it can be used for cooling,” said Marin Soljačić, a physicist at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. “You could use this on buildings to spend much less on air conditioning, or maybe not need it at all. You could put it on top of shopping malls. With a large enough area, you could get a lot of cooling.”

A new invention could be as important as Trevor Baylis’s wind-up radio from the 1990s. It is a cheap light that uses gravity for power and could replace dangerous kerosene lamps in Africa and India.

British designer Patrick Hunt tried to get money from banks and investors to start his business, but it was slow and difficult. He said, “We tried to get funding, but it’s slow, complex, and unproven. Nobody wants to take a risk.” So, he used crowdfunding on a US website called Indiegogo, which had just started in the UK. In five days, he reached his goal and raised £36,200. By the end of 40 days, he had raised £400,000 because many people wanted to help.

The LED light works with a dynamo powered by a 10kg bag of rocks. You attach the weight to the light and lift it about 2 meters high. As the weight slowly falls, it creates enough power for 30 minutes of light.

Hunt is getting ready to make the lights in China. He will first send 1,000 lights to Africa to test the market before making millions more.

Hunt is one of many new business people using crowdfunding to get money. Another new site, InvestingZone, connects rich people with new business owners.

Indiegogo does not give shares, but people who donate can get “perks.” For example, people who helped fund Hunt’s light got their own light and felt good about helping others.

Danae Ringelmann, co-founder of Indiegogo, says the “gravity light” shows how fair crowdfunding can be. She says it is fast, efficient, and fair because it is not about knowing the right people in banks or investment companies. Instead, you prove your idea to customers and fans, and they decide to support you.

Ringelmann also says that even if an idea does not get funding, it is still useful to test it. This way, you learn quickly if your idea is not good and can improve faster.

Ringelmann started her career as a Wall Street analyst in the US. In 2008, she left her job to help friends in the arts raise money. Indiegogo first focused on films and started at the Sundance Film Festival that year.

Five years later, Indiegogo was raising about $2 million a week for new businesses. In December 2012, it started using euros and pounds to grow in Europe. Britain is now its third biggest market, and international activity has grown by 41% since December.

There are many competitors like Kickstarter, Seedrs, and Funding Circle. But Ringelmann says Indiegogo is the only site where anyone can start a campaign, no matter how unusual the idea.

Indiegogo charges a 4% fee for successful campaigns. If a campaign does not reach its goal, users can either return all the money for free or keep the money but pay a 9% fee.

A British woman, Lauren Pears, raised £100,000 on Indiegogo to open a “cat café” in London called Lady Dinah’s Cat Emporium. It has not opened yet, but it will be a place where people can relax with tea, a book, and a cat.

Ringelmann says that sometimes investors reject ideas because they are not sure if people want them. But if entrepreneurs use Indiegogo and get support, it proves there is a market for the idea. Crowdfunding helps test the market, pricing, features, and get important feedback.

With her experience on Wall Street and helping 100,000 businesses, Ringelmann gives advice to new entrepreneurs. She says, “Ideas are common. What matters is how you make them real. If you are afraid someone else can do it better, you are not the right person for the idea. You need confidence to move fast and learn.”

Ringelmann wants to make finance more open to everyone. Indiegogo now has more than 7,000 live campaigns. The site now allows payments through local cards like Maestro in the UK and Carte Bleue in France, as well as PayPal.

Crowdfunding is growing as an alternative to banks, but big investors still prefer to own part of a business. This could change in the UK with the launch of InvestingZone.

JMW Turner, one of Britain’s most famous painters, will be on the new £20 note after a vote across the country. This is the first time an artist will appear on a British banknote. The governor of the Bank of England, Mark Carney, asked people to suggest a famous person from culture who has died and deserves this honour.

Turner, who is well known for his dramatic paintings of the sea, was chosen over 590 other people, including painters, sculptors, fashion designers, photographers, film-makers, and actors. These people were suggested by 30,000 members of the public. The list included Alfred Hitchcock, Alexander McQueen, Derek Jarman, Laura Ashley, William Morris, and Vanessa Bell. A group of artists, critics, and historians then chose five final names from this list.

The final five were Barbara Hepworth, Charlie Chaplin, Josiah Wedgwood, William Hogarth, and Turner. They were chosen because they made a big and lasting contribution to the visual arts and to British society.

The announcement about the new banknote was made at the Turner Contemporary gallery in Margate. This gallery is on the site where Mrs Booth’s lodging house used to be, where Turner often stayed. Mark Carney and the artist Tracey Emin, who grew up in Margate, made the announcement together.

Carney said it was very important to choose the right person and to involve the public in the process. He said that banknotes are not just for spending, but can also be like a piece of art that everyone can carry. He also said, “Money is memory for a country and its people.” He explained that Bank of England notes celebrate the UK’s history, culture, and achievements, and that money has cultural value, not just economic value.

Carney said Turner is probably the most important British artist ever. Turner’s work changed art and is still important today. Now, his work will appear on two billion new £20 notes.

Tracey Emin said that having Turner on the £20 note shows that British people value creativity and the arts.

The new note will show Turner’s self-portrait from 1799, which is now in Tate Britain, and one of his most famous paintings, The Fighting Temeraire. This painting is about a ship that was important in Nelson’s victory at the Battle of Trafalgar in 1805.

The note will also have a quote from Turner, “light is therefore colour,” and his signature, which comes from his will, where he left many of his works to the nation.

The new £20 note will replace the one with Adam Smith, a famous thinker about society and economics. It will start being used by 2020. This is the first time the public could help choose whose face is on a British banknote.

For almost 100 years, police and intelligence agencies around the world have used lie detectors to help catch criminals and find spies or traitors. The polygraph, a type of lie detector, is often shown in movies, where guilty people sweat a lot while being tested. However, this invention might soon become outdated. Researchers in Britain and the Netherlands have made a new discovery. They have developed a method that works more than 70% of the time in tests, and it could be used in police stations worldwide within ten years. 

Instead of looking for signs like facial movements, talking too much, or waving arms—which are often seen as signs of lying—the new method checks the movements of the whole body to find signs of guilt. The polygraph is used a lot in the United States for criminal cases and for security checks for the FBI and CIA, but it is not very popular in Europe. Many scientists and lawyers do not trust the polygraph because they doubt how reliable it is. In contrast, the new method has worked well in experiments.

The main idea is that people who lie move or fidget more. The researchers use a special suit, like the ones used in movies to create computer characters, to measure this. The suit has 17 sensors that record movement 120 times per second in three directions for 23 joints in the body.

Ross Anderson, a professor at Cambridge University and part of the research team, said that after many years of research, interviewers can only tell if someone is lying a little better than guessing, about 55 out of 100 times. The polygraph, which has been used since the 1920s, measures stress from anxiety and can reach about 60% accuracy. However, it can be misused during questioning, and many people feel nervous just because their job or freedom depends on the test.

Anderson said the new method is more reliable, with over 70% accuracy, and he believes it can get even better. In some tests, the team has already reached more than 80% accuracy. Anderson said, “The main point is that guilty people fidget more, and we can measure this well.”

Anderson also said this research is important now, especially after the US Senate report on CIA torture. Besides the moral reasons against torture, Anderson said torture is not a good way to get true information. “We have known for a long time that torture does not work,” he said. The new method gives a practical, science-based way to do interviews. The research paper was written by Dr. Sophie van der Zee from Cambridge University, Professor Ronald Poppe from Utrecht University, Professor Paul Taylor from Lancaster University, and Anderson.

The polygraph was invented in 1921 by policeman John Larson, based on research by psychologist William Marston. It records changes in pulse, blood pressure, sweating, and breathing to see if someone is lying. Movies often show the polygraph as almost perfect, but in 1998, the US Supreme Court said there was no agreement that the polygraph was reliable. The US National Academy of Scientists agreed in 2003.

Anderson and his team tested their new method with 180 students and workers at Lancaster University. Half were told to tell the truth, and half were told to lie. Each person was paid £7.50 for taking part in the 70-minute experiment, which had two tests. In one test, some people played a computer game called Never End for seven minutes, while others only read about it and then lied about playing. In the second test, there was a lost wallet with £5 inside. Some people were asked to put the wallet in a lost-and-found box, while others hid it and lied about it.

The report says, “Overall, we correctly identified 82.2% of the people as telling the truth or lying, based on their body movements. We got 88.9% right for truth-tellers and 75.6% right for liars.” Anderson said their first try looked at how different body parts and signals showed lying. They found that liars move their arms more, but this only gave about 60% accuracy, like the polygraph.

“The real success came when we looked at total body movement. This can tell truth from lies over 70% of the time, and we think it can get even better if we use the best questioning methods,” Anderson said.

Another benefit is that total body movement is not much affected by culture, anxiety, or how much a person is thinking, which can confuse other lie-detection methods, Anderson said.

The full-body suits are expensive—they cost about £30,000—and can be uncomfortable. Anderson and his team are now looking for cheaper options, like using motion-sensing technology from computer games, such as Microsoft’s Kinect for the Xbox.

Anderson admits that agencies like the CIA could train their agents to beat the full-body motion method by staying very still, but he said that not moving at all would also be a sign of lying.

After being told many times that the beer she wanted was “too dark and too strong for you, love – have something sweeter,” Rebecka Singerer got tired of it.

“No, I don’t want a fruit beer. Women can drink whatever we want,” she says.

Now Singerer, who works as a childminder, has joined FemAle, a group of women beer drinkers in Gothenburg, to launch Sweden’s first beer made by women.

The beer, called We Can Do It, is a bottled pale ale and is now being sold in stores across Sweden. The label shows a version of Rosie the Riveter, a famous image from a US World War II campaign that became a symbol of women’s strength at work.

The group’s founder is Elin Carlsson, 25, who paints cars at the Volvo factory near the city. “We Can Do It is not a beer just for women, but a beer made by women that anyone can drink,” she says. “It’s not about feminism; it’s about equality – we wanted to show we can do it.”

FemAle faces many years of prejudice in the beer world. Ironically, big companies like Carlsberg have spent millions trying to sell beer to women by making it lighter, sweeter, or in smaller bottles, thinking this would appeal to women. Beers like Carlsberg’s Eve, Foster’s Radler, and Coors’s Animée were lighter, flavored, or “bloat-resistant,” but they did not become popular.

FemAle does things differently. They hold women-only tastings where women can try different flavors and styles of beer they might not usually taste. The group says this helps “get more girls into the beer world.” They invite women to bring their mothers, sisters, girlfriends, aunts, and grandmothers so everyone can learn more about beer.

The idea for FemAle started when the women kept meeting each other at beer festivals.

We Can Do It was the idea of Felicia Nordström, a bar worker who was tired of men telling her: “What do you know about beer, sweetie?” She joined FemAle, and together they worked with Ocean, a small local brewery. One weekend they created the recipe, and the next weekend they brewed 1,600 liters.

“This is not a beer made just for women – it’s our hoppiest brew,” says Thomas Bingebo, the head brewer at Ocean. “When big breweries try to make beer for women, it usually fails. This is something completely different.”

The first batch of We Can Do It sold out almost immediately. Other breweries have already asked FemAle if they can make new beers together.

We Can Do It uses three types of malt – Maris Otter, Amber, and Thomas Fawcett wheat malt – and two types of hops, Galaxy and Cascade. Its IBU (bitterness level) is 65, and its alcohol content is 4.6%.

“Women often choose wine because they don’t know much about beer or what to order,” says Carlsson. “We help them discover new things.”

“I used to not like stout, but back then I only drank Pripps, a light Swedish lager,” says Singerer, 38. “Now Guinness tastes like water to me. There are imperial stouts that taste like biscotti dipped in espresso.”

The women are part of a beer boom in Sweden, where people are becoming more interested in “craft” ales, both bottled and on tap. The usual stor stark (large strong) lager is now “almost extinct” in Gothenburg, as pubs and bars replace big brands with special beers.

“All the girls are different – there is no typical woman beer-lover. Anyone can do it,” says Emma Henriksson, 22, a group member who works at a garden equipment company.

“Every pub wants to know how to attract women,” adds Singerer. “And Elin has found the way. It’s great. We feel so proud.”

Donald Trump walked onto the stage and made a surprisingly modest statement for someone doing so well in politics. “Unless we win, it doesn’t mean anything,” he told a campaign rally in South Carolina, even though he had been leading in the polls for four months. “I want to choose my own date for the election. I want it next Tuesday,” he joked to the crowd of 11,000 people. This strong support from regular people would need to continue until March 2016 for him to win the Republican nomination, and even longer to win the general election in November. These moments of doubt do not last long for Trump. He quickly returns to his usual confident style, showing off his image as a “winner,” which is a big part of his campaign.

Trump is not the only one wondering if his unlikely campaign can surprise everyone and last until the end, especially since recent controversies have only made his poll numbers stronger compared to his confused rivals. Normally, any one of these controversies would have ended another politician’s campaign.

First, Trump upset prisoners of war by questioning the heroism of Vietnam veteran John McCain, saying McCain was not a hero because he was captured. Then, during the first TV debate, Trump insulted Fox News moderator Megyn Kelly because she asked him tough questions.

Trump has also insulted Mexican immigrants, said that a Black Lives Matter protester who was violently removed from a rally deserved to be “roughed up,” seemed to make fun of a New York Times journalist’s disability, and falsely accused Muslim Americans of celebrating the 9/11 attacks.

Trump says that the media, which he calls “scum,” has made these incidents seem worse than they are. Still, he refuses to take back any of his comments. “I could have said, ‘Oh, I misspoke,’ but I don’t like doing that,” Trump told the South Carolina crowd. Some of his rivals hope that Trump’s supporters will eventually get tired of what critics see as his constant attacks on minorities. One poll shows his support among Republicans has dropped by 12 points, but at 31%, he is still in the lead.

Other opponents wonder if Trump really has any strong political beliefs. “He is an egomaniac; he’s a narcissist. He’s not a conservative, he’s not a liberal – he believes in himself,” said Bobby Jindal, a former presidential rival, before leaving the race.

Liz Mair, a Republican strategist who is raising money to oppose Trump, worries that many of the things the liberal media call mistakes are actually planned to make Trump more popular with his main supporters. “I think people who don’t like Trump and his policies should work hard to stop him,” she says. “Not just hope he ruins his own campaign.”

But Trump is not just about making shocking statements. He often talks about three main issues: immigration reform, free-trade deals, and Barack Obama’s national security policy. These have become some of the most important topics in the election.

Trump’s plans to deport every undocumented immigrant in the US and to make Mexico pay for a border wall – “A real wall. A very tall wall, taller than that ceiling.” – may sound unrealistic, but they have hurt the campaign of Jeb Bush, who supports immigration reform.

So, what could stop Trump? Some opponents hope that polls taken this far before the election are often wrong by about eight percentage points, because most people have not decided who to support yet. Among Republicans, current polls show Trump has 25-30% of the vote.

It will be hard to change the minds of Trump’s passionate supporters. To reduce his lead, another candidate would need to win over his supporters without losing their own. Polling experts think this is unlikely, because it is hard to imagine anyone doing what Trump does better than Trump himself.

This can be seen in answers to the question: “Are there any of these candidates you would definitely not support for the Republican nomination for president?” While 20-30% of voters say they would support Trump, another 20-30% say they definitely would not.

Steve Deace, a well-known conservative from Iowa, said that Trump’s behavior is “both a good and a bad thing. On one hand, it creates loyal followers who will not leave you. On the other hand, it makes it hard to get more supporters.”

Top Republican pollster Frank Luntz believes Trump speaks for voters who, for the first time, feel like they have someone who says what they are thinking. “Trump says what they’re thinking and, the more outrageous he is, the more they agree with him. He’s saying what no politician would say and that’s another reason they like him,” Luntz says.

This is how many regular supporters feel at Trump’s crowded campaign events. “I like the way he speaks,” says Sandra Murray from Dubuque, Iowa. “This country is a huge mess and we need to fix it. Honestly, he could be the man to do it.”

Other supporters have a simpler reason. “He’s not afraid of anybody or anything. That’s pretty cool.”

A long time ago, movie audiences were taken to a galaxy far away, where imperial ships fought against rebel fighters, where robots met Wookiees, and where a spaceship called the Millennium Falcon could travel the Kessel Run in less than 12 parsecs. This happened in 1977. In 2015, as the seventh Star Wars movie was about to come out, people were still very interested in Star Wars. There was news about a new film about Han Solo and that Darth Vader would return. Paul Dergarabedian, a senior media analyst at Rentrak, said, “Countless fans around the world are always waiting for new posters, trailers, and other news. It’s hard to think of any other movie series that makes people so passionate and excited.”

The latest Star Wars excitement started when Disney bought Lucasfilm from George Lucas, the creator of Star Wars, in 2012. Disney paid $4 billion and announced three more movies—Episodes VII, VIII, and IX—and also planned other spin-off movies to fill the time between the main films. Now, details about the second spin-off are public: it will be an “origin story” about Han Solo, the space smuggler played by Harrison Ford in the first three movies. This film is planned for release in May 2018.

Before that, Episode VII, called Star Wars: The Force Awakens and directed by JJ Abrams, will come out in December 2015. Episode VIII will be released in 2017, and the first spin-off, Rogue One, will be in cinemas in 2016.

Rogue One will show a rebel mission to steal the plans for the Death Star, which was an important part of the first 1977 film. Many people are interested in the rumor that Darth Vader, the main villain in the original series, will appear in Rogue One. This shows how strong Star Wars nostalgia is.

By creating a big movie “universe” with many stories and characters, Lucasfilm and Disney are following the example of Marvel Studios, which Disney also bought in 2009 and which has been very successful.

Disney has used smart marketing to make Star Wars even more popular. Dergarabedian says that making all six Star Wars movies available on streaming services was “a brilliant way to build excitement for the new film and remind fans about Star Wars.”

It is not clear if Star Wars really needed more excitement. For at least the last twenty years, Star Wars has had a lot of enthusiasm from fans. This is shown by the “Expanded Universe,” which includes many novels, comic books, video games, and merchandise that Lucasfilm has created or allowed others to make.

This extra material started as early as 1978, but it became much bigger with the rise of the internet in the 1990s. Fans continue to play roles and take part in Star Wars activities. In the UK, Secret Cinema has been very successful with live shows of The Empire Strikes Back.

Michael Rosser, news editor for Screen International, says that this “shared universe” and strong nostalgia keep Star Wars at the top among movie series. “The great thing about the original films was that they created a huge universe of characters and possibilities that made viewers imagine more,” he said.

“For years, people have wondered how the different stories would continue. This new film, because it goes back to Han Solo and Luke Skywalker, seems like it will connect with the original Star Wars in a way that the prequels did not.”

Rosser is talking about the three films George Lucas directed between 1999 and 2005—The Phantom Menace, Attack of the Clones, and Revenge of the Sith—which told the story of Luke Skywalker’s father, Anakin, who becomes Darth Vader. Even though these films did not get great reviews, they still made $2.5 billion at the worldwide box office. The special editions of the first trilogy, released in 1997, made $469 million.

“It shows the power of Star Wars that, even though the prequels were disappointing, they still made a lot of money,” said Rosser.

In today’s film business, where branding is very important and successful series are highly valued, some people worry that studios might focus only on brands and forget about making good movies.

Rosser does not think this will happen. “They want the Star Wars series to last a long time and keep the quality high. They also want to bring people back to the cinema, since many now stay home for entertainment. But you don’t want to watch Star Wars on your phone, so I don’t think interest will end soon.”

Meanwhile, Dergarabedian expects huge business when The Force Awakens comes to cinemas in December 2015. “We are looking at a record opening for December, and it should make at least a billion dollars worldwide. Truly, Star Wars is the ultimate movie brand.”

In 2010, the old city of Srinagar was very dangerous. Police only went there wearing body armour. Violent separatists who wanted Kashmir to be independent controlled the area. Many protests happened there, and more than 100 people died. People lost hope for peace in this part of north India.

But things have changed quickly. Now, tourists happily wait in the same streets to buy barbecued mutton tikka and hot plates of rogan josh. The Nowhatta mosque, where young people used to throw stones at police after Friday prayers in 2010, will soon be part of an official walking tour about the city’s history, crafts, and markets. Near Dal Lake, houseboats are fully booked months ahead. In the beautiful gardens by the lake, visitors take photos with one of Asia’s prettiest views. Until the snow melted, rich Russians filled the nearby ski resorts.

In 2002, only about 27,000 tourists visited the Kashmir Valley because they were scared of the anti-Indian violence, which has killed up to 70,000 people. But in 2012, almost one million tourists have come, including more than 23,000 from outside India. However, fewer than 150 British people visited. This is mostly because the UK’s Foreign Office still gives strong warnings about the area, listing recent security problems, which scares most travellers.

Omar Abdullah, the Chief Minister of Jammu and Kashmir, was born in the UK. He has asked the British High Commission in Delhi to change the travel advice, but they have not agreed. Abdullah said, “It’s frustrating. Because of this travel warning, people’s insurance does not work if they visit here.” The last time foreign tourists were killed in Jammu and Kashmir was in 1995, when six westerners, including two Britons, were kidnapped by Al-Faran, a Kashmiri militant group. Only one person escaped alive.

Abdullah said, “British citizens have been killed more recently in other countries, but you still let people visit those places. How many British people died in 9/11? Did you stop people from going to New York? People have died in Spain and Bali too. We have lost Indians in London, but we don’t stop Indians from going there. There is no reason to say Jammu and Kashmir, or Srinagar, is unsafe.”

Germany changed its travel advice in 2011, saying that foreigners are usually not targets in fights. Many people thought this was a brave decision, because it was less than a year after the 2010 violence ended. On 15 August, India celebrated 65 years of independence. In the past, this day was dangerous in Kashmir, where many people do not feel part of India. But this year, there was no trouble during the celebrations.

Abdullah says tourists are safe in the state, “as long as you take normal precautions.” For example, do not go hiking near the border between Indian and Pakistani parts of Jammu and Kashmir. Syed Ali Shah Geelani, who leads a pro-independence party, disagrees with Abdullah on many things, but both agree on tourism. At the start of summer, Geelani wrote a letter to tourists and pilgrims, saying, “No matter your faith, language, or where you come from, we are all connected by humanity. You are our honoured guest. Respecting and protecting guests is our duty and our belief.”

Some visitors may worry about enjoying themselves in a place where many people suffer from anxiety and mental health problems. But all the local people we spoke to in Srinagar strongly support tourism. Amjid Gulzar, 26, said Abdullah should work for peace and also bring in foreign visitors. “He must do both. Without tourism, our economy will be in chaos,” he said. He welcomed the million tourists this year, but said Kashmir needs to attract more wealthy visitors, especially from other countries.

“We need better infrastructure, better roads, and reliable electricity. We need more things for tourists to do in the evening – we don’t even have one cinema in this city, and there isn’t enough for tourists to do after dark,” he said. But will tourists feel welcome? In June, a local Islamic group gave a “dress code” for foreign tourists. Abdullah is tired of talking about this. “Nobody expects tourists to cover their faces. I think they were talking about short shorts and sleeveless shirts, which would not get much attention anyway. The main point is: be sensitive to our culture and dress properly. That’s just common sense.”

Abdullah said he is promoting tourism “because I need to help the economy.” Jammu and Kashmir’s finances are in very bad shape after more than 20 years of trouble. The state gets only £72 million each year in taxes, but pays £155 million in salaries for 500,000 public workers. This is why he needs more money quickly. For now, he is happy to see tourists returning. “I’m not saying that having one million tourists means everything is normal,” he said. “But I am glad that people can come, enjoy themselves, and go home safely.”

James Hamblin, a senior editor at The Atlantic magazine, recently tried living without regular showers. For his series ‘If Our Bodies Could Talk’, Hamblin, who seems like a normal person, stopped showering often to see what happens when we clean our bodies too much. He took fewer showers and stopped using shampoo and soap. He found out what many others have learned: the more we try to clean ourselves with soap, body wash, and scrubbers, the more our skin tries to fix itself, making us want to clean even more. Showering removes the skin’s natural oils and bacteria. Many people think this is good, but sometimes it works too well, especially with hot water and strong cleaning products.

After a shower, you might feel like your skin is tight. This is because you have washed away your skin’s natural moisture. Also, our skin, like our stomach, has millions of good bacteria. Showering too much destroys these helpful bacteria because we rub and scrub so much. When the bacteria come back, the ones that make bad smells grow faster. So, showering too often can actually make you smell worse. If you stop showering and using soap, your skin will go through a short, possibly unpleasant, period of adjustment. After that, your skin usually balances itself, makes less oil, and the good bacteria return.

After his experiment, Hamblin learned what others who avoid soap and showers already know: the human body can take care of itself quite well. It’s not just about smell or looks. Dermatologists say that using less soap can help with acne and eczema.

Taking fewer showers and using fewer cleaning products is also good for the environment. The average shower lasts seven minutes and uses 65 litres of water. That’s 65 litres of clean water that we mix with soap and send down the drain every day, sometimes more than once. Clean water is becoming more important, especially as places like California face droughts. Clean water is one of the world’s most valuable resources and may soon be hard to find. Also, all those bottles of body wash are bad for the environment. These are strong reasons to let your body be more natural.

If this idea makes you uncomfortable because you remember being close to someone who didn’t shower enough and still smelled, don’t worry. Many people who shower less still use deodorant if they need it. Everyone’s natural smell is different and can change with diet, water intake, and exercise. Washing your hands with soap is still very important to stop the spread of diseases.

You don’t have to stop showering completely like Hamblin did. Between showering three times a day and never showering at all, there is a middle ground. Try skipping a few showers, use less soap, and let your skin’s good bacteria grow.

Since Moses King, 48, found out he was HIV positive, he has had one big problem. He could handle the shame of being HIV positive, which is common in Liberia, and he could get antiretroviral medicine from the Global Fund and the Liberian government. But King and his six children could not get enough good food. He is a small farmer who grows vegetables and buys rice. 

However, meat and fish are very expensive in Liberia, but they are important sources of protein. King said, “Farming helped us survive, but we had many problems. We could not get any protein, and we were not getting the nutrients we needed to stay healthy.”

Pate K Chon, a counselor who helps people with HIV in Liberia, found a surprising solution. After watching a film about a fish farm in Thailand, she wanted to start a similar project in Liberia. This would give people with HIV both work and a steady source of protein. Chon, who was diagnosed with HIV in 1992, said, “I saw this film about fish in a cement pool and thought it was a good idea. Many people I work with cannot get enough protein, and fish is a clean source of protein. It does not cause health problems like some other foods, and we can farm it.”

Chon started a faith-based NGO and began building a pool to farm fish. In June 2012, she met John Sheehy, a ‘strategic philanthropist’ and founder of Emerging Business Lab. He raised money for the non-profit fish farm in northeast Monrovia, Liberia’s capital. He also learned about fish farming by taking an online course at Cornell University and talking to other fish farmers in Africa.

Sheehy said, “I raised the money and built the farm, learned how to set up the tanks and water system. I taught myself a lot, and now I want to write a manual to help others.”

Now, the project is called Grow2Feed Liberia Fish Farm. It has 12 tanks, and when full, each tank has 5,000 fish. This means the farm can produce up to 200,000 fish each year, helping a community of 1,200 people, most of whom are HIV positive, including King and his family.

The waste from the fish tanks is used to water crops, which also gives food and money to the community. The community has 503 women, 206 men, and 346 children.

Sheehy said, “The community members live near the farm and have agreed to join the co-operative. Many work on the farm or take care of the crops. When the fish are fully grown after 90 days, they get fish in return. They can eat the fish or sell them in the market to buy other important things.”

“The fish farm helps people with HIV return to society. Now they can trade and do business in the market every week.”

According to Liberia’s health survey, 1.5% of Liberia’s 3.5 million people are HIV positive, and 60% of them are women or girls. There is still a lot of shame and discrimination about HIV, and about half of all cases in the country are not treated.

Good nutrition is very important for people with HIV. Research shows they need much more protein to stay healthy and grow well. Chon said, “Nutrition is very important if you are taking antiretroviral drugs. The drugs are strong, and if you do not have enough food, they can make you very sick. But food in Liberia is very expensive. We buy expensive imported rice, even though we should grow it ourselves, and most people cannot afford fish.”

Sheehy says Grow2Feed is the first co-operative fish farm in Liberia to help an HIV-positive community. The project has interested the Liberian government and the UN Food and Agriculture Organization, which has helped Grow2Feed with training and will also support teaching at the University of Liberia.

Fish farming experts say fish farming can work very well in Africa. Paul White, owner of HydroFish fish farm in Ivory Coast, which produces 3,000 tonnes of fish each year, said, “Fish farming is possible in Africa. A lot of fish in the market comes from China and is imported frozen. It is not good enough for Europe or America. There has not been enough investment or knowledge in fish production, but this is changing now.”

Some people worry about farmed fish, saying they can be inbred or have high levels of toxins. But Sheehy said good practices can solve these problems. “A lot of farmed fish are inbred, which causes problems, but we use local fish from Liberia, not from other places. This means we can keep using local fish to get new breeding stock. We do not use lakes, where fish can get toxins. We use tanks, and we test and watch the water all the time.”

Sheehy hopes to use this model in other parts of Liberia and the region. “A rice-growing co-op in Sierra Leone asked us to do this on their land so they can feed their workers. We have also had interest from Nigeria and Central America,” said Sheehy. “But we are 100% non-profit and will always focus on social justice.”

For 85 years, Pluto was just a grey spot on maps in classrooms. But on July 15, Pluto was seen in clear detail for the first time. The new pictures showed big mountain ranges made of solid water ice, as large as the Alps or the Rockies.

These amazing images of Pluto and its large moon, Charon, were sent back to Earth from the New Horizons spacecraft, which is 4 billion miles away. This was the highlight of a mission that has been going on quietly for almost ten years.

Alan Stern, the main scientist for the mission, said the images were a big success for the team. He said, “New Horizons is already giving us amazing results. The data looks beautiful, and Pluto and Charon are incredible.”

One of the biggest surprises was finding mountains in the Kuiper belt, which is the solar system’s “third zone.” Pluto is in this area, along with about 100,000 smaller icy objects. John Spencer, another scientist, said the mountains are about 11,000 feet high and several hundred miles wide. “These are very big mountains,” he said.

A close-up image of Pluto’s edge showed no craters, which suggests the surface is new and has been changed recently by geological activity. This activity could include geysers shooting ice into the air or volcanoes that erupt with ice instead of hot rock.

At the NASA press conference, they started by showing amazing images of the sun and the eight official planets, remembering that Pluto used to be the ninth planet before it was called a dwarf planet in 2006. Dwayne Brown, a NASA spokesman, said, “We have turned what was once a blurry point of light into a clear picture,” as everyone waited to see the new image.

Stern said these images are just the beginning of what we will learn about Pluto this year. Scientists were surprised to find that the mountains are made of water ice, with only a thin layer of other ices like methane and nitrogen on top. Spencer explained, “You can’t make mountains out of methane and nitrogen. Water ice is strong enough to make big mountains, and that’s what we think we’re seeing. The methane and nitrogen are just a thin coating.”

The mountains on Pluto probably formed less than 100 million years ago, which is very recent compared to the solar system’s age of 4.56 billion years. This means the area, which is about 1% of Pluto’s surface, may still be changing today. These are the first ice mountains seen outside the moons of giant planets. Scientists now wonder what kind of geological processes could create such mountains.

The mountains and the smooth surface of Pluto suggest that geological activity is happening, which smooths out craters made by asteroid impacts. Scientists think this “paving” could be caused by heat inside Pluto that softens rock and ice, or by snowfalls that cover the surface. The images are so detailed that, if the spacecraft flew over London, we could see the runways at Heathrow airport.

Because Pluto is 5 billion kilometers away, it takes New Horizons hours to send back just one picture. It will take 16 months to send all the data collected during the fly-by. The team also announced that the heart-shaped area on Pluto will now be called Tombaugh Regio, to honor Clyde Tombaugh, who discovered Pluto in 1930.

The new image of Charon shows a complex surface with cliffs and long valleys about 1,000 kilometers long, which suggests the surface has many cracks, possibly from geological activity. There is also a deep canyon, about 7 to 9 kilometers deep.

Cathy Olkin, another scientist, said, “Charon surprised us with the new image today. The team is very excited. There is so much interesting science in just this one picture.” Pluto is thought to be about two-thirds rock, covered in a lot of ice, with surface temperatures around minus 230 degrees Celsius. As the £460 million mission continues into the Kuiper belt, scientists hope it will help us learn about the early solar system and how planets, including Earth, were formed.

Andrew Coates, a planetary science expert, said, “These Kuiper belt objects are the building blocks of the outer solar system. They are all very cold, like a cosmic freezer. This is the best way to keep the history of the solar system safe. That’s why this is so exciting. It’s a great time for exploring the solar system.”

In August 2015, the mission scientists will choose which of two objects to visit next. NASA thinks the spacecraft can keep working and sending data until the mid-2030s. After that, its plutonium power will run out, and it will shut down, drifting toward the edge of the solar system and into deep space.

New Horizons also looked at Pluto’s four smaller moons: Nix, Hydra, Styx, and Kerberos. A new image of Hydra shows its irregular shape and size, about 43 by 33 kilometers. John Grunsfeld, a NASA official, said, “New Horizons is a true exploration mission, showing us why basic science is so important.”

He added, “The mission had nine years to build up hopes for what we would see at Pluto and Charon. Today, we get the first look at the scientific treasures collected during those important moments, and I can say it is even better than we hoped.”

The observations also show that Hydra’s surface is probably covered with water ice. Future images will give more clues about how this and the other moons formed billions of years ago.

Roger McKinlay, former president of the Royal Institute of Navigation, wrote in the journal Nature that we depend too much on GPS (global positioning system) technology. He says this could make us lose our natural ability to find our way. “If we do not value these skills, our natural navigation abilities will get worse as we use smart devices more,” he wrote.

McKinlay thinks that a lot of money must be spent before navigation systems are good enough for things like self-driving cars. Until then, he says we need better research into navigation systems, and children should learn to find their way using traditional methods. “Schools should teach navigation and map reading as important life skills,” he wrote.

According to Ofcom (the Office of Communications), about 66% of adults in the UK had a smartphone in 2015, up from 39% in 2012. This means GPS technology is now common. But McKinlay, who is a satellite communication and navigation consultant, warns that we should not trust our devices too much for navigation. “Navigation is a skill you must use or you will lose it,” he wrote.

There are not many scientific studies on this topic, but research from 2009 supports the idea. Dr. Hugo Spiers, a neuroscientist at University College London, studied current London taxi drivers and those who had retired for about four years. The retired taxi drivers did worse on navigation tests than those still working. “We showed that their abilities got worse if they did not use their knowledge,” Spiers said.

Spiers also thinks it is risky to rely on GPS, but he says the biggest danger is that people can be led into dangerous situations without knowing. For example, in 2010, a driver in Spain died after following a satnav (satellite navigation device) into a reservoir. “There is a real risk in relying on a satnav,” Spiers said. “But we do not know the health risk of not using your brain for navigation.”

Spiers says the way we use navigation technology can change how it affects our skills. Audio instructions from GPS mean drivers do not have to think about navigation, but using smartphone apps as digital maps is different. “In the past, you had to carry a paper map. Now, we use computer information and still have to think about where we are going and interact with the device,” he said. “Modern technology is not making us completely less smart.”

McKinlay still believes that navigation technology is not ready for things like driverless cars and smart cities. “For very important uses, like landing planes or navigating aircraft, GPS is still not good enough,” he said.

Spiers thinks that artificial intelligence using machine learning could create new navigation tools, but McKinlay is not sure. “We will see smarter machines that are good at specific tasks, but the big change will come when they can understand what you are thinking and what you want to do,” he said.

In the end, McKinlay says it is very important that people can still control their own navigation. “Do you really want people to be helpless if the technology stops working or the battery dies?” he said. “Technology is not magic – it is just a tool.”

The start of the year is often a time when people feel unhappy about work. The next holiday is far away, and it is dark when you leave for work and when you come home. If you do not like your job, you might start thinking about finding a new one. But before you look for a new job, try to think about your situation. What other jobs could you do? We asked five people with unusual jobs about their pay, the hardest parts of their work, and why they enjoy it.

1. Dog-food taster
The job: Tasting dog food to make sure it is good enough for a top brand.
What you do: Open tins of new dog or cat food, smell them, and taste them. Philip Wells, the main taster for Lily’s Kitchen pet food, says that even though dogs taste things differently than humans, tasting is important to check the balance of ingredients. Tasting also helps to notice small differences in how the food is cooked, especially with dry food.
Typical salary: £20,000 for a beginner in the quality department. Wells says that an experienced technical director can earn £50,000 or more. This person also creates new recipes and gives advice about technical and legal matters.
Worst part: The deadlines. Wells says he actually likes the food. The meat in pet food must come from animals that are safe for humans to eat, according to the Animal Feed Regulations 2010. The company uses “human-grade” fresh raw food. Wells says some pet foods from other companies smell very bad, and just smelling them during market research can make him feel sick.
Job satisfaction: “No two days are the same.” Wells feels good knowing his work helps pets be happier and healthier. He also says that Lily, the border terrier, is an important part of the tasting team.

2. Hygiene technician
The job: Cleaning places that might be dangerous because of germs or chemicals.
What you do: Clean up crime scenes, road accidents, suicides, and houses full of rubbish, rats, and waste. Richard Lewis, a hygiene technician for Rentokil, says the job is about keeping people safe. He often works in very dirty places.
Typical salary: Beginners usually earn about £14,500, and the top salary is about £22,000.
Worst part: Cleaning up after suicides. Lewis says you get used to the dirty work, but the emotional side is still hard. He says you learn not to take your work home with you, and you need a sense of humor because some days are tough.
Job satisfaction: Lewis likes that his work is different every day. One day he might clean up after a dead body, another day he might clean a prison cell or go high up to clean a silo. He feels proud when he makes a dangerous place safe again, and he knows his work helps society.

3. Biogas engineer
The job: Building biogas plants in developing countries.
What you do: Connect systems that use human waste, animal dung, and other rubbish to toilets, so they produce biogas for cooking and lighting. Baburam Paudel, chief technical officer in Nepal for the charity Renewable World, says you need to know how big and what shape the mixing pit should be, how to keep the right temperature, and where to put the plant. You also have to convince poor communities that using waste can be useful, even though many people do not like the idea of connecting toilets to kitchens.
Typical salary: Beginners earn about £10,000, and a chief technical officer earns about £30,000.
Worst part: Paudel says it is hard to see people living with very little money. Also, you must be willing to get your hands dirty during building and inspections. The process of making biogas smells like rotten eggs, and it can be disgusting. There is no room for mistakes.
Job satisfaction: Paudel feels very happy knowing he helps people earn more money and lets girls go to school instead of collecting firewood. His work also improves health and hygiene for whole communities.

4. Eel ecologist
The job: Protecting the endangered European eel.
What you do: To check the size of the eels, ecologists walk into rivers and marshes, sometimes up to their armpits, and catch eels with their hands from nets. Stephen Mowat, an eel conservationist for the Zoological Society of London, says adult eels can be a meter long and weigh up to 2kg. They are not dangerous, but they are strong and slippery. Ecologists have to weigh and measure them, but the eels move a lot, so it is hard to look professional while chasing them.
Worst part: Eels are difficult to work with, and it can be embarrassing when an eel escapes. You also have to switch quickly between different projects. Mowat once had to cut open dead eels to look for parasites, then quickly change into a suit for a meeting. He says the worst part is not the eels, but learning how much damage people are doing to the environment.
Job satisfaction: Mowat enjoys working outdoors and seeing British wildlife up close. He thinks eels are beautiful, and helping eels also helps rivers, estuaries, and coastal areas. He believes this work is important.

5. Shopping channel presenter
The job: Selling and showing many different products on live TV.
What you do: Present for many hours, show the products, and act excited and knowledgeable about everything you sell. Shaun Ryan, a presenter for Ideal World TV, says he prepares by learning as much as possible about each product. He also needs to connect with all types of products and viewers.
Typical salary: A new presenter starts at a minimum of £30,000, and an experienced presenter can earn over £55,000.
Worst part: The hours are not good. Ryan says experienced presenters usually work during the busiest times, which means weekends, holidays, late evenings, and sometimes early mornings. His hardest task was selling slimming pants for women by himself, which he found very difficult.
Job satisfaction: Ryan loves the excitement of live TV and thinking quickly. He also enjoys knowing that thousands of viewers might buy the product he is showing.

Showing a car with a top speed of 25 mph, two seats, and no pedals or steering wheel might not seem exciting at a car show. However, Google in the US surprised the car and taxi industries when it showed its newest driverless car.

This electric car, which Google is testing near its headquarters in Mountain View, California, does not have normal controls like foot pedals. Instead, you use a smartphone app to call the car and tell it where to go. There is also a single STOP button between the two front seats in case the passengers need to stop the car.

The car does all the driving tasks by itself, including navigation, steering, speeding up, and braking.

Google is making about 100 of these cars for a two-year test. Sergey Brin, one of Google’s founders, said at a conference in California that the car is “still in the prototype stage,” but the project is “about changing the world for people who are not well served by transportation today.”

He said about the car: “You just sit there; no steering wheel, no pedals. For me, it was very relaxing. About ten seconds after getting in, I forgot I was there. It felt like riding a chairlift alone – a quiet moment I really enjoyed.”

Google says the main goal of the project is to make roads safer. The car has soft, impact-absorbing foam at the front and a plastic windscreen, so “it should be much safer than any other car for pedestrians.”

The cars are being specially built by a company in Detroit, but the company’s name has not been given. Google will use these cars to learn more about how to make driverless vehicles work. Google will run a test program with these cars, but they are not for sale yet.

One problem is that the cars need high-quality maps of the roads and surroundings before they can drive, because they cannot collect and process enough information in real time. Right now, there are detailed maps for about 2,000 miles of roads in California, but the state has more than 170,000 miles of public roads.

Google says it wants to license the technology to traditional car makers once it is ready. Some team members have worked on this project for more than ten years, even before joining Google.

However, some people are worried that driverless cars could replace taxi drivers. Dennis Conyon, the southeast director for the UK National Taxi Association, said, “If you get rid of the driver, then they’re unemployed. It would have a big effect on jobs.”

London has about 22,000 licensed black cabs, and Conyon thinks there are about 100,000 taxi drivers in the UK.

Steve McNamara, general secretary of the London Taxi Drivers’ Association, which has 10,500 members, said, “You won’t see these driverless cars in London for 20 or 25 years. Maybe by then, they’ll have a charging point – because there isn’t even one in London now.”

Other car companies, like Volvo, Ford, and Mercedes, are working on cars that help the driver, but these cars still have normal controls. Google’s car is different because it has no steering wheel or pedals.

Chris Urmson, director of Google’s self-driving car project, said the new cars do not have a steering wheel or brakes because there is no guarantee that a person could take control in an emergency. It is simpler to just have an emergency stop button.

Urmson said, “The cars will be very simple. We want to learn from them and improve them quickly. But they will take you where you want to go at the push of a button. This is an important step to make roads safer and change travel for millions of people.”

So far, Google’s self-driving cars have driven 700,000 miles without any accident caused by the computer. The company says that thousands of people die on the roads every year and about 80% of crashes are caused by human mistakes.

However, it may be hard to beat Conyon from the National Taxi Association. He is 79 years old, has been driving a taxi for 50 years, and says he has never had an accident.

Valdevaqueros is one of the last natural beaches in southern Spain. The sky above its golden sand is full of kites pulling surfers over the waves. Right now, the beach only has a small road with camper vans from Germany, France, Italy, and Britain. These vans are full of windsurfers and kitesurfers who come for the strong winds.

For many years, Valdevaqueros has been very different from the crowded, built-up beaches of Torremolinos and Marbella. But on May 29, the local council in Tarifa agreed to build a tourist complex next to the beach. The plan is for 1,400 hotel rooms and 350 apartments. Environmental groups are protesting because they say the project will damage the homes of protected animals. However, most council members think the main issue is jobs. Tarifa has 18,000 people, and 2,600 of them are unemployed. Spain is facing its worst economic crisis in at least 50 years, and people are worried about the future of the euro.

Sebastián Galindo, a councillor from the Socialist Party, said, “Old jobs like fishing are disappearing because fishing boats are being taken apart and there are fewer fish. So, tourism is the only solution, as long as it is sustainable.” The Socialist Party is in opposition in Tarifa, but they voted with the ruling People’s Party to approve the project.

Tarifa’s Mayor, Juan Andrés Gil, did not comment on the project, but Galindo said it meets environmental rules. The complex would be 800 meters from the coast, which is much more than the 200 meters required by law. This law was made to stop ugly buildings like those that ruined much of Spain’s coast in the 1960s and 1970s.

People against the complex say Spain already has a million empty homes, so there is no need for more. Last week, the central government suggested selling these homes by giving non-Spaniards residency permits if they buy property worth at least €160,000. The Socialist opposition in Madrid criticized this idea. Galindo said it is unfair to migrant workers, many from Morocco, who came to Spain during the economic boom. Morocco is only 14 km away and can be seen from Tarifa. “It helps rich people, not those who came here to help Spain,” he said.

Surfers are worried that new buildings in Valdevaqueros will make the famous Levant wind weaker and will not attract normal holidaymakers. “It’s not really a family place. Wait until they see what the Levant wind is like,” said Henning Mayer, who has come from Augsburg, Germany, for 20 years. “Ten years ago, they said they would build a new highway here. It didn’t happen, so I think it will be impossible to build new hotels.”

Tarifa is at the southernmost point of Spain, where Africa and Europe meet, and where the Mediterranean Sea meets the Atlantic Ocean. Campaigners say it is also very important for animals that migrate between continents.

The campaign to save the beach started just hours after the council voted for the project. The campaign has a Facebook page and is supported by groups like Greenpeace, the World Wide Fund for Nature, and Birdlife Spain. “It’s like putting a shopping centre in the middle of the Alhambra,” said Noelia Jurado, who uses her media skills to fight the project. She also said the resort would be near the ancient Roman town of Baelo Claudia. “They could be building on top of more Roman ruins. Nobody knows.”

The Andalusian College of Geographers also opposes the resort. Their early study says that “free areas,” including car parks, will overlap part of the Alcornocales National Park. They also say the site will affect two wildlife conservation areas. One area in Valdevaqueros is home to two types of bats that are in danger.

“Money is again more important than city laws and European environmental rules,” said Raúl Romeva, a member of the European Parliament and Vice-President of the Greens group. He also said the project is a problem because there is not enough water in Tarifa, which already has water shortages in the hot Andalusian summer. A lack of water recently made the Andalusian Supreme Court stop another complex in the region, which would have had golf courses, hotels, and luxury homes.

Many local people also ask why the resort should be built 10 km away, instead of on empty land near Tarifa’s old town, which has whitewashed walls, narrow streets, and a 10th-century Moorish castle. “My opinion, and that of other restaurant workers, is that we support the complex if it creates jobs in the town, which is needed, but we are against it if it only helps a few people,” said Cristóbal Lobato, who has worked at the same beach bar in Tarifa for 30 years. “If they build it in the centre of Tarifa, where there is space, then customers could visit shops, tapas bars, and restaurants.”

Looking at the green fields planned for building, biologist Aitor Galán, who studies environmental impacts, pointed to one of only two seaside vulture breeding grounds in Europe. “Anywhere else in Europe, this place would be fully protected, but here they want to destroy it and build,” he said. “They want to turn this into Benidorm, but people come here for the wildlife and the wind. By using the crisis and unemployment, builders and mayors can justify destroying nature.”

Scientists have made a “brain atlas” that shows how the meanings of words are spread out in different parts of the brain. The atlas looks like a colorful map over the brain’s surface, showing how words and their meanings are grouped together in certain areas.

Jack Gallant, a brain scientist at the University of California, Berkeley, said, “Our goal was to make a big atlas that shows how one part of language—word meanings—is shown in the brain.”

No single part of the brain holds just one word or idea. Each small area is linked to several related words, and each word lights up many different areas. These areas work together as networks to show the meaning of each word we use. For example, words like “life,” “love,” “death,” “taxes,” “clouds,” “Florida,” and “bra” each light up their own networks in the brain.

One researcher, who was not part of the study, called the atlas a “tour de force.” The atlas shows how new brain scanning technology can help us understand how the brain does important jobs. In the future, this technology could change medicine and other fields.

Alexander Huth, the main author of the study, said, “It might be possible to use this method to find out what words a person is hearing, reading, or even thinking.” One possible use is a language decoder that could help people who cannot speak, such as those with motor neurone disease or locked-in syndrome, to talk through a computer.

To make the atlas, scientists recorded people’s brain activity while they listened to stories from The Moth Radio Hour, a US radio show. They matched the words from the stories with the brain activity to see how groups of related words made certain brain areas respond. They found that 50,000 to 80,000 small spots all over the brain’s surface reacted to the words.

Huth chose stories from The Moth Radio Hour because they are short and interesting. The more interesting the stories, the more likely the people being scanned were paying attention. Seven people listened to two hours of stories each. Each person heard about 25,000 words and more than 3,000 different words while lying in the scanner.
