The atlas shows that words and related terms use the same brain areas. For example, on the left side of the brain above the ear, there is a small area for the word “victim.” This area also responds to words like “killed,” “convicted,” “murdered,” and “confessed.” On the right side, near the top of the head, there is an area for family words like “wife,” “husband,” “children,” and “parents.”

Each word is shown in more than one area because words often have several meanings. For example, one part of the brain responds to the word “top” and other clothing words. But “top” also lights up other areas, such as those for numbers, measurements, buildings, and places. The scientists have made an interactive website where people can explore the brain atlas.

Surprisingly, the brain atlases were similar for all the people in the study, which suggests that their brains organize word meanings in the same way. However, the scientists only scanned five men and two women, all native English speakers, and two of them were authors of the study published in Nature. People from different backgrounds and cultures might have different brain atlases for word meanings.

With the atlas, researchers can now study how the brain shows very different ideas, from numbers to murder and religion. Gallant said, “The idea of murder is shown a lot in the brain.”

Using the same data, the team is working on new atlases to show how the brain handles other parts of language, like sounds and grammar. But making a brain atlas for story structure has been difficult. Gallant said, “Every time we come up with a set of story features, we are told they are not the right ones.”

Uri Hasson, a brain scientist at Princeton University, praised the work. He said that, unlike many studies that only look at single words or sentences, Gallant’s team showed how the brain works in real-life situations. The next step, he said, is to make a more complete and exact brain atlas for word meanings. Hasson believes that one day it will be possible to find out what words a person is thinking by looking at their brain activity. This could have big ethical effects. One less serious use could be to see if political messages are getting through to people. “There are so many possible uses, and we are just starting to understand them,” he said.

Lorraine Tyler, a brain scientist at Cambridge University, said the research was a “tour de force in its scope and methods.” But she said the current atlas does not show small differences in word meanings. “While this research is groundbreaking, there is still a lot to learn about how word meanings are shown in the brain.”

A Canadian man became famous after he offered a free trip around the world to a woman with the same name as his ex-girlfriend. He has now returned from the trip with the woman he chose, but, to the disappointment of people following the story, they did not fall in love.

Jordan Axani, a 28-year-old from Toronto who works in real estate and started a charity, came back to Canada with Elizabeth Quinn Gallagher. However, he said they became like brother and sister.

In 2014, Axani made news when he offered a plane ticket to any Canadian named Elizabeth Gallagher. He had planned a three-week holiday with his ex-girlfriend, but after they broke up, he could not change the name on the tickets.

That is when his new travel partner, a 23-year-old student from Cole Harbour, Nova Scotia, joined him. Gallagher, who is called Quinn, answered Axani’s post on Reddit, along with other women named Elizabeth Gallagher, and was chosen. Before the trip, Gallagher said she already had a serious boyfriend, but many people still hoped the two travelers would fall in love. Sadly, this did not happen.

“It wasn’t easy and it didn’t happen right away. It took us about a week to really understand each other,” Axani said. They had some problems at first as they learned how to travel together.

“I want to be very clear,” Axani said after they returned to Toronto. “This was never about romance. It was only friendship. I do not see Quinn in a romantic way at all. There is no romantic future for us. She is a good friend. I think of her as a little sister, and that’s all. She feels the same way.” It took some effort to build this brother-sister, good-friend relationship. “By the end, we had a great way of traveling together. Sometimes we joked together, and other times we knew when the other person needed space.”

Even though they did not fall in love, Axani said the trip, which included Milan, Venice, Vienna, Prague, Khao Lak (in Thailand), and Hong Kong, was “fantastic.” His favorite place was Prague, where many people wanted to meet them.

“In just two and a half days, I think we met about 24 people. That’s a lot of stories, a lot of people, and a lot of love for Prague,” Axani said.

People followed their journey on Twitter and Instagram, and they were even recognized on the street in Hong Kong. “It was a real adventure. We had a lot of fun. We learned a lot about ourselves and each other. I think the trip went as well as it could have.”

Axani returned to Toronto at 3 a.m. on Monday, January 12, when the trip suddenly ended. He went straight to a meeting with his charity, A Ticket Forward. Axani started this non-profit group after his Reddit post became popular. He plans to give free trips around the world to people who have survived abuse, cancer, or war.

Axani is also talking to people about making his story into a TV show or movie, but he did not say what kind. “There is a lot of interest from production companies. We are making good progress.” About his love life, Axani said he is not looking for another Elizabeth Gallagher right now. “I’m not looking for anything, but life is full of surprises. We’ll see,” he said. “Life is a journey.”

A nasal spray containing the "love hormone" oxytocin might help children with autism deal better with social situations, according to US researchers. Brain scans of children with autism showed that one dose of oxytocin improved how their brains responded to facial expressions. This change could help make social interactions feel more natural and enjoyable for them.

The researchers said that using oxytocin together with behavioral therapies could help people with autism learn to manage social situations better. Kevin Pelphrey, director of the Child Neuroscience Lab at Yale University, said that over time, children might show better social responses, more interest in talking to others, more eye contact, and better conversation skills.

Autism is a developmental disorder that affects more than one in 100 people. It affects people in different ways, but usually causes problems with social interaction and communication. There is currently no proven treatment for the social difficulties caused by autism. Yale researchers have studied oxytocin as a possible treatment because it is important for bonding and trust. However, results have been mixed. One recent study found no clear benefit for young people who took oxytocin for several days. Pelphrey said oxytocin might help the brain learn from social experiences, and it could work best when used with therapies that encourage social interaction.

Pelphrey said, "Our study shows that oxytocin affects the brain and could work as a social enhancer when combined with behavioral treatments." The scientists used a method called functional MRI to scan the brains of 17 children aged 8 to 16 with autism. The children looked at pictures of cars or the eyes of people showing different emotions. The scans were done 45 minutes after the children used a nasal spray with either oxytocin or a placebo.

The scans showed that the reward system in the children's brains worked more normally after they took oxytocin. Their brains were more active when looking at faces and less active when looking at cars. The study was published in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences in the United States. Pelphrey told the Guardian that if these results are repeated, oxytocin might help treat the main social motivation problem in autism, for which there is no current treatment.

However, he warned that it is too early to use oxytocin as a treatment for social problems in autism and advised against buying oxytocin online. He said, "We don't want people trying oxytocin at home based on this or any other study. We don't know what they are buying. This is not a ready treatment. More research is needed."

Simon Baron-Cohen, director of the Autism Research Centre at Cambridge University, said, "This is an important new study showing changes in brain activity in key areas involved in social understanding in autism after oxytocin is given." However, he also said that oxytocin nasal spray did not change how well the children did on social tasks. It is also not clear if oxytocin only helps people with autism or if it has any unwanted side effects.

Also, the effects of oxytocin only last about 45 minutes, so there are practical questions about whether it could be used as a treatment.

Baron-Cohen said, "From a scientific point of view, this study has a lot of evidence to support more research, but doctors should be careful about using this hormone as a treatment until we know much more about its benefits and risks from larger studies."

Uta Frith, who studies autism at University College London, said, "According to this study, oxytocin may make faces more interesting, as shown by more activity in brain areas related to reward. Sadly, this effect is only seen in brain activity and not in behavior. Showing a change in behavior will be very important if nasal spray treatment is to be useful."

While swimming off the coast of Greece, Cathal Redmond saw colorful fish and thought he had taken great photos with his first underwater camera. But when he looked at the pictures on land, they were brown and unclear. He had taken the photos while holding his breath underwater and thought he did not have enough time to set up the shots. As an industrial designer, he believed he just needed a little more time to take better pictures of the fish in their natural home.

He decided to make this extra time possible. This led to his invention, the Express Dive. The Express Dive is a refillable air device that you hold in your mouth. It lets people swim underwater for two minutes. The device is meant to be something between snorkelling, which is simple but limited, and scuba diving, which lets you breathe underwater but needs heavy and expensive equipment. The first version of the Express Dive, which is still being tested, looks like a mix between a scuba mouthpiece and a water bottle.

Redmond, who is 27, says, “I wanted people to do more. Instead of just going underwater and holding their breath for 30 seconds, I wanted them to be able to do a bit more.” In 2006, Redmond, who is from Ireland, finished a scuba-diving course and loved being able to breathe underwater and watch fish. But he did not like wearing all the equipment, like fins, a weight belt, wetsuit, air tank, and mask.

He says, “I noticed I had about 50kg of equipment on me, and getting into the water felt strange when you are used to staying at the surface. It was a very unusual experience. The real problem is that scuba diving limits what you can do. Even though you can stay underwater longer, you have to plan your whole day around it. You have 20kg to 50kg of gear, so you can’t just walk on the beach and decide to go in. Planning is a big part of it. It takes a lot of effort and you have to learn many new things.”

Redmond made the Express Dive during his final year at the University of Limerick, where he studied product design. The device has two main parts. When above water, a fan in the mouthpiece pulls in air through a vent. The air goes around a small motor, is compressed through several valves, and is stored in a tank. The tank has a light that flashes green when it is full. When the user stops taking in air, the vent closes. When the user dives, air comes back through the mouthpiece.

The display, which the user can see, works like a health bar. It changes from green to red as the air runs low. The device can hold enough air for two minutes underwater and takes about two minutes to refill. Redmond says, “When you put the compressor, batteries, electronics, and scuba parts together, the big challenge was making it small enough to hold in your mouth with your teeth.”

The electrical parts are protected from water inside the case. The device is recharged using inductive power transfer, which uses an electromagnetic field, like wireless phone chargers, so there are no open wires.

Redmond says the mouthpiece feels like using a snorkel. He says it is like an extension of the lungs because the user takes a deep breath and then uses it underwater. “It is an extension of the body’s ability to store air,” he says. The prototype is made from strong foam, aluminium, and silicone. Redmond has tested the parts and shown that the motor can compress two minutes of air into the device and that it can be held in the mouth. He has not yet tested the device on a diver underwater for two minutes. But with more testing, Redmond believes he can make a safe device for swimmers.

Redmond recently won second place in the International James Dyson Award, which gave him £5,000 to develop the project further. He says the device will probably cost £280 and weigh between 1kg and 3kg, depending on the safety features.

Some people think two minutes of air is not much better than snorkelling, but Redmond says it makes a big difference underwater. Most swimmers can only hold their breath for about 40 seconds. “Two minutes is not a lot of time, but it is much longer than that,” he says.

On a normal day, Starbucks stores are busy places where people meet for business or join reading groups, all while enjoying their morning coffee. But Starbucks now faces a problem. The protest group UK Uncut plans to turn many Starbucks stores in the UK into places like nurseries, shelters, and homeless centers. They want to show people that Starbucks is avoiding paying taxes.

This protest was announced on the same day that a Starbucks executive had to answer questions from the House of Commons Public Accounts Committee. The committee wanted to know why Starbucks has not paid any corporation tax in the UK for the past three years, even though the company says it is making good profits in Britain.

Starbucks’ Chief Financial Officer, Troy Alstead, will try to fix the company’s image, which has been damaged by this tax issue. Some Members of Parliament (MPs) have accused the UK tax office (HMRC) of being too friendly with big companies. Conservative MP Richard Bacon said about Starbucks, “It smells. And it doesn’t smell of coffee – it smells bad.”

UK Uncut is trying to show a connection between government spending cuts, especially those that hurt women, and big companies not paying enough tax. Sarah Greene, a member of UK Uncut, said that services like shelters and rape crisis centers will lose money unless companies pay their fair share of tax. HMRC says about £32 billion was lost to tax avoidance in 2011.

Greene said the government could easily get billions of pounds to pay for important services if it stopped tax avoidance. UK Uncut became well-known after protests at Vodafone, Topshop, and Fortnum & Mason stores. They started focusing on Starbucks after a Reuters investigation found that Starbucks had paid only £8.6 million in corporation tax since 1998, even though it had sales of £3 billion in the UK.

Anna Walker, a long-time UK Uncut campaigner, said, “We want to show how the cuts affect women. So we will turn Starbucks stores into places like shelters and nurseries, which are losing money because of government cuts.” She also said, “Starbucks is a good target because it is on every high street in the country. This makes it easy for people to protest in their own towns.”

Other big international companies like Amazon, eBay, Facebook, Google, and Ikea have also been criticized for paying little or no corporation tax in the UK, even though they do a lot of business there. But according to a YouGov BrandIndex poll, Starbucks’ reputation has suffered the most.

Starbucks says it pays the right amount of tax. The company’s Chief Executive, Howard Schultz, said, “Starbucks has always paid taxes in the UK, even though some people say we haven’t. In the last three years, we have paid more than £160 million in different taxes, including National Insurance, VAT, and business rates.”

Margaret Hodge, who leads the Public Accounts Committee, told parliament last month that Apple, eBay, Facebook, Google, and Starbucks had avoided almost £900 million in tax. The Prime Minister, David Cameron, replied, “I am not happy with the current situation. HMRC needs to look at this carefully. We want these companies to invest in our country, but they should also pay fair taxes.”

A Starbucks spokeswoman said, “Tax law is very complicated, but Starbucks follows the tax laws and accounting rules in all 61 countries where we do business, including the UK. We are committed to staying in the UK for a long time. We have put information about our tax practices on our website.

“Starbucks helps the UK economy in many ways, not just through our stores and employees. We spend hundreds of millions of pounds with local suppliers for things like milk, cakes, sandwiches, and store design. When you include the jobs created by our investments, Starbucks’ total impact on the UK economy is more than £80 million each year.

“We hope UK Uncut will respect our employees and customers, and see the value we bring to the economy by creating jobs, apprenticeships, and paying our fair share of taxes in the UK.”

The government is preparing for thousands of legal claims from people who were put in prison and say they were mistreated during the last days of the British Empire. This comes after the High Court in London decided that three elderly Kenyans who were detained and tortured during the Mau Mau rebellion can sue for damages.

On Friday, the court rejected the government’s argument that too much time had passed since the seven-year rebellion in the 1950s, making a fair trial impossible. In 2011, the same judge, Mr Justice McCombe, also rejected the government’s claim that the three Kenyans should sue the Kenyan government, not Britain, because Kenya took over Britain’s legal responsibilities after independence in 1963.

Human rights activists in Kenya believe that more than 5,000 of the over 70,000 people detained by the British colonial authorities are still alive. Many of them may now sue the British government. This court decision may also allow victims of colonial violence in other countries to sue Britain.

Many other people around the world who were imprisoned and say they were mistreated during the conflicts that happened as Britain left its colonies may also think about making claims. These cases could show new evidence of harsh treatment of colonial subjects and change how people see recent British history.

The Foreign Office said the court’s decision could have “important and wide-reaching legal effects” and plans to appeal. A spokesman said, “Normally, people have three to six years to bring a civil case. In this case, it has been more than 50 years, and the main decision makers are dead and cannot say what happened.”

Friday’s important win for Paulo Muoka Nzili, 85, Wambugu Wa Nyingi, 84, and Jane Muthoni Mara, 73, came after three years in court. Their lawyers said they suffered “terrible acts of brutality,” including castration, beatings, and serious sexual attacks. A fourth person dropped out, and a fifth, Susan Ciong’ombe Ngondi, died two years ago at age 71.

In Nairobi, Kenya’s capital, the news from London was given to Nyingi and Mara by mobile phone. They were sitting quietly with supporters in a sunny garden and were very happy when they heard the news. They hugged, danced, and raised their hands to the sky to pray.

Nyingi, who was detained for about nine years, beaten unconscious, and still has marks from leg chains, whipping, and caning, said, “For me, I just wanted the truth to come out. Even my grandchildren should know what happened. People should get compensation so they can start to forgive the British government.” Mara said, “I’m very happy and my heart is clean.” When asked what she would tell her four children, she said, “I will tell them I won.”

In 2011, McCombe said there was “plenty of evidence” that there may have been systematic torture of detainees. On Friday, he said a fair trial was possible, especially because thousands of documents were found in 2011 after the Foreign Office admitted it had a secret archive of colonial-era files.

While trying to stop the claims, which the claimants’ lawyer Martyn Day called “morally wrong,” the British government’s lawyers admitted that all three elderly Kenyans were tortured by the colonial authorities.

Day said, “The British government has admitted that these three Kenyans were brutally tortured by the British colony, but they have used legal technicalities for three years to avoid responsibility. There will surely be victims of colonial torture from Malaya to Yemen, from Cyprus to Palestine, who will read this judgment carefully.”

Some people who watched the case closely are veterans of the Eoka rebellion in Cyprus in the 1950s. One has already met with the Mau Mau claimants’ lawyers. Any Cypriot claimants could use not only British documents but also the archives of the International Committee of the Red Cross in Geneva. These files are kept secret for 40 years and then made public. The Red Cross recorded hundreds of torture cases in Cyprus, where reporters called British interrogators “Her Majesty’s Torturers.”

There may also be claims from Malaysia, where many people were detained during the 12-year war with communist fighters and their supporters that started in 1948. Families of 24 unarmed rubber plantation workers killed by British troops are now fighting in British courts for a public inquiry. Many former prisoners of the British in Aden may also have claims, but since Aden is now part of Yemen, British lawyers may have trouble contacting possible clients there.

In the past, not sleeping much was seen as a sign that you were busy, important, and needed by others. People thought sleeping was for weak people. But now, Arianna Huffington’s book, The Sleep Revolution, is very popular. She tells people that getting enough sleep can change their lives and help them succeed. The sleep business is also growing fast. Many new companies are creating new ways for people to sleep better and are selling expensive sleep products. For example, luxury hotels now offer “sleep retreats” where you can pay over $1,000 for dinner and a movie about sleep. At home, you can buy things like a mattress cover with a sensor to track your sleep for $249, or a sleeping mask that measures your brainwaves for $299.

Sleep is now a big part of many companies. Some offices have nap pods, and Huffington thinks that nap rooms will soon be as common as meeting rooms. But why has sleep become so popular? Getting enough sleep fits well with a lifestyle where people spend a lot of money on things like green juice and fitness classes. Also, with new technology, people can now track their sleep and try to improve it, just like they do with exercise and diet. Huffington says sleep is not just for rest, but it helps you perform better. Now, getting eight hours of sleep is seen as a sign of success.

How does Arianna Huffington get her eight hours of sleep? She has about nine assistants who help her with everything, from running errands to planning her travel and even opening her website for her in the morning. According to the New York Times, most of her assistants can only work for her for about a year because the job is very hard and the pay is low, so many of them need second jobs. This means her assistants do not get much sleep so that Huffington can, and she can write books about it.

Getting enough sleep is not just about going to bed on time. It also depends on where you live and your life situation. Many studies show that poor people often sleep badly. It is hard to sleep if you are worried about safety or do not have enough food. It is also hard for the 15 million Americans who work at night or have changing work hours. Research shows there is a difference in sleep between black and white people in the US. One study found that white people sleep about 6.85 hours a night, while African Americans sleep about 6.05 hours and have worse sleep quality. This may be partly because of the stress from discrimination.

Who sleeps the most and best in America? Rich white women. This is probably the group Huffington is writing her book for. She calls her work a “revolution,” but really, it is just a new way to talk about sleep. The real problem is not that rich people think sleep is a waste of time, but that most people cannot afford to spend time sleeping.

Even though sleep is popular now, this may not last. Sleep helps people perform better, but it is not very efficient. The real goal is to find a way for people to need less sleep. The military is already working on this. In 2008, the Pentagon wrote a report about the idea of soldiers who could work well with only a few hours of sleep, like a giraffe, which sleeps only 1.9 hours a night. This would make soldiers much more effective. The report also talks about drugs called ampakines that could help people avoid the bad effects of not sleeping.

In the future, humans may find a way to stop needing sleep. Then, spending a third of your life sleeping will not be a luxury, but something only poor people have to do. At that point, we might need a new kind of sleep revolution.

People call him the Robin Hood of the banks. He took out many loans, worth almost half a million euros, and never planned to pay them back. Instead, Enric Duran gave the money to projects that tried to create and support alternatives to capitalism.

After hiding for 14 months, Duran does not feel sorry for what he did, even though he could go to jail. “I’m proud of what I did,” he said in a Skype interview from a secret place. He said the money helped create new opportunities. “It started a movement that helped us build alternatives. It also helped us make a strong network that connects these projects.”

Between 2006 and 2008, Duran took out 68 loans from 39 banks in Spain. He gave the money to social activists, paying for speaking tours against capitalism and for TV cameras for a media network. “I saw that social movements were trying to build alternatives, but they did not have enough resources or ways to communicate,” he said. “At the same time, our system depended on endless growth and created money from nothing.”

He said that taking money from banks was his way to protest and show what was wrong with the system. He started slowly. “I filled out a few credit applications with my real information. They said no, but I just wanted to see what they asked for.”

After that, the former table-tennis coach started to make a complicated system of accounts, payments, and transfers. “I was always learning.” By summer 2007, he learned how to use the system, applying for loans with a fake television company. “Then, I managed to get a lot.” In total, he got €492,000.

Duran was arrested in Spain in 2009, after six of the 39 banks that gave him money made charges against him. He spent two months in prison before being released on bail for €50,000. In February 2013, when he could have faced up to eight years in prison, he decided to run away instead of going to court. “I don’t think the court system is fair, because I don’t accept its authority,” he said.

He said his actions were part of a worldwide discussion about the economic crisis. His timing helped the anti-capitalist movement become more visible, just as many people in Spain were looking for new systems after the old one caused many problems in their lives.

He said that today, people in Spain would probably understand his actions better, but they would not be needed now. The anti-capitalist movement has grown from a small group to one supported by thousands of Spaniards, as shown by popular movements like the Indignados.

Because of this success, the movement can now support itself. “We can now create our own resources,” said Duran. He added, with some irony, that this is exactly why banks give credit – “to help you grow and become independent.” Duran is now also focusing on Spain’s justice system, by supporting restorative justice. “People in Spain who think banks don’t work believe I don’t owe anything. I have already done my part,” he said. “But there are some people who do not agree with us, and I think I should answer to them.”

He said that, in his case, he could give something back to the banks by sharing what he learned from taking out loans dishonestly. He could share his ideas about “which best practices work and which do not,” he suggested, “for the general public and for bank workers.”

Fake allergy tests are making thousands of people take treatments they do not need and put themselves or their children on poor diets. Sometimes, these diets are so bad that people become malnourished, according to a group of experts and charities. Allergies and food intolerances are increasing, but many people do not understand the difference between them. There are also many wrong diagnoses, which are causing real harm, said Sense About Science, an information group that worked with allergy specialists and charities to make a guide.

Tracey Brown, director of Sense About Science, said, “This is probably the biggest problem for science communication. Myths, misunderstood studies, and fake treatments mix with too many or too few diagnoses. The costs are high—some people do too much, while others do not do enough, even though their lives depend on it.”

Experts are worried that restaurants and caterers see so many people saying they have allergies (which can be dangerous), when they really have food intolerances (which are not dangerous). Because of this, restaurants may not be careful enough when serving someone with a real allergy.

Moira Austin from the Anaphylaxis Campaign said, “This is very important. If a caterer thinks someone is just avoiding a food to stop feeling bloated, they may not be careful. There have been deaths where people told restaurant staff about their allergy, but their meal still contained the food they were allergic to.”

The guide says that most allergy tests sold online or in shops are not based on science. One example is a home test that looks for IgG antibodies in the blood. These antibodies are part of the immune system, but the best medical evidence shows that high IgG levels do not mean someone has an allergy. The results are often positive in people who do not have an allergy or food intolerance.

The guide also says that other tests, like a mix of acupuncture and homeopathy that measures electronic resistance on the skin while holding food, do not work. Testing hair follicles is also useless, because hair is not involved in allergic reactions. Testing hair cannot give any useful information about allergies. People should also not believe that allergies are caused by “energy blockages” that can be found by muscle testing or cured by acupuncture.

Paul Seddon, a children’s allergy doctor from the UK Cochrane Centre, said, “I often see children on very limited diets because their parents believe, with good intentions, that they have many food allergies based on ‘allergy tests’ that are not scientific. This must stop, and it will only stop if we show these ‘tests’ are not real.”

Another children’s allergy doctor, Adam Fox from Guys and St Thomas’ Hospital in London, said, “Many patients come to me after sending their hair for testing or removing many foods from their children’s diets. It is very hard to fix this. There are two problems: children need proper diets, and avoiding foods that are not harmful makes life much harder. For example, a child who cannot eat wheat or drink milk cannot go to parties.”

Some parents believe their child’s tiredness, headaches, or eczema are caused by an allergy. It takes a long time and many tests to prove or disprove this. It is tempting to go to an alternative therapist who will do one test and give a quick, but wrong, answer.

Allergies are increasing in developed countries. The number of children diagnosed with allergic rhinitis and eczema has tripled in the last 30 years. Better diagnosis is part of the reason, but the real number of cases is also rising. This makes more people think allergies are the cause of their or their children’s health problems. The guide lists several myths about what causes allergies, such as E numbers in food colorings, “toxic overload,” and fast food.

You can no longer legally smoke a cigarette inside a bar in New Orleans, Louisiana, which is famous for its drinking culture. Many cities have banned smoking indoors, but New Orleans is different because it attracts tourists by promoting a “let the good times roll” attitude. A smoking ban here will have special effects because of the city’s unique culture.

Since Hurricane Katrina in 2005, the New Orleans city government has tried to make the city quieter. With help from neighborhood groups, the city has started to watch bars and nightclubs more closely and is trying to create a new rule about noise, especially music.

Bar owner William Walker does not like the anti-smoking law. He says, “This is just the wrong time for them to do this. Forcing people to smoke outside will make the tension worse.” Many of the best bars and live music places in New Orleans are in quiet neighborhoods. This mix of bars and homes is part of what makes New Orleans special. But now, some people do not like this arrangement, and some worry that the city’s music culture is in danger.

Martha Wood lives next to a loud bar with live music. She says, “The bar was one reason I bought my house, so I won’t complain about the noise.” She also manages a live-music bar that, after noise problems in 2013 (including complaints about loud smokers outside), became one of the first bars in New Orleans not allowed to sell drinks to go. “Now, any small mistake could get us shut down,” says Wood. “We recently put in a smoke eater to help with the smoke because we can’t open the doors at night because of the noise.”

The Maple Leaf club stopped allowing smoking in 2014, as did another club where artists wanted smoke-free nights. Zalia BeVille, manager of the All Ways Lounge, says, “Many venues were already starting to think about the performers, so I wish the city had let that happen naturally instead of forcing the ban on every bar.” Her club went smoke-free in 2013 because, she says, “The horn players and singers asked us for it.”

All Ways has an outdoor patio, but Lost Love Lounge does not. Its owner, Geoff Douville, likes the ban. Before, he felt he had to allow smoking to keep his business going. “I could not ban smoking in my bar unless it was a rule for the whole city,” says Douville. “If I made that rule alone, customers would just go to another bar that allowed smoking. So I need the rule to be the same for everyone.”

Many small business owners worry they will lose money if they cannot allow smoking. Neil Timms, a smoker who owns an English pub, saw the smoking ban in England. “Back home in Coventry, every pub I went to closed within a year of the smoking ban,” he remembers. To avoid this, he is building a patio.

Douville, however, thinks the ban is good for business. “Now, people who didn’t want to come to our bar because of the smoke can come,” he says. He is not worried about noise complaints: “No court will call a bar a ‘nuisance’ after the city has made a rule that forces people to smoke outside! I want to see a judge deal with ‘no loitering’ and ‘no smoking inside’ at the same time.”

Councilwoman LaToya Cantrell, who started the ban, disagrees with the worries. She says, “Bar owners must make sure their customers are respectful outside. Owners and bartenders should tell people to smoke outside but be respectful to the neighborhood. The idea that we can’t have clean air because it will cause noise problems is silly. It can be good for everyone. It’s about talking and working together.”

Cantrell also says New Orleans is special when it comes to a smoking ban. “New Orleans is known as ‘the City that Care Forgot,’” she says. “But we need to show we care about our people. The workers in smoky places are important to our hospitality industry, which is very important for Louisiana’s economy.” She adds, “New Orleans is also different because you can take your drink outside when you go out to smoke.”

Some people worried that the New Orleans Police Department did not need to spend time on smokers. So, the health department will give warnings and fines to bars. Customers are encouraged to fill out a form or call 311 and send photos with the date and time to report illegal smoking. Because of this, Neil Timms says he will follow the ban: “I don’t want someone to be smoking in the corner, have their photo taken, and then get in trouble.”

Geoff Douville is not worried. He is used to noise complaints and welcomes the ban. “The neighbors who complain about noise now are the same ones who wanted the smoking ban,” he says. In the end, Douville agrees with Cantrell that it can be good for everyone. “Of course they’ll complain,” he says. “But that doesn’t mean they’ll win.”

A degree in Spanish helped me get my first job as a journalist with an international news agency in Mexico City, but it did not stop me from making big mistakes as a new reporter.

I had just arrived in Mexico City after taking a Greyhound bus all the way from New York. The job interview tested my Spanish skills. In my new job, I spent my days outside at political rallies and my nights alone in the office, helping to organize news from troubled places like El Salvador, Nicaragua, Guatemala, and other parts of Central America. I also had to report on disasters like fires, floods, and explosions at fireworks factories.

As a reporter, I quickly learned that I was as bad at understanding numbers in Spanish as I was at doing math in English. Sometimes, when I made phone calls, I dialed the wrong number because I misunderstood it, waking up Mexican grandmothers at 2am instead of reaching the police. Even worse, I often reported the wrong numbers of victims in my stories. For example, I wrote that almost 83 people died in a fire at 6pm, but by 7pm, it turned out to be only 38. I said 12 people were hurt in a bus crash, but later it was only two. This kept happening. Finally, I got a call from the main office in Washington. An editor shouted, “I don’t know what training you have had, but has no one ever told you a death toll can’t go down?!”

Why are numbers in another language so confusing? It might be because different languages have different ways of saying numbers. For example, in German, 2:30pm is called “half three” and 21 is “one and twenty.” These differences can cause confusion, and some native languages have number systems that are so rare they might disappear.

Some experts think there is a connection between dyscalculia (trouble understanding math) and problems learning foreign languages, especially if you learn by memorizing, because this uses the same step-by-step thinking that people with dyscalculia find hard. But some students who have trouble learning languages from grammar books do better when they learn by speaking and listening in real life, where learning is more natural and not focused on grammar rules. For me, I always found languages easy, except for the numbers.

Maybe it is also because we often hear numbers in a foreign language without any context, or when we are not paying attention, so it is hard to suddenly understand them. I asked some friends who speak many languages, and many said they can speak well in French or Italian when ordering food, but they freeze when they have to say numbers, especially on the phone. Numbers seem difficult, but no one really knows why.

For me, having trouble with numbers in another language followed me from Mexico to other countries, and from Spanish to German and Portuguese. But in that first journalism job, getting the numbers wrong did not always mean I failed.

One night, a Mexican coworker found out that the American consul in the port city of Veracruz was being held hostage at gunpoint in his office. There was no senior English-speaking reporter in the office, so I had to try to call the consulate. I dialed the wrong number and was connected to another extension in the building. The person who answered was clearly the gunman. I talked to him for 15 minutes. I did not convince him to put down his gun, but my reputation as a new reporter still improved overnight.

No one knows if the economic crisis in Greece started before shisha, the drug now called the “cocaine of the poor,” or if shisha came first. But everyone agrees that shisha is deadly. At €2 or less for each use, it has become common in Greece, a country badly hurt by Europe’s financial problems.

“As drugs go, it is the worst. It burns your insides, makes you aggressive, and makes you lose your mind,” said Maria, a former heroin addict. “But it is cheap, easy to find, and everyone is using it.”

This drug problem has made things even harder for Athens’s health services, which are already struggling because of big budget cuts.

Shisha is the drug many homeless Greeks use after losing their homes to poverty and sadness. Addicts and officials say shisha is a type of crystal meth. It can make people very violent, especially because it is often mixed with dangerous things like battery acid, engine oil, and even shampoo.

Even worse, shisha is not only easy to find but also easy to make. This makes it popular in a society where people feel hopeless.

“It is a killer, but it also makes you want to kill,” said Konstantinos, a drug addict. “You can kill someone without even knowing it. And it is spreading faster than death. Many users have died.”

Charalampos Poulopoulos, the head of Kethea, Greece’s main anti-drug center, says shisha shows how bad the crisis is, with record levels of poverty and unemployment. He calls it an “austerity drug”—a cheap drug made by dealers for people who cannot afford expensive drugs like heroin and cocaine.

“The crisis has given dealers the chance to sell a new, cheap drug, a cocaine for the poor,” said Poulopoulos at a center for addicts in Exarcheia, an area in Athens known for anarchists. “Shisha can be sniffed or injected and can be made at home. You don’t need special skills. It is extremely dangerous.”

After six years of recession, Greece is suffering. Depression, drug and alcohol abuse have increased a lot. Crime has gone up as Greek society struggles with austerity measures that have cut people’s incomes by 40%. Prostitution, often used to pay for drugs, has also risen sharply.

“Many women are so desperate that they agree to have unprotected sex because they get more money,” said Eleni Marini, a psychologist with Kethea. “Shisha is linked to a strong sexual drive, but it damages your ability to think clearly. We are seeing more pregnancies among drug-addicted prostitutes.” In 2012, two sex workers gave birth on the streets of Athens.

At the same time, suicides have increased and HIV infections have reached epidemic levels. Drug addicts—about 25,000 people—are becoming more self-destructive. Experts say young Greeks, who face the highest youth unemployment in the EU at 64%, are most affected.

“The crisis has created a feeling of hopelessness,” said Poulopoulos. “People who might have stopped using drugs now have no reason to quit. There is a mood of misery, and people who know they won’t find work are harming themselves more. In Athens, where the crisis is worst, shisha is part of this problem.”

Greece’s government has tried to solve the problem by moving drug users and homeless people out of the city center. Police have cleared busy streets and shopping areas.

“But with these actions, the authorities are just hiding the problem,” said Poulopoulos. “They are actually making things worse by pushing these people closer to drug dealers, who offer them protection.”

At the same time, when more people need help, state-funded groups like Kethea have had their budgets cut by a third, as demanded by the “troika”—the EC, ECB, and IMF—to keep Greece’s economy going.

Since the crisis began in 2009, Kethea has lost 70 of its 500 workers. These cuts happened even though studies show that for every euro spent on programs like Kethea, the state saves about €6 in criminal justice and healthcare costs. “These cuts are a big mistake,” said Poulopoulos.

On the streets of Athens, where shisha is common, people are more and more afraid that austerity not only fails to help—it kills.

According to the UN, if the world reduced food waste by just 25%, there would be enough food to feed all people who do not get enough to eat. Every year, 1.3 billion tonnes of food—about one third of all food produced—is wasted. This includes about 45% of all fruit and vegetables, 35% of fish and seafood, 30% of cereals, 20% of dairy products, and 20% of meat. At the same time, 795 million people suffer from serious hunger and malnutrition.

Some countries are trying to fight food waste. For example, France has a law that makes supermarkets give unsold food to charities. The UN says food waste is a big problem for food security. Experts think that by 2050, the world will need to produce 60% more food than in 2005 to feed the growing population.

Reducing food waste would help save resources as the world tries to produce more food. The problem is global, but it looks different in different places. In developing countries, most food is lost by accident, often because of bad equipment, poor transport, and weak infrastructure. In rich countries, most food is wasted on purpose. Consumers throw away food because they buy too much, and shops throw away food that does not look perfect.

In rich countries, people and shops throw away 30% to 40% of all food they buy. In poorer countries, only 5% to 16% of food is thrown away. In Europe and North America, each person wastes 95 to 115 kg of edible food every year. In sub-Saharan Africa and south and southeast Asia, each person wastes only 6 to 11 kg.

Robert van Otterdijk, who works for the UN Food and Agriculture Organization’s Save Food programme, says that food waste is almost non-existent in developing countries. He says food waste happens in countries where people can afford to throw food away. For example, people in rich countries waste 222 million tonnes of food each year, which is almost as much as the total food produced in sub-Saharan Africa (230 million tonnes). In developing countries, food loss is common because of poor conditions in production, transport, and distribution.

Food loss and waste also harm the environment. The carbon footprint of food that is produced but not eaten is 3.3 gigatonnes of CO2. If food waste were a country, it would be the third largest emitter of greenhouse gases after the US and China. About 1.4 billion hectares, or almost 30% of all farmland, is used to grow food that is later wasted. More water is used to produce wasted food than is used for farming by any single country, including India and China.

Van Otterdijk says that climate change is linked to how we produce and use food. Food production is one of the biggest industries in the world, and if one third of it is wasted, it has a huge impact on land, water, energy, and greenhouse gas emissions. The countries that waste the most food are the US, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand, where people waste 39% of all food they buy. In Europe, people waste about 31% of all food they buy. In the UK, 15 million tonnes of food is lost or wasted each year. British people throw away 4.2 million tonnes of edible food each year. This means that 11.7% of all food bought is wasted, costing each family about £700 a year, or almost £60 a month.

The foods most often found in British bins are bread, vegetables, fruit, and milk. In the UK, the most wasted food by weight is bread—people throw away 414,000 tonnes (22.4%) of all bread they buy. By percentage, the most wasted food is lettuce and leafy salads—people throw away 38% (64,000 tonnes) of all they buy. The most wasted meat is poultry, with 13% of all edible parts thrown away. The most wasted fruit by percentage is melon, with more than a quarter of each melon thrown away.

The UK has made progress in the last ten years, thanks to campaigns to reduce food waste. Van Otterdijk says the UK is “one of the great successes” in fighting food waste. Between 2007 and 2012, avoidable food waste in UK homes fell by 21%, from 5.3 million tonnes to 4.2 million tonnes, mostly because people are more aware. Less food now goes to landfill. In 2000–01, only 14% of household waste was recycled or composted, but by 2011–12, this had risen to 43%.

Van Otterdijk says there is now a lot of interest in the problem of food waste, which helps local campaigns around the world. He says, “We have to do much more and it needs both public and private sectors to help. But if we keep going like this, maybe in ten years we will see big results around the world.”

Sometimes life is not fair. Mark Zuckerberg created Facebook and is now worth about $48 billion. James Goodfellow also invented something used by millions of people every day—the cash machine (ATM)—but he did not become rich. He only earned £10 from the patent and has not made any more money from it.

Goodfellow says, “You can imagine how I feel when I see bankers getting £1 million bonuses. I wonder what they did for the banking industry that was more important than what I did to deserve such a big bonus. It doesn’t make sense to me, but that’s how the world is.”

He is also upset that people do not see him as a good example for inventors and engineers. He made an important invention that made banks billions of pounds, but he got almost nothing. He asks, “Who would want to follow in my footsteps and get only £10 if they have a great idea?”

For years, people have argued about who should be called “the inventor of the ATM.” In 2005, John Shepherd-Barron received a UK honor for services to banking as the “inventor of the automatic cash dispenser.” But now, the UK government says Goodfellow invented the ATM, so after all the arguments, his place in history is now secure.

In the mid-1960s, Goodfellow was working as a development engineer. He was asked to find a way for customers to get cash from banks on Saturdays. Most people worked during the week and could not go to the bank. The solution was a machine that would give cash to a recognized customer. Goodfellow says, “I started to develop a cash machine, and to make it work, I invented the PIN (personal identification number) and a special coded token.”

This token was a plastic card with holes punched in it. The patent described a system with a card reader and buttons on the outside wall of the bank. It said, “When the customer wants to take out money, he puts his punched card in the reader and presses the buttons for his PIN.”

Except for the punched cards, this is almost the same as today’s ATM. After Goodfellow showed that his idea worked by making a model, prototypes were built, and the first machines were installed in 1967.

At the same time, Shepherd-Barron was making a different cash machine. His machine did not use plastic cards. Instead, it used cheques with carbon-14, a slightly radioactive material. The machine checked the carbon-14, matched the cheque with a PIN, and gave out cash.

Most people agree that Shepherd-Barron’s ATM was the first to be installed and used by the public. The first one opened at a bank in north London on 27 June 1967, a month before Goodfellow’s ATM was used by the public. However, Goodfellow’s patent was filed on 2 May 1966, 14 months before the London ATM started working.

The rivalry between the two men became stronger when Shepherd-Barron received an official honor for his work. Goodfellow says, “My biggest regret is that I did not say anything until John Shepherd-Barron got the OBE in 2005. He got this honor because people thought he invented the automatic cash dispenser. That really upset me, and I complained.” Shepherd-Barron is no longer alive to give his side, but in a 2005 interview, he said about Goodfellow, “I don’t know him, but the difference between Goodfellow and us was that we thought about the whole system, and that was important to the banks. His invention reminds me of the hovercraft, an elegant failure.”

The cash machine has become a very important technology, and nothing—like contactless payments, bitcoin, or wearable technology—seems to be stopping its growth. There are now 3 million ATMs worldwide, and the number is expected to reach 4 million by 2020.

Goodfellow agrees that he did not invent the idea of a cash machine, “but I did invent a way to do it. When people talk about the Wright brothers, they did not invent the idea of flying—everyone was trying to do it—but they did it and got the credit for inventing the airplane. So I think I should get the credit for inventing the cash dispenser.”

The good news for Goodfellow is that this is now happening. The website ATMInventor.com says, “Who invented the idea of an ATM? We think it was Luther George Simjian. Who invented the ATM as we know it? We think it was James Goodfellow in Scotland, because he had a patent in 1966. Who invented the ATM design we see today? We think it was John D White for Docutel in the US.”

Even better for Goodfellow, his achievement is now officially recognized in the latest edition of a 180-page guidebook called Life in the United Kingdom. In the section about “great British inventions of the twentieth century,” it says, “In the 1960s, James Goodfellow (1937-) invented the cash-dispensing automatic teller machine (ATM) or ‘cashpoint’.”

So after all these years, Goodfellow is finally being talked about with other famous inventors like John Logie Baird (television), Alan Turing (the Turing machine), Sir Frank Whittle (the jet engine), and Sir Tim Berners-Lee (the World Wide Web). When asked what he did with the £10 he got in the 1960s, Goodfellow says he thinks he spent it on a wild night out, adding, “It didn’t change my life.” But he says he had a good working life: “I was very happy doing the job I was doing.”

“There are definitely people who take MOOCs just because they are free and they enjoy being part of them,” says Dr. Ben Brabon from Edgehill University. His online course about vampire fiction is one of only two accredited MOOCs in the UK. Brabon is not criticizing people who join MOOCs; he is just explaining why some people sign up. Because MOOCs are open to everyone, with no entry requirements and no fees, people behave differently than in traditional universities.

MOOCs are a new and popular way to make higher education available to everyone. A lot of money from investors is going into these online platforms, which can deliver advanced and interactive courses to hundreds or even tens of thousands of people at once. Investors hope to find a way to make MOOCs profitable. Until now, universities have paid for their best teachers to create and teach these courses. One possible way to make money is by using the data collected about how and why millions of people join, interact, do assignments, talk to each other, or leave the course.

However, it is still not clear who MOOCs are really for. Are they for universities that want to attract international students by showing their best courses online? Are they for students in developing countries who want access to top universities? Are they for workers who want to improve their skills? Are they for people without qualifications who want to use MOOCs to get into higher education? Or are they for hobby learners who just want to learn about something they like?

Even though many people start MOOCs, very few finish them, says Brabon. For his vampire fiction course, 1,000 people signed up, but only 31 finished. “Almost all of those who finished already had a university degree,” he says. “So MOOCs may not be helping new groups of people get into higher education.”

“Learning online is different and needs advanced study skills,” says David Kernohan, programme manager for eLearning Innovation at Jisc, a charity that supports digital technology in UK education. “With MOOCs, there is very little support. Students are left on their own and usually do not get personal help. Instead, they get support from other students in online forums.” This means that online study can be hard for people without high-level qualifications, but MOOCs could be “a very good tool for continuing education,” he says.

As the number of part-time students drops because university degrees are getting more expensive, could free and open courses like MOOCs offer a new way to get a university education? Could someone earn a whole degree through MOOCs? “I don’t think that’s how MOOCs work,” says Brabon. He suggests a “blended approach,” which means mixing campus learning with MOOCs. He also thinks it might be possible to use MOOCs to create a global degree, where students take courses from different countries.

But this is still in the future. Right now, employers do not care much about MOOC certificates, because there is no guarantee about the quality of the courses or how they are graded. Accreditation, or official recognition, is now the main challenge for MOOCs if they want to be trusted by universities and employers, says Brabon. He is part of a group working to create agreed standards for MOOCs.

Some people hope that MOOCs will bring the best teaching from developed countries to students in poorer countries. But others are skeptical, saying that universities might use MOOCs mainly to advertise their courses to more international students, who pay higher fees.

Mike Sharples, chair of Educational Technology, does not agree with this negative view. He says MOOCs are mainly a way for universities to show and share their best teaching, and to get feedback from students around the world. He thinks that attracting international students is only a secondary goal, but MOOCs can still be a smart way to market universities. “If 20,000 people sign up for a MOOC, you only need 20 of them to later join a master’s course,” he says.

Matthew Poyiadgi, managing director at Pearson VUE, warns that soon UK universities may have no choice but to offer MOOCs in other countries. “If we don’t have a presence in China, we will be left behind,” he says.

“In South America, China, and Africa, there is a huge demand for learning, and some of the world’s best courses are now online,” adds Sharples. “If people really love learning, why not? The real challenge is to help these countries not only study MOOCs, but also create their own.”

Apple’s brand and logo are the most valuable in the world. They are worth almost $119 billion, which is more than the total value of all goods and services produced in Morocco, Ecuador, or Oman.

Apple is already the biggest company in the world. Its brand value grew by 21% in just one year, according to the Interbrand Best Global Brands annual report.

Apple is known everywhere for its simple logo: an apple with a bite taken out. In the 2014 report, technology companies like Apple became more valuable, while older brands like Coca-Cola, McDonald’s, and Gillette moved down the list.

Google’s brand value went up by 15% to $107 billion, making it second on the list. Coca-Cola is third, up 3% to $81.5 billion, followed by IBM at $72.2 billion and Microsoft at $45.5 billion.

Facebook had the biggest increase, with its brand value rising by 86% to $14.3 billion. It is now in 29th place, ahead of well-known companies like Volkswagen, Kellogg’s, and Ford.

Jez Frampton, the head of Interbrand, said that brands like Apple have become stronger because of the growth of digital and mobile technology.

Apple was started by Steve Jobs in his garage in Los Altos in 1976. It only entered the top ten of the Interbrand study in 2011.

The Apple logo was made by Rob Janoff in 1977. The bite was added so people would not confuse it with a cherry. Janoff said, “Our logo is a symbol of desire and knowledge. It is an apple with a bite, with rainbow colors in the wrong order. You couldn’t dream of a better logo.”

Graham Hayles, Interbrand’s chief marketing officer, said it is not strange that Apple’s brand is worth about one-fifth of the company’s total value. He said, “Apple makes a lot of money because it has a very strong brand. There is a strong link between branding and making a profit.”

Many technology companies moved up the list, but some went down. Nokia, a Finnish mobile phone company, fell 41 places to 98th, with a brand value of $4.1 billion, just ahead of Nintendo in 100th place, which dropped 33 places. Hayles said, “They are just barely in the chart now. This shows how important it is to keep innovating.”

For the first time, a Chinese company entered the top 100. Huawei, a mobile phone and broadband company, is in 94th place with a brand value of $4.3 billion. The US and Australian governments have partly banned Huawei because they worry its equipment could be used for spying.

Most of the top 100 brands are from the US. The highest non-US brands are Samsung from South Korea (6th), Toyota from Japan (8th), and Mercedes-Benz from Germany (10th). The top British brands are HSBC (33rd), Shell (65th), and Burberry (73rd).

Other fashion brands in the top 100 are Boss, Prada, and Ralph Lauren. Louis Vuitton is the highest fashion brand at 19th place, worth $23 billion, just ahead of H&M at 21st place with $21 billion.

Nike is in 22nd place with a brand value of almost $20 billion, ahead of Adidas, which is in 59th place with $7 billion.

He said customers now have more control than ever because of social media. Customers expect companies to interact with them, respond quickly, be available all the time, offer choices, and give a personal experience.

On top of a hill, above Northumberland’s beautiful Kielder Water reservoir, a group of people wait in a car park next to a strange wooden building. They are looking for darkness because this is Kielder Observatory, the centre of Britain’s newest industry: astrotourism. The people waiting are lucky. Many more people want to spend a night stargazing at the observatory, but only a few can go each night.

Inside, under a soft light, the observatory’s founder and main astronomer, Gary Fildes, gives a speech to his team and volunteers. The group talks about the chance to see the northern lights, but Fildes thinks it is unlikely. Instead, they decide to use their strong telescopes to look at Jupiter and Venus, and later, to find stars like Capella and Betelgeuse. Another special thing to see is the International Space Station.

Fildes, who is 49 years old, is a leader in the UK’s growing astrotourism business. The most important moment for Northumberland was in 2013, when the whole national park, about 1,500 square kilometres, was given Dark Sky Park status. It is the only one in England. Dark Sky Parks are rare. In 2013, a Star Count showed that only 5% of people in the UK can see more than 31 stars on a clear night.

The International Dark-Sky Association (IDA), based in Arizona, gives Dark Sky Park status only to places that work hard to stop light pollution. These places must also show that their night skies are very dark. In Northumberland Dark Sky Park, which is the new name for the area, it is so dark that Venus can make a shadow on the ground.

Duncan Wise, who works for the Northumberland National Park Authority, helped lead the campaign for dark-sky status. “We usually think of the landscape as everything up to the horizon,” Wise said. “But what about what’s above it?” Wise and others spent years preparing their application to the IDA. They collected thousands of light readings and made a lighting plan that controls how new buildings use lights in the area.

Their hard work has paid off. Many of the 1.5 million people who visit Northumberland each year now know about its Dark Sky status. “We get a lot of people coming here to see the sky now,” says a man at a car-hire company in Newcastle. “They come in autumn and winter, when it’s darkest. It’s good for local hotels because they get business all year now.” Local hotels now give guests night-vision torches and put out deckchairs at night.

Wise agrees that Northumberland should do more to use its special dark skies. He thinks the area needs a few more observatories so visitors can see what they came for. A new £14 million national landscape discovery centre will have an observatory when it is finished in a few years.

Fildes has big dreams. He is planning Britain’s first “astrovillage.” It would have the largest public observatory in the world, a 100-seat auditorium, a 100-seat planetarium, a telescope with a one-metre opening, and radio and solar telescopes. The project, which will cost several million pounds, would also have a hotel and could bring in 100,000 people a year—four times more than can visit the observatory now. Fildes believes the astrovillage will be ready by 2018.

However, Northumberland has competition. Galloway Forest Park in Scotland also has Dark Sky Park status. Since Exmoor became Europe’s first International Dark Sky Reserve (one level below Dark Sky Park) in 2011, many local businesses now offer stargazing trips and tours. The UK still has a long way to go to catch up with northern Chile, which has more than twelve tourist observatories and some of the clearest skies in the world. Teide National Park in Tenerife is also becoming a popular place for astrotourism.

Why do people want to look at the night sky? The media has helped. TV presenters like Brian Cox have made a new generation interested in stargazing. “Brian Cox has made astronomy easy to understand,” says Wise. “It’s not just for professors with telescopes anymore.” Technology has also helped. Apps like Stellarium can turn smartphones into small planetariums. But Fildes thinks the most important thing is that people are starting to enjoy what is above them. “If you had to build a new tourist attraction, what could be better than the universe?”

Benjamin Carle is 96.9% made in France, including his underpants and socks. However, six Ikea forks, a Chinese guitar, and wall paint with no clear origin stopped him from being 100% French-made, but nobody is perfect.

Carle, who was 26 years old in 2013, wanted to see if he could live using only French-made products for ten months. He did this for a television documentary. He got the idea after Arnaud Montebourg, the Minister for Economic Renewal, asked French people to buy French products to help the country’s factories.

For the experiment, Carle had to give up his smartphone, television, and refrigerator (all made in China), his glasses (made in Italy), his underpants (from Morocco), his morning coffee (from Guatemala), and his favorite David Bowie music (from Britain).

Luckily, his girlfriend, Anas, and his cat, Loon, are both French.

“Politicians say many things. I wanted to see if it was possible to do what the minister asked us to do,” Carle said.

He had three rules: eat only food made in France, avoid all foreign-made goods, and live on €1,800 a month (which is above the minimum wage of €1,430, to cover the higher cost of living in Paris).

At the start, Carle was surprised to find that only 4.5% of the things in his apartment were made in France. He had to get rid of the rest, including lightbulbs (from China) and green beans (from Kenya).

Without a refrigerator (because none are made in France), he had to keep his food cold on the window ledge.

He replaced his foreign-made clothes, including underwear, with more expensive French ones: underpants (€26), socks (€9), a polo shirt (€75), and espadrille sandals (€26). He could not buy jeans because none are made in France.

During the experiment, Carle searched supermarkets for 100% French-made products, learned to cook with seasonal French fruit and vegetables, brushed his teeth with a French-made toothbrush, and washed his underwear by hand until he found a French-made washing machine (which opened from the top and did not fit under the kitchen counter).

Going out with friends was difficult—no American films, no Belgian beer, no sushi or pizza. Staying home, with no sofa for the first few months and no television, meant listening to French singer Michel Sardou and reading French novels. French wine was allowed, and French-Canadian singer Céline Dion, but not French bands like Daft Punk, who sing in English.

He could not use his British-made bicycle or even a French car, because he found out that the cheaper Peugeot, Renault, and Citroën cars are mostly made in other countries. So, he bought an orange Mobylette moped.

The last things he changed were his computer, which he replaced with a Qooq (a recipe tablet that connects slowly to the internet), and his iPhone, which he swapped for an old Sagem mobile phone.

Carle said his goal was to help the French economy. He admits the experiment was both serious and a bit of a joke. At one point, he asked a French language expert if he should use English words like “cool.” He was told to use the French word “chouette” instead.

He found out that France does not make refrigerators (except for wine coolers) or televisions, but does make airplane seats and windmills. He joked, “Great. Nothing that will fit into my apartment.”

At the end of the experiment, Carle took out a bank loan to buy new furniture and clothes. An auditor said he was 96.9% made in France, and Montebourg visited him to give him a medal.

Carle’s conclusion: It is not really possible or even a good idea to live 100% made in France, especially with new technology. But that was not the main point.

He said, “This was not about French nationalism or patriotism. It was to show that we should think about how we buy things and make different choices. This is true in every country. If we want to save jobs and industries, wherever we are, we should think about supporting them.”

“A T-shirt is more expensive in France, but I know it is made by workers who are paid well and have good working conditions. I cannot be sure about a cheaper T-shirt made in Asia or Morocco. People could do more as consumers.”

Carle says he wants to keep supporting French industry and producers, but not 100%. “It is a full-time job just finding the stuff,” he said.

Virunga National Park is home to rare mountain gorillas, but a British company wants to look for oil there. According to a WWF report, the park could bring $400 million each year to DR Congo through tourism, hydropower, and carbon credits.

However, if the Congolese government and the company SOCO International start oil exploration in this UNESCO World Heritage Site, it could cause serious pollution and ongoing conflict in the area, says WWF. SOCO International is the only company that wants to search for oil inside the park. SOCO says their work would only happen in a part of the park called Block V and would not harm the gorillas.

SOCO’s chairman, Rui de Sousa, said that even though WWF disagrees, SOCO understands how important Virunga is for the environment. He also said that oil companies are still important for the world’s energy needs, and a successful oil project could help the country’s economy and society.

But Raymond Lumbuenamo, the WWF director in DR Congo, said that security in and around the park would get worse if SOCO starts exploring for oil. The security is already bad. The UN is fighting armed groups, and the M23 rebel group is inside the park. Oil would make things worse and could cause more conflict, like in the Niger Delta. Developing Virunga for oil will not help.

The area is already crowded, with more than 350 people per square kilometre. If land is used for oil, there will be more pressure on the rest of the land. Oil would not create many jobs, but many people would come looking for work.

There is also a risk because the area has volcanoes. Another eruption could damage oil equipment and cause oil spills in the lakes. Lumbuenamo said that Virunga’s natural resources should help the Congolese people, not foreign oil companies. He said the country’s future depends on sustainable development. He believes protecting the park is the best choice because once oil drilling starts, it cannot be undone.

Lumbuenamo also said that, even though the gorillas are safe now, it is unlikely the park will make $400 million a year. It is hard to earn that much money. Virunga used to be peaceful and could be again, but now the security is bad and the UN is fighting there. It is not as quiet as before.

The WWF report says the park’s ecosystems could support hydropower, fishing, and ecotourism. The park also helps provide clean water, control the climate, and stop soil erosion.

Virunga is Africa’s oldest and most diverse park, with over 3,000 types of animals. Many poor people now live there, including many who came after the Rwanda massacre in 1994.

The park could support about 45,000 permanent jobs. Also, people around the world would know the park is well managed and safe for the future, says the report.

The report says Virunga is valuable for DR Congo and Africa as the oldest and most biodiverse park. Plans to search for and use oil put Virunga’s value at risk.
