Swedish prisons are known for being modern and progressive. But are they too easy for prisoners?

In November 2013, Nils Oberg, the head of Sweden’s prison and probation service, said that four prisons in Sweden would close because there were fewer prisoners than usual. Even though crime rates did not go down, the number of prisoners in Sweden dropped by 6% between 2011 and 2012. Now, there are just over 4,500 prisoners. A similar drop was expected in 2013 and 2014. Oberg said he did not know why this happened, but he hoped it was because of the way Swedish prisons work. He said he hoped that their work to help prisoners change and not commit crimes again was making a difference.

Kenneth Gustafsson, the governor of Kumla Prison, Sweden’s most secure prison, said that prisons in Sweden are very different now compared to when he started working in 1978. He does not think prisons are too soft. When he started, prisons focused a lot on treating prisoners well—maybe too well, some people thought. But after several escapes in 2004, they had to focus more on security.

Sweden still tries to be kind when giving sentences, even for serious crimes. Prison sentences are usually not longer than ten years. People who get life sentences can ask the court after ten years to change their sentence to a fixed number of years, usually between 18 and 25 years. Sweden was the first country in Europe to use electronic tags for criminals and tries to keep prison sentences short by using community service and other programs. These programs have helped stop criminals from committing more crimes.

In Sweden, about 30 to 40% of prisoners commit another crime within three years. This is about half the rate in the UK. One reason for fewer prisoners and less reoffending is that people under 15 cannot be held responsible for crimes. In the UK, children as young as ten can be sent to prison, and young people under 21 have the highest rates of reoffending. In Sweden, no one under 21 can get a life sentence, and they try to keep young people out of prison.

Another reason for fewer prisoners in Sweden is the support given after prison. The government runs a probation service that supervises people on probation and gives treatment to those with drug, alcohol, or violence problems. About 4,500 volunteers from the public help by supporting and befriending people under supervision.

A former prisoner, Peter Soderlund, now runs a group called X-Cons Sweden. He spent almost three years in prison for drug and weapons crimes and was released in 1998. He got help from an organization called Kris, which is run by former prisoners. Both Kris and X-Cons help prisoners return to society after they are released. Soderlund said that when he was in Osteraker Prison, he was treated well, but not all prisons were the same. He met many people who needed help. After getting help from Kris, he wanted to help others. With X-Cons, they meet prisoners at the gate, help them find a place to live, and give them support.

Gustafsson says that in Sweden, they believe strongly in helping prisoners change. He says that some people cannot or do not want to change, but most prisoners want to change, and it is important to help them.

Swedish prisons are known for being modern and kind. But some people ask if they are too soft. In November 2013, Nils Oberg, the head of Sweden’s prison and probation service, said that four prisons in Sweden will close. This is because there are fewer prisoners than before. 

The number of crimes has not gone down, but from 2011 to 2012, there were 6% fewer people in prison. Now, there are a little more than 4,500 prisoners in Sweden. Oberg said he does not know why there are fewer prisoners, but he hopes it is because the prisons help people not to commit crimes again. He said, “We hope our work to help prisoners change has made a difference.”

Kenneth Gustafsson, the boss of Kumla Prison, Sweden’s most secure prison, said, “Prisons in Sweden are very different now from when I started working in 1978. At that time, prisoners were treated very well, maybe too well. But after some prisoners escaped in 2004, we made the prisons safer.”

In Sweden, most prison sentences are not longer than ten years. Sweden was the first country in Europe to use electronic tags for criminals. Sweden also tries to give short prison sentences and uses punishments in the community instead of prison when possible. These things have helped stop many people from committing crimes again.

In Sweden, about 30 to 40% of prisoners commit another crime after leaving prison. In the UK, this number is about twice as high. Another reason for fewer prisoners in Sweden is that children under 15 cannot be punished for crimes. Also, people under 21 cannot get a life sentence, and Sweden tries not to send young people to prison.

Another reason for fewer prisoners is the help people get after leaving prison. The government has a probation service that helps people with problems like drugs, alcohol, or violence. About 4,500 people in Sweden volunteer to help and support people who have been in prison.

Gustafsson said, “In Sweden, we believe in helping prisoners change. Some people cannot change, but most want to change, and we must help them.”

You have worked eight hours in the office. The most important tasks are finished; the rest can wait until tomorrow. At this point, many workers would think about going home.

However, for millions of Japanese workers, leaving work early enough to have dinner at home can make others think they are not loyal to their company.

For many years, the Japanese government let companies push workers to be as productive as possible. Now, the government wants to change Japan’s culture of overwork. It is thinking about making a law that would require workers to take at least five days of paid holiday each year.

Japanese workers can get an average of 18.5 days of paid holiday each year, which is only two days less than the world average. The minimum is ten days, plus 15 national holidays. But in reality, very few workers use all their days off. Most take only nine out of their 18.5 days, according to the labor ministry. In Britain, many workers expect a two-week summer holiday. In Japan, taking a four-night trip to Hawaii feels like too much luxury.

By the end of the decade, the government hopes the new law will help Japanese workers act more like British workers, who use an average of 20 days of paid holiday, or French workers, who take 25 days.

Japan’s strict work culture helped the country become an economic superpower. Japanese workers are respected around the world for their dedication, but they have little time for anything except work.

Japan’s low birth rate and falling population are partly because couples do not have enough time to start families. More workers are getting sick from stress, or even dying from karoshi, which means death from overwork.

Japanese people still work very hard, even though studies show that working longer hours does not always make people more productive.

About 22% of Japanese people work more than 49 hours a week. In the US, it is 16%, and in France and Germany, it is 11%. In South Korea, 35% of workers do even more hours.

Erika Sekiguchi works 14 hours a day and gives up many of her paid holidays. But she is not unusual. She is 36 and works for a trading company. In 2014, she used only eight of her 20 paid vacation days, and six of those were for sick leave. “Nobody else uses their vacation days,” Sekiguchi said.

Yuu Wakebe, a health ministry official who manages work hour policies, says he does 100 hours of overtime each month. He says this is because of pressure to work as many hours as your coworkers. “It is a worker’s right to take paid vacations,” Wakebe said. “But working in Japan means you need a lot of volunteer spirit.”

The fear of being left out at work is causing more stress-related sickness, early death, and suicide. Official data shows about 200 people die each year from heart attacks, strokes, and other karoshi events because of long work hours.

Prime Minister Shinzo Abe is not known for taking long holidays. But even he has said that companies expect too much from their workers and that working hours in Japan are too long.

You have worked eight hours in the office. You have finished your most important work for the day. Most people would think about going home now. 

But in Japan, millions of workers do not go home early. If they leave work and get home in time for dinner, people say they are not loyal to their company.

Now, the Japanese government wants to change this culture of working too much. The government wants workers to take at least five days of paid holiday every year.

Japanese workers can get about 18.5 days of paid holiday each year. Companies must give at least ten days of paid holiday, plus 15 national holidays. But most workers do not take all these days. Most workers only take nine days of holiday, says the labour ministry. 

In Britain, many workers think they should have a two-week summer holiday. But in Japan, workers think a four-night trip to Hawaii is a big treat.

By 2020, the government hopes that Japanese workers will take more holidays, like workers in Britain, who take about 20 days of paid holiday each year, and workers in France, who take about 25 days.

Japanese workers are respected in other countries because they work hard for their companies. But they often have no time for other things.

Couples do not have time to start families. Because of this, Japan has a low birth rate and the number of people in the country is going down. More workers are getting sick from stress or even dying because they work too much.

About 22% of Japanese workers work more than 49 hours a week. In the US, it is 16%. In France and Germany, it is 11%, says the Japanese government.

Erika Sekiguchi is 36 years old. She says, “Nobody else uses their vacation days.” She works 14 hours a day and used only eight of her 20 paid vacation days in 2014. Six of these days were for sickness.

Yuu Wakebe works at the health ministry. He says he does 100 hours of extra work every month. “It is a worker’s right to take paid vacations,” he says. “But workers in Japan have to do a lot of extra work for no money.”

Workers are afraid their co-workers will think they are lazy if they take holidays. This is one reason why more people are getting sick from stress, dying early, or killing themselves. About 200 people die every year in Japan from heart attacks and strokes because of long hours and hard work.

Famous British writer David Mitchell is used to critics looking closely at his books. So, he feels relieved that his newest work will not be read by anyone until the year 2114. He finished writing it at 1am on a Tuesday, just before a car took him to the airport for a flight to Norway.

Mitchell is the second writer to join the Future Library project, started by Scottish artist Katie Paterson. In 2014, 1,000 trees were planted in Oslo’s Nordmarka forest for this project. The first writer, Margaret Atwood, gave her story called Scribbler Moon in 2015. Every year for the next 100 years, one writer will give a new story. These stories will only be read in 2114, when the trees are cut down to make paper for printing all 100 stories.

Each year, a new writer is chosen by a group of experts and Paterson, as long as she is alive. The writer’s name is announced, and they travel to the forest near Oslo to give their story in a small ceremony.

Mitchell said, “It’s a small sign of hope in a time with a lot of sad news. It shows that maybe in 100 years, people, trees, books, and readers will still be here. The Future Library gives hope that we are stronger than we think and that civilization will continue.”

Mitchell said writing this book felt freeing because he will not be alive to see if people think it is good or bad. But he also felt pressure because he is between Margaret Atwood and probably another great writer. He joked, “It had better be good. I would look silly if they read it in 2114 and it wasn’t any good.”

Mitchell usually spends a lot of time making his writing perfect. He said, “I usually over-polish my work. But this time was different—I wrote until the last minute. The first two-thirds are polished, but I didn’t have time for the last part. It felt freeing.”

Paterson asked the writers to write about imagination and time, but they can choose how to do this. Mitchell only shared the title of his story, From Me Flows What You Call Time, at a ceremony in the Norwegian woods near the 1,000 trees. The title comes from a piece of music by Japanese composer Toru Takemitsu. Mitchell said the story is longer than he expected, but he did not give any more details.

When he gave his story in the forest, Mitchell read a short story and a poem by William Wordsworth called A slumber did my spirit seal to the people there, including children and adults. The poem’s ending, “Rolled round in earth’s diurnal course / With rocks, and stones, and trees,” felt right for the forest, which will be cared for over the next 98 years before it is used for the Future Library books.

Mitchell wrote for the Future Library that it feels strange to think his writing will still be interesting to people in the future. He also said it feels quiet and simple to work hard on a story that no one will ever thank him for or say, “Nice job” or “I loved that part.”

Now that his story is finished, it will be sealed and kept with Atwood’s story in a special wooden room in Oslo’s new public library, which will open in 2019. A group of experts will watch over the stories until they are printed. Mitchell said his story is now “as gone from me as a coin dropped in a river.”

An octopus escaped from the National Aquarium in New Zealand by leaving its tank, sliding down a 50-metre drainpipe, and going into the sea. The octopus, named Inky, is a common New Zealand octopus. He escaped because the lid of his tank was left slightly open by accident. Staff think that during the night, when no one was there, Inky climbed to the top of his glass tank, went down the side, and moved across the aquarium floor.

Rob Yarrell, the national manager of the aquarium in Napier, said that octopuses are well known for escaping. He does not think Inky was unhappy or lonely, because octopuses like to be alone. But Inky was very curious and wanted to see what was outside. That is just how he is.

One idea is that Inky moved across the aquarium floor, which is three or four metres, and then went into a drainpipe that leads straight to the sea. The drainpipe is 50 metres long and goes to the water at Hawkes Bay, on the east coast of New Zealand’s North Island.

It is also possible that Inky escaped by squeezing into an open pipe at the top of his tank, which goes under the floor to the drain. When staff came in the next morning and saw his tank was empty, Yarrell was very surprised. He and the staff felt sad, but Inky was always a surprising octopus.

Reiss Jenkinson, who takes care of the exhibits at the aquarium, is sure that Inky was not stolen. He understands octopus behaviour very well. He has seen octopuses escape from boats through small pumps. Also, the security at the aquarium is too strong for anyone to steal Inky, and there is no reason to do so.

Octopuses have no bones, so they can fit into very small spaces and squeeze through holes as small as coins. They are also very smart and can use tools. At the Island Bay Marine Education Centre in Wellington, one octopus used to visit another tank at night to steal crabs and then return to its own tank. Another octopus there, named Ozymandias, broke a world record for opening a jar.

A local fisherman brought Inky to the National Aquarium a few years ago after finding him in a fishing pot. Yarrell said Inky looked rough and had very short arms because he had been living on the reef and fighting with fish, so he was not in good shape. Inky, who is about the size of a rugby ball, was a very smart octopus. He was friendly and popular with visitors. The aquarium has another octopus, Blotchy, but he is smaller and does not have Inky’s personality.

The aquarium does not plan to increase security because they do not think another escape will happen. However, the staff now know more about what octopuses can do. The aquarium is not looking for a new octopus, but if a fisherman brings another one, they might accept it. Yarrell said there is always a chance that Inky could come back.

Why do they do it? The top football referees of the future smile when you ask them this question. This season, people have criticized referees more than before, and some former referees have started to complain about the quality of refereeing. This is important because referees usually support each other no matter what.

So why do they do it? Why spend many hours driving around the country? Why make people angry by enforcing rules? Why try to move up until you can make decisions on TV in front of millions of people who watch you closely with many cameras and slow-motion replays?

You might find the answer on Lee Swabey’s face just after he finishes a match where Grimsby beat Woking 2-1, a game in the fifth level of English football. He gets what all referees want after a match: twenty-two handshakes, he says proudly. Getting a handshake from every player and a “well done” from both managers means he did a good job. He loves the feeling, or “buzz,” when a game goes well. He says, “I wouldn’t spend so much time away from my family if this didn’t mean everything to me.”

Swabey is one of the referees respected by the Professional Game Match Officials Limited (PGMOL). He knew he was being watched at that match. PGMOL’s boss, Mike Riley, and his colleague Steve Dunn were there, watching every important move the referees made.

A few weeks earlier, Riley, Dunn, and another former referee, Peter Jones, went to another level-5 match to watch a young referee, John Brooks. Brooks says, “I hope to get promoted to the Premier League and referee some of the top games in this country.”

But that day, the PGMOL group only saw how Brooks handled a difficult situation: he had to cancel the match because the pitch was frozen. This is part of the experience Brooks needs before he can referee more important games. There are many problems to solve—clubs often do not want to cancel a match late, especially when they have to pay staff who will not get any ticket money.

Brooks called his coach for advice and made the hard but correct decision. Later, the club secretary came with envelopes to pay the referees for their time. The match fee at level 5 is £95, so it is clear that referees do not do it for the money.

Brooks, like Swabey, wants to move up. He knows that dealing with disappointments is a big part of being a referee. How does he feel when he watches football on TV and sees a referee being criticized? “Not great,” he says. “I sometimes wish people understood the time and effort we put in. It is easy to criticize a decision, but we do everything to get these decisions right. Sometimes, people will not like you, but if you cannot accept that, you are probably in the wrong job.”

The former referees agree that today’s referees have much better support, education, and tools than they did. When Riley was a young referee, he had to buy his own books on psychology and nutrition because there was no information for him.

Brooks, on the other hand, has a coach he can call. They talk every week, discuss his games, watch videos of important decisions, and work on how to improve. He also has help from a sports psychologist, Liam Slack, who gives him advice and an exercise plan to help him run the 11 kilometers needed during a game.

Brooks says psychology is very important for him. “One thing we have talked about is forgetting decisions and moving on,” he explains. “There may be a big decision in the first 30 seconds of the game. After that, you need to stay focused for the next 89 minutes and not worry about that decision. Liam has taught us ways to forget about it. Working with the sports psychologist is really important for mental strength.”

About technology, the three former referees all agree it is good. Riley says, “We all support anything that makes the referee’s job better and helps them do better on the pitch.” The goal is to make fewer mistakes. After all, a bad decision can stay with you for a long time. “The rest of your life,” adds Jones, laughing.

Behind the bright lights and mirrors in stores, cameras are watching you. If you pick up a boot, a camera will check that you do not put it in your bag. When you enter a department store, you are being watched. But now, new technology is less interested in stopping shoplifting and more interested in your age, gender, and shopping habits.

A few months ago, the IT company Computer Sciences Corporation (CSC) wrote a report saying that about 30% of stores use facial recognition technology to follow customers in the store. Facial recognition is a technology that can identify people by looking at their faces and comparing them to a database. It uses devices like Intel RealSense cameras, which can study everything from your facial expressions to the brands of clothes you are wearing.

Intel spokesman Joe Jensen says that the goal of using RealSense technology in shops is not to make databases about specific people’s lives, but to create general models of people’s lifestyles and shopping habits. “We do not need to know a particular customer. We need to know that this shopper has these characteristics, and when these characteristics are present, this is what a person usually does.”

If you combine recognition technology with databases of past customer behavior, you can start to predict what a person might do in a shop. For example, if a woman is walking quickly to the sock section, you can use that information to guess she wants to buy socks. This could let a store show special ads on screens just for her. If she looks like someone who wants to buy socks, the store will show her ads for socks.

If this sounds familiar, it is because online stores have used these methods for years. If you search for something on Amazon, you will see ads for similar products on other websites. But it is not easy to use these systems in real stores. People do not react to cameras the same way they react to browser cookies.

Hoxton Analytics, a group of data scientists in London, has made a technology that uses machine learning and artificial intelligence to group people by the shoes they wear. By looking at the style and size of people’s shoes as they walk past a sensor, the system can guess a customer’s gender with 75-80% accuracy.

Owen McCormack, the CEO of Hoxton Analytics, says that the system was partly created as a response to facial recognition. “My idea was, why don’t we just look at the clothes someone is wearing?” he said. “If I showed you a photo of someone’s body, you could probably tell me their gender. But pointing a camera at someone’s chest or hips feels just as strange as facial recognition. So, what about people’s shoes?”

People often use the word “creepy” when talking about in-store tracking. For stores and data scientists, the goal is to get information without making people feel uncomfortable.

For McCormack, the main point is that personal information is not collected. “Right now, shops are doing many very invasive things, but we just do not know about it. What we say is that if you know someone is male or female, your advertising will be much more effective. If you know that everyone in your shop right now is male, you will advertise PlayStations, not hairdryers.”

From the store’s point of view, it makes sense that physical shops want the same information that online shops collect. We allow this online, so why not in real life? Online, you get a pop-up asking you to accept cookies. But you cannot ask for people’s permission in the same way when they move from one shop to another.

It is also true that the younger generation, who grew up with online shopping, do not see online advertising as so invasive. In the CSC report, a survey showed that 72% of people aged 55 or older said they felt very uncomfortable with these technologies in physical shops. But only 51% of people aged 16-24 said they were uncomfortable.

Are younger people more open because they know more about digital technology, or do they trust companies that offer free services? Is this kind of technology always creepy, or does it depend? In any case, there are more and more eyes watching between the shelves, and they care a lot about what you are wearing.

When you go into a department store, cameras are watching you. If you pick something up, a camera checks that you do not put it in your bag. Cameras follow you as you walk around the store. But now, new technology is not just looking for people who steal. It is more interested in your age, if you are a man or a woman, and how you shop.

In most places, people do not usually eat insects, but this is starting to change. In spring 2013, there will be a campaign to show people that eating insects is not disgusting and to try to sell insects in supermarkets.

In April, London will have a festival called Pestival 2013, where people will talk about eating insects. The festival will have a restaurant from the Nordic Food Lab, the team behind the famous Danish restaurant Noma. In 2012, Noma served dishes with ants at Claridges hotel in Mayfair, and most tickets were sold out.

Noma has been named the world’s best restaurant by Restaurant magazine for three years. Its chef, René Redzepi, says ants taste like lemon, and a puree made from fermented grasshoppers and moth larvae tastes like strong fish sauce. Bee larvae can be used to make a sweet mayonnaise instead of eggs. Scientists are always finding new ways to use insects in food.

In March, a BBC documentary will show food writer Stefan Gates looking for and eating deep-fried locusts and barbecued spiders. But there is a serious reason behind this. Many experts think that eating insects is good for the environment.

The United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) has been supporting projects since 2011 to encourage eating and farming insects in southeast Asia and Africa. In these places, about two billion people already eat insects and larvae as a normal part of their diet. In 2012, the FAO published a list of 1,909 types of edible insects and plans to hold a big international meeting about this food in 2013.

There are 40 tonnes of insects, so it is unlikely they will become endangered. Redzepi said, “I know it is not normal to eat bugs in the western world, but why not? In southeast Asia, it is common. People eat insects all over the world. If you like mushrooms, you have probably eaten many worms without knowing it. We also eat honey, which is actually bee vomit. Think about that next time you put honey in your tea.”

He also said that the main idea of the Nordic Food Lab is: Nothing is not edible.

Insects are very important for life on Earth. There are more than a million species, making them the most varied group of animals. But people often do not like them and kill them just because they are there.

In the next 30 years, the world’s population will grow to nine billion. Already, one billion people do not have enough food. This growth will put more pressure on farmland, water, forests, fish, and other resources.

Meat is becoming more expensive, not only in money but also because forests are destroyed to make fields or to grow food for cattle. Cows also produce methane gas, which is bad for the environment. Livestock farming creates a lot of greenhouse gases: 35% of the world’s methane, 65% of its nitrous oxide, and 9% of its carbon dioxide.

Edible insects make fewer gases, have good protein, vitamins, and amino acids, and need only a quarter of the food that sheep need, and half as much as pigs and chickens, to make the same amount of protein. They also make less greenhouse gas and ammonia than cows and can be raised on organic waste. China already has large maggot farms. Zimbabwe has a successful caterpillar business, and Laos got almost $500,000 from the FAO to start an insect-harvesting project.

A study by FoodServiceWarehouse.com said that if people stopped eating pork and beef and ate crickets and locusts instead, greenhouse gas emissions could go down by up to 95%. But maybe the most fair thing about eating insects is that, when we die, insects get a chance to eat us.

In Western countries, people usually do not eat insects. But in some other parts of the world, insects are an important food. In spring 2013, people will try to show that eating insects is not disgusting. Soon, we may be able to buy insects in supermarkets.

Coal will probably become as important as oil as the world’s main source of energy in the next five years. This could be very bad for the climate, says the world’s top energy economics group.

One big reason for the rise in coal use is the huge increase in shale gas use in the US. New research from the International Energy Agency (IEA) shows that coal use is going up in almost every country, even in places that want to cut carbon emissions. The only exception is the US, where shale gas is now more popular than coal. Because the US uses less coal, coal prices have dropped around the world. This makes coal more attractive, even in Europe, where the Emissions Trading Scheme was supposed to make coal less popular.

Maria van der Hoeven, the head of the IEA, said that coal use is growing every year. If nothing changes, coal will become as important as oil in less than ten years.

Coal is easy to find in many parts of the world, unlike oil and gas, and it is cheap to mine. The IEA says that China and India will use more and more coal in the next five years. India will probably use more coal than the US and become the world’s second biggest coal user. China is the biggest coal importer, and Indonesia is the biggest exporter.

The IEA’s Medium-Term Coal Market Report says that by 2017, the world will burn 1.2 billion more tonnes of coal each year than it does now.

Coal produces more carbon emissions than any other major fossil fuel, so it is a big cause of climate change, especially when burned in old, inefficient power stations. If these power stations do not have special equipment to clean the smoke, burning coal also creates sulphur emissions, which cause acid rain, as well as mercury and soot pollution.

Van der Hoeven said that unless there is a high price on carbon to make coal less attractive and to support cleaner energy like renewables, only cheaper gas can reduce coal use. This has happened in the US because of the big increase in shale gas production in the last five years.

She said the US shows that a better gas market can lower coal use, cut carbon dioxide emissions, and reduce electricity bills for people. She said Europe, China, and other regions should pay attention to this.

If nothing is done, the world will face a higher risk of climate change because coal use is rising so quickly.

Coal will probably become as important as oil for the world’s energy in the next five years. This could be very bad for the climate.

One big reason for more coal use is that people in the US are now using more shale gas instead of coal. New research from the International Energy Agency (IEA) shows that people everywhere are using more coal, except in the US, where shale gas is now more popular. Because the US uses less coal, coal prices have gone down in the world. This makes coal cheaper and more attractive, even in Europe.

She said, “The US shows that a better gas market can lower coal use, carbon dioxide emissions, and electricity bills. Europe, China, and other places should learn from this.”

If we do not act soon, climate change will get worse.

Many people know they do not get enough sleep, but imagine if we could fix this with a simple solution: getting up later. At the British Science Festival, Dr. Paul Kelley from the Sleep and Circadian Neuroscience Institute at Oxford University said that schools should start at different times to match the natural body clocks of students. This would help students think better, get better exam results, and be healthier. Not getting enough sleep can cause problems like diabetes, depression, obesity, and a weak immune system.

In 2014, Dr. Kelley wrote a paper that explained when children and teenagers naturally wake up. When children are about ten years old, they naturally wake up at 6:30am. At 16, they wake up at 8am, and at 18, their natural wake-up time is 9am. So, a teenager who seems lazy is actually waking up at the right time for their age. The usual school start time is good for 10-year-olds, but not for 16- to 18-year-olds. For older teenagers, it would be better to start school at 11am or even later. Dr. Kelley and his team wrote that a 7am alarm for older teenagers is like a 4:30am start for a teacher in their 50s.

Dr. Kelley says we should not try to make teenagers go to bed earlier. The body’s natural rhythm is controlled by a special kind of light. The eyes have cells that send signals to the brain, which controls our body clock over 24 hours. Light controls this rhythm. It is like asking someone to control their heartbeat—it is not possible.

It is not only students who would benefit from starting later. Dr. Kelley says that work hours should also match our natural body clocks. He explains that people between 14 and 24 years old lose more than two hours of sleep each night. People between 24 and about 35 lose about an hour and a half. This continues until about age 55, when sleep and wake times are balanced again. Ten-year-olds and 55-year-olds naturally wake up and sleep at the same times.

This may be why the usual nine-to-five workday is so common. Many bosses are in their mid-50s or older, so these hours are best for them. Should workplaces also have different starting times? Should people in their 50s start at 8am, people in their 30s at 10am, and teenage workers at 11am? Dr. Kelley says that matching work hours to people’s natural rhythms could have many good results. People would work better, feel happier, and be healthier. It would make people less sick and better at their jobs.

There would probably be fewer accidents because drivers would be more awake. It could also end rush hour because people would travel at different times. Dr. Kelley says that starting later would help everyone, especially families. Parents often try to wake up teenagers who are waking up three hours too early, which causes stress for everyone.

So, what time does Dr. Kelley start work? He is 67 years old, so his body clock is like a 10-year-old’s. He gets up just after six and wakes up naturally. He says it is much easier for him to start work now than when he was younger.

Felix Baumgartner stood at the edge of space above New Mexico and stopped for a moment. It was only a small step from the capsule, but he was about to fall 24 miles down to Earth. “Our guardian angel will take care of you,” said mission control. Then, the man called Fearless Felix jumped.

Ten scary minutes later, the Austrian landed safely back on Earth. He reached speeds up to 725 miles per hour and broke three world records. He became the first person to skydive faster than the speed of sound, reaching Mach 1.24. “We love you Felix,” cheered the control room. Baumgartner raised his arms in victory.

He wore a special survival suit to protect him from the huge pressure changes during the jump. Without it, his blood could have boiled and his lungs might have exploded. Later, Baumgartner told reporters that he only thought about staying alive, but he also said, “Sometimes you have to go up really high to see how small you are.”

His other two records were for the highest manned balloon flight and the highest skydive. The jump happened on a sunny morning with good weather. Baumgartner went up into the clear sky in a huge balloon. The balloon was 30 million cubic feet in size, and its skin was only one-tenth as thick as a sandwich bag. At the bottom of the balloon was a capsule where Baumgartner sat in his suit.

When he reached the right height, Baumgartner checked 40 things with his mentor, Joe Kittinger. Kittinger was the previous record holder for the highest manned balloon flight.

Baumgartner had a problem with his visor. “This is very serious, Joe,” he told Kittinger. “Sometimes it gets foggy when I breathe out.” But they decided to continue, watched by a record 8 million people live on YouTube.

The trip up took two and a half hours. During this time, Baumgartner could see the curve of the Earth and the sky turned black. The fall down was much faster. Three cameras on Baumgartner’s suit filmed his free-fall, which lasted just over four minutes, and then his parachute opened.

The success of the mission and the suit means that astronauts might survive a high-altitude accident, like the space shuttle Columbia disaster in 2003, by jumping out. Baumgartner’s main doctor was Dr. Jonathan Clark, whose wife Laurel Clark died in the Columbia accident. Dr. Clark now works to help astronauts survive such disasters.

Baumgartner is known for daring stunts. He is a former paratrooper and has parachuted off buildings, mountains, and once into a 600-foot deep cave. He did two practice jumps for this mission—one from 71,000 feet and another from 97,000 feet. But nothing was like his jump above Roswell, a town famous for UFO stories.

He tried to break five records: first person to break the sound barrier in free-fall, highest free-fall jump, highest manned balloon flight, longest free-fall, and using the largest manned balloon in history. The stunt took seven years to plan, was sponsored by Red Bull, and broke two of Kittinger’s records. Kittinger, a retired US Air Force colonel, jumped from a balloon 19 miles above Earth in 1960 and gave Baumgartner advice during the ascent.

After the jump, Baumgartner was asked what he wanted to do next. He said, “I want to inspire a generation. I hope in four years, I’ll be giving advice to a young person who wants to break my record.” He said the most exciting moment was standing outside the capsule on top of the world. He added, “The most beautiful moment was when I landed and saw Mike Todd [the life support engineer who dressed him] smiling like a little kid.”

Baumgartner said he felt like Todd’s son, adding, “He was so happy that I was alive.” Earlier, Todd told reporters, “The world needs a hero right now, and they have one in Felix Baumgartner.”

“This will be my last jump,” Baumgartner said. He promised to settle down and enjoy life with his girlfriend, Nicole Oetl, and to fly helicopters on rescue missions in the US and Austria.

Barack Obama flew back to Washington and returned to his office on Wednesday, just hours after giving a victory speech in Chicago. In his speech, he asked Americans to come together and support him.

This time, unlike after his 2008 election, Obama is not expected to have an easy start. Both Republican House Speaker John Boehner and Democratic Senate Leader Harry Reid said it is important to work together to solve the economic crisis. However, there may be big disagreements between the White House and Congress during Obama’s presidency.

Obama won easily against his Republican opponent, Mitt Romney, by winning many important states. Still, the election showed that America is still very divided.

Although the official start of his second term is in January, Obama began working as president again on Wednesday. Many supporters were disappointed with his first term, so now he wants to create a strong legacy and be remembered as a great president.

Obama hopes to continue improving the economy and also wants to work on other issues like immigration reform, better education, fighting climate change, and foreign policy problems such as Iran and the conflict between Israel and Palestine.

Obama won more than the 270 electoral college votes needed and also got a higher percentage of the popular vote.

Boehner made a statement that sounded friendly. He said both parties should work together to help the economy grow and create jobs, which is important for solving the country’s debt problem.

Reid also sounded friendly. He said he wanted to work with Republicans in the Senate and House to solve the country’s problems.

However, there will be problems when they discuss details. Republicans want to keep military spending high, but Democrats want to cut it. Obama wants to raise taxes for households earning more than $250,000, but Boehner does not agree with any tax increases.

In the election, Romney only won one important state, North Carolina. Obama won New Hampshire, Virginia, Ohio, Wisconsin, Nevada, Iowa, and Colorado.

In his victory speech, Obama talked about the long lines to vote and said the voting system needs to be improved.

He used inspiring language, like he did in 2008, but did not use much during the 2012 campaign because his team thought it was not the right time. Now that he has won, he used famous lines from earlier speeches, such as his 2008 slogan about hope.

Obama told his happy supporters: “Tonight, you, the American people, reminded us that even though our journey has been hard and long, we have stood up again and fought back. We know that the best days for the United States are still ahead.” In his speech, which lasted more than 25 minutes, Obama thanked his wife Michelle, his daughters Malia and Sasha, and his Vice-President Joe Biden. He also repeated the message that made him famous.

He said, “We are not as divided as our politics shows. We are more than just red states and blue states. We are, and always will be, the United States of America.”

Obama made it clear that he has plans for his second term. He talked about changing the tax system, immigration reform, and making sure America is not threatened by climate change.

Just before Obama’s speech, Romney called him to admit defeat. Romney said, “This is a time of great challenges for America, and I hope the President will succeed in leading our country.”

During the campaign, many people judged Obama’s first term. Even though the economy was slow to recover and unemployment was high, Americans chose not to change presidents.

If Obama, the first black president, had lost, it would have been a big disappointment for African Americans and many white liberals.

Sweden is the best country for older people, while Afghanistan is the worst. However, being a rich country does not always mean better living conditions for people over 60, according to the first global index on ageing. Sweden is ranked first, followed by Norway, Germany, the Netherlands, and Canada. These results are expected, but the Global AgeWatch index also has some surprises.

The United States, which is the richest country in the world, is only in eighth place. The United Kingdom is 13th. Sri Lanka is 36th, much higher than Pakistan at 89th, even though both countries have similar levels of GDP. Bolivia and Mauritius also have higher scores than their economies suggest. Brazil and China are ranked fairly high, but India and Russia are much lower.

Mark Gorman, director of HelpAge International, said that history is important. The top countries are as expected, but Scandinavian countries were not rich when they first gave pensions to everyone. Older people in Sri Lanka now benefit from good basic education and health care because of past policy choices. Every country has limited resources, but when making decisions about spending, they should also think about older people.

The index was made with the UN Fund for Population and Development. It covers 91 countries and 89% of the world’s older people. The survey comes at a time of big changes: by 2050, there will be about two billion people aged 60 and over, which will be more than one-fifth of the world’s population.

Population ageing—when older people make up a bigger part of the population—is happening fastest in developing countries. More than two-thirds of older people live in poor countries, and by 2050, this will rise to about four-fifths. The fastest ageing countries—Jordan, Laos, Mongolia, Nicaragua, and Vietnam—are in the lower half of the ranking. This means that leaders in these countries need to pay more attention to the needs of older people.

There are also differences between men and women. Women usually live longer than men. In 2012, for every 84 men aged 60 and over, there were 100 women. Many older women have problems because they did not have paid jobs, so they have less savings. They also have less power in the family and are more at risk of violence.

However, the report says that an ageing population does not always mean much higher health care costs. It is important to invest in education and health care for older people over the long term. Bolivia, which is ranked 46th and is one of the poorest countries, has good policies for older people, such as a national plan on ageing, free health care, and a pension for everyone.

Good basic health care started many years ago in Chile and Costa Rica, which helps their older people today. A good education system is also very helpful later in life. Basic reading and writing skills are important for older people, especially when dealing with pension paperwork. In the Philippines, older people benefit from education reforms made after independence in 1946, which made elementary and high school education required. The same is true for Armenia, which, like other former Soviet Union countries, had a strong education system. South Korea is ranked low at 67, partly because it only recently started a pension system.

The ageing index uses 13 indicators in four areas: income security, health care, employment and education, and a positive environment. All indicators are equally important, except for pension income coverage, life expectancy at 60, healthy life expectancy at 60, and psychological well-being, which are given more weight because there is better data for them. Countries were only included if there was enough data.

Professor Sir Richard Jolly, who created the human development index, said this new index helps us understand the needs and opportunities of older people. It uses new methods and challenges all countries to do better for their older citizens.

Clay Cockrell is sitting in his office across the street from 1 Central Park West, which is the address of the Trump International Hotel and Tower. In front of the tower is Central Park, where Cockrell does his popular walk and talk therapy sessions.

Cockrell used to work on Wall Street, but now he is a therapist. He spends much of his day walking through Central Park or Battery Park in downtown Manhattan near Wall Street. He listens to and gives advice to some of the richest people in New York.

Many of these very rich people—the top 1% of the 1%—feel like their problems are not real problems. But Cockrell says their problems are real.

So, what problems do America’s richest people have? Cockrell says they often feel guilty because they are rich. They feel like they have to hide their wealth. Also, being in the 1% can feel lonely.

Counsellors say things have become worse since the financial crisis and the talk about income inequality, which was made bigger by movements like Occupy Wall Street.

Jamie Traeger-Muney, a psychologist who works with rich people and started the Wealth Legacy Group, says the Occupy Wall Street movement was good and talked about important things like income inequality. But it also made the 1% look bad. She says the media is partly to blame for making rich people feel like they need to hide or feel ashamed.

Traeger-Muney runs a global business and works with people who inherit money. These people often get a bad reputation in the news. She says, “Sometimes I am shocked by what people say. You would never talk about another group of people the way it seems normal to talk about rich people.”

Barbara Nusbaum, an expert in money psychology, says, “It is really lonely to have a lot of money. People’s reactions to you can be scary. We are all taught not to talk about money because it is not polite. But it is harder to talk about having money than not having money. It is more acceptable to say, ‘I am broke. Things are hard.’ You cannot say, ‘I have a lot of money.’ You have to keep much of your life private.”

Because of this, Cockrell says, rich people usually spend time with other rich people who understand them and their problems.

In the US, over the last 30 years, the number of very rich people has grown. According to research from Spectrem Group, in 2014, the number of US households with $1 million or more (not counting their main home) went up by 500,000 to 10.1 million. Households with $5 million or more reached 1.3 million, and 142,000 households are now worth $25 million or more.

Since the 2008 financial crisis, the gap between rich and poor has grown, and things have become worse for the rich, Cockrell says. The main reason is not knowing if your friends like you for who you are or for your money.

Cockrell says, “Someone else who is also a billionaire—they don’t want anything from you. But never being able to trust your friendships with other people is difficult.” As the gap has grown, the rich have become more and more alone.

These are real fears for the richest people. In 2007, the Gates Foundation and Boston College’s Center on Wealth and Philanthropy started to study what it feels like to be in America’s 1%. For the next four years, researchers asked 165 of America’s richest households questions—120 of these households had at least $25 million. The report, called The Joys and Dilemmas of Wealth, was 500 pages long and seemed to show that money cannot buy happiness.

“Wealth can stop you from connecting with other people,” said the wife of a tech entrepreneur who made about $80 million. Some Americans keep their wealth secret. “We call it stealth wealth. Many people hide their wealth because they are worried about negative judgment,” said Traeger-Muney. If rich Americans talk about the problems that come with their money, people often say, “Oh, poor you.” There is not much sympathy, she said.

Cockrell, who speaks in a soft, calming voice, says that a common mistake his rich clients make is letting their money define who they are.

“If you are part of the 1%, you still have problems, and they are real to you. Even if you say, ‘I don’t have to worry about money,’ there are other parts of your life. Money is not the only thing that defines you,” he said. “Your problems are real.”

Because of this, Cockrell says, rich people spend time with other rich people who understand them and their problems.

In the US, in the last 30 years, the number of very rich people has grown. In 2014, there were 10.1 million US households with $1 million or more, not counting their main home. There were 1.3 million households with $5 million, and 142,000 with $25 million or more.

Since the 2008 financial crisis, the gap between rich and poor has grown, and things “have gotten worse for the wealthy,” Cockrell said. The main reason is not knowing if your friends like you for yourself or for your money.

“If someone else is also a billionaire, they do not want anything from you. But with other people, you can never be sure if they are your friend or if they want your money. That is hard,” said Cockrell.

“Wealth can stop you from connecting with other people,” said the wife of a man who made about $80 million. Some Americans keep their wealth secret.

“Many people hide their wealth because they are worried about negative judgment,” said Traeger-Muney. If rich Americans talk about their problems, people do not feel sorry for them,” she said.

Cockrell said many of his rich clients make the same mistake—they let money be the most important thing in their lives.

“If you are part of the 1%, you still have problems. There are other parts of your life. Money is not the only thing,” he said. “Your problems are real.”

Takahito Iguchi says the problem with Google Glasses is that they are not cool. He might be right. There is already a website that shows people wearing Google Glasses looking silly or proud, or both. If you search Google Images, one of the first pictures you see is a big, naked man wearing them in the shower. Iguchi, a Japanese businessman, hopes this is Google’s weak point. He is making a new product that is more stylish, more like something from the movie Blade Runner, and more Japanese.

Iguchi’s new device is not really glasses. It is a single piece of metal with a camera and a small projector. The device is called Telepathy One. When it was first shown to the public in Austin, Texas, it got $5 million from investors. Like Google Glass, Telepathy One is planned to come out in 2014.

Telepathy One is a simpler version of Google Glass. Google Glass can do many things—you can use the internet, read emails, and take photos. Telepathy One will be more for communication. It connects to your phone with Bluetooth and focuses on sharing pictures and sound in real time. You can post photos and videos from your point of view on Facebook, send them by email, or see and talk to a friend’s video image.

“It will help you feel closer to your friends and family. We are very focused on communication and sharing,” says Iguchi, who has worked in Japanese technology for 20 years.

Not everyone wants to get closer to someone wearing a futuristic headset, I tell him. Iguchi shakes his head. “I am a visionary. I dream that people will understand each other. When I go to London, I am a stranger. Sometimes I feel afraid. But I believe everyone wants to be understood and to understand others. With this device, you can know more about people before you even talk to them.”

Compared to Google, Telepathy is very small, but Iguchi is not worried. In his shared office in San Francisco, which is a cool, old warehouse, he quotes Sun Tzu’s The Art of War and says that even small armies can sometimes beat big ones. When he was young, Japanese technology was the best in the world: the Sony Walkman was like the iPhone of its time. Now, to compete, he has left Tokyo and moved to Silicon Valley.

“Tokyo has a lot of fashion and culture, but it is still an island. It is isolated. There is no way to grow. But in Silicon Valley, everyone comes from everywhere. It is the place to connect with the world.” The hardware will be made in Japan, and he is building a team of software engineers in the US to make the apps.

Building the first Telepathy One was easy, Iguchi says. “We have all kinds of technology in Tokyo. The hard part is showing it to the world.” The best manufacturers want to work with him because they have the technology but have trouble selling it. “There needs to be a story for the product. Like Apple did with the iPod—1,000 songs in your pocket. Steve Jobs was inspired by Akio Morita, the co-founder of Sony, and he inspired me, so maybe it will come full circle.”

Maybe. Iguchi is very confident like Jobs, but because of his strong Japanese accent, sometimes people do not understand him well. This may be one reason he thought of Telepathy One. When he went to London to show the headset, he stayed in an Airbnb. “The house owner was not my friend, but I talked with him for three hours, and now he is my friend. That is how long it takes to understand each other, to share our feelings, background, and work. Maybe Telepathy can make that faster. If you get information from the cloud and social networks, it will be easier.”

Iguchi hopes that seeing someone else’s point of view will help you understand their ideas and feelings. As a student, he studied philosophy during the day and taught himself computer coding at night. One day, he opened the door of his apartment and suddenly realized that everything is code. Everything can be shared between people. Everything can be coded and decoded. If people can share code, maybe that will end all wars.

Google’s vice-president, Vint Cerf, has warned that a lot of digital material—like blogs, tweets, photos, videos, official documents, and emails—could be lost forever because the programs needed to view them might stop working. Cerf told the American Association for the Advancement of Sciences that our first digital records could disappear for future historians. He said we might have a forgotten generation or even a forgotten century because of “bit rot,” which is when old computer files become useless.

Cerf says we need to find ways to save old software and hardware so we can still open old files, even if they are very old. He explained that much of our daily life is now recorded digitally, such as emails, tweets, and websites, and we could lose a lot of our history. He said we do not want our digital lives to disappear. If we want to keep them, we must make sure that the digital things we create today can still be seen in the future.

Bit rot is when digital files become unreadable because the programs or machines needed to open them no longer exist. Some people think that accessing digital content in the future might not be as hard as Cerf believes. His warning shows a strange problem: we digitize music, photos, letters, and other documents to save them for a long time, but the programs and machines needed to read them often become outdated.

We are putting all our data into what could become an “information black hole” without realizing it. We digitize things to save them, but unless we take extra steps, these digital versions might not last any longer than the original items. Cerf says, if you have photos you really care about, you should print them.

Ancient civilizations did not have this problem because their histories were written on clay tablets or papyrus, which only needed eyes to read. In the future, people studying our culture will find PDFs, Word documents, and many other file types that need special software and sometimes special hardware to read.

This problem is already happening. In the 1980s, people saved documents on floppy disks and bought computer games on cassettes. Even if the disks and cassettes are still good, the machines needed to use them are now mostly in museums.

Cerf warns that important political and historical documents could also be lost to bit rot. In 2005, historian Doris Kearns Goodwin wrote a book about Abraham Lincoln. She went to libraries, found real letters, and used them to tell the story. Today, those letters would be emails, and it would be very hard to find them in one hundred years, Cerf said.

He admits that historians will try to save material that seems important today. But he says that sometimes we do not know what is important until many years later. For example, we learned about the mathematician Archimedes and his ideas about infinity and calculus because his writings were found hidden under a prayer book from the thirteenth century. Sometimes we learn about old civilizations from things that were saved by accident.

Researchers in Pittsburgh are working on a solution to bit rot. They take digital copies of computer hard drives while they are running different software. These copies can be uploaded to a computer that acts like the old one, so it can read old files.

However, inventing new technology is only part of the solution. It might be even harder to get legal permission to copy and save software before it disappears. When technology companies close, they might sell the rights to someone else, making it hard to get approval. To do this correctly, we might need to change how we think about copyright, patents, and licenses, so we can save digital things for hundreds or even thousands of years, Cerf said.

The day started with more police raids at the Baur Au Lac hotel in Zurich and ended with 16 football officials being charged with corruption in the United States. Five of these people were current or former members of FIFA’s executive committee. Among them were Ricardo Teixeira, the former head of the Brazilian football federation, and Marco Polo Del Nero, who replaced him and recently left the FIFA executive committee.

These 16 people were accused of fraud and other crimes by the US Department of Justice. The US gave details about several kickback schemes in a new 240-page document. In total, 27 people have now been charged by the US, including former FIFA executive committee members. US Attorney General Loretta Lynch said the betrayal of trust was shocking and the level of corruption was unacceptable.

Swiss police arrested Juan Ángel Napout, the president of the South American football confederation from Paraguay, and Alfredo Hawit, the head of the North and Central American and Caribbean football body. Hawit had only taken over from Jeffrey Webb in May 2015, after Webb was arrested as part of the US investigation that caused a crisis in FIFA and led to Sepp Blatter’s downfall. Webb’s predecessor, Jack Warner, was also arrested in May.

The Swiss Federal Office of Justice said the latest people arrested are in jail while they wait to be sent to the US. According to the US, they are suspected of taking millions of dollars in bribes. Webb and Luis Bedoya, a former executive committee member from Colombia, were among those who pleaded guilty in the US.

Now, eleven current and former members of FIFA’s executive committee have been charged in the investigation. The investigation says there were $200 million in bribes, mostly as kickbacks from TV and marketing contracts, but also from FIFA’s development programs.

Lynch said the message should be clear to anyone still trying to hide from the investigation: they will not escape. Teixeira, who was once the son-in-law of former FIFA president João Havelange, was charged along with Del Nero and his predecessor José Maria Marin, who was charged in May.

Fourteen men were charged in May 2015. A few days later, Blatter won a fifth term as FIFA president but then agreed to step down as the crisis got worse. He was then temporarily suspended, along with UEFA President Michel Platini, because of a suspected $1.3 million payment to Platini. Both men could be banned for life if they are found guilty when their case is heard by the FIFA ethics committee in December.

Others charged on Thursday included Rafael Salguero, a Guatemalan who left the executive committee in May; Eduardo Deluca, the former Secretary General of the South American confederation; Manuel Burga, the former president of the Peruvian football federation; and Carlos Chaves, the president of Bolivia’s football federation, who is already in jail in his own country.

Lynch said the US Department of Justice is determined to stop the widespread corruption in international football leadership. She said this is not only because of the size of the crimes and the effort needed to keep such corruption going, but also because this behavior goes against international values.

The acting FIFA President, Issa Hayatou, refused to talk about the details of the latest arrests. But he said that neither he nor FIFA was corrupt. Speaking to the media for the first time since taking over in September 2015, when Blatter was suspended, Hayatou said, like his predecessor, that the crisis was caused by a few bad people.

“FIFA is not corrupt. We have individuals who have behaved badly. Do not generalize the situation,” said Hayatou, who has been president of the Confederation of African Football for more than 25 years. He added that many people have worked at FIFA for more than 20 or 30 years and have not been accused of anything.

How long can you hold your breath? I am trying it right now. The first 30 seconds are easy. At 45 seconds, I want to stop, but I keep going and it feels a bit easier for a short time. But after one minute, my heart is beating fast. I let out a small breath, which helps. Finally, I give up, breathe out, and take a big breath in. I manage to hold my breath for one minute and 12 seconds. I feel proud of myself.

Being able to hold your breath is very important in some sports, especially freediving. In 2006, I was making a TV show about how the lungs work for the BBC. I was lucky to meet Sam Amps, the captain of the UK freedive team. At a swimming pool in Bristol, she showed me some easy exercises to help me hold my breath longer while swimming underwater. By the end of the lesson, I could hold my breath for 90 seconds, which was enough to swim across the pool. Sam could swim across the pool three times easily. She could hold her breath for five minutes while swimming. Five minutes!

I asked her how she did it. She said she breathed very slowly for a few minutes before each dive, then took a big, deep breath before going underwater. She also said that training helped her stop the feeling that she needed to breathe for much longer than most people.

Some people think that being able to hold your breath shows that, long ago, humans lived in water. Some even say that humans can slow down their heart rate to hold their breath longer. Other things, like our lack of body hair, the way our body fat is spread, and the fact that we walk on two legs, have also been linked to a time when humans lived in water. But, sadly, the idea that humans were once "aquatic apes" is not true.

When we look at breath-holding, we are not the only land mammals that can do it. (But it is hard to study this in other mammals because, unlike humans, it is difficult to make them hold their breath on purpose.) Also, research shows that our heart rate does not go down when we hold our breath on land. But when we are in cold water, our heart rate does slow down. Still, this is not proof that humans came from water animals. This slower heart rate is just one of the body’s normal reactions to being in water, called the mammalian diving reflex. These reactions help with diving, but they are also important for not drowning.

Even though our breath-holding is not special compared to other animals, it is now very useful in medicine. Radiotherapy for breast cancer uses radiation to target the tumor very exactly. This can take several minutes, so it is usually done in short times between breaths. But if the patient can keep her chest still for a few minutes, the whole treatment can be given at once, in the right place. The problem is that most people, like me, cannot hold their breath for more than a minute. But doctors at University Hospital Birmingham found that if patients breathe oxygen-rich air before holding their breath, they can do it for five and a half minutes.

Surprisingly, the secret is to trick the diaphragm. When you breathe in, your diaphragm muscle moves down so your chest gets bigger and air goes into your lungs. When you hold your breath, you keep your diaphragm in that position. If you raise the oxygen level and lower the carbon dioxide level before holding your breath, like in the Birmingham experiments, you can stop the diaphragm from getting tired so quickly. So, your diaphragm, the main breathing muscle, controls how long you can hold your breath. In the end, even if you trick it for a while, the signals from the diaphragm become too strong and you have to breathe.

After one minute, my heart beats very fast. I breathe out a little, and this helps. I reach one minute and 12 seconds. I feel proud of myself.

In some sports, it is very important to hold your breath. This is true in freediving. In 2006, I met Sam Amps. She was the captain of the UK freedive team. At a swimming pool in Bristol, she showed me simple ways to hold my breath longer while swimming underwater. At the end of the lesson, I could hold my breath for 90 seconds. This was enough time to swim across the pool. Sam could swim across the pool three times without breathing. She could hold her breath for five minutes while swimming. Five minutes!

I asked her how she did it. She said she breathed very slowly for a few minutes before each dive. Then, she took a big, deep breath before going underwater.

Our heart rate does not slow down when we hold our breath on land. But, when we are under cold water, most people’s heart rate slows down. This change helps us when we dive. It also helps us not to drown.

Holding your breath is now useful in medicine. Radiotherapy for breast cancer uses radiation to treat the tumour. The radiation must go to the right place. Usually, doctors give the radiation in short times, between breaths. But if the patient can hold their breath for a few minutes, doctors can give all the radiation at once, in the right place. The problem is that most people cannot hold their breath for so long. But doctors at University Hospital Birmingham found a way. If patients breathe air with extra oxygen before holding their breath, they can hold it for five and a half minutes.

This works because of the diaphragm. The diaphragm is the main muscle for breathing. When you breathe in, the diaphragm moves down and your chest gets bigger. This pulls air into your lungs. When you hold your breath, you keep your diaphragm flat. If you breathe extra oxygen before holding your breath, your diaphragm does not get tired so quickly. So, the diaphragm controls how long you can hold your breath. But, after some time, the diaphragm sends strong signals, and you must breathe again.

The Duke and Duchess of Cambridge won the first part of their fight for privacy. A French magazine is now banned from selling or using photos of the couple at a private house in Provence.

French prosecutors must now decide if the magazine editor and the photographer or photographers who took pictures of the duchess sunbathing topless on holiday in the south of France should face criminal charges.

A court in Nanterre, Paris, ordered the gossip magazine Closer to give the couple the digital files of the photos within 24 hours. If the magazine does not do this, it must pay 10,000 euros for every day it is late.

The court also ordered Mondadori Magazines France, which owns Closer, to pay 2,000 euros for legal costs.

The court said these photos, which showed the couple partly naked on the terrace of a private home, were very intrusive. The house was surrounded by a park and was several hundred meters from a public road.

The court decided that if Mondadori publishes any of these photos again in France, they will have to pay a fine of 10,000 euros each time.

However, this decision is only about the 14 photos that have already been published. The editor of Closer has suggested that there are other, more private photos.

The couple are happy with the judge’s decision. A source said they always believed the law was broken and that they had a right to privacy. Maud Sobel, the couple’s lawyer in Paris, called it a wonderful decision.

The royal couple are pleased, but they also want a public criminal case against the magazine and the photographer or photographers for invading their privacy.

Paris police started an investigation on Tuesday. In France, if you invade someone’s privacy, you can go to prison for up to one year and pay a fine of 45,000 euros.

The couple hope this punishment will send a message to the world and stop paparazzi from invading their privacy in the future.

The Irish Daily Star has also published the photos. The Italian celebrity magazine Chi, which is also owned by Mondadori, published a special 26-page edition with the photos of the future queen.
