Will drones deliver packages soon? Amazon thinks so, but others are not sure. We still need better technology, and there are also safety concerns.

Amazon’s spokesman, Paul Misener, told the US Congress that Amazon will be ready when all the rules are made. The Federal Aviation Authority (FAA) will have rules for commercial drones by June 2016. But the technology still needs to improve, and only drones up to 25kg will be legal. The FAA also says that if there are many drones in the sky, each one must use a different radio frequency so that no one can jam or take control of them.

Professor Sajiv Singh, who runs a cargo delivery company called NearEarth, said that flying a modern drone is simple. You just give it basic instructions: go to a certain height, do a short task, and return home. But even short flights from a mobile landing pad can cause big problems.

Drones will not deliver from one empty place to another. They will deliver from a warehouse to a customer, usually in a city or suburb. In these places, there are dangers the drone must see. There might be things on the ground that are not on the map, like new construction equipment. Sometimes GPS signals are blocked, so the drone might not know where it is. All these problems can be solved, but it is difficult.

One big problem is keeping radio contact with the drone. We also need to plan what happens if the contact is lost. Daniel Huber, a robotics expert, said that if you use a normal drone, it will just keep flying and crash if it loses contact.

Jay McConville from Lockheed Martin said you cannot do everything with a 25kg drone. People who use drones do not care about every detail of the aircraft. They want to see the drone’s status and video on their phone or laptop.

Huber said that most of the technology we need is already here. He is working on a program for drones to inspect things like pipelines, telephone lines, and bridges. They have made a system where you draw a box around an area, and the drone will fly around and check every surface, then report back.

Huber, who works with 3D images, said that Amazon says many packages are light. A drone can carry one kilogram for 15 minutes. If you have a base in a neighborhood, the drone can deliver from there. Most normal drones can fly for 15 minutes, which is enough for one trip. This helps keep people safe. Bigger drones are more dangerous.

Huber said that some drone problems can be solved in interesting ways. At a recent conference, a company showed a drone that could land on its own charging station and change its batteries when it was low on power.

But safety is still a big worry. Singh says that for a commercial aircraft to fly, it must have only one serious failure every one million hours. Drones are far from this. The Reaper drone fails once every 10,000 hours. But they do not count small problems like oil leaks as serious failures—something must actually fall from the sky.

Air travel is dangerous, so the safety standards are very high. Singh said that commercial airlines often return to the gate if a part fails, and airlines have 60 years of experience. He does not want a drone to fall on a busy road. Singh says we need to plan for every situation. If something goes wrong, the drone must react in a safe way.

One day, drones might bring packages to your house. When will this happen? Amazon says it will happen soon. Other people are not sure. They need to make the right technology, and they also need to think about safety.

Amazon says they will be ready when the Federal Aviation Authority (FAA) makes rules for drones. The FAA will make rules for drones by June 2016. But the technology is not ready yet, and big drones are not legal now. Only drones up to 25kg are legal. The FAA also says that drones must use special radio signals that no one can block or take over.

Professor Sajiv Singh works for a delivery company called NearEarth. He says flying drones is easy. You just tell the drone: go up, do a small job, and come back. But even short flights can have big problems.

“They do not want to deliver to empty places. They want to deliver from a warehouse to people, usually in a town or city,” he said. “The drone must see dangers. There may be things the map does not show. There may be new building machines. GPS signals may not work, so the drone does not know where it is.” He says these problems can be fixed, but it is hard.

One big problem is keeping radio contact with the drone. What happens if the drone loses contact? “If a drone loses radio contact, it will keep flying and crash,” said robot expert Daniel Huber.

“We already have most of the technology we need,” said Huber. He is making a program to use drones to check telephone lines and bridges. “We can make drones fly in an area and look at everything.”

Huber said about Amazon: “They say many packages are light. A drone can carry one kilogram for 15 minutes. If you have a car in a neighborhood, the drone can deliver from the car. You need a 15-minute flight, and most drones can do that.” This is one way to keep people safe. “If the drone flies farther, it is more dangerous.”

Safety is still a big worry. Singh says that for a passenger airplane to fly, it can only have one big problem every one million hours. Drones are not as safe. “The Reaper drone, for example, has one problem every 10,000 hours,” Singh said.

This is because flying is dangerous, so the rules are very strict. “If you fly a passenger airplane, sometimes they say, ‘A small part is not working; we must go back,’” Singh said. “And people have flown airplanes for 60 years! I do not like to think a drone could fall on a busy road.” Singh says the answer is to plan for every problem: “If something goes wrong, the drone must do something safe.”

Angry waiters are asking the public to help them keep their tips. Protesters are planning to target PizzaExpress restaurants to make the company stop taking part of the tips that staff get from credit and debit card payments. Campaigners have also started an online petition to get support from people who eat at restaurants.

PizzaExpress takes 8p out of every £1 given as a tip by card. This is called an admin fee. Some workers are very unhappy about this rule. PizzaExpress has 430 restaurants in the UK and is popular with families. The union Unite says the company makes about £1 million a year from this admin fee.

Chantal Chegrinec from Unite said, “We think this 8% fee is unfair. If PizzaExpress cares about its staff, it should give them all the tips customers leave.” She also said they will focus on other companies after PizzaExpress.

Local Unite branches are organizing the protests. The first protest is at the British Museum PizzaExpress in London. The union has also written to the company’s CEO. Unite started this campaign after asking its PizzaExpress members about their problems, especially after the company was sold to a Chinese owner in 2014. One of the biggest problems was the 8% taken from their tips.

One unhappy PizzaExpress worker, who wants to stay anonymous, said the admin fee costs her £3 every night. She wrote to Unite, “I have worked at PizzaExpress for 15 years. I still only get the national minimum wage of £6.50 an hour. My coworkers and I really need customer tips to add to our low pay. I work hard and do my job well, but when PizzaExpress takes part of our tips left on a card, it makes me upset.”

Ask and Zizzi, two other restaurant chains, also take 8% of tips paid by card. Some other chains take even more. Café Rouge, Bella Italia, and Belgo take 10%, as do Strada and Giraffe.

A PizzaExpress spokesperson said the admin fee pays for the cost of running a “tronc,” which is a system to share tips among staff. She said, “We worked hard to set up this tronc system, which is managed by staff. They decide how tips from card payments are shared between the team. It is a system run by employees for employees.”

PizzaExpress, which sells 29 million pizzas a year in the UK, says it does not make a profit from the admin fee. But some other restaurant groups do not take any admin fee from tips. Wagamama, Pizza Hut, and TGI Friday do not take anything. Frankie & Benny’s, Chiquitos, and Garfunkel’s used to take 10%, but they stopped several years ago.

Unite recently protested at ten PizzaExpress restaurants in south London. They gave out leaflets to customers, who were shocked and upset by the company’s rule. PizzaExpress says the admin fee is written in small print at the bottom of its menus. But the worker who wrote to Unite said customers are always surprised when she tells them about the fee. Most customers then give tips in cash. Almost 6,000 people have signed Unite’s online petition.

One waiter, who does not work for PizzaExpress but has worked for another restaurant chain for 11 years, said at least a third of his income comes from tips. He does not want to give his name because he is afraid of losing his job. He said, “I work in a busy London restaurant. On an average night, I serve 150 people and get £40 to £50 in tips. That sounds like a lot, but it is very important to me because my basic pay is only £6.50 an hour.”

Conservative MP Andrew Percy has asked for a new law to give restaurant staff more control over their tips. He said he plans to talk about this in parliament.

A top-secret document says that the National Security Agency (NSA) has direct access to the systems of Google, Facebook, Apple, and other big US internet companies. This access is part of a program called PRISM. PRISM lets officials collect information such as search history, email content, file transfers, and live chats.

The document says that the NSA collects data directly from the servers of these big US companies. It also says that the companies help with the program. However, all the companies that answered questions about this denied knowing about PRISM. 

Google said in a statement that it cares about user data security. Google said it only gives user data to the government when the law requires it and checks all requests carefully. Google also said it does not have a secret way for the government to access private user data.

Several top tech company leaders said they did not know about PRISM or any similar program. They said they would never take part in such a program. One person said, “If they are doing this, they are doing it without our knowledge.” An Apple spokesperson said he had never heard of PRISM.

The NSA was able to get this access because US surveillance laws changed under President Bush and were renewed under President Obama in December 2012. The program allows a lot of deep surveillance of live and stored communications. The law allows the targeting of any customers of these companies who live outside the US, or Americans who communicate with people outside the US.

The news about PRISM came after a leak of a secret court order that made Verizon, a phone company, give millions of US customers’ phone records to the government. The involvement of internet companies in PRISM has increased the debate about how much surveillance the intelligence services should have. Unlike the Verizon case, PRISM allows the government to collect the actual content of communications, not just information about them.

It is said that some of the world’s biggest internet companies are part of PRISM, which started in 2007. Microsoft was the first to join in December 2007. Yahoo joined in 2008; Google, Facebook, and PalTalk in 2009; YouTube in 2010; Skype and AOL in 2011; and Apple in 2012.

US law says companies must follow requests for user communications, but PRISM lets intelligence services access company servers directly. The NSA document says that US communication providers help with these operations.

When the FISA Amendments Act (FAA) was renewed in December 2012, some US senators warned that the law allowed too much surveillance and did not have enough safeguards. When the FAA was first introduced, supporters said the NSA could not get electronic communications without the companies’ permission. But PRISM makes this permission unnecessary because it lets the NSA take communications directly from company servers. This includes emails, video and voice chats, videos, photos, Skype calls, file transfers, and social networking information.

PRISM lets the NSA, the world’s largest surveillance agency, get targeted communications without asking the companies or needing individual court orders. The NSA can access both stored and live communications directly from company servers.

A senior government official said that the Guardian and Washington Post articles talk about collecting communications under Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA). This law does not allow targeting US citizens or anyone inside the US. The program is supervised by the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court, the Executive Branch, and Congress. Only non-US people outside the US are targeted. The program must limit the information it collects, keeps, and shares about US citizens.

Congress recently approved this program again after much debate. The information collected is considered very important and is used to protect the country from many threats.

Do you want your child to be good at sports, play for the school team, and maybe one day compete in international competitions? If so, you might want your future Olympian or World Cup winner to be born in November or October. A study by one of the UK’s top experts on children’s physical activity found that students born in these months are better than others in their class.

Children born in November and October were fitter, stronger, and more powerful than those born in the other ten months, especially compared to children born in April or June. Dr. Gavin Sandercock from Essex University and his team found that children born in autumn had a clear physical advantage over their classmates.

The research included 8,550 boys and girls aged 10 to 16 from 26 state schools in Essex. All students were tested between 2007 and 2010 on three types of fitness: stamina, handgrip strength, and lower-body power. The results showed that a child’s birth month could make a big difference in their cardiovascular fitness, muscle strength, and ability to move quickly. These things are important for being good at sports.

Children born in November were the fittest overall. They had the most stamina and power and were the second strongest. Children born in October were almost as fit. They were the strongest and came third in power, with December children close behind.

The difference in physical ability between children in the same class but born in different months was sometimes very large. For example, a boy born in November can run at least 10% faster, jump 12% higher, and is 15% more powerful than a boy of the same age born in April. This is a big physical advantage, said Sandercock. Such differences could decide who becomes a top athlete because being chosen for elite sports often depends on small differences in physical performance.

The study, published in the International Journal of Sports Medicine, found that when the three fitness scores were combined, children born in April were the least fit, followed by those born in June. This could mean these children are left out of school teams and do not do as well in sports, Sandercock said.

The findings show that children born early in the school year have a double autumn advantage. They are already known to do better in school, and now they also seem to be better at sports. The results show that something other than just being older in the school year is the reason, because the fittest children were not the tallest or heaviest, Sandercock added.

The authors believe that children born in autumn get more vitamin D in the womb during the summer months, which is probably the reason for their advantage. Seasonal differences in vitamin D levels before birth seem to be the most likely explanation, they say. John Steele, head of the Youth Sport Trust, said that the quality of a child’s first experience with sport at school is also very important for their development. Children who have a good first experience are more likely to have better agility, balance, and coordination, and are more likely to enjoy and do well in sports as they grow up, he said.

UK Sport could not say if most of the 1,300 athletes it supports in 47 sports were born in November and October. Natalie Dunman, its head of performance, said that while the differences found in the study were seen in teenagers in junior competitions, they disappeared by the time athletes competed as adults. She said that for top adult athletes, many things make a champion, and their work has not found that birth month is one of the main reasons.

Do you want your child to be good at sports, play for the school team, and maybe one day play in international competitions? Then you should try to have your child born in November or October. Children born in November or October are fitter, stronger, and more powerful than children born in other months. They are much fitter, stronger, and more powerful than children born in April or June. Dr. Gavin Sandercock from Essex University and his team found that children born in autumn have a clear physical advantage over their classmates.

The research studied 8,550 boys and girls aged 10 to 16 from 26 state schools in Essex. All the children were tested between 2007 and 2010 on three things: stamina, handgrip strength, and lower-body power. The results showed that the month a child is born can make a big difference to their fitness, muscle strength, and speed. These things are important for being good at sports.

Children born in November were the fittest because they had the most stamina and power and were the second strongest. Children born in October were almost as fit. They were the strongest and came third for power. Children born in December were also close behind.

The difference in physical ability between children in the same class but born in different months was sometimes very big. For example, a boy born in November can run at least 10% faster, jump 12% higher, and is 15% more powerful than a boy of the same age born in April. This is a big advantage. These differences could decide who becomes a top athlete because being chosen for top sports teams can depend on small differences in physical ability.

The study found that, when all three fitness scores were added together, children born in April were the least fit, followed by children born in June. The results show that children born at the start of the school year have a double “autumn advantage.” We already know they do better in school, and now it seems they are also better at sports.

The authors of the study think the most likely reason is that children born in autumn get more vitamin D from the sun during the last months of pregnancy. John Steele, head of the Youth Sport Trust, said that the way children start sport at school is also very important for their development. He said, “Children who have a good first experience in sport will have better agility, balance, and coordination, and are more likely to enjoy physical activity and be good at sport as they grow up.”

UK Sport could not say if most of the 1,300 athletes it supports were born in November or October. Natalie Dunman, head of performance at UK Sport, said that the differences in the study are true for teenagers in junior competitions, but these differences disappear in adult competitions. She said, “With adult athletes, there are many things that make a champion, and we do not think that month of birth is one of the most important.”

The last time Kate Bush performed on stage, mobile phones were just being tested. Now, thirty-five years later, she is performing again in a very different world.

Today, most concerts are full of people using phones and tablets. However, Kate Bush does not want her fans to watch her shows through a screen. Before her much-awaited concerts at the Hammersmith Apollo in London, Bush asked her fans not to use their mobile phones during her shows.

On her website, Bush wrote: I have a request for everyone coming to the shows. We chose a small, intimate theatre instead of a big stadium. It would mean a lot to me if you do not take photos or videos during the shows. I want to connect with you as an audience, not with your phones, tablets, or cameras. I know this is a big request, but it will help us all enjoy the experience together.

Bush is known for her dramatic shows and beautiful costumes. She may also want to stop fans from uploading videos to YouTube so that the show stays a surprise for the thousands of people who have tickets for her 22 concerts.

Bush is not the first singer to talk about the problem of phones at concerts. Roger Daltrey, the lead singer of The Who, recently said it was strange that people come to a show but spend their time looking at their screens instead of watching the artist. He said, I feel sorry for them. If you are looking at life through a screen, you are only half there. It is strange to me.

In 2013, Beyoncé told a fan at her concert to stop filming. She said, You can’t even sing because you’re too busy filming. You have to enjoy this moment. Put that camera down!

The discussion about phones at live events is not only in music. Recently, football fans in the Netherlands at PSV Eindhoven protested against wi-fi in their stadium. They held up signs saying things like No wi-fi. Support the team, You can sit at home, and Stand united. Manchester United football club has also asked fans not to bring large electronic devices to games.

Jarvis Cocker, another musician, has also complained about fans using phones at concerts. He says it drives him crazy. He thinks it is silly to watch something happening in front of you on a small screen.

Johnny Marr said in 2013 that fans miss out on the real feeling of live music when they are busy filming. He said, If you are just looking at the show through your phone, you are wasting your chance. I don’t want to be rude, but you should put your phone down and enjoy the concert.

Even in classical music, this is a problem. In June 2013, famous pianist Krystian Zimerman left the stage because someone was filming him on a smartphone. He came back and said that YouTube is hurting music a lot.

But Sam Watt, who works for Vyclone, a phone app that lets people film concerts and then mixes the videos together, thinks filming at concerts makes the experience better. He said, Fans filming is now part of concerts. We take the videos people film and mix them together to make great content. We believe filming adds to the experience, not takes away from it. If Kate Bush came to talk with us, we could have a good discussion about this. People want to film and keep memories, and that is important. We should accept it.

Recently, Dutch football fans at PSV Eindhoven protested against wi-fi in their stadium. They held up banners that said “No wi-fi. Support the team,” and “You can sit at home.” Manchester United also told fans to leave their big electronic devices at home.

Singer Jarvis Cocker said, “It seems stupid to have something happening in front of you and look at it on a small screen.”

Even in classical music, a famous pianist, Krystian Zimerman, left the stage in June 2013 because a fan was filming him on a smartphone. He came back and said, “The destruction of music because of YouTube is enormous.”

But Sam Watt thinks filming at concerts makes the experience better. He works for Vyclone, a phone app that puts together many videos from fans to make one long video of a show. He said, “Fans filming is now part of the concert experience – that is just a fact. We take the videos people film at concerts and mix them together. The result is a really fantastic video.”

He also said, “We think filming at concerts adds to the experience. If Kate Bush came for tea, we could have a good talk about this. People are going to film and they want those memories – you have to accept it.”

Water scientists have given a very strong warning about the world’s food supply. They say that by 2050, people may need to eat almost only vegetarian food to avoid very serious food shortages.

Right now, people get about 20% of their protein from animal products. But, according to top water scientists, this may need to go down to just 5% to feed the extra two billion people expected by 2050.

A report by Malik Falkenmark and other scientists at the Stockholm International Water Institute (SIWI) says there will not be enough water to produce food for the expected nine billion people in 2050 if we keep eating like people in western countries. There will only be enough water if animal-based foods are limited to 5% of total calories.

Warnings about water shortages affecting food production come as Oxfam and the UN prepare for a possible second global food crisis in five years. Prices for corn and wheat have gone up almost 50% on world markets since June. This price rise is because of bad droughts in the US and Russia, and weak monsoon rains in Asia. More than 18 million people in the Sahel region already face serious food shortages.

Oxfam says that higher food prices will badly affect developing countries that depend on food imports, such as parts of Latin America, North Africa, and the Middle East. In 2008, food shortages caused fighting and riots in 28 countries.

The scientists say that changing to a vegetarian diet is one way to save water and grow more food, especially as the climate becomes more unpredictable. Food rich in animal protein uses five to ten times more water than a vegetarian diet. One third of the world’s farmland is used to grow crops to feed animals. Other ways to feed people include stopping food waste and increasing trade between countries with extra food and those without enough.

Already, 900 million people are hungry and two billion are malnourished, even though food production per person is still rising. Seventy percent of all water is used in farming, and growing more food for two billion more people by 2050 will put even more pressure on water and land.

The report is being released at the start of the annual world water conference in Stockholm, Sweden. Here, 2,500 politicians, UN groups, non-governmental organizations, and researchers from 120 countries meet to talk about global water supply problems.

The scientists say that competition for water between food production and other uses will increase pressure on important resources. The UN says we must increase food production by 70% by the middle of the century. This will put more pressure on water, which is already under stress, at a time when we also need more water for energy and to make electricity for the 1.3 billion people who do not have it.

Overeating, malnutrition, and food waste are all increasing. We will need a new way to feed the world in the future, said the report’s editor, Anders Jagerskog.

Cities do not usually move to a new place, but Kiruna, a town in northern Sweden, has to do this to stop the ground from swallowing it up.

Krister Lindstedt from White, the Swedish architecture company leading the project, says it is a very hard decision. Kiruna has 23,000 people, and they must move the city away from a huge iron-ore mine that is making the ground under the city unsafe. If the mine stops working, many people will lose their jobs. If the city moves, people can keep working, but they must leave their homes.

Kiruna was started in 1900 by the state-owned mining company LK (Luossavaara-Kiirunavaara). The city became rich because of the iron ore under it, but now the mine is also the reason the city is in danger. Deputy Mayor Niklas Siren says the city only exists because of the mine; otherwise, no one would have built a city there.

Kiruna is 145 kilometers inside the Arctic Circle. The weather is very cold, with winters that have no sunlight and average temperatures below -15°C. Still, people stay because of the mine. It is the largest underground iron-ore mine in the world and makes 90% of all the iron in Europe. This is enough iron to build more than six Eiffel Towers every day, and the need for iron is still growing.

In 2004, the mining company told the city that it was in danger. The mine was digging under the city at a 60-degree angle, and soon the ground would start to sink, causing buildings to crack and fall. Ten years later, cracks are already appearing and getting closer to the city.

Viktoria Walldin, a social anthropologist working with the architects, says people in Kiruna have lived in uncertainty for ten years. They cannot make big decisions like buying a house, redecorating, having a child, or starting a business because they do not know what will happen.

After many years, the city now has a plan. Lindstedt’s plan shows the city’s streets and squares slowly moving east along a new main street. By 2033, the whole city should be in a safe place away from the mine.

A new town square is already being built 3 kilometers to the east, with a round town hall designed by Danish architect Henning Larsen. Twenty important buildings will be taken apart and rebuilt in the new city, like building a large Ikea set. Kiruna’s red wooden church, built in 1912 and once voted Sweden’s most beautiful building, will be in a new park, and the bell tower will be next to the new town hall. But not everything can be saved.

Walldin says she spoke to an old woman who walks past the bench where she had her first kiss. Things like this, or the hospital where someone’s first child was born, are important to people, but these places will disappear.

This project is called the most democratic move in history. The mining company will give 320 million euros to build new places like a high school, fire station, community center, library, and swimming pool. But most people are worried about where they will live and how they will get a new house or apartment.

People in Kiruna are used to low rents and high salaries, but this will change. The mining company LK has agreed to pay people the value of their homes plus 25%, but many people say this is not enough to buy a new house.

The new city will not look like the old Kiruna. The old city has winding streets and houses with gardens. The new plan has tall apartment buildings around shared courtyards and straight streets.

The architects say this is a chance for Kiruna to become a new city that will attract young people. There will be new cultural places and even a cable car above the main street. But many people who live in Kiruna now may not be able to afford to live in the new city.

US researchers say that government programs that collect large amounts of telephone records are a danger to people’s privacy. The researchers used simple phone records to find out who people were and to learn private details about their lives.

With only information about who called or texted whom, when, and for how long (but not the actual conversations), two scientists at Stanford University were able to find out people’s names, where they lived, and the names of their partners. But they found even more.

The same phone data helped them discover private information about some people. For example, they learned that one man owned a gun and another man had a heart problem. Other information showed that one person was pregnant and another had multiple sclerosis.

These results show how powerful telephone metadata is. Metadata means information like the phone number called, the time, and the length of the call. This information becomes even more powerful when combined with public information from websites like Google, Yelp, and Facebook. Security agencies understand how important this data is. Stewart Baker, who used to be a lawyer for the US National Security Agency (NSA), said, “Metadata tells you everything about somebody’s life.”

Patrick Mutchler, a computer security researcher at Stanford, said that people who collect this data know how powerful it is, but the public does not. This makes it hard for people to fight against these programs. “Now, we have strong proof that we did not have before,” he said.

For the study, 823 people agreed to let the researchers collect metadata from their phones using an Android app. The app also collected information from their Facebook accounts, which the scientists used to check if their results were correct. In total, the researchers collected data on more than 250,000 calls and over 1.2 million texts.

Mutchler explained that, with very little money, he and Jonathan Mayer found a lot of personal and private information about the people in the study. They could find out 82% of people’s names. They also learned the names of businesses people called. When they put these businesses on a map, they could guess where people lived. They correctly named the city where people lived 57% of the time and were almost 90% correct in finding the area within 50 miles of their home.

By using a simple computer program to study call patterns, the scientists could see who was in a relationship. Once they knew someone had a partner, it was easy to find out who the partner was.

In the last part of the study, the researchers looked even deeper to see what private information they could find from phone metadata. They collected details about calls to and from hospitals, pharmacies, religious groups, and legal services. From this, they learned a lot about people’s private lives.

For example, one person often called a local gun shop and later made long calls to a big gun company’s customer service. The data from two other people suggested that one had multiple sclerosis and the other was pregnant.

Mutchler said that all of this was possible with just two graduate students and little money. He believes that these results should make government leaders think carefully before allowing mass surveillance programs. The scientists said that programs like the NSA’s will reveal very private information about ordinary people.

This information, called metadata, showed which numbers people called, when they called, and how long the calls lasted. It did not show what people said in the calls.

But that was not everything. With the same metadata, the scientists could find out private things about some people. For example, they learned that one man had a gun and another man had a heart problem. They also found out that someone was going to have a baby and someone else had a serious illness.

Mutchler said the study showed how easy it is to find out private information about people. He said that governments should think carefully before they collect this information. “Metadata programs, like the NSA’s, will show very private information about ordinary people,” the scientists said.

Stewart Baker, who worked at the US National Security Agency (NSA), said, “Metadata tells you everything about somebody’s life.”

Patrick Mutchler, a researcher at Stanford, said that people who collect this information know how powerful metadata is, but most people do not know this.

For the study, 823 people agreed to let the scientists collect metadata from their phones using an app. The app also got information from their Facebook pages, which the scientists used to check their results. The scientists collected metadata from more than 250,000 calls and over 1.2 million texts.

Angela Erdmann never met her grandfather because he died in 1946, six years before she was born. But on April 8, 2014, she talked about an amazing moment when she received a message in a bottle that her grandfather had thrown into the Baltic Sea 101 years earlier. This bottle is believed to be the oldest message in a bottle in the world. A museum in Germany, which is now showing the bottle, gave it to Erdmann.

Erdmann, who is 62 years old, said she was very surprised when she learned about the bottle. She explained that a man came to her door and told her he had mail from her grandfather. He said that a message in a bottle had been found and that the name on the card was her grandfather’s. The man was a family history researcher who found Erdmann in Berlin after the letter was given to a museum in Hamburg, a city in northern Germany.

A fisherman found the brown beer bottle, which had been in the water for 101 years, while fishing in the Baltic Sea near the city of Kiel. Holger von Neuhoff, a museum worker, said this was the oldest bottled message he had ever seen. He said there are older documents in the museum, but they were not found with bottles. With both the bottle and the message together, this is the oldest one they have. The bottle and message are in very good condition.

Researchers think that Erdmann’s grandfather, Richard Platz, threw the bottle into the sea during a hike in 1913, when he was 20 years old. Most of the message on the postcard is too hard to read, but the address in Berlin on the front can still be read. The message also politely asked the finder to send the card to his home address.

Erdmann said her grandfather also put two stamps from that time in the bottle, so the person who found it would not have to pay for postage. But he probably did not think it would take 101 years to arrive.

Erdmann said she felt emotional when she got the message, even though she never knew her grandfather because he died at age 54, six years before she was born.

She said she did not know much about her grandfather, but she learned that he was a writer who was open-minded, believed in freedom, and thought everyone should respect each other. He helped young people and later traveled with his wife and two daughters. Erdmann said it was wonderful to learn about her family history.

Erdmann also likes culture and traveling, just like her grandfather. She said she is open-minded too. She explained that what her grandfather taught his daughters, her mother taught her, and she has taught her sons. She was very happy to get the message in the bottle, but she hopes people will not throw bottles with messages into the sea today. She said the sea is already full of bottles and trash, so people should not add more.

The message and the bottle will be shown at Hamburg’s Maritime Museum until early May 2014. After that, experts will try to read the rest of the message. It is not clear what will happen to the bottle after that, but Erdmann hopes it will stay in the museum.

She said, “We want to put some photos with the bottle to give it a face, so visitors can see the young man who threw the bottle into the water.”

The customer next to you in the line looks normal. But instead of a shopping list, she has handwritten notes about how the store looks and how clean it is. She is timing how fast the line moves on her phone, and you notice a small camera lens in her purse. She is probably a mystery shopper.

According to the Mystery Shopping Providers Association, about 50,000 mystery shopping trips happen every month in the UK. As more people shop online, the need for mystery shoppers is increasing. Simon Boydell, a spokesman for Marketforce, which has over 300,000 mystery shoppers, says that stores know people who come to shop in person want good service and a special experience that they cannot get online. Stores want to check how well they give this experience.

Jill Spencer from the mystery shopping company ABa says they send shoppers to different store locations and make sure they do not return to the same shop within three months. Each day, a mystery shopper usually spends up to eight hours visiting five to ten stores. They also spend one or two more hours writing detailed reports about their visits. For this work, mystery shoppers can earn up to £155 a day and get their expenses paid back. If they use a hidden camera to film their visits, they can earn even more—about £300 a day.

Mystery shoppers usually get back any money they spend in the stores and sometimes can keep the things they buy. Laura, a mystery shopper, says she is usually given between £5 and £20 to spend at each store to check the service at the checkout. She is always given a situation, like buying something from a certain department or a new product, but she can often choose what to buy and keep it.

Most full-time mystery shoppers, like Laura, are self-employed. She earns about £30,000 to £40,000 a year, not counting the free products she gets. With these extras, it is enough to live on. She feels happy when she returns to a store she has checked before and sees that things have improved. She believes her feedback helps stores get better. Some stores she visits win awards for customer service, and she thinks mystery shoppers help make this happen. She feels she is helping not just her company, but all shoppers.

It is estimated that more than 500,000 people in the UK have signed up to be mystery shoppers, but only about 10% or fewer get regular work each month. Because of this, pay has gone down a lot. In the past, mystery shoppers got a fee, money back for their purchase, and travel costs. Now, they often only get some money towards their purchase. Val, a 51-year-old former mystery shopper, says she worked for 40 different companies for almost 20 years but stopped three years ago because the pay was too low and she had bills to pay.

Today, most mystery shopping companies give free products or meals to encourage people to work for them. Boydell says Marketforce shoppers usually get a few pounds for a visit as a small thank you for their time. At most, they pay £15 to £25 plus money back for a meal for two or a hotel stay. They do not directly employ shoppers, so they do not have to pay minimum wage.

Laura says she would go on a cruise for free, but she thinks companies that pay only a small amount for traveling to a restaurant and eating a meal are taking advantage of people. She does not do those jobs anymore, but many people still do. Hannah, a 41-year-old lawyer, has done almost 500 visits for the Mystery Dining Company in her free time without getting paid or having her travel costs covered. She does their most special jobs, like eating £200 meals at Michelin-starred restaurants and staying overnight at boutique hotels.

But even for mystery dining, there is no such thing as a free meal. Hannah says she usually spends two to four hours after each visit writing detailed reports about everything, from the quality of the food to how the staff act. She always needs to remember the names or descriptions of the staff. She has to remember all these details while eating because she cannot write anything down in the restaurant.

There is a lot to remember. You have to give feedback while it is still fresh, so sometimes Hannah gets up at 5am to write a report before work. It is a difficult job; you need to be focused, able to explain things well, and pay attention to details.

There are about 50,000 mystery shopping trips every month in the UK. Mystery shoppers act like normal customers in shops, but they are really checking how good or bad the service is. More people are needed for this job because more people are shopping online now.

Simon Boydell, a spokesman for Marketforce, says, “Shops know that people who come to the store want good service and a special experience they can’t get online. Our clients want to know how well their stores are doing.” Marketforce has more than 300,000 mystery shoppers.

Jill Spencer from ABa, another mystery shopping company, says, “We send shoppers to different stores and make sure they don’t go back to the same shop for three months. Each day, they visit five to ten stores for up to eight hours. Then, they spend one or two more hours writing reports about their visits.” Mystery shoppers can earn up to £155 a day, and their travel costs are paid. If they use a hidden camera, they can earn about £300 a day.

Mystery shoppers usually get back the money they spend in the shops and sometimes can keep the things they buy. Laura, a mystery shopper, says, “They give me between £5 and £20 to spend in each shop to check the service at the till. I am given a special task, like buying something from a certain department or a new product, but I can often choose what I want and keep it.”

Most full-time mystery shoppers, like Laura, work for themselves. She earns about £30,000 to £40,000 a year, not counting the free things she gets. “With the extra benefits, it’s enough to live on,” she says. Laura feels happy when she goes back to a shop and sees things have improved. “I know it’s because of my feedback. I feel I am helping not just my company, but all shoppers.”

More than 500,000 people in the UK have signed up to be mystery shoppers, but only about 10% or less get regular work each month. Because of this, the pay has gone down. Before, people got paid and travel costs, but now, “you often just get some money to buy something,” says Val, a 51-year-old former mystery shopper. Now, companies mostly give free things as a reward. Boydell says, “Marketforce shoppers usually get a few pounds for a visit. Sometimes, we pay £15 to £25 plus costs for a meal for two or a hotel stay. We don’t employ shoppers directly, so we don’t have to pay them minimum wage.” Laura says, “I would go on a cruise for free, but I think companies that pay very little for travel and a meal are taking advantage of people. I don’t do those jobs anymore.” But many people still want to do these jobs.

Hannah, a 41-year-old lawyer, has done almost 500 visits for the Mystery Dining Company in her free time without pay or travel money. She has enjoyed £200 meals at Michelin-starred restaurants and stayed overnight at expensive hotels.

But the job can be hard. Hannah says she spends two to four hours after each visit writing reports about everything, like the quality of the food and what staff said. She always needs to remember the names or looks of the staff. She has to remember all these details while eating because she cannot write anything down in the restaurant.

A new survey shows that more than one million British workers may have zero-hours contracts. This means British companies are using these contracts much more than people thought before.

The survey was done by the Chartered Institute of Personnel and Development (CIPD) and asked more than 1,000 employers. After the results came out, many people asked the government to investigate how these contracts are used. Recently, many organizations, including shops and even Buckingham Palace, have been criticized for hiring people without promising them work or pay every week. Workers on zero-hours contracts often do not get holiday or sick pay, and they must ask for permission before taking another job.

The CIPD found that 38% of people on zero-hours contracts say they work full-time, usually 30 hours or more each week. One-third of voluntary sector employers use these contracts, and one in four public sector organizations use them too.

Peter Cheese from the CIPD said there should be a closer look at what a zero-hours contract really means, and both the good and bad sides for businesses and workers should be considered.

Recently, the shop Sports Direct was in the news because it was reported that about 20,000 of its 23,000 workers have zero-hours contracts. After this, it was found that other companies, like the cinema chain Cineworld and Buckingham Palace, also use these contracts. Buckingham Palace uses them for 350 summer workers. The pub group J D Wetherspoon has 24,000 workers—80% of its staff—on zero-hours contracts.

Vidhya Alakeson from the Resolution Foundation said that if there are really about one million people on zero-hours contracts, this is a large part of the workforce and not just a small problem.

Unions and groups fighting poverty say that employers force workers to sign these contracts to avoid giving them benefits and to reduce their responsibilities.

Dave Prentis from the union Unison said most workers only accept these contracts because they have no other choice. He said the contracts may give some flexibility, but they mostly help employers and make it hard for workers to complain.

Workers on zero-hours contracts often only find out how many hours they will work when the weekly or monthly schedule is made. They are expected to be ready for extra work at short notice. They should get holiday pay, but they do not get sick pay.

The charity National Trust, which uses zero-hours contracts for many of its seasonal workers, said it gives these workers the same pay and benefits, in proportion to hours worked, as full-time staff. However, it needs some workers to have flexible contracts. A spokeswoman said zero-hours contracts are important for the National Trust because their work depends on the weather. They need to change staff schedules quickly, and zero-hours contracts help them do this.

Politician Chuka Umunna said zero-hours contracts should be rare. He said that while some workers like the flexibility, many feel insecure and do not know when they will get work.

Some people think that zero-hours contracts helped the UK avoid higher unemployment during the economic crisis.

The survey found that 17% of private sector employers use zero-hours contracts. This is lower than the 34% of voluntary sector organizations and 24% of public sector organizations that use them.

Industries most likely to have at least one worker on a zero-hours contract are hotels, catering and leisure (48%), education (35%), and healthcare (27%).

A new census shows there are now more tigers in Nepal than at any time since the 1970s. This gives hope to conservationists who want to save the big cats. For 100 years, the number of tigers in south Asia has been going down.

The number of wild royal Bengal tigers in Nepal is now 198. This is a 63.6% increase in five years, according to a government survey. Maheshwar Dhakal, an ecologist from Nepal’s Department of National Parks and Wildlife Conservation, said this is very good news.

The census used pictures from over 500 cameras in five protected areas and three wildlife corridors. More than 250 conservationists and wildlife experts worked on the survey, which cost about $250,000. Dhakal said a similar survey is happening in India, and results from both countries will be published later in 2013. India, which has 1,300 big cats in several large protected areas, will finish its survey in a few months. Nepal has promised to double its tiger population by 2022, starting from 121 tigers in 2009, when the last full count was done.

As people in Asia become richer, the price for tiger skins and body parts used in traditional Chinese medicine has gone up. International gangs pay poor Nepali people a lot of money to kill tigers. The skin and bones are given to middlemen, who easily cross the border into India, where the main dealers are.

One big problem is that some high officials help the mafia networks involved in this trade. Conservation experts think the increase in tiger numbers is because of better protection of national parks and better management of tiger habitats in Nepal, where forests cover 29% of the land. But they say Nepal must do more to protect the land and the animals that tigers eat, so tigers have enough space and food.

As the number of tigers has grown, there have been more conflicts with villagers. In 2012, tigers killed seven people near national parks, compared to four in 2011, park officials said. Villagers want better protection. The government is making plans to protect tigers, but it should also make plans to protect people from tigers, said Krishna Bhurtel, a village leader, to a Nepali newspaper. Wildlife authorities caught a tiger after it killed two people, including a villager who was taken from his bed in May.

Thousands of tigers once lived in the forests of Bangladesh, India, and Nepal. Now, there are only about 3,000 left, which is a 95% drop in 100 years. Chitwan National Park in central Nepal has the most adult tigers, with 120. Bardiya National Park has 50, and Shukla Phanta Wildlife Reserve has 17.

Diwakar Chapagain, head of a World Wildlife Fund Nepal group that watches wildlife trade, said tiger skins are wanted in Tibet, where rich people use them for festival clothes.

In Nepal, kings used to stand on tiger skins for special events. Some rich Nepali people have tiger heads on their living room walls. Tiger bones are used in traditional Chinese medicine. The trade in tiger parts is very profitable and brings thousands of dollars in illegal markets, Chapagain said.

I got a Dyson vacuum cleaner, but I’m not sure if I want it. I just picked it up, said Louise Haggerty, a 56-year-old hairdresser and waitress, at the end of her Black Friday shopping trip at one o’clock in the morning. It was crazy in there. It was horrible.

Haggerty went to a 24-hour Sainsbury’s supermarket in north-east London with a friend. She wanted to buy a cheap flat-screen TV. But so many people pushed into the line that we didn’t have a chance, she said. The poor woman who was second in line was pushed out by a group of young people. She didn’t get anything. People were acting like animals—it was terrible, she said. I only saw two security guards.

Haggerty was upset when she couldn’t buy a 40-inch TV that was reduced from £299.99 to £149.99, so she quickly picked up a vacuum cleaner, reduced from £319.99 to £159.99. I don’t even know how much it costs; I don’t even know if I’m going to buy it. I just wanted something, she said. There are guys in there with three, four, five TVs. It’s not fair.

One of those guys was Andy Blackett, 30, who had two shopping carts full of bargains. I got two coffee makers, two tablets, two TVs, and a stereo, he said. I don’t know the prices, but I know they’re good deals. But his friend Henry Fischer wasn’t as lucky. Someone took my TV from me—it’s because I’m the smaller one.

Blackett, Fischer, and some friends drove to Sainsbury’s at 12:45 am after leaving the chaos at a Tesco 24-hour supermarket, where the Black Friday sale started at midnight. Tesco was scary, so we came here instead, Blackett said.

More than twelve police officers went to another Tesco store because fights started between excited and angry shoppers. Customers took down cardboard barriers that were holding back sale items until midnight. Tesco delayed selling its most popular items—TVs—for almost an hour until police controlled the situation. One officer criticized the manager for not having enough security and suggested stopping the sale completely.

Police also went to several other stores just before the doors opened at midnight. Meanwhile, Manchester Police said at least two people were arrested at Black Friday sales. South Wales Police also got several calls from Tesco staff who were worried because so many people came to the sales.

TV sales at the Tesco store started just before 1 am. One of the first people to buy a flat-screen TV was James Alled. He bought two and was already trying to sell one to someone further back in the line. I bought them for £250. I’ll sell it to you for £350, £300 cash, he said. Further back in the line, Christine Ball, 62, was not happy. I got here at 10:15 pm and I’m further back now than when I arrived, she said. These people don’t know how to queue.

Ball had not heard of the American Black Friday sales before, like most shoppers. She said she came out especially to buy her grandson a TV for Christmas. Not a huge one, just a normal one for about £100, she said. In her basket was a pint of milk and a loaf of bread. TV, milk, and bread—the necessities, she said.

Mel Mehmet, 23, had been to Black Friday sales in 2013 and expected lines, but she said the atmosphere in Tesco scared her this time. It’s crazy to have the sale at midnight—the police must have more important things to do at night than come to sales. We’re going to PC World first thing in the morning—their sale starts at 8 am.

Barack Obama told young people not to be negative and to talk with people who have different opinions if they want to change the world.

On his last visit to Britain as US president, Obama spoke to 500 young leaders in London. He said, “I’m here to ask you not to believe that there are problems we can’t solve. As JFK said, our problems are made by people and can be solved by people.”

He told the students, “You have better tools than ever to make a difference. Don’t be negative or think nothing can change. Progress is possible, but it doesn’t happen by itself. It needs hard work, discipline, and hope.”

Obama said he understood that young people face many problems. He said this is a time of big changes, from events like 9/11 and 7/7, and with so much information and bad news on social media like Twitter.

The audience cheered when Obama was introduced. He talked about his policies, such as healthcare and education.

He told the audience to talk with people who have different political views. He said, “Find people who don’t agree with you. This will help you learn to compromise.”

Obama said he was proud of his healthcare reforms, which made the audience cheer. He also talked about the US response to the 2008 financial crisis, saying, “Saving the world from a great depression was very good.”

He also mentioned important agreements with Iran and the response to the Ebola crisis as some of the best parts of his presidency. He said, “I’m proud; I think I have stayed true to myself.”

When asked about the Transatlantic Trade and Investment Partnership (TTIP), Obama said, “The answer to globalization is not to close ourselves off,” but he also said it is very important to protect workers’ rights.

Before Obama arrived, Tanya Williams, a community officer, told the Guardian, “I love Michelle, but I also like Barack Obama. It’s exciting to hear someone who has changed so much and encouraged many people to vote for the first time.”

Oliver Sidorczuk, 26, said, “Everyone is very excited to hear what he will say. I want to ask him about voting rights.”

At the end of the session, a young Sikh man from London asked Obama about racial profiling at airports and being mistaken for a Muslim.

Obama said that even though some people have extreme ideas, it is important to live together peacefully. He said, “I visited a mosque a few months ago and said our best allies are American Muslims who are part of our society.”

Furqan Naeem, a campaigner from Manchester, said, “I recently visited the United States and saw important work the president did. His work celebrated America’s diversity and brought communities together.”

Kenny Imafidon, the leader of a youth organization, said after the event, “I will remember what he said about meeting people with different political views and making compromises. Also, what he said about being a good leader and finding talented people.”

Later, Obama met Jeremy Corbyn. Corbyn said they had a very good 90-minute talk. When asked if they talked about Britain’s EU membership, Corbyn said they spoke about it briefly.

After the meeting, Obama played golf with David Cameron. He finished the day with dinner with the British prime minister and the US ambassador, Matthew Barzun, before traveling to Germany.

It is well known that millennials use technology a lot. More than eight out of ten say they sleep with their mobile phone next to their bed. Almost two thirds say they text while driving. One in five has posted a video of themselves online, and three out of four have made a profile on a social networking site. However, there are some millennials who do not use social media at all. Here are four of them.

Celan Beausoleil, 31, from Oakland, California, is a social worker. She has used Facebook on and off, but she last deactivated her account in December 2015. She found that seeing so much personal information from others was too much for her, especially because her job is already very demanding.

She said, “In my job, I listen to people talk about their lives all day, every day. It became overwhelming to go on social media and see every detail of everyone’s lives, even people I don’t really know. I already spend a lot of time with people at work, and it felt like too much to do the same in my personal life.”

But Beausoleil does like how social media connects people around the world. She said, “One thing I liked about Facebook was that I could spend hours clicking from one friend to another, and end up on someone’s page from the other side of the world. I used to do that a lot.”

Jason Mathias, 26, from Baltimore, Maryland, realized one day that he was spending too much time on social media. He thought, “These little seconds add up. What if I used this time to do something else? Would I enjoy it more?”

Mathias had Facebook and Twitter accounts for years, but he deleted them both in November 2012. After he left social media, he quickly forgot about Facebook. He still sees some good things about social media, like how easy it is to organize big events online. Now, he depends on friends to invite him to parties.

He enjoys having more free time. He spends his time in elevators and during breaks at work reading news articles and books. Since he does not follow friends online, he calls them on the phone, which he now likes.

Lauren Raskauskas, 22, from Naples, Florida, says she is a private person, so social media does not interest her much. She said, “My privacy is important to me, and I worry about giving out my data.” She recently deleted her Twitter account and deactivated her Facebook account two years ago when she realized she did not like everyone knowing what she was doing. Still, she can see some good things about social media. For example, when a friend she had lost contact with moved to Naples for a month, Lauren did not know until after her friend had left, which made her sad.

But in the end, her worries about privacy were more important than the benefits of social media. She also found it helpful when she went through a recent break-up. She said, “The last time I ended a relationship and was on Facebook, it was not pleasant. I wondered if I should change my profile photo or status. This time, I don’t have to worry about any of that.”

Hariharan Rajagopalan, 18, from Boston, Massachusetts, is a student at Boston College. He does not think there is any problem with not using social media. He says he has not noticed any difference so far. Even though his classmates post about parties and events on Facebook, they also send him a text message.

The only time Rajagopalan used social media was when he had no other choice. Before starting college, he needed to contact his new roommate, so he made his first and only social media account on Facebook to talk about their plans for the year.

He still has the account, but he says, “I don’t use it. I don’t check it or anything like that.” He has avoided other social media accounts, but as a sports fan, he knows that most news appears on Twitter first. Still, he does not want to get an account because, as he says, “I don’t really need one to read tweets.”

A new report says that the average six-year-old child knows more about digital technology than a 45-year-old adult.

Ofcom, an organization that checks communication standards in the UK, says that broadband internet, which started in 2000, has created a generation of “digital natives.” These are children born after 2000. They learn to use smartphones and tablets before they can even talk.

Jane Rumble from Ofcom says that children today grow up with digital technology, so the way they communicate is different from older people, even from people aged 16 to 24.

Ofcom gave a “digital quotient” (DQ) test to 800 children and 2,000 adults. The test checks how much people know about tablets, smart watches, fast internet, 4G mobile networks, and mobile apps. It also asks how comfortable people feel using these things.

Children aged 6 to 7, who have always had YouTube, Spotify, and online TV, had an average DQ score of 98. Adults aged 45 to 49 had an average score of 96. The highest DQ scores were for 14- to 15-year-olds, with an average of 113.

Now, anyone can take a short version of the DQ test online. The website gives you a DQ score and advice on how to learn more and stay safe online.

The way children talk to each other is very different from older people. The biggest change is in phone calls. Twenty years ago, teenagers spent hours talking on the home phone about friends and love.

Now, children aged 12 to 15 spend only 3% of their communication time making phone calls. For all adults, phone calls are 20% of their communication time. For young adults, it is 9%. Today, children mostly send written messages or share photos and videos.

Over 90% of the time children use devices, they are sending messages. They chat on social networks like Facebook, send instant messages on WhatsApp, or send text messages. Only 2% of their device time is spent emailing. Adults spend 33% of their device time emailing.

When not using their phones, 12- to 15-year-olds also use other media differently. A digital diary shows that they spend only half their viewing time watching live TV, while adults spend almost 70% of their time watching live TV. Children spend 20% of their time watching short videos, like on YouTube or Facebook. The rest of their viewing time is spent watching DVDs, streaming shows on Netflix or iTunes, or watching recorded TV programs.

A new study says that the forests and suburbs of Europe are now home to many large predators. Brown bears, wolves, and lynx are doing well in Europe, even though many people think these animals will soon disappear because of more people and too much use of land. The study found that the numbers of these big animals are staying the same or even increasing.

Brown bears, wolves, and Eurasian lynx live in almost one-third of mainland Europe (not counting Belarus, Ukraine, and Russia). Most of these animals live outside of nature reserves. This shows that people’s changing attitudes and new conservation rules are helping to protect these animals, which were hunted a lot in the past.

Bears are the most common large meat-eating animals in Europe, with about 17,000 living there. There are about 12,000 wolves and 9,000 Eurasian lynx. Only Belgium, Denmark, the Netherlands, and Luxembourg in mainland Europe, like Britain, do not have breeding groups of at least one of these big animals. But the main author of the study and other experts say that these animals now live in areas with many people, so even the British countryside could have big predators.

Guillaume Chapron from Sweden’s University of Agricultural Sciences and other researchers found that wolves sometimes live in suburbs with up to 3,050 people per square kilometer. On average, wolves in Europe live in areas with 37 people per square kilometer, lynx in areas with 21 people per square kilometer, and bears in areas with 19 people per square kilometer. The Scottish Highlands have only nine people per square kilometer.

Chapron said, “To have wolves, we do not need to remove people from the land.” He said that the return of big predators shows that sharing land between people and animals works. This is different from the way North America and Africa keep people and predators apart by putting up fences.

Chapron also said, “I am not saying it is always peaceful—living together can mean problems—but it is important to manage these problems and solve them. Wolves can be hard to live with. The real conflict is not just between people and predators, but also between people who have different opinions about predators. These animals make us think about how we use the land.”

The researchers say that this way of sharing land could work in other parts of the world. Reasons for its success in Europe include stable governments, more wild deer and other prey animals, and money to help farmers protect their animals without killing predators, for example by using electric fences. The most important reason, said Chapron, is the EU Habitats Directive, which makes countries protect and bring back rare animals.

Chapron said, “Without the Habitats Directive, I do not think we would have seen this recovery.” He said this shows that if people want to protect nature and if politicians make strong laws, it is possible to help wildlife. Author George Monbiot, who is starting a new charity called Rewilding Britain to bring back wild land and lost animals, welcomed the news.

Monbiot said, “It is great to see this happening, but Britain is very different—we have lost more big mammals than any country except Ireland. Apart from wild boar coming back by accident, we have done almost nothing, while in much of Europe, bears, lynx, and wolves are returning.”

The study found that the Eurasian lynx now lives in 11 groups in 23 European countries, and only five of these groups are native. This shows that bringing lynx back has worked. Monbiot said that more people now support bringing lynx back to the Scottish mountains.

He said, “If it works in the rest of Europe, there is no reason it cannot work in the UK.” He also said that bears and wolves live close to Rome, so there is no reason why the UK cannot also have more wild animals again.

The view from the visitors’ centre at the south edge of Doñana National Park in southern Spain is perfect for bird lovers. The park has 200,000 hectares of wetlands that are very important for birds in western Europe. Every year, many of Britain’s favourite migratory birds stop here on their way from Africa. Doñana is also home to some of Europe’s rarest birds, like the Spanish imperial eagle.

The landscape is beautiful and full of life, but it is in danger. In 1998, almost two billion gallons of acidic water mixed with waste metals spilled into the park from the Los Frailes mine, which is 45 km away. This toxic waste flowed down the Guadiamar river into the park. After the disaster, more than 25,000 kilos of dead fish were collected, and nearly 2,000 adult birds, chicks, eggs, and nests were killed or destroyed.

This was Spain’s worst environmental disaster, and cleaning it up cost 90 million euros. After this, Spain realized how important Doñana was and decided to spend another 360 million euros, some from the EU, to restore the area. In the 1950s and 60s, some parts of the park were drained to make rice and cotton fields. Now, some of this farmland is being turned back into wetlands.

Restoring Doñana has been expensive but good. However, the park still faces many problems because of modern life. There are plans to build an oil pipeline through Doñana, and some developers want to build new hotels and golf courses, which would need a lot of water. Sand and soil from nearby farms are also blocking the water channels in Doñana.

But the biggest problem for people who want to protect the park is the recent decision by the Andalusian government to reopen the Frailes mine, which almost destroyed Doñana in 1998. “This is Europe’s most precious bird sanctuary, for local birds and for birds that travel between Africa, Britain, and other parts of northwest Europe,” says Laurence Rose of the Royal Society for the Protection of Birds (RSPB). “Doñana already faces many threats, but now they want to bring back the cause of the disaster 16 years ago. This is very worrying.”

The local economy helps explain the government’s decision. The crash of Spain’s banks in 2008 was very bad for the region, and unemployment in some parts of Andalusia is now over 30%. Reopening the mine would create more than 1,000 jobs.

“There are riches here, riches that local people really need,” said energy spokesman Vicente Fernández Guerrero. “We think mining is a good way to help local people stay in the area. This is a mining area. People have been digging for metals here since Roman times.”

Fernández said the mine would only use modern mining methods, which do not create poisonous wet waste. Also, the Canadian company that ran Los Frailes during the disaster cannot run it again. “The best technology in the world will be used here,” Fernández said. “Liquid will not be used. We will make sure of that.”

Some people in the area support the plan, but many are against it. Carlos Dávila, who works for the Spanish Ornithological Society in Doñana, is also worried. “This is a very, very bad idea,” he said. “They say the new mine will be safe, but they said it was safe in 1998, and look what happened. We had the worst environmental disaster in Spain’s history.”

Almost every visitor at a local restaurant had a camera with a long lens or binoculars. Many tourists come to see the birds in Doñana. This is not surprising because it is a very special place. The sky is huge above this flat but interesting landscape. Birds of all shapes and sizes fill the air and sometimes the road. During my visit, a stork stood calmly in front of our car until it decided to fly away.

“The problem is that Spain does not have as much public money as it did 16 years ago. If there was another toxic spill today, it would be much more damaging,” said Rose. Dávila agrees. “After the disaster, Spain realized Doñana was very important and did a lot to clean and protect it,” he said. “Now, we seem to be forgetting that lesson. It is very sad.”

Introduction

Did you know that in the UK, restaurants do not have to give tips to their staff by law? A new government report asked workers, employers, and customers what they think about tipping. After reading the report, government ministers said they want to change the rules so that low-paid workers get the tips that customers leave for them.

The report said that some waiters have to pay up to 15% in administration fees on tips left by customers who pay with credit or debit cards. The government said it might stop employers from charging workers this fee.

The government also said that customers should know that tips are optional, and they want restaurants to clearly show their tipping policy.

We asked waiters around the UK what they think about tipping, how much they earn from tips, if they think it is fair, and what could make it better.

1. Rodri, 37, London: About 50% of a waiter’s income is from tips
Average tips: £60 per eight-hour shift
Rodri thinks waiters are treated best in the US.

Rodri says things have become fairer since the tipping scandal in summer 2015, when many restaurants were found to be taking money from tips for administration fees. But there are still problems. Some restaurants take 4% of all sales to pay chefs and for admin fees, no matter how much the waiter gets in tips. This means if a table spends £100 and does not tip, the waiter has to pay £4 from their own money. This can lead to bad service because waiters feel the company is taking their money and they feel angry at customers who do not tip.

Rodri usually gets about £60 in tips per shift. On a good night, he can get over £100, but on a bad night, it is about £40. About half of a waiter’s income comes from tips. Rodri thinks all restaurants should clearly show their tipping policy. He says tipping is better in America because everyone tips.

2. Elle, 22, Edinburgh: We never know if it’s fair
Average tips: £20 per eight-hour shift
Elle thinks waiters are treated best in France.

Elle has three part-time catering jobs. In her main day job at a café, the small team works both in the café and the kitchen, and all tips are put together and shared equally. In her main evening job at a restaurant, they do not get tips, but their pay is minimum wage plus an extra £2.50 per hour. In her third job, which is event catering, nobody tips.

In restaurants, many customers add tips by card, so staff do not see how much the tip is. This means they do not know if what they get is fair. Elle thinks the system is better in France, where people do not tip much, but being a waiter is seen as a real job with job security and a good income.

3. Ashley, 22, London: Tips pay for customer breakages
Average tips: £10-15 per eight-hour shift
Ashley thinks waiters are treated best in Australia.

Ashley works in a London pub in the evenings and at a local restaurant during the day. In both places, all tips are collected and shared at the end of the night. Some money from the tips is used to pay for things broken by staff or customers.

Ashley thinks it is very unfair that tips are shared, especially when some team members do not work hard. Also, when someone works very well, they do not get the tips they earned. Ashley also thinks it is unfair that tips are used to pay for things broken by customers. Managers should pay for broken glasses and plates without using tips. Ashley usually makes about £20 in tips per shift, but often only gets £10-15 of that money.

Ashley depends on tips because the basic pay is only £7 an hour. Ashley would prefer to have a good basic wage, like in Australia, and not have to rely on tips.

4. Tom, Manchester: A big night of tips can help pay the rent
Average tips: £40 per eight-hour shift
Tom thinks waiters are treated best in Italy.

Where Tom used to work, waiters kept 80% of cash tips and 40% of card tips. The other 20% of cash tips went to junior waiters and bar staff. The other 60% of card tips went to kitchen staff.

Tom says it is hard to say exactly how much he earned per shift, but maybe about £40. A good night of tips could make a big difference to his weekly money. Sometimes, waiters needed a good night to pay their rent.

Tom thinks tipping is better in Italy, where customers do not add a service charge but usually round up their bill. For example, if the meal is £19, they leave a £20 note and do not ask for change. Customers respect the staff. In Italy, being a waiter is often a career, and the experience of the waiters shows in the good service they give.
